params.to: The row number the activity goes to, counted from 0. A number outside the matrix is an error; the same number as from leaves everything in place and returns false.

activities.help: The activities (rows) in display order, addressed by their row number from 0.

stakeholders.help: The stakeholders (columns) in display order, addressed by their column number from 0.

assignments.help: The roles that are set, addressed as assignments["row:column"] with numbers from 0. The value is R, A, C or I; a cell without a role is absent from the map.

raci-matrix.emptyHint: Add activities and stakeholders to build the RACI matrix.
raci-matrix.addStakeholderHint: Now add stakeholders to assign roles.

sipoc.name: SIPOC
sipoc.whenToUse: When the boundaries of a process need clarifying — who supplies, what goes in, which steps run, what comes out and who receives it; not for the flow itself with its decisions and branches, which is what a flowchart is for.

addItem.help: Appends an entry to one of the five SIPOC columns.

params.colKey: The column: suppliers, inputs, process, outputs or customers. Any other value is an error.
params.text: The entry; surrounding whitespace is dropped. An empty text adds nothing and returns -1 — that is a refusal, not an error.

setItem.help: Replaces the entry at a position of a SIPOC column.

params.colKey: The column: suppliers, inputs, process, outputs or customers. Any other value is an error.
params.idx: The position of the entry in the column, counted from 0. A position where the column holds no entry is an error.
params.text: The new entry. An empty text is rejected and leaves the old entry in place (returns false).

removeItem.help: Removes the entry at a position of a SIPOC column.

params.colKey: The column: suppliers, inputs, process, outputs or customers. Any other value is an error.
params.idx: The position of the entry in the column, counted from 0. A position where the column holds no entry is an error.

moveItem.help: Moves an entry within its column or into another column.

params.sourceCol: The column the entry comes from: suppliers, inputs, process, outputs or customers. Any other value is an error.
params.sourceIdx: The position of the entry in the source column, counted from 0. A position without an entry is an error.
params.targetCol: The column the entry goes to: suppliers, inputs, process, outputs or customers. Any other value is an error.
params.dropIdx: The insert position in the target column, counted from 0; the length of the target column means "at the end". A value beyond that is an error.

columns.help: The entries of each SIPOC column in display order, addressed as columns[column]. The five column keys are suppliers, inputs, process, outputs and customers.

five-why.name: 5-Why Analysis
five-why.description: Root cause analysis with branching question paths
five-why.whenToUse: When a single concrete incident is to be traced to its root and the domain knowledge is in the room — not for statistical relationships across many cases.

read.help: Returns the problem statement and the question tree as read state.

setProblem.help: Sets the observed problem statement the question chain starts from.

params.text: The problem in one sentence, descriptive rather than judgemental.

addRoot.help: Adds a new level-1 Why question and returns its id.

addChild.help: Adds the next Why level below a question and returns its id. Returns null when the question is already at level 5 (root cause) — that is a domain refusal, not an error. A parentId that matches no question is an error.

params.parentId: Id of the question the new level is added to.

setAnswer.help: Writes the answer to a Why question.

params.nodeId: Id of the question whose answer is set. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The answer — a cause, not a culprit.

removeNode.help: Removes a question together with every question below it.

params.nodeId: Id of the question to remove. An unknown id is an error.

toggleCollapse.help: Collapses or expands a question's subtree; purely visual, the content stays.

params.id: Id of the question whose subtree is toggled. An unknown id is an error.

collapseAll.help: Collapses every question that has sub-questions.

problem.help: The observed problem statement the question chain starts from.

nodes.help: The branching question tree. Each node carries id, level (1 to 5), parentId, question, answer, children and collapsed; level 5 is the root cause. Bulk data: without options.fields = ['nodes'] only the extent (node count and depth) is returned.

five-why.emptyHint: No questions yet. Click "Add Why" to start.

dmaic-calendar.name: Calendar
dmaic-calendar.title: Title
dmaic-calendar.invalidTimeRange: The end time must be after the start time.
dmaic-calendar.requiredFields: Title and date are required fields.
dmaic-calendar.phaseAdjusted: This appointment carried a phase the active cycle does not know. The form shows the first phase of the cycle — saving will write it.
dmaic-calendar.whenToUse: When the appointments of a project should be kept — meetings, measurement windows, deadlines —, each assigned to a phase and shown in a month or week view; not for tasks without a fixed point in time, that is what the todo list is for, and not for planning activity durations and dependencies.

addEvent.help: Adds an appointment and returns its id.

params.fields: The fields of the appointment: title (the label, must not be empty), date (the day as YYYY-MM-DD), time (the start time as HH:MM, 09:00 if omitted), duration (the duration in whole minutes, at least 5, 60 if omitted), desc (the description, empty if omitted) and phase (the phase of the active cycle the appointment is coloured by; the first phase if omitted). Title and date must be present. An unknown key, a value outside the value set of its field and a missing argument are errors.

updateEvent.help: Changes the supplied fields of an appointment; the others stay as they are.

params.id: The id of the appointment as read() lists it under events. An unknown id is an error.
params.fields: The fields to change, at least one of title, date, time, duration, desc and phase — with the same meaning and the same value sets as in addEvent. An empty field set, an unknown key, a value outside the value set of its field and a missing argument are errors.

params.id: The id of the appointment as read() lists it under events. An unknown id is an error.

setView.help: Sets the calendar view to the month (month) or the week (week).

params.v: The view: month shows the month, week the week. Any other value is an error.

setAxisFrom.help: Sets the first hour shown on the day axis. If it is not before the last hour shown, the axis stays as it is and the call reports false.

params.hour: The hour from 0 to 23. Any other value is an error.

setAxisTo.help: Sets the last hour shown on the day axis. If it is not after the first hour shown, the axis stays as it is and the call reports false.

params.hour: The hour from 1 to 24; 24 is the end of the day. Any other value is an error.

setDayFrom.help: Sets the first weekday shown. If it is after the last weekday shown, the selection stays as it is and the call reports false.

params.dayIndex: The weekday, 0 for Monday through 6 for Sunday. Any other value is an error.

setDayTo.help: Sets the last weekday shown. If it is before the first weekday shown, the selection stays as it is and the call reports false.

params.dayIndex: The weekday, 0 for Monday through 6 for Sunday. Any other value is an error.

events.help: The appointments, each entry described individually under keys. The end of an appointment is computed from start time and duration and is held in no field. Bulk data: without options.fields = ['events'] only the extent is delivered.

axisFrom.help: The first hour shown on the day axis, 0 to 23. It only bounds the display of the week view, not the appointments themselves.

axisTo.help: The last hour shown on the day axis, 1 to 24. It only bounds the display of the week view, not the appointments themselves.

dayFrom.help: The first weekday shown, 0 for Monday through 6 for Sunday.

dayTo.help: The last weekday shown, 0 for Monday through 6 for Sunday.

viewMode.help: The calendar view: month shows the month, week the week. The choice is persisted and survives a restart.

CalendarEvent.id: The identifier of the appointment; the app assigns it when the appointment is created. Use it to address the appointment when changing or deleting.
CalendarEvent.title: The label of the appointment. It must not be empty; spaces at the edges are removed.
CalendarEvent.date: The day of the appointment as YYYY-MM-DD, for example 2026-03-14. Title and date are the required entries.
CalendarEvent.time: The start of the appointment as HH:MM between 00:00 and 23:59; 09:00 when not given. In the dialog the field moves in steps of 5 minutes.
CalendarEvent.duration: The duration of the appointment in whole minutes, at least 5; 60 when not given. In the dialog it is calculated as end minus start and only displayed.
CalendarEvent.desc: A description of the appointment as free text; empty when not given.
CalendarEvent.phase: The phase of the cycle the appointment is coloured by; the phases of the active cycle count, the first one when not given. If the active cycle does not know the phase of an appointment, the dialog shows the first phase and saving writes it in.
CalendarEvent.source: Where the appointment comes from. Only appointments reported from the task list carry this entry, with the value todo; changes made in the calendar are lost at the next report from the task list; change them there.

todo.name: Todo
todo.description: Task list with status, due date, and owner
todo.filterHelp: Narrows the list: by status, by responsible person and by search text in the task text and the owner. The filter does not change any task.
todo.emptyState: No tasks yet. Click "+ Add Task" to get started.
todo.noMatch: No tasks match the current filter.
todo.whenToUse: When the open tasks of a project need tracking with an owner, a due date and a status — not for scheduling in a calendar view and not for rating or selecting measures, which is what the calendar module and the rating matrices are for.

moveTodo.help: Moves a task before another and switches the list to manual order, like dragging the grip. If the list is sorted, the visible order first becomes the stored one; filtered-out tasks follow behind.

params.itemId: The id of the task to move. An unknown id is an error.
params.beforeId: The id of the task it goes before. An unknown id is an error; equal to itemId changes nothing.

addTodo.help: Appends an empty task to the list and returns its id.

setTodoText.help: Sets the text of a task, i.e. what has to be done. Each row has a text field for it. Clicking the column header sorts the list by it; a second click reverses the direction.

params.itemId: The id of the task as read() lists it under items. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The new text. An empty string clears it; a missing argument is an error.

setTodoOwner.help: Sets the owner of a task as a freely typed name; empty means no owner. Clicking the column header sorts the list by it; a second click reverses the direction.

params.itemId: The id of the task as read() lists it under items. An unknown id is an error.
params.owner: The name of the owner. An empty string leaves the task without an owner; a missing argument is an error.

setTodoDue.help: Sets the due date of a task in the notation YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-11-30; empty clears it. Clicking the column header sorts the list by it; a second click reverses the direction.

params.itemId: The id of the task as read() lists it under items. An unknown id is an error.
params.isoDate: The due date written as YYYY-MM-DD. An empty string clears it; any other value is an error.

setTodoStatus.help: Sets the status of a task: open, in progress, done or blocked. The checkbox at the start of the row sets it to done and back to open. Clicking the column header sorts the list by it; a second click reverses the direction.

params.itemId: The id of the task as read() lists it under items. An unknown id is an error.
params.status: One of the four values open, in-progress, done or blocked. Any other value is an error.

setTodoCalendar.help: Decides whether a task is reported to a calendar module of the project. Without a calendar module the mark is still stored and takes effect once one is added.

params.itemId: The id of the task as read() lists it under items. An unknown id is an error.
params.inCalendar: true reports the task, false does not. Any other value — a missing argument included — is an error.

removeTodo.help: Removes a task from the list.

params.itemId: The id of the task as read() lists it under items. An unknown id is an error.

setFilterStatus.help: Sets the status filter of the list. The filter only decides which tasks the list shows; it removes none.

params.value: all shows every task, otherwise one of the four status values open, in-progress, done or blocked. Any other value is an error.

setFilterOwner.help: Sets the filter to one owner. The filter only decides which tasks the list shows; it removes none.

params.value: all shows every task, otherwise the name of an owner that at least one task carries. A name no task carries is an error.

setSearch.help: Sets the search text; it searches task text and owner, case-insensitively.

params.text: The search text. An empty string lifts the search; a missing argument is an error.

setSort.help: Sets the sort column and the sort direction of the list.

params.column: The column to sort by: text, owner, due or status. Any other value is an error.
params.ascending: true sorts ascending, false descending. Any other value — a missing argument included — is an error.

items.help: The tasks in entry order. Per task: id (this is how the actions address it), text, owner, due (due date as YYYY-MM-DD or empty), status (open, in-progress, done or blocked) and cal (whether it is reported to a calendar module).

filterStatus.help: The stored status filter: all or one of the four status values open, in-progress, done, blocked.

filterOwner.help: The stored filter on one owner: all or that owner's name.

search.help: The stored search text over task text and owner; empty means no search.

sortCol.help: The sort column: text, owner, due or status.

sortAsc.help: true means sorted ascending, false descending.

gage-run-chart.whenToUse: Look at a measurement system study before computing statistics: every measurement per part and operator, against a reference line.

read.help: Read the chosen columns, all settings, the grand mean, the reference line, the mean per part and operator and every measurement.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: 'part' — the part of each measurement (required); 'operator' — the operator (optional; without it all repeats count as one operator); 'measurement' — the measured value, numeric or 0/1 (required).
params.ref: A column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from read().pickableColumns of that role, or null to clear it.

setParam.help: Set an option. Everything except the header lines recomputes.

params.key: Which parameter; each key is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. An empty refValue uses the grand mean.

runAnalysis.help: Recompute with the current column values, for example after the data changed.

columnRefs.help: Per role (part, operator, measurement) the column, or null.

refValue.help: The reference line as entered; '' uses the grand mean.

connectWithin.help: Whether the repeats of one operator within a part are joined.

showOperatorMean.help: Whether each operator's mean within a part is marked.

gageInfo.help: The header lines { name, date, reporter, tolerance, misc } as text.

activeColumnSlots.help: The roles setColumn accepts: part, operator, measurement.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts.

pickableColumns.help: Per role the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; the key is instanceId|sheetId|columnId.

errorMsg.help: Why nothing was computed, for example no usable rows; '' otherwise.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null without part and measurement column or without usable rows.

points.help: One row per measurement in panel order: { part, operator, value }. read({ fields: ['points'] }) returns them in full.

Params.refValue: Position of the horizontal reference line in every strip, entered as a number with a decimal point. Empty or not readable as a number, the line sits at the grand mean of all measurements; a change recomputes.
Params.partsPerRow: How many parts stand side by side in one strip, a whole number from 1 to 20, default 7. More parts give further strips below, all with the same vertical axis.
Params.connectWithin: Whether the repeat measurements of one operator on a part are joined by a line in recording order. On by default; display only.
Params.showOperatorMean: Whether the mean of the repeat measurements per part and operator is drawn as a short tick. On by default; display only.

gageInfo.name: Name of the gage for the header above the chart. Free text with no effect on the computation; left empty, the line is omitted.
gageInfo.date: Date of the study for the header, as free text in any format. No effect on the computation; left empty, the line is omitted.
gageInfo.reporter: Who prepared the study, for the header. Free text with no effect on the computation; left empty, the line is omitted.
gageInfo.tolerance: Tolerance of the feature for the header, as free text. It is only a label and enters no computation; left empty, the line is omitted.
gageInfo.misc: Further notes for the header, as free text. No effect on the computation; left empty, the line is omitted.

Result.n: Number of usable measurements: rows with a part label and a finite number in the measurement column. Each one is a point in the chart.
Result.droppedRows: Number of discarded rows: an empty part label or no finite number as the measurement, plus every row past the end of the shortest chosen column.
Result.partCount: Number of distinct parts with at least one usable measurement; one panel per part in the chart.
Result.operatorCount: Number of distinct operators in the operator column. 0 without an operator column. With one, an empty operator cell counts as an operator of its own without a name.
Result.operators: The operators in order of first appearance in the data. Without an operator column a single entry with an empty name.
Result.hasOperators: Whether an operator column is chosen. Without it all repeats of a part count as one series.
Result.grandMean: Arithmetic mean of all n usable measurements, equally weighted. It is the default for the reference line as long as no reference value of your own is entered.
Result.refValue: Where the reference line actually lies: the entered reference value if it reads as a number, the grand mean otherwise.
Result.yMin: Smallest usable measurement. It is the lower end of the vertical axis shared by all strips.
Result.yMax: Largest usable measurement. It is the upper end of the vertical axis shared by all strips.
Result.warnings: Codes about the data: "unbalanced" when not every combination of part and operator occurs or they do not all have the same number of measurements; "droppedRows" when at least one row was discarded. Empty when everything fits.
Result.cellMeans: One mean for each part and operator that occur together. Order as in the chart: parts sorted numerically when every label is a number, alphabetically otherwise; within them the operators in order of first appearance. Missing combinations have no entry.

CellMean.part: The part label as it appears in the part column, as text.
CellMean.operator: The operator as it appears in the operator column, as text; empty without an operator column.
CellMean.mean: Arithmetic mean of this operator's repeat measurements on this part; in the chart the short tick when the operator mean is switched on.

gage-run-chart.name: Gage Run Chart
gage-run-chart.description: Plots every single measurement grouped by part and appraiser against a common reference line — reveals appraiser bias and unusual parts.
gage-run-chart.operatorHint: Optional — without an operator column one series per part is drawn.
gage-run-chart.refValueHint: Leave empty to use the mean of all measurements.
gage-run-chart.warn_unbalanced: Unbalanced design — not every part × operator combination has the same number of measurements.
gage-run-chart.warnDroppedRows: {count} row(s) skipped: empty part or non-numeric measurement.
gage-run-chart.errNoData: No usable measurements in the selected columns.

msa-typ1.name: MSA Type 1 (Cg/Cgk)
msa-typ1.description: Measurement System Analysis Type 1 — Repeatability (Cg) and Bias (Cgk)
msa-typ1.whenToUse: When the capability of a single gage should be checked: a standard or reference part is measured repeatedly, giving repeatability (Cg) and bias (Cgk) — not for measurement systems with several appraisers or parts, which the type 2, 4, 5 and 6 studies cover. Requires the measurements as a numeric column of a data collection.

read.help: Returns the inputs, the selectable sets and the computed result. result is null while the inputs are incomplete.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets one parameter of the study; the recalculation follows after a short pause.

params.key: Which parameter; each key is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value as text, for example '10' or '0.5'. The allowed range per key is given under keys; for the free text fields '' clears the field.

setColumn.help: Picks the data collection column holding the repeated measurements of the master part (at least 25, 50 recommended). The calculation follows after a short pause.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeColumnSlots; this module only has 'value'.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns, or null to clear.

runAnalysis.help: Computes with the current inputs. Repeated calls are harmless; incomplete inputs leave result at null.

scheduleAnalysis.help: Triggers the computation after a short pause; a second request before that replaces the first.

clearResults.help: Discards the result; the inputs stay.

params.help: The entered parameters, values as text; each is described individually under keys.

columnRef.help: The chosen measurement column as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }, or null.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts in the current state.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null while the inputs are incomplete.

Params.name: Name of the characteristic under study, for example “Shaft A diameter”. It appears in the result and does not affect the calculation.
Params.ref: The known reference value of the master part. Every measurement is compared with it; the deviation of their mean from it is the bias.
Params.unit: Unit of the measured values, for example mm. It is only used for labelling.
Params.lsl: Lower tolerance limit of the characteristic. Both limits give the tolerance T = USL − LSL on which Cg and Cgk are based. If one limit is left empty, only the bias is tested.
Params.usl: Upper tolerance limit of the characteristic. Both limits give the tolerance T = USL − LSL on which Cg and Cgk are based. If one limit is left empty, only the bias is tested.
Params.k1: Share of the tolerance the gage spread may use: 0.2 (20 %, common), 0.15 or 0.1. A smaller value is stricter.
Params.k2: How many standard deviations the spread covers: 3 stands for 6·s (common), 4 for 8·s, 6 for 12·s. A larger value is stricter.

Result.mode: Tolerance type of the study: two-sided when both the lower and upper limit are set, otherwise one-sided. One-sided only the bias is assessed; Cg and Cgk are omitted.
Result.n: Number of evaluated measurements. At least 25 are required, 50 are recommended.
Result.xbar: Mean of all repeated measurements of the master part.
Result.sg: Standard deviation of the repeated measurements (sample, n − 1). It measures the repeatability of the gage.
Result.bias: Systematic deviation: mean minus reference value. Positive means the gage reads high on average.
Result.biasTest: t-test whether the bias differs significantly from zero.
Result.resolution: Smallest step between the measurements, detected from the data; 0 if it cannot be determined.
Result.upperThreshold: Upper outlier limit: mean plus 3 standard deviations.
Result.lowerThreshold: Lower outlier limit: mean minus 3 standard deviations.
Result.details: One entry per measurement in measuring order, with deviations and an outlier flag.
Result.noSpread: True when all measurements are equal. Cg and Cgk cannot be computed then.
Result.params: The parameters the calculation used, as numbers.
Result.T: Tolerance: upper minus lower limit. Only for a two-sided tolerance, otherwise empty.
Result.biasPercent: Bias as a percentage of the tolerance, with sign.
Result.Cg: Capability index from the spread alone: Cg = (k₁ · T) / (2 · k₂ · sg). From 1.33 the gage counts as capable.
Result.Cgk: Capability index including bias: Cgk = (k₁ · T / 2 − |bias|) / (k₂ · sg). From 1.33 the gage counts as capable.
Result.cgStatus: Verdict on Cg: capable from 1.33, conditionally capable from 1.00 to below 1.33, not capable below. Empty when Cg cannot be computed.
Result.cgkStatus: Verdict on Cgk, with the same limits as for Cg.
Result.overall: Overall verdict: capable when Cg and Cgk are capable; not capable when either is not capable; otherwise conditionally capable. No verdict for a one-sided tolerance or without spread.
Result.tolUsage: Share of the tolerance taken up by the gage spread: 2 · k₂ · sg / T as a percentage.
Result.varEv: %Var(EV): gage spread as a share of the tolerance, 100 · k₁ / Cg. The same value as the tolerance usage.
Result.varEvBias: %Var(EV+bias): like %Var(EV) but computed with bias, 100 · k₁ / Cgk. Empty when Cgk is not positive.
Result.resPercent: Resolution as a percentage of the tolerance. At most 5 % is the usual requirement.
Result.zoneHi: Upper limit of the zone reference value ± k₁ · T / 2 drawn in the run chart.
Result.zoneLo: Lower limit of the zone reference value ± k₁ · T / 2 drawn in the run chart.

BiasTest.t: Test statistic of the t-test: bias divided by sg / √n.
BiasTest.df: Degrees of freedom of the t-test, n − 1.
BiasTest.p: Two-sided p-value. Below 0.05 the bias counts as significant.

Detail.index: Running number of the measurement, from 1.
Detail.deviation: Deviation of the measurement from the reference value.
Detail.devFromMean: Absolute deviation of the measurement from the mean.
Detail.isOutlier: True when the measurement lies outside mean ± 3 standard deviations.

ResultParams.lsl: Lower tolerance limit the calculation used; empty for a one-sided tolerance without a lower limit.
ResultParams.usl: Upper tolerance limit the calculation used; empty for a one-sided tolerance without an upper limit.
ResultParams.k1: Share of the tolerance the calculation used.

msa-typ1.errRefMissing: Reference value is missing or invalid.
msa-typ1.errUslLeqLsl: USL must be greater than LSL.
msa-typ1.statusNoSpread: No spread measured – check gage resolution
msa-typ1.interpCgPass: Repeatability is sufficient — gage spread is small enough relative to tolerance.
msa-typ1.interpCgkPass: Systematic deviation (bias) of the gage from the reference value is acceptable.
msa-typ1.interpWarn: Conditionally capable — action recommended (calibration, check environment, etc.).
msa-typ1.interpFail: Not capable — gage must not be used for inspection.

msa-typ2.name: MSA Type 2/3 (Gage R&R)
msa-typ2.description: Measurement System Analysis Type 2 (with operator, Gage R&R) and Type 3 (no operator, automated measurement systems)
msa-typ2.whenToUse: When a measurement system with several parts (and usually several appraisers) should be assessed: a crossed study gives repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R) by ANOVA; without an operator column the module computes as type 3 for automated measurement systems — not for the capability of a single gage on a standard, which type 1 covers. Requires parts, optionally appraisers, and the measurements as columns of a data collection.

read.help: Returns the inputs, the selectable sets and the computed result. result is null while the inputs are incomplete or invalid; errorMsg then gives the reason.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets one parameter of the study; the recalculation follows after a short pause.

params.key: Which parameter; each key is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value as text, for example '10' or '0.5'. The allowed range per key is given under keys; for the free text fields '' clears the field.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeColumnSlots: part, operator (optional) or measurement (numeric).
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns, or null to clear.

runAnalysis.help: Computes with the current inputs. Repeated calls are harmless; missing columns clear result silently, invalid inputs clear it and set errorMsg.

params.options: Optional; { showErrors: false } suppresses the message in errorMsg.

scheduleAnalysis.help: Triggers the computation after a short pause; a second request before that replaces the first.

clearResults.help: Discards the result; the inputs stay.

params.msg: Optional; a message to put into errorMsg.

params.help: The entered parameters, values as text; each is described individually under keys.

columnRefs.help: The chosen columns per slot (part, operator, measurement) as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }, or null.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts in the current state.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null while the inputs are incomplete or invalid.

errorMsg.help: The rejection of the last computation as text, empty if none.

Params.lsl: Lower specification limit (LSL) as text, for example '24.9'. Together with the upper limit it gives the tolerance T = USL − LSL that %GRR (tolerance) refers to; empty means there is no lower limit.
Params.usl: Upper specification limit (USL) as text, for example '25.1'. Together with the lower limit it gives the tolerance T = USL − LSL that %GRR (tolerance) refers to; empty means there is no upper limit.
Params.alpha: Significance level α of the ANOVA as text, for example '0.05'; empty counts as 0.05. If the p-value of the part × operator interaction is below α, it stays a source of its own, otherwise it is pooled with repeatability. A newly added module pre-fills α from the global confidence level, so 0.05 at 95 %.
Params.k: Spread factor k of the study variation k · σ: 6 covers 99.73 % of the values, 5.15 covers 99 % (AIAG, 3rd edition). It affects the study variation and %GRR (tolerance), not %GRR (study variation).
Params.verdictBasis: Basis of the %GRR verdict: automatic takes the tolerance when both limits are set, otherwise the study variation; tolerance takes the tolerance as long as both limits are set and, without them, falls back to the study variation just like automatic; study variation always relates the verdict to the total variation of the study.
Params.sigmaHist: Historical process standard deviation σ as text, optional and greater than 0. When set, the variance components table also gives each source's share of this process variation; empty means there is no process reference.

Result.mode: Method of the study: type 2 (gage R&R) with parts, operators and replicates when an operator column is chosen; without an operator column type 3, which uses only parts and replicates and has no operator influence.
Result.n: Number of evaluated measurements: parts times operators times replicates, parts times replicates for type 3.
Result.r: Number of replicates per part and operator, per part for type 3.
Result.partLabels: The part names in the order of their first appearance.
Result.operatorLabels: The operator names in the order of their first appearance; empty for type 3.
Result.anova: Analysis of variance with the sources parts, operators, part × operator interaction, repeatability and total; per source the sum of squares, degrees of freedom, mean square, F value and p-value.
Result.interactionSignificant: True when the p-value of the part × operator interaction is below α: then an operator measures certain parts differently from the other operators. Always false for type 3.
Result.interactionPooled: True when the interaction is not significant and was therefore combined with repeatability into one error term (sums of squares and degrees of freedom added). False for type 3, which has no interaction.
Result.alpha: Significance level α used in the computation; 0.05 without input. A newly added module takes α from the global confidence level.
Result.varComp: Variance components from the ANOVA: repeatability (EV), reproducibility (AV) with its parts operator and interaction, measurement system (GRR), parts (PV) and total (TV); per component the variance, standard deviation, study variation and percentages.
Result.ndc: Number of distinct categories: ndc = 1.41 · σ parts / σ GRR, rounded down to a whole number. From 5 on, the resolution of the measurement system is sufficient for the part variation. 999 means the measurement system has no spread but the parts do; 0 when neither has spread.
Result.verdictBasis: Basis the verdict actually rests on: tolerance or study variation. With the automatic choice it is the tolerance when both limits are set, otherwise the study variation.
Result.pctGRRVerdict: The %GRR value the verdict rests on: %GRR (tolerance) or %GRR (study variation), depending on the effective basis.
Result.grrStatus: Verdict on the measurement system from %GRR on the effective basis: below 10 % acceptable, 10 % to below 30 % conditionally acceptable, 30 % or more not acceptable.
Result.ndcStatus: Verdict on ndc: sufficient from 5 on, insufficient below.
Result.cellData: The measurements per part and operator in measurement order, per part for type 3.
Result.cellMeans: Mean per part and operator, per part for type 3.
Result.cellRanges: Range per part and operator, largest minus smallest replicate, per part for type 3. They give the average range of the R chart.
Result.partMeans: Mean per part across all operators and replicates.
Result.operatorMeans: Mean per operator across all parts and replicates; empty for type 3.
Result.controlChart: Limits of the x̄-R chart; a subgroup is one part × operator cell, one part for type 3, with r replicates.
Result.params: The parameters used in the computation, as numbers.
Result.warnings: Notes on the study, for example when type 3 has only 2 replicates per part; at least 3 are recommended.

Anova.part: Source parts: variation between the part means. Its F test checks whether the parts differ; the reference is the interaction when it is significant, otherwise repeatability.
Anova.operator: Source operators: variation between the operator means, tested like the parts. Empty for type 3.
Anova.interact: Source part × operator interaction, tested against repeatability. Empty when it was pooled, and for type 3.
Anova.equip: Source repeatability: variation of the replicates within a cell, including the interaction when it was pooled. No F value and no p-value.
Anova.total: Source total: variation of all measurements around the grand mean, with sum of squares and degrees of freedom only.

AnovaRow.ss: Sum of squares SS: the sum of squared deviations attributed to this source.
AnovaRow.df: Degrees of freedom df: parts p − 1, operators o − 1, interaction (p − 1) · (o − 1), repeatability p · o · (r − 1) (p · (r − 1) for type 3), total n − 1. Pooling adds the degrees of freedom.
AnovaRow.ms: Mean square MS = SS / df. Missing for the total source.
AnovaRow.f: F value: the MS of the source divided by the MS it is tested against. Only for parts, operators and interaction.
AnovaRow.pValue: p-value of the F test. Below α the influence of the source counts as significant. Only for parts, operators and interaction.

VarComp.repeatability: Repeatability (EV): the variation when the same operator measures the same part several times; σ² EV is the mean square of repeatability. %EV is its share of the study variation, 100 · σ EV / σ total.
VarComp.reproducibility: Reproducibility (AV): the variation between operators, σ² AV = σ² operator + σ² interaction; 0 for type 3. %AV is its share of the study variation, 100 · σ AV / σ total.
VarComp.operator: Operator share of reproducibility: σ² = (MS operators − MS reference) / (p · r), not below 0; the reference is the interaction or, when pooled, repeatability.
VarComp.interact: Interaction share of reproducibility: σ² = (MS interaction − MS repeatability) / r, not below 0; 0 when the interaction was pooled.
VarComp.grr: Measurement system (GRR): σ² GRR = σ² EV + σ² AV. %GRR (study variation) = 100 · σ GRR / σ total. If the study variation is the effective basis of the verdict: below 10 % the measurement system is acceptable, 10 % to below 30 % conditionally acceptable, 30 % or more not acceptable.
VarComp.part: Part variation (PV): σ² = (MS parts − MS reference) / (o · r), not below 0; divided by r for type 3.
VarComp.total: Total variation (TV): σ² total = σ² GRR + σ² parts.

VarCompEntry.variance: Variance σ² of the component, estimated from the mean squares of the ANOVA.
VarCompEntry.sigma: Standard deviation of the component, σ = √σ².
VarCompEntry.studyVar: Study variation k · σ with the spread factor k (6 or 5.15).
VarCompEntry.pctContribution: Share of the total variance: 100 · σ² / σ² total. GRR and parts add up to 100 %.
VarCompEntry.pctStudyVar: Share of the study variation: 100 · σ / σ total. Because standard deviations do not add up, the shares do not sum to 100 %.
VarCompEntry.pctTolerance: Share of the tolerance: 100 · k · σ / T with T = USL − LSL; empty unless both limits are set. If the tolerance is the effective basis of the verdict, for GRR: below 10 % acceptable, 10 % to below 30 % conditionally acceptable, 30 % or more not acceptable.
VarCompEntry.pctProcess: Share of the historical process variation: 100 · σ / σ historical; empty without a historical process σ.

ControlLimits.xbarCL: Center line of the x̄ chart: the grand mean.
ControlLimits.xbarUCL: Upper control limit of the x̄ chart: grand mean + A₂ · R̄.
ControlLimits.xbarLCL: Lower control limit of the x̄ chart: grand mean − A₂ · R̄.
ControlLimits.rCL: Center line of the R chart: the average range R̄.
ControlLimits.rUCL: Upper control limit of the R chart: D₄ · R̄.
ControlLimits.rLCL: Lower control limit of the R chart: D₃ · R̄.
ControlLimits.rBar: Average range R̄ over all part × operator cells, over all parts for type 3.
ControlLimits.A2: Chart factor A₂ for the subgroup size r, the number of replicates; with more than 6 replicates the factors for 6 apply.
ControlLimits.D3: Chart factor D₃ for the subgroup size r. In this analysis it is always 0 (for 2 to 6 replicates, above that the factors for 6 apply), so the lower limit of the R chart is always 0.
ControlLimits.D4: Chart factor D₄ for the subgroup size r.

ResultParams.alpha: Significance level α as a number; 0.05 without input.
ResultParams.studyVarMultiplier: Spread factor k as a number, 6 or 5.15.
ResultParams.tolerance: Tolerance T = USL − LSL; empty unless both limits are set.
ResultParams.lsl: Lower specification limit as a number; without input not a valid number.
ResultParams.usl: Upper specification limit as a number; without input not a valid number.
ResultParams.verdictBasis: Chosen basis of the verdict, tolerance or study variation; missing with the automatic choice.
ResultParams.historicalSigma: Historical process σ as a number; empty when none was given.

msa-typ2.operatorHint: Leave operator column empty for Type 3 (no operator influence)
msa-typ2.warnFewReplicatesTyp3: Only 2 replicates per part — Bosch/VDA recommend at least 3 for Type 3 (e.g. 25×2 or 10×3).
msa-typ2.chartGageRunTitle: Gage run chart (raw values by part and operator)
msa-typ2.interpPass: Measurement system acceptable — measurement variation is small enough relative to the verdict basis (tolerance or study variation).
msa-typ2.interpWarn: Conditionally acceptable — action recommended. Only acceptable for non-critical characteristics.
msa-typ2.interpFail: Not acceptable — measurement system must not be used for inspection.
msa-typ2.interpNdcPass: Adequate resolution — measurement system can distinguish enough categories.
msa-typ2.interpNdcFail: Inadequate resolution — measurement system cannot sufficiently resolve part variation.
msa-typ2.interactionPooledNote: The Part × Operator interaction was not significant (p ≥ α) and was pooled with repeatability.
msa-typ2.errUnbalanced: Unbalanced design — every operator must measure every part the same number of times.
msa-typ2.errUnbalancedTyp3: Unbalanced design — every part must be measured the same number of times.
msa-typ2.errTooFewReplicates: At least 2 replicates per cell required (currently: {n}).
msa-typ2.errUslLeqLsl: USL must be greater than LSL.
msa-typ2.errHistSigmaInvalid: Historical process σ must be a positive number.

msa-typ4.name: MSA Type 4 (linearity)
msa-typ4.description: Measurement System Analysis Type 4 — linearity and bias across the measurement range (AIAG %Lin, VDA 5 Q_MS,BI)
msa-typ4.whenToUse: When you need to check whether a measurement system measures equally correctly across the whole range: reference values and measured values as columns give the bias per reference point and a regression of the bias over the range (AIAG %linearity or VDA 5 Q_MS,BI) — not for capability on a single standard, which type 1 covers. Requires a reference column and a measured column of a data collection.

read.help: Returns the inputs, the selectable sets and the computed result. result is null while the inputs are incomplete or invalid.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets a parameter of the linearity study; the recomputation follows after a short pause.

params.key: Which parameter; each key is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value as text, for example '10' or '0.5'. The allowed range per key is given under keys; for the free text fields '' clears the field.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeColumnSlots: reference (reference values, numeric) or measured (measured values, numeric).
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column in pickableColumns, or null to clear.

runAnalysis.help: Computes with the current inputs. Calling it repeatedly is harmless; missing or invalid inputs clear result.

scheduleAnalysis.help: Triggers the computation after a short pause; a second request before then replaces the first.

clearResults.help: Discards the result and the charts; the inputs stay.

params.help: The entered parameters, values as text; the tolerance limits are nested under tolerance with LSL and USL. Each parameter is described at setParam under keys.

refColumn.help: The chosen reference column as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }, or null.

measColumn.help: The chosen measured column as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }, or null.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state; sigmaP is missing in the tolerance mode.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts in the current state.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null while the inputs are incomplete or invalid.

Params.name: Name of the studied feature, for example “coating thickness”. It labels the result and has no effect on the computation.
Params.unit: Unit of the reference and measured values, for example mm. It is only used for labels.
Params.norm: Assessment standard: AIAG MSA assesses %linearity, the largest %bias and the significance of slope and intercept; VDA 5 assesses the capability figure Q_MS_BI. Both are computed; the standard decides the tiles, the traffic light and the interpretation.
Params.pvMode: Reference quantity for the percentages %linearity and %bias: the tolerance T = USL − LSL or the process spread 6 · σP.

tolerance.LSL: Lower specification limit (LSL) of the feature. Together with the upper limit it gives the tolerance T = USL − LSL. In tolerance mode T is the reference quantity; under VDA 5, T always enters Q_MS_BI, also in 6 · σP mode.
tolerance.USL: Upper specification limit (USL) of the feature. Together with the lower limit it gives the tolerance T = USL − LSL. In tolerance mode T is the reference quantity; under VDA 5, T always enters Q_MS_BI, also in 6 · σP mode.

Params.sigmaP: Process standard deviation σP. Only asked for in 6 · σP mode; the reference quantity is then 6 · σP.
Params.alpha: Significance level of the t-tests per reference value and for slope and intercept; it also sets the level of the confidence intervals (1 − α). The choices are 0.01, 0.05 (usual) and 0.10.

Result.ok: Always true: a result exists only when the computation succeeded.
Result.perReference: One entry per reference value, sorted ascending, with mean, bias, t-test and traffic light. At least 5 distinct reference values with at least 3 repeats each are required.
Result.regression: Least-squares line of the individual deviations (measured minus reference value) over the reference value. A slope other than 0 means the bias changes over the measuring range.
Result.kpi: The figures of both standards, AIAG MSA and VDA 5; both are always computed.
Result.pv: The reference quantity that %linearity and %bias refer to.
Result.interpretation: The interpretation of the result as a sentence, depending on standard and traffic-light colour, with the figures filled in.

ReferencePoint.xRef: The reference value (nominal value of the master part) the repeated measurements belong to.
ReferencePoint.n: Number of repeated measurements at this reference value, at least 3.
ReferencePoint.mean: Mean of the repeated measurements at this reference value.
ReferencePoint.bias: Systematic deviation at this reference value: mean minus reference value. Positive means the system measures too high on average.
ReferencePoint.sd: Standard deviation of the repeated measurements at this reference value (sample, n − 1).
ReferencePoint.tStat: Test statistic of the t-test for bias = 0: t = bias / (s / √n). Empty when all repeats are equal and the bias is not 0.
ReferencePoint.pValue: Two-sided p-value of the t-test for bias = 0 with n − 1 degrees of freedom. Below α the bias counts as significant.
ReferencePoint.percentBias: Absolute bias in percent of the reference quantity: %bias = |bias| · 100 / reference quantity.
ReferencePoint.verdict: Traffic light per reference value: green when the bias is not significant (p ≥ α); yellow when it is significant but at most 10 % of the reference quantity; red otherwise.

Regression.slope: Slope of the fitted line of bias over reference value: how much the bias changes per unit of the reference value. Ideally 0; if it is significant (p < α), the measurement system is not linear.
Regression.intercept: Intercept of the fitted line: the bias the line would have at reference value 0. Ideally 0; if it is significant (p < α), there is a constant bias.
Regression.seSlope: Standard error of the slope: √(MSE / Sxx), where Sxx is the sum of squared distances of the reference values of all individual measurements from their mean.
Regression.seIntercept: Standard error of the intercept: √(MSE · (1 / N + x̄² / Sxx)), with x̄ the mean of the reference values of all individual measurements.
Regression.tSlope: Test statistic for slope = 0: the slope divided by its standard error.
Regression.tIntercept: Test statistic for intercept = 0: the intercept divided by its standard error.
Regression.pSlope: Two-sided p-value for slope = 0 with N − 2 degrees of freedom. Below α the slope counts as significant.
Regression.pIntercept: Two-sided p-value for intercept = 0 with N − 2 degrees of freedom. Below α the intercept counts as significant.
Regression.MSE: Mean squared error: sum of the squared distances of the individual deviations from the line, divided by N − 2.
Regression.N: Number of all individual measurements that enter the regression.
Regression.dfResid: Residual degrees of freedom: N − 2, at least 1.
Regression.ciSlope: Confidence interval of the slope at level 1 − α, as lower and upper limit. If it contains 0, the slope is not significant.
Regression.ciIntercept: Confidence interval of the intercept at level 1 − α, as lower and upper limit. If it contains 0, the intercept is not significant.

Kpi.aiag: Figures and verdict according to AIAG MSA.
Kpi.vda5: Figures and verdict according to VDA 5.

KpiAiag.percentLinearity: %Linearity: change of the bias over the measuring range in percent of the reference quantity, 100 · |slope| · (largest − smallest reference value) / reference quantity. The larger of %linearity and largest %bias decides: up to 5 % acceptable, up to 10 % conditionally acceptable, above that not acceptable.
KpiAiag.maxPercentBias: Largest %bias over all reference values: 100 · largest |bias| / reference quantity. The larger of %linearity and largest %bias decides: up to 5 % acceptable, up to 10 % conditionally acceptable, above that not acceptable.
KpiAiag.slopeSignificant: True when the slope differs significantly from 0 (p < α). The AIAG verdict is then red.
KpiAiag.interceptSignificant: True when the intercept differs significantly from 0 (p < α). The AIAG verdict is then red.
KpiAiag.verdict: Verdict according to AIAG MSA: red when slope or intercept is significant or the larger of %linearity and largest %bias exceeds 10 %; yellow when it exceeds 5 %; green otherwise.

KpiVda5.u_BI: Standard uncertainty from bias and linearity: u_BI = √(largest |bias|² + (standard error of the slope · measuring range)²); the measuring range is the largest minus the smallest reference value.
KpiVda5.U: Expanded uncertainty from bias and linearity: U = 2 · u_BI.
KpiVda5.Q_MS_BI: Capability figure according to VDA 5: Q_MS_BI = U / T · 100 % with the tolerance T = USL − LSL, also in 6 · σP mode. Up to 15 % capable, up to 30 % conditionally capable, above that not capable. Empty when T is not positive.
KpiVda5.verdict: Verdict according to VDA 5: green up to Q_MS_BI 15 %, yellow up to 30 %, red above that.

Verdict.color: Traffic-light colour of the verdict: green, yellow or red. The limits depend on the standard.
Verdict.key: Key of the verdict text in the translation file, per standard and traffic-light colour.

ProcessVariation.mode: How the reference quantity was determined: from the tolerance or from 6 · σP.
ProcessVariation.value: The reference quantity: T = USL − LSL in tolerance mode, 6 · σP in 6 · σP mode. It must be positive, otherwise nothing is computed.
ProcessVariation.source: Origin of the reference quantity; always the same as the mode.

Interpretation.textKey: Key of the interpretation sentence in the translation file, per standard and traffic-light colour.
Interpretation.params: The figures filled into the interpretation sentence, as text with two decimals.

InterpretationParams.pctLin: %Linearity as text with two decimals; AIAG MSA only.
InterpretationParams.maxPctBias: Largest %bias as text with two decimals; AIAG MSA only.
InterpretationParams.qMsBi: Q_MS_BI as text with two decimals; VDA 5 only.

msa-typ4.title: MSA Type 4
msa-typ4.titleLong: Linearity & Bias Across the Measurement Range
msa-typ4.emptyState: Select reference and measured columns to start the analysis.
msa-typ4.errLengthMismatch: Reference and measured columns must have the same length.
msa-typ4.errTooFewReferences: At least 5 distinct reference values required (currently {got}).
msa-typ4.errInvalidPv: Invalid process variation basis. Tolerance must be > 0, or σₚ > 0.
msa-typ4.interpAIAG_green: No significant slope (p={pSlope}) and no significant bias. %Linearity {pctLin} %, max. %Bias {maxPctBias} % — measurement system is linear and unbiased across the measurement range.
msa-typ4.interpAIAG_yellow: %Linearity {pctLin} % or max. %Bias {maxPctBias} % in the gray zone (5–10 %). Investigate cause (calibration, gage).
msa-typ4.interpAIAG_red: %Linearity {pctLin} % or max. %Bias {maxPctBias} % > 10 %, or slope/intercept significant. Measurement system not suitable for this tolerance range — calibrate or replace.
msa-typ4.interpVDA5_green: Q_MS,BI = {qMsBi} % ≤ 15 %. Bias/linearity contribution to measurement uncertainty unremarkable.
msa-typ4.interpVDA5_yellow: Q_MS,BI = {qMsBi} % in the range 15–30 %. Conditionally suitable, review the overall uncertainty budget.
msa-typ4.interpVDA5_red: Q_MS,BI = {qMsBi} % > 30 %. Not suitable — rework the measurement system.

msa-typ5.name: MSA Type 5 (attribute)
msa-typ5.description: Attribute Measurement System Analysis — multiple appraisers, kappa-based agreement (Cohen, Fleiss, weighted)
msa-typ5.whenToUse: When an attribute measurement system (good/bad, classes, ordinal levels) is to be assessed: several appraisers rate parts, repeatedly, against an optional reference. The result is kappa agreement, effectiveness and a verdict by AIAG or Bosch rules — not for measured characteristics, which types 1 to 3 cover. Requires a data collection with a part, an appraiser and a rating column; the wide layout (one column per appraiser and trial) cannot be fully operated through the surface.

read.help: Returns the inputs, the selectable sets and the computed result. result is null while no rows can be evaluated; with invalid inputs only meta is present, the reason under meta.errors.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets a parameter of the study; the recomputation follows after a short pause. A new feature type resets the positive level.

params.key: Which parameter; each key is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value as text; the allowed range per key is given under keys. positiveLevel takes one of the levels from detectedLevels.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeColumnSlots: part, appraiser, rating, reference or replicate. appraiser, rating and replicate apply only in the long layout. The rating columns of the wide layout cannot be set.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column in pickableColumns, or null to clear.

runAnalysis.help: Computes with the current inputs. Calling it repeatedly is harmless; missing or invalid inputs clear result.

scheduleAnalysis.help: Triggers the computation after a short pause; a second request before then replaces the first.

clearResults.help: Discards the result and the charts; the inputs stay.

params.help: The entered parameters as setParam takes them and describes them under keys, plus ordinalOrder (order of the levels, null while automatic; not settable through the surface).

columns.help: The chosen columns: part, appraiser, rating, reference and replicate each as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } or null, plus ratings as the list of rating columns of the wide layout (not settable through the surface).

detectedLevels.help: The rating levels found in the chosen rating column (or the columns of the wide layout); the values setParam accepts for positiveLevel. Empty while no rating column is chosen.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state; weights is missing outside the ordinal type, trials outside the wide layout, positiveLevel outside the binary type or without detected levels.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts in the current state. In the wide layout appraiser, rating and replicate are missing, and the matrix slot ratings is not included: the wide layout cannot be fully operated through the surface.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null while no rows can be evaluated. With invalid inputs only meta is present, the reason under meta.errors.

Params.type: Feature type of the ratings: binary (two levels, such as OK and NOK), nominal (several classes without order) or ordinal (ordered levels, such as a grading scale). It decides which figures arise: miss, false alarm and signal detection exist only for binary data, weighted κ only for ordinal data. A new type resets the positive level.
Params.weights: Weighting of κ for the ordinal type, so that a near miss counts less than a far one: linear w = 1 − |i − j| / (k − 1), quadratic w = 1 − ((i − j) / (k − 1))², with i, j the level positions and k the number of levels. The default is quadratic.
Params.layout: Data layout of the ratings: long with one row per rating (part, appraiser, rating, optionally reference and replicate) or wide with one column per appraiser and trial.
Params.trials: Number of trials per appraiser in the wide layout, as text, for example '2'. The columns are grouped in order: first all trials of appraiser 1, then appraiser 2; the number of columns must be divisible by the number of trials.
Params.ruleSet: Verdict rule. AIAG MSA (4th ed.) takes the worst of its criteria: Fleiss' κ (acceptable from 0.75, marginal from 0.40), lowest effectiveness (from 90 % or 80 %) and, only for binary data with a reference from a column, highest miss rate (up to 2 % or 5 %) and highest false-alarm rate (up to 5 % or 10 %). Bosch booklet 10 rates the smallest available κ: acceptable from 0.9, marginal from 0.7.
Params.alpha: Significance level α. It sets the level of the confidence intervals (1 − α); the p-values of the κ tests are judged against it. The choices are 0.01, 0.05 (usual) and 0.10.
Params.positiveLevel: The level that counts as positive (OK) for binary data, one of the detected levels; without a choice the most frequent rating. The miss rate counts negative parts rated positive, the false-alarm rate positive parts rated negative; if the level is chosen wrongly, the two are swapped.

Result.meta: Framework data of the study: feature type, levels, number of parts, appraisers and trials, origin of the reference, plus the notes and, with invalid inputs, the reasons why nothing was computed.
Result.perAppraiser: One entry per appraiser with their repeatability, the κ within their trials, the comparison with the reference and the cross table against the reference.
Result.betweenAppraisers: Agreement of the appraisers with each other: Cohen's κ per pair of appraisers and Fleiss' κ over all appraisers and trials together.
Result.allVsReference: Fleiss' κ over all ratings of all appraisers, the reference per part counted as one more rater (Bosch booklet 10). Missing without a reference.
Result.signalDetection: Signal detection per appraiser: sensitivity d′ and decision criterion. Only for binary data with a reference, otherwise empty.
Result.perPart: One row per part with reference, the ratings per appraiser and the deviations, sorted by severity: first by the number of deviations from the reference, then by the number of inconsistent appraisers.
Result.disagreement: Per appraiser their confusions (which reference level they rated as which other level) and the parts on which they contradicted themselves across trials.
Result.overall: Overall agreement across all appraisers per AIAG: all appraisers agree, and all agree and are also correct.
Result.verdict: Overall verdict acceptable, marginal or not acceptable. It follows the worst criterion of the chosen verdict rule; if no criterion can be rated, it is marginal.
Result.interpretation: The interpretation of the result as a sentence, depending on the verdict, with the figures filled in.

Meta.type: Feature type the computation used: binary, nominal or ordinal.
Meta.levels: The rating levels of the computation in their order: for binary data the positive level comes first, ordinal ascending (numbers by value), nominal alphabetical.
Meta.parts: Number of distinct parts in the study.
Meta.appraisers: Number of distinct appraisers in the study.
Meta.reps: Highest number of ratings one appraiser gave for a single part, i.e. the largest number of trials.
Meta.referenceSource: Origin of the reference: from the reference column, from the appraisers' consensus (without a reference column; binary and nominal by majority, ordinal by median) or none, if the chosen reference column holds no values. With a consensus, miss and false alarm are not rated.
Meta.ambiguousParts: Parts for which the appraisers' consensus is not unique (a tie). They count neither towards effectiveness nor towards κ against the reference. Empty when the reference comes from a column.
Meta.warnings: Notes on the data, for example unequal numbers of trials, a non-unique consensus or too few repeats. The computation runs anyway.
Meta.errors: Reasons why nothing was computed, for example too few parts, appraisers or levels, or an unknown reference value. Present only with invalid inputs; everything else is then missing.

Message.code: Identifier of the note or error; the matching text is in the translation.
Message.params: The values filled into the text, such as a count or the affected parts.

AppraiserStats.repeatability: Agreement of the appraiser with themselves: share of parts with at least two trials that they rated the same in all trials. Missing when no part has two trials. The tile above shows the mean over all appraisers.
AppraiserStats.withinKappa: Fleiss' κ within the appraiser: their trials are counted like different raters (Minitab “Within Appraisers”). Missing when no part has two trials. Under Bosch booklet 10 a candidate for the smallest κ.
AppraiserStats.vsReference: Comparison of the appraiser's ratings with the reference: effectiveness, miss, false alarm, bias and κ. Missing without a reference.
AppraiserStats.confusionMatrix: Cross table of the appraiser's ratings against the reference: rows are their rating, columns the reference, the diagonal the hits.

Rate.agree: Number of agreeing cases, the numerator of the share.
Rate.total: Number of all cases, the denominator of the share.
Rate.rate: Share of agreeing cases: agreements divided by all cases, between 0 and 1.
Rate.ci95: Wilson confidence interval of the share, as lower and upper bound, at level 1 − α (95 % for α = 0.05). It stays within 0 to 1 even for shares near 0 or 1.

FleissKappa.kappa: Fleiss' κ = (P̄ − Pₑ) / (1 − Pₑ): the observed agreement P̄, corrected for the agreement Pₑ expected by chance. 1 means complete agreement, 0 no better than chance. AIAG: acceptable from 0.75, marginal from 0.40; Bosch booklet 10: acceptable from 0.9, marginal from 0.7.
FleissKappa.se0: Standard error of κ under the null hypothesis κ = 0 after Fleiss, Nee and Landis (1979); it serves the test only, not a confidence interval. Without a value for the Randolph method.
FleissKappa.z: Test statistic of the one-sided test of κ = 0: z = κ / SE₀. Without a value for the Randolph method.
FleissKappa.p: One-sided p-value against κ > 0: p = 1 − Φ(z). Below α the agreement is significantly better than chance. Without a value for the Randolph method.
FleissKappa.method: Method: fleiss-1971 when every part has the same number of ratings; otherwise randolph with free marginals (Pₑ = 1 / k for k levels). With randolph, z and p stay without a value.

VsReference.effectiveness: Effectiveness: share of the appraiser's ratings that match the reference. AIAG: acceptable from 90 %, marginal from 80 %; the lowest value across appraisers is rated. The tile above shows the mean over all appraisers.
VsReference.missRate: Miss rate: share of ratings on parts with a negative reference (NOK) that the appraiser rated positive (OK). Binary only. AIAG: acceptable up to 2 %, marginal up to 5 %; the highest value is rated, and only with a reference from a column.
VsReference.falseAlarmRate: False-alarm rate: share of ratings on parts with a positive reference (OK) that the appraiser rated negative (NOK). Binary only. AIAG: acceptable up to 5 %, marginal up to 10 %; the highest value is rated, and only with a reference from a column.
VsReference.biasRate: Bias of the appraiser: miss rate minus false-alarm rate. Above 0 they judge too leniently, below 0 too strictly. Binary only.
VsReference.kappa: Cohen's κ between appraiser and reference, weighted for the ordinal type. The tile above shows the mean over all appraisers.
VsReference.fleissKappa: Fleiss' κ over the appraiser's trials with the reference as one more rater (Bosch booklet 10, procedure 7). Under Bosch a candidate for the smallest κ; the tile above then shows the mean over all appraisers.

ErrorRate.rate: Share of wrong ratings: errors divided by the cases in the denominator. With no cases it is 0 and does not count towards the verdict.
ErrorRate.ci95: Wilson confidence interval of the share, as lower and upper bound, at level 1 − α (95 % for α = 0.05).
ErrorRate.n: Number of cases in the denominator: for the miss rate the ratings on parts with a negative reference, for the false-alarm rate those on parts with a positive reference.

BiasRate.value: Miss rate minus false-alarm rate. Positive means too lenient (bad parts slip through), negative too strict (good parts are rejected). Without a value when there are no negative or no positive reference parts.

CohenKappa.kappa: Cohen's κ = (pₒ − pₑ) / (1 − pₑ) from the observed agreement pₒ and the chance agreement pₑ of the cross table. Weighted for the ordinal type, so that a near miss counts less than a far one. 1 means complete agreement, 0 no better than chance.
CohenKappa.se: Standard error of κ after Cohen (1960) for the confidence interval: SE = √(pₒ · (1 − pₒ) / (N · (1 − pₑ)²)), with N the number of rating pairs.
CohenKappa.se0: Standard error of κ under the null hypothesis κ = 0 after Fleiss, Cohen and Everitt (1969); it serves the test only.
CohenKappa.z: Test statistic of the one-sided test of κ = 0: z = κ / SE₀.
CohenKappa.p: One-sided p-value against κ > 0: p = 1 − Φ(z). Below α the agreement is significantly better than chance.
CohenKappa.ci95: Confidence interval of κ as lower and upper bound: κ ± z(1 − α/2) · SE, at level 1 − α (95 % for α = 0.05). Under Bosch booklet 10 the table against the reference shows Fleiss' κ, which has no interval; the column then stays without a value.
CohenKappa.method: Method: cohen unweighted for binary and nominal data, weighted-linear or weighted-quadratic for the ordinal type.

PairKappa.kappa: Cohen's κ between the two appraisers of the pair: κ = (pₒ − pₑ) / (1 − pₑ), weighted for the ordinal type. 1 means complete agreement, 0 no better than chance.
PairKappa.se: Standard error of κ after Cohen (1960) for the confidence interval: SE = √(pₒ · (1 − pₒ) / (N · (1 − pₑ)²)), with N the number of rating pairs.
PairKappa.se0: Standard error of κ under the null hypothesis κ = 0 after Fleiss, Cohen and Everitt (1969); it serves the test only.
PairKappa.z: Test statistic of the one-sided test of κ = 0: z = κ / SE₀.
PairKappa.p: One-sided p-value against κ > 0: p = 1 − Φ(z). Below α the two appraisers agree significantly better than chance.
PairKappa.ci95: Confidence interval of κ as lower and upper bound: κ ± z(1 − α/2) · SE, at level 1 − α (95 % for α = 0.05).
PairKappa.method: Method: cohen unweighted for binary and nominal data, weighted-linear or weighted-quadratic for the ordinal type.
PairKappa.confusion: Cross table of the pair: rows are the ratings of the first appraiser, columns those of the second. Per part, as many trials count as both have in common.

ConfusionMatrix.rows: The levels of the rows, in the order of the level list.
ConfusionMatrix.cols: The levels of the columns, the same as those of the rows.
ConfusionMatrix.counts: The frequencies: row i, column j counts how often row level i met column level j. The diagonal holds the agreements.

BetweenAppraisers.pairwiseCohenKappa: Cohen's κ per pair of appraisers; the entry is named after both appraisers, separated by a vertical bar.
BetweenAppraisers.fleissKappa: Fleiss' κ over all appraisers and trials together. Under AIAG a criterion of the verdict: acceptable from 0.75, marginal from 0.40.

SignalDetection.perAppraiser: Per appraiser their sensitivity, decision criterion, hit rate and false-alarm rate according to signal detection theory.

Detection.dPrime: Sensitivity d′ = Φ⁻¹(hit rate) − Φ⁻¹(false-alarm rate): how well the appraiser tells positive from negative parts. 0 means guessing, the larger the better.
Detection.criterion: Decision criterion c = −½ · (Φ⁻¹(hit rate) + Φ⁻¹(false-alarm rate)). Positive means reluctant with the positive rating, negative generous; 0 is neutral.
Detection.hitRate: Hit rate: share of positive ratings on parts with a positive reference. At 0 % or 100 % corrected after Hautus (1995): (hits + 0.5) / (n + 1), so that d′ stays finite.
Detection.falseAlarmRate: False-alarm rate of signal detection: share of positive ratings on parts with a negative reference; in substance the miss rate, not the false-alarm rate of the effectiveness table. At 0 % or 100 % likewise corrected after Hautus.

PartRow.reference: Reference rating of the part; empty when none is known, also with a non-unique consensus.
PartRow.byAppraiser: Per appraiser their ratings of the part in the order of the trials.
PartRow.vsRefErrors: Number of individual ratings that deviate from the reference; so a consistently wrong appraiser weighs more than a one-off slip. Empty when the part has no reference.
PartRow.mixedAppraisers: Number of appraisers who did not rate the part consistently across their trials.
PartRow.isDisputed: True when at least one rating deviates from the reference or an appraiser rated the part inconsistently.

Disagreement.confusionPairs: The appraiser's kinds of confusion: which reference level they rated as which other level, how often and on which parts. Parts without a reference do not count.
Disagreement.mixed: Number of parts the appraiser did not rate consistently across their trials; this needs no reference.

ConfusionPair.to: The level the appraiser gave instead.
ConfusionPair.count: How often this confusion occurred, counted in individual ratings.
ConfusionPair.parts: The affected parts, each named once.

Overall.betweenAppraisers: Share of parts on which all appraisers gave the same rating in all trials (AIAG “Between Appraisers”). Needs no reference.
Overall.allVsReference: Share of parts on which all appraisers agree and also match the reference (AIAG “All Appraisers vs Standard”). Only parts with a reference are in the denominator; missing without a reference.

AgreementShare.agree: Number of parts that meet the condition.
AgreementShare.n: Number of parts in the denominator.
AgreementShare.rate: Share: parts with agreement divided by the parts in the denominator, between 0 and 1.
AgreementShare.ci95: Wilson confidence interval of the share, as lower and upper bound, at level 1 − α (95 % for α = 0.05).

Verdict.ruleSet: The verdict rule applied: AIAG MSA (4th ed.) or Bosch booklet 10.
Verdict.level: The verdict: acceptable, marginal or not acceptable, after the worst criterion. If no criterion can be rated, it is marginal.
Verdict.driver: The criterion that decides the verdict: the first in table order at the worst level. Empty when no criterion can be rated.
Verdict.driverAppraiser: The appraiser the deciding criterion belongs to; empty for a criterion across all appraisers, such as the overall Fleiss' κ.
Verdict.referenceNote: Note for binary data with a reference from the consensus: miss and false alarm are then not rated, because an error all appraisers share stays invisible in the consensus. Otherwise empty.
Verdict.criteria: The criteria in table order, each with value, level and limits. AIAG: Fleiss' κ, lowest effectiveness, highest miss rate and highest false-alarm rate; Bosch booklet 10: the smallest κ.

Criterion.id: Identifier of the criterion: fleissKappa, effectiveness, missRate or falseAlarmRate under AIAG, minKappa under Bosch booklet 10.
Criterion.value: The rated value; for per-appraiser criteria the extreme across all appraisers, i.e. the lowest effectiveness, the highest miss rate and the highest false-alarm rate.
Criterion.level: The level of this criterion: acceptable, marginal or not acceptable.
Criterion.appraiser: The appraiser with the extreme value, on a tie the first in alphabetical order; empty for the overall Fleiss' κ and, under Bosch, when the smallest κ comes from all appraisers with the reference.
Criterion.limits: The limits of this criterion for acceptable and marginal.
Criterion.direction: Direction of the limits: min means higher is better, the value must reach the limit (κ, effectiveness); max means lower is better, the value must not exceed the limit (miss rate, false-alarm rate).
Criterion.source: Where the smallest κ under Bosch booklet 10 comes from: the overall Fleiss' κ, κ within one appraiser, κ of one appraiser with the reference, or all appraisers with the reference.

Limits.good: Limit for acceptable: under AIAG 0.75 for κ, 0.90 for effectiveness, 0.02 for the miss rate and 0.05 for the false-alarm rate; under Bosch booklet 10 0.9 for κ.
Limits.marginal: Limit for marginal: under AIAG 0.40 for κ, 0.80 for effectiveness, 0.05 for the miss rate and 0.10 for the false-alarm rate; under Bosch booklet 10 0.7 for κ. Beyond it the criterion is not acceptable.

Interpretation.textKey: Translation key of the interpretation sentence, depending on the verdict.
Interpretation.params: The values filled into the interpretation sentence.

InterpretationParams.kappa: Fleiss' κ over all appraisers as text with three decimals; a dash when κ cannot be computed.
InterpretationParams.minEff: The lowest effectiveness in percent as text with one decimal; a dash without a reference.
InterpretationParams.driver: The identifier of the deciding criterion as text; empty when none can be rated.
InterpretationParams.ruleSet: The verdict rule applied as an identifier, aiag or bosch.

msa-typ5.title: MSA Type 5

table.noDisputes: No part is disputed — all appraisers agree.
table.noDisagreement: No misclassification and no inconsistent repeat.

charts.gageRun: Gage run chart (ratings by part and appraiser)

msa-typ5.emptyState: Select part, appraiser and rating columns to start the analysis.
msa-typ5.errUnknownReferenceLevel: Reference value "{value}" not among detected classes (part {part}).
msa-typ5.errOrdinalLevelsUnordered: Ordinal ordering is not uniquely defined.
msa-typ5.warnUnbalancedReps: Unequal replicate counts ({min}–{max}). Cohen κ uses min-alignment, Fleiss κ switches to Randolph.
msa-typ5.warnAmbiguousConsensus: {count} part(s) without a unique consensus reference — excluded from effectiveness/κ vs. reference.
msa-typ5.warnLowRepCount: None or too few replicates for: {appraisers}. Repeatability cannot be computed.
msa-typ5.wideHint: Columns in worksheet order: all trials of appraiser 1 first, then appraiser 2 … The appraiser name is the common start of the column names (A-1, A-2 → A).
msa-typ5.emptyStateWide: Choose the part column and the rating columns to start the analysis.
msa-typ5.errWideInvalidTrials: Trials per appraiser: please enter a whole number of at least 1.
msa-typ5.errWideColumnsNotDivisible: The {columns} rating columns cannot be split into groups of {trials} trials.
msa-typ5.positiveHint: Default: the most frequent rating counts as OK. If that is wrong, use "Swap positive" — otherwise miss and false-alarm rate are swapped.
msa-typ5.ordinalHint: Order follows sorted values; drag reordering will follow in a later version.
msa-typ5.interp_good: Fleiss κ = {kappa}, effectiveness ≥ {minEff} %. Inspection process reproducible and consistent with the reference.
msa-typ5.interp_marginal: Fleiss κ = {kappa}, minimum effectiveness {minEff} %. Marginal — train appraisers or sharpen rating criteria.
msa-typ5.interp_unacceptable: Fleiss κ = {kappa}, minimum effectiveness {minEff} %. Not acceptable — the inspection process must be reworked.
msa-typ5.interp_marginal_driver: {decisive}. Marginal — train appraisers or sharpen rating criteria.
msa-typ5.interp_unacceptable_driver: {decisive}. Not acceptable — the inspection process must be reworked.

verdictNote.missFaNotRated: Miss and false-alarm rate not rated — the reference is the appraisers' consensus.

msa-typ6.name: MSA Type 6 (stability)
msa-typ6.description: Stability / long-term behavior — control chart (I-MR/x̄-R) over a repeatedly measured reference part, Nelson rules 1–8 and a linear drift test
msa-typ6.whenToUse: When a measurement system has to stay stable over time: a reference part is measured repeatedly, the control chart (I-MR or x̄-R) shows violations of the Nelson rules, and a linear drift test checks for a trend. Needs a data collection with a value column, optionally a timestamp column and, for x̄-R, a subgroup column — not for the spread of a single measurement series, use types 1 to 3 for that.

read.help: Returns the inputs, the selectable sets and the computed result. result is null while the inputs are incomplete or invalid; errorMsg then names the error code of a failed analysis.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets one parameter of the study; the analysis reruns after a short pause.

params.key: Which parameter; each key is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. null or '' clears mu0 and sigma0.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeColumnSlots: timestamp (timestamp or order), value (measurement) or subgroup. subgroup applies only with chartType xbar-r.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column in pickableColumns, or null to clear.

runAnalysis.help: Computes with the current inputs. Calling it repeatedly is harmless; missing or invalid inputs clear result.

scheduleAnalysis.help: Triggers the computation after a short pause; a second request before then replaces the first.

clearResults.help: Discards the result and the charts; the inputs stay.
