params.help: The entered parameters as setParam takes them and describes them under keys, plus sourceTyp1InstanceId (the adopted type 1 instance, not settable through the surface).

columns.help: The chosen columns: timestamp, value and subgroup, each as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } or null.

exampleWorksheetId.help: Internal bookkeeping: the data collection a loaded example created; null without an example.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state; baselineK is absent with limitsMode given, mu0 and sigma0 are absent with limitsMode from-study.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts in the current state; subgroup is absent unless chartType is xbar-r.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null while the inputs are incomplete or invalid.

errorMsg.help: The error code of a failed analysis, otherwise null.

Params.measurementName: Name of the observed feature, for example “shaft diameter”. It labels the result and has no effect on the computation.
Params.unit: Unit of the measured values, for example mm. It is only used for labels.
Params.chartType: Chart type: I-MR for individual values with moving range, at least 10 values; x̄-R for subgroup means with their range, at least 5 subgroups of equal size with 2 to 25 values. x̄-R needs a subgroup column.
Params.limitsMode: Origin of the control limits: from the study data, computed from the first k baseline subgroups, or given as target mean µ₀ and target spread σ₀, for example from a type 1 study.
Params.baselineK: Number k of baseline subgroups (for I-MR, of the first individual values) from which the center line and control limits are computed. At least 5 and at most as many as the data hold are allowed; below 20 a warning appears. The default is 20.
Params.mu0: Given target mean µ₀; it is the center line of the location chart. Only with given limits.
Params.sigma0: Given target spread σ₀ of the individual values, greater than 0. The control limits lie at µ₀ ± 3 · σ₀, for x̄-R at µ₀ ± 3 · σ₀ / √n. Only with given limits.
Params.enabledRules: The Nelson rules 1 to 8 the points of the location chart are checked against. The default is rules 1 to 6; with none ticked, nothing is checked.
Params.alpha: Significance level of the drift test: 0.01, 0.05 (usual) or 0.10. A drift with p < α makes the verdict at least marginal, one with p < α/10 unstable.

Result.meta: Frame data of the analysis: chart type, origin of the limits, size and warnings.
Result.primary: The location chart: individual values for I-MR, subgroup means for x̄-R, with center line, control limits and rule violations.
Result.secondary: The spread chart: moving ranges for I-MR, subgroup ranges for x̄-R, with center line and control limits.
Result.drift: Linear regression of the location chart points over time, with a t-test of whether the slope differs from 0.
Result.ruleViolations: One entry per location chart point that violates at least one Nelson rule, with time, value and violated rules, sorted by point.
Result.verdict: Stability verdict with its driver and the limits it was judged by.
Result.interpretation: The interpretation of the result as a sentence, depending on verdict and driver.

Meta.chartType: The computed chart type: I-MR or x̄-R.
Meta.limitsMode: Where the limits come from: the study data or given values.
Meta.n: Subgroup size: 1 for I-MR, for x̄-R the number of values per subgroup.
Meta.subgroupCount: Number of points on the location chart: individual values for I-MR, subgroups for x̄-R.
Meta.pointCount: Number of all analysed measured values.
Meta.baselineK: The set number k of baseline subgroups; it only takes effect when the limits come from the study data.
Meta.warnings: Notes on reliability: fewer than 20 baseline subgroups, timestamps that do not increase monotonically, or a rule violation within the baseline that can distort the limits computed from it.

Warning.code: Identifier of the warning: W_BASELINE_LT_20 (fewer than 20 baseline subgroups), W_TIMESTAMPS_NON_MONOTONIC (timestamps not monotonically increasing) or W_LIMITS_FROM_UNSTABLE_BASELINE (rule violation within the baseline).
Warning.params: Values filled into the warning text; present only for a too small baseline, then with the number k of baseline subgroups.

PrimaryChart.series: The points of the location chart in time order: the individual values for I-MR, the subgroup means for x̄-R. The mean tile shows the mean of these points.
PrimaryChart.cl: Center line of the location chart: mean of the baseline when the limits come from the study data, otherwise the target mean µ₀.
PrimaryChart.ucl: Upper control limit of the location chart: center line + 3 · σ.
PrimaryChart.lcl: Lower control limit of the location chart: center line − 3 · σ.
PrimaryChart.sigma: Estimated spread of the location chart points. From the study data: for I-MR the mean moving range of the baseline / d₂, for x̄-R the mean range of the baseline / (d₂ · √n). Given: σ₀, for x̄-R σ₀ / √n.
PrimaryChart.label: Chart kind: i for individual values, xbar for subgroup means.
PrimaryChart.violations: One entry per point and violated Nelson rule; a point that violates several rules appears several times.

Violation.index: Position of the point on the location chart, counted from 0.
Violation.ruleId: Number of the violated Nelson rule, 1 to 8.

SecondaryChart.series: The ranges in time order: for I-MR the absolute difference of two consecutive values, with the first value missing; for x̄-R the largest minus the smallest value per subgroup.
SecondaryChart.cl: Center line of the spread chart: mean range of the baseline when the limits come from the study data, otherwise d₂ · σ₀.
SecondaryChart.ucl: Upper control limit of the spread chart: D₄ · center line.
SecondaryChart.lcl: Lower control limit of the spread chart: D₃ · center line; for subgroups of up to 6 values it is 0.
SecondaryChart.label: Chart kind: MR for moving ranges, R for subgroup ranges.

Drift.slope: Slope of the regression line through the location chart points over time: change per point when no time column is chosen, otherwise per unit of the timestamps (per millisecond for dates). Ideally 0.
Drift.se: Standard error of the slope: square root of the residual variance divided by the sum of squared distances of the time values from their mean.
Drift.tStat: Test statistic for slope = 0: the slope divided by its standard error.
Drift.pValue: Two-sided p-value of the drift test for slope = 0. Below α the drift counts as significant, below α/10 as strong; a strong drift makes the verdict unstable.
Drift.intercept: Intercept of the regression line: its value at time 0.
Drift.df: Degrees of freedom of the drift test: number of location chart points minus 2.
Drift.ciSlope: Confidence interval of the slope at level 1 − α, as lower and upper limit. If it contains 0, no drift can be shown.
Drift.slopeUnit: Unit label of the slope; currently always measurement unit per point, even when the time axis comes from timestamps.
Drift.tScale: Time axis of the regression: the timestamps when a time column is chosen, otherwise the running number of the points from 1.

RuleViolation.primaryIndex: Position of the point on the location chart, counted from 0.
RuleViolation.time: Time of the point: the timestamp from the time column, for x̄-R the mean of the subgroup's timestamps (dates in milliseconds); without a time column the running number from 1.
RuleViolation.value: Value of the point on the location chart: individual value for I-MR, subgroup mean for x̄-R.
RuleViolation.ruleIds: The numbers of the Nelson rules this point violates, ascending.

Verdict.level: Stability verdict: stable without rule violations and without significant drift (p ≥ α); unstable from 3 violating points or with strong drift (p < α/10); marginal in between.
Verdict.driver: What drives the verdict: nothing, Nelson violations, drift or both.
Verdict.nelsonCount: Number of points that violate at least one Nelson rule. From 3 the verdict is unstable, from 1 at least marginal.
Verdict.driftP: p-value of the drift test, the same as in the drift regression.
Verdict.thresholds: The limits the verdict was judged by: unstable from 3 violating points or with strong drift at p < α/10; significant drift at p < α.

Thresholds.nelsonUnstable: Number of violating points from which the verdict is unstable: 3.
Thresholds.driftStrong: p limit for strong drift: α/10, so 0.005 at α = 0.05. Below it the verdict is unstable.
Thresholds.alpha: Significance level of the drift test as a number; below it a drift counts as significant.

Interpretation.textKey: Key of the interpretation sentence in the translation file, per verdict and driver.
Interpretation.params: The values filled into the interpretation sentence.

InterpretationParams.nelsonCount: Number of violating points, as in the verdict.
InterpretationParams.driftP: p-value of the drift test as text with four decimals.
InterpretationParams.slope: Slope of the drift as text with four decimals.

msa-typ6.emptyHint: Select a timestamp/order and a value column to start the analysis.
msa-typ6.empty: Select a timestamp/order and a value column to start the analysis.

stable.none: No Nelson violations and no significant drift (p = {driftP}). The measurement system behaves stably over time.

marginal.nelson: {nelsonCount} Nelson violation(s), but no significant drift (p = {driftP}). Marginal — investigate the cause of the violation(s).
marginal.drift: No pattern in the Nelson rules, but a weak trend is emerging (slope {slope}, p = {driftP}). Marginal — keep monitoring the development.

unstable.nelson: {nelsonCount} Nelson violations — the measurement system shows an unstable pattern over time. Investigate the cause (calibration, reference part, operator).
unstable.drift: Significant linear trend (slope {slope}, p = {driftP}) — the measurement system is drifting systematically. Check calibration/adjustment.
unstable.both: {nelsonCount} Nelson violations AND significant drift (slope {slope}, p = {driftP}) — the measurement system is unstable and drifting systematically. Immediate investigation required.

warnings.W_BASELINE_LT_20: Baseline subgroups k = {k} < 20 — the computed control limits are statistically less robust.
warnings.W_TIMESTAMPS_NON_MONOTONIC: Timestamps are not monotonically increasing; the series was automatically sorted by time.
warnings.W_LIMITS_FROM_UNSTABLE_BASELINE: A Nelson violation lies within the baseline subgroups — the control limits computed from them may be contaminated.

errors.E_SUBGROUP_MISMATCH: The subgroup column and value column must have the same length.
errors.E_SUBGROUP_SIZE_OUT_OF_RANGE: Subgroup size n = {n} is outside the allowed range ({min}–{max}).
errors.E_BASELINE_EXCEEDS_DATA: Baseline subgroups k = {k} exceeds the available data ({available}).
errors.E_INVALID_ALPHA: Significance level α invalid — allowed values are 0.01, 0.05, 0.10.

multi-vari.name: Multi-Vari Chart
multi-vari.description: Stages single measurements across up to four factors and splits the spread into variance components — shows where the variation actually comes from.
multi-vari.whenToUse: When the spread of a measured characteristic must be traced to its sources: stages every single measurement by two to four factors (for example shift, cavity, part) and splits the variance into components, nested or crossed, by ANOVA or REML; needs one numeric measurement column and two factor columns.

read.help: Returns the measurement column, the factor rows in order, model form, estimator, the four display switches, the selectable columns and the result. result is null until a measurement column and two factor columns are chosen; errorMsg then names the reason (fewer than two factors, invalid design, no usable data), except while the measurement column is still missing (errorMsg stays empty).

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets the model form, the estimator or one of the four display switches; the analysis reruns. The display switches only change the chart, not the result.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. The factor columns are chosen per factor row below.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeColumnSlots; this module only has 'measurement'.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns.measurement, or null to clear.

addFactor.help: Appends an empty factor row at the end (innermost nesting level). Four factors are the limit: a fifth row cannot be added.

removeFactor.help: Removes a factor row; the analysis reruns. An error when only two rows remain.

params.rowId: The id of a row from read().factors. An unknown id is an error.

moveFactor.help: Moves a factor row directly before another one; the row order is the nesting, so the analysis reruns.

params.rowId: The id of the row to move, from read().factors.
params.beforeRowId: The id of the row it is placed in front of, from read().factors. Required; an unknown id is an error. To make a row last, move each row after it in front of it, in turn.

setFactorColumn.help: Points a factor row at a column of a data collection; the analysis reruns.

params.rowId: The id of a row from read().factors. An unknown id is an error.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns.factor, or null to clear the row.

runAnalysis.help: Computes with the chosen columns. Without a measurement column, with fewer than two filled factor rows, with an invalid design or without usable data result stays null; errorMsg then names the reason (without a measurement column errorMsg stays empty).

columnRefs.help: The chosen measurement column as { measurement: { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } }, or measurement null.

factors.help: The factor rows in order, each { id, ref }; ref is the column reference or null. The order is the nesting: row 0 is outermost (X axis).

modelForm.help: Variance model: 'nested' (A > B(A) > …) or 'crossed' (A, B, A×B, …).

showPoints.help: Display switch: draw the single measurements. Changes only the chart, not the result.

connectMeans.help: Display switch: connect the group means. Changes only the chart, not the result.

showGroupMean.help: Display switch: mark the group means. Changes only the chart, not the result.

showRefLine.help: Display switch: draw the grand-mean reference line. Changes only the chart, not the result.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts in the current state.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot (measurement, factor) the columns setColumn and setFactorColumn accept, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'.

result.help: Groups of the multi-vari chart and variance components, each figure described individually under keys; null without a measurement column, with fewer than two factors or without data; if only the decomposition fails, the result stays with empty variance components and errorMsg gives the reason.

errorMsg.help: The reason no result exists (fewer than two factors, no usable data, invalid design) or that the variance decomposition failed; an empty string otherwise, including while the measurement column is missing.

Params.modelForm: The model form of the variance decomposition, selector Model form, default Nested. Nested builds the terms A, B (in A), C (in A, B) …: each factor sits inside all factors before it, the order of the factor rows is the nesting. Crossed builds all main effects and interactions (A, B, A × B …). The model form also decides which factor combinations are expected and therefore whether the note “Unbalanced design” appears.
Params.estimator: The estimator of the variance components, selector Estimator, default ANOVA (Henderson I). ANOVA solves the equations of the expected mean squares in one step and sets negative estimates to 0; REML estimates iteratively (at most 100 iterations, tolerance 10⁻⁸) and stays non-negative, the more dependable choice for unbalanced designs. With more than 500 measurements REML falls back to ANOVA; the estimator that actually ran is reported with the variance components.
Params.showPoints: Display switch Show single measurements, default on: draws every single measurement as a point in the colour of its series. Changes only the chart, not the result.
Params.connectMeans: Display switch Connect means, default on: in every panel, joins the cell means of a series across the X axis levels with a line. Changes only the chart, not the result.
Params.showGroupMean: Display switch Show group means, default on: marks the mean of each X axis group, across all series, with a short horizontal tick. Changes only the chart, not the result.
Params.showRefLine: Display switch Show grand mean, default on: draws the grand mean of all usable measurements as a horizontal reference line. Changes only the chart, not the result.

Result.strips: The rows of the chart: one per level of the fourth factor (panel row), exactly one with fewer than four factors.
Result.seriesLevels: The levels of the second factor (series), in legend order; numbers are ordered numerically (3, 4, 10).
Result.factorNames: The names of the assigned factors in role order: first X axis, second series, third panel column, fourth panel row.
Result.grandMean: The grand mean, tile Grand mean: the arithmetic mean of all usable measurements. The tile subline gives the range from the smallest to the largest measurement.
Result.n: Number of usable measurements, tile Measurements: rows with a numeric measurement and an assigned level in every factor. The tile subline gives the number of factors.
Result.droppedRows: Number of discarded rows: empty or non-numeric measurement or an empty factor level. Rows are counted up to the longest chosen column.
Result.warnings: The warnings of both computations as codes, without duplicates: unbalanced (unequal cell sizes; also for a missing factor combination, provided the variance decomposition was computed), emptyCells (a factor combination is missing), tooManyAxisLevels, tooManySeriesLevels, tooManyPanels (display limit exceeded) and the warnings of the variance decomposition. The interface additionally shows the number of skipped rows when rows were discarded; that message is not in the list.
Result.yMin: The smallest usable measurement, lower end of the range under the grand mean and of the y axis.
Result.yMax: The largest usable measurement, upper end of the range under the grand mean and of the y axis.
Result.balanced: Whether the design is balanced: true when all occupied cells hold the same number of measurements and no expected factor combination is missing; which combinations are expected depends on the model form. When false, the interface shows a note under the table that REML is the more dependable choice.
Result.panelCount: Number of panels: levels of the panel row times levels of the panel column, each 1 when the factor is absent.
Result.limits: The exceeded display limits, one row each: more than 30 X axis levels, more than 12 series levels or more than 48 panels; empty when everything fits.
Result.renderable: Whether the chart is drawn: true when no display limit is exceeded. When false, the warning names the column; the variance component table stays valid.
Result.vc: The variance components, table under the chart; empty when the decomposition fails, for example on a design that cannot be estimated. The error message then gives the reason.

Strip.idx: The running number of the chart row, from 0.
Strip.rowLevel: The level of the fourth factor (panel row) of this chart row; an empty text with fewer than four factors.
Strip.panels: The panels of this chart row, one per level of the third factor (panel column), exactly one with fewer than three factors.

Panel.panelLevel: The level of the third factor (panel column) of this panel; an empty text with fewer than three factors.
Panel.groups: The groups on the X axis, one per level of the first factor, empty ones included, so that all panels share the same X positions.

Group.level: The level of the first factor (X axis) of this group.
Group.mean: The group mean: the mean of all measurements of the group across all series, drawn as a short horizontal tick (Show group means); empty for an empty group.
Group.series: The occupied series of this group, one per level of the second factor that has measurements; none for an empty group.

Series.level: The level of the second factor (series), also its colour and legend entry.
Series.values: All single measurements of this cell in data order, drawn as points (Show single measurements).
Series.mean: The arithmetic mean of the cell; Connect means draws the line through these values.

Limit.code: The exceeded limit: tooManyAxisLevels (X axis), tooManySeriesLevels (series) or tooManyPanels (panels).
Limit.column: The responsible column; for panels the names of the third and fourth factor, separated by a comma.
Limit.count: The actual number of levels or panels.
Limit.max: The allowed number: 30 X axis levels, 12 series levels, 48 panels.

Vc.modelForm: The model form used for the decomposition, as chosen under Model form: nested or crossed.
Vc.estimator: The estimator that actually ran: ANOVA for REML with more than 500 measurements, with the warning rowCapExceeded.
Vc.balanced: Whether the design is balanced from the point of view of the variance decomposition: all cells equally sized and no missing combination.
Vc.n: Number of measurements in the decomposition, the same usable rows as in the chart.
Vc.terms: The table rows in model order, the residual (repeat) last. Without replicates the finest term is merged into the residual.
Vc.totalVariance: The total variance, footer Total: the sum of all variance components including the residual.
Vc.converged: REML only, empty otherwise: yes when every component last changed by less than 10⁻⁸ relative or by less than 10⁻⁸ times the sum of the components in absolute terms before 100 iterations were reached; no otherwise, and then the warning notConverged applies and the components are approximations.
Vc.iterations: REML only, empty otherwise: the number of iterations until convergence or up to the limit of 100; 0 for a constant measurement.
Vc.warnings: The warnings of the variance decomposition as codes: unbalanced, noReplicates (no replicates, finest term merged into the residual), rowCapExceeded (more than 500 measurements, switched to ANOVA), aliasedTerms (term with 0 degrees of freedom removed before REML, reported as 0), notConverged (REML did not converge), negativeComponent (negative ANOVA estimate set to 0).

VcTerm.id: The term code with one letter per factor: nested A, B(A), C(AB), D(ABC), crossed A, B, A*B …, plus Error for the residual.
VcTerm.label: The component, column Component: the term with column names, nested for example “Cavity (in Tool)”, crossed for example “Shift × Line”; the last row is the residual (repeat), the spread between repeat measurements.
VcTerm.df: Degrees of freedom of the term, column DF, from the ANOVA table; ANOVA only, empty for REML (the table shows –).
VcTerm.ss: The sum of squares of the term, column SS, from the ANOVA table; ANOVA only, empty for REML (the table shows –).
VcTerm.ms: The mean square, column MS: SS divided by DF; ANOVA only, empty for REML (the table shows –).
VcTerm.variance: The estimated variance component σ² of the term, column Variance, never negative. ANOVA solves the equations of the expected mean squares and sets a negative solution to 0; REML estimates the components iteratively and also bounds them at 0 or above.
VcTerm.sd: The standard deviation of the term, column StDev: √σ², in the unit of the measurements.
VcTerm.percent: The share of the total variance, column Share %: σ² of the term divided by the total variance times 100, one decimal; 0 when the total variance is 0. The tile Largest share shows the largest share, residual included, its subline names the term.
VcTerm.clamped: Whether the estimate was set to 0: true when ANOVA produced a negative variance; the row then carries “clamped to 0” and a note appears under the table. Always false for REML.

multi-vari.factorsHint: The order drives layout and nesting alike — drag to reorder.
multi-vari.interpretation: {term} contributes the largest share of the total variation at {percent} %.
multi-vari.interpretationError: Repeat variation is the largest share at {percent} % — the chosen factors barely explain the spread.
multi-vari.unbalancedNote: Unbalanced design: the variance components depend on the estimator here. REML is the more dependable choice in this case.
multi-vari.clampedNote: Negative variance estimates were clamped to 0 — a sign of too little data for the finest level.
multi-vari.warn_unbalanced: Unbalanced design — not every factor combination is equally occupied.
multi-vari.warn_noReplicates: No replicates — the finest source has a single observation per cell and was pooled into the residual error.
multi-vari.warn_rowCapExceeded: Too many rows for the REML estimate — the calculation fell back to the ANOVA method.
multi-vari.warn_notConverged: The REML estimate did not converge — the variance components are approximations.
multi-vari.warn_negativeComponent: A negative variance estimate was set to zero — this source is not distinguishable from zero.
multi-vari.warn_aliasedTerms: At least one component is not estimable in this design (0 degrees of freedom) and was removed before the REML fit — the reported value of 0 is not an estimate, it is aliasing.
multi-vari.warn_emptyCells: Empty cells — at least one factor combination does not occur in the data.
multi-vari.warn_tooManyAxisLevels: “{col}” has {count} levels on the x axis (limit: {max}) — the chart is therefore not drawn. Put a factor with fewer levels in position 1.
multi-vari.warn_tooManySeriesLevels: “{col}” has {count} series levels (limit: {max}) — the chart is therefore not drawn. Put a factor with fewer levels in position 2.
multi-vari.warn_tooManyPanels: “{col}” produces {count} panels (limit: {max}) — the chart is therefore not drawn. The variance-components table below remains valid.
multi-vari.warnDroppedRows: {count} row(s) skipped: empty factor level or non-numeric measurement.
multi-vari.errNoData: No usable measurements in the selected columns.
multi-vari.errCompute: Variance components could not be computed: {msg}

process-capability.name: Process Capability
process-capability.description: Process Capability Analysis — Cp, Cpk, Pp, Ppk, PPM, Sigma Level
process-capability.whenToUse: When it must be shown how well a process keeps a measured characteristic inside its specification limits: Cp and Cpk (short term, from the within-subgroup spread), Pp and Ppk (long term), PPM and sigma level, with confidence intervals. Works with one-sided or two-sided limits, individual values or subgroups. Needs at least one limit (lower or upper) and at least 2 numeric values from a data collection column or from loaded example data.

read.help: Returns the entered specification and settings, the chosen columns, any loaded example data, the selectable sets, the estimator note and the computed result. result is null while no data are chosen, no limit is entered, the upper limit does not exceed the lower, fewer than 2 values are available, the estimator cannot be computed, or in column mode no matching subgroup column is chosen (withinHint then names the reason). Example data (embeddedValues) are bulk data: without options.fields = ['embeddedValues'] only the extent is returned.

params.options: Optional: fields: ['embeddedValues'] returns the example values in full, rows: { from, to } trims them.

setParam.help: Sets one parameter. The estimator, the subgroup mode and size, the moving-range span and the unbiasing switch recalculate at once and can change which parameters and estimators apply; the other parameters recalculate after a short pause.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. lsl, target, usl as text containing a number or '' for no limit; confidence in percent (50 to 99.99).

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. Choosing the measurement column discards loaded example data; the subgroup ID column is offered from the sheet of the measurement column, without the measurement column itself.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeColumnSlots: 'value' (the measurements) always, 'subgroup' (the subgroup IDs) only while the subgroups come from a column and no example data are loaded.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns, or null to clear the slot.

clearEmbedded.help: Discards loaded example data; afterwards the module computes on a column again and recalculates at once. Without example data nothing changes.

runAnalysis.help: Computes with the current inputs. Repeated calls are harmless; incomplete or invalid inputs leave result at null without an error, and an estimator that cannot be computed or a missing subgroup column is named in withinHint.

scheduleAnalysis.help: Triggers the computation after a short pause; a second request before that replaces the first.

clearResults.help: Discards the result; the inputs stay. The next computation fills it again.

params.help: The inputs, each described under keys; numbers appear as text.

columnRef.help: The chosen measurement column as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }, or null. Loaded example data take precedence over it.

subgroupColumnRef.help: The chosen subgroup ID column as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }, or null. It counts only while the subgroups come from a column.

embeddedValues.help: The values of loaded example data that replace the measurement column, or null. Bulk data: without options.fields = ['embeddedValues'] only the extent is returned.

embeddedLabel.help: The title of the loaded example data, '' when none are loaded.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state.

subgroupModeValues.help: The values setParam accepts for subgroupMode: 'size' always, 'column' only while no example data are loaded.

withinMethodOptions.help: The values setParam accepts for withinMethod: '' (the default of the data) and the estimators that fit the data. They depend on the subgroups: with individual values only the moving-range estimators, with subgroups the pooled, range and standard-deviation estimators.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts in the current state.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'. value lists the numeric columns, subgroup the other columns of the sheet of the measurement column (empty without a measurement column).

result.help: The capability result, each figure described individually under keys; null while the inputs are incomplete or invalid.

withinHint.help: A note on the estimator or the subgroup column: the stored estimator does not fit the data and another one is used, the subgroup column is missing, or the estimator cannot be computed for these data. '' when there is nothing to note.

Params.name: The name of the feature, label “Feature / Characteristic”; free text. It appears in the status bar after the verdict and does not enter the computation.
Params.lsl: The lower specification limit, label “LSL”, as text containing a number; a decimal comma is accepted. Empty means no lower limit; CPL, PPL and all fractions below LSL are then missing. At least one of the two limits must be set, and USL must lie above LSL, otherwise there is no result.
Params.target: The target, label “Target”, as text containing a number. It enters no index; the table shows it, and without it the table shows the tolerance midpoint (USL + LSL)/2 when both limits are set. Empty is allowed.
Params.usl: The upper specification limit, label “USL”, as text containing a number; a decimal comma is accepted. Empty means no upper limit; CPU, PPU and all fractions above USL are then missing. At least one of the two limits must be set, and USL must lie above LSL, otherwise there is no result.
Params.unit: The unit of the measurements, label “Unit”, preset mm. It follows the values of the summary table and does not enter the computation.
Params.confidence: The confidence level of the intervals in percent, label “Confidence (CI) (%)”, preset 95. A value outside 50 to 99.99 is clamped to that range when computing; an empty or unusable entry takes the confidence level from the settings.
Params.subgroupMode: Where the subgroups come from, label “Subgroups”: “Fixed size” splits the values in order into groups of equal size, “Column with IDs” groups them by a second column of subgroup IDs. “Column with IDs” can only be chosen while no example data are loaded. The subgroups decide which estimators for σ within are offered.
Params.subgroupSize: The fixed subgroup size, label “Subgroup size”, whole number from 1, preset 1. At 1 the values are individuals and σ within comes by default from the average moving range (the median moving range and the square root of MSSD can be chosen too); from 2 the subgroup estimators apply. Only adjustable in the mode “Fixed size”.
Params.withinMethod: The estimator for σ within, from which Cp, Cpk, CPL and CPU are computed. Empty means automatic choice: the average moving range for individuals, the pooled standard deviation for subgroups. For individuals the choices are average moving range, median moving range and square root of MSSD; for subgroups pooled standard deviation, R̄/d2 and S̄/c4. If a stored estimator does not fit the data, the automatic one applies and a note says so.
Params.mrSpan: The span w of the moving ranges, label “Moving range span w”, whole number from 2 to 100, preset 2: each range covers w consecutive values. Applies only to the average moving range and the median moving range.
Params.unbiased: Whether the unbiasing constant is applied, label “Use unbiasing constant (c4 or c4′)”, preset on: the estimate of σ within is divided by c4 or c4′ so that it is not too small on average. Applies only to pooled standard deviation, S̄/c4 and square root of MSSD.

Result.n: The number of evaluated measurements n, label “Number of measurements n”; only numbers count, empty and non-numeric cells are dropped. At least 2 are needed.
Result.xbar: The mean x̄ of all measurements, label “Mean x̄”. It is the reference point for CPL, CPU, PPL and PPU.
Result.s: The overall standard deviation s of all measurements with divisor n − 1, label “Standard deviation overall s (n−1)”. Pp, Ppk and the expected overall fractions are computed from it.
Result.sigmaWithin: The within spread σ within, estimated by the chosen estimator from the subgroups or the moving ranges, label “Standard deviation within”. It measures only the short-term spread; Cp, Cpk, CPL, CPU and the expected within fractions are computed from it.
Result.sigmaOverall: The overall spread, equal to s: the standard deviation of all measurements with divisor n − 1. It appears here a second time as the counterpart of σ within.
Result.withinMethod: The estimator actually used for σ within: pooled standard deviation, R̄/d2, S̄/c4, average moving range, median moving range or square root of MSSD. With automatic choice or a stored estimator that does not fit, the automatic one is given here.
Result.withinDf: The degrees of freedom ν of the estimator for σ within, used by the confidence intervals of Cp and Cpk: pooled Σ(nᵢ − 1) over the subgroups with at least 2 values, R̄/d2 0.9 · k · (n̄ − 1), S̄/c4 f(n̄) · k · (n̄ − 1) with a table factor f, the moving-range estimators the number of ranges, square root of MSSD n − 1. For R̄/d2 and S̄/c4, ν can be fractional.
Result.subgroupSize: The fixed subgroup size used in the computation. In the mode “Column with IDs” this shows 1, although the subgroups come from the column; their number and average size are given by the subgroup count and the average subgroup size.
Result.subgroupCount: The number k of subgroups with at least 2 values, for individuals the number of values. It enters the degrees of freedom of the estimator.
Result.nBar: The average size n̄ of the subgroups with at least 2 values, 1 for individuals.
Result.unbiased: Whether the unbiasing constant c4 or c4′ was switched on. The value appears even when the estimator used does not apply it.
Result.mrSpan: The span w of the moving ranges used in the computation. It appears even when the estimator used takes no moving ranges.
Result.T: The tolerance T = USL − LSL, label “Tolerance T (USL − LSL)”. Empty when only one limit is set; Cp and Pp are then missing as well.
Result.mid: The tolerance midpoint (USL + LSL)/2; empty when only one limit is set.
Result.targetVal: The target in the table, label “Target”: the entered target, otherwise the tolerance midpoint. Empty with only one limit and no target. It enters no index.
Result.hasLsl: Whether a lower specification limit LSL is set.
Result.hasUsl: Whether an upper specification limit USL is set.
Result.twoSided: Whether both limits are set; only then are there a tolerance, Cp, Pp and their intervals.
Result.lsl: The lower specification limit LSL as a number, label “LSL” in the summary table; empty without a lower limit.
Result.usl: The upper specification limit USL as a number, label “USL” in the summary table; empty without an upper limit.
Result.Cp: The potential capability Cp = T / (6 · σ within), tile “Cp (Potential)”: how often the process width fits into the tolerance, regardless of location. From 1.33 capable, from 1.0 conditionally capable, below that not capable. Empty when only one limit is set.
Result.CPU: The capability towards the upper limit CPU = (USL − x̄) / (3 · σ within), tile “CPU (Upper)”. Empty without an upper limit.
Result.CPL: The capability towards the lower limit CPL = (x̄ − LSL) / (3 · σ within), tile “CPL (Lower)”. Empty without a lower limit.
Result.Cpk: The actual capability Cpk, tile “Cpk (Actual)”: the smaller of CPU and CPL, with only one limit its value. It accounts for within spread and location. From 1.33 capable, from 1.0 conditionally capable, below that not capable; this verdict is the overall verdict of the status bar.
Result.Pp: The potential overall performance Pp = T / (6 · s), tile “Pp (Overall Potential)”: like Cp, but with the overall standard deviation s, that is with the long-term spread. Empty when only one limit is set.
Result.PPU: The overall performance towards the upper limit PPU = (USL − x̄) / (3 · s). Empty without an upper limit.
Result.PPL: The overall performance towards the lower limit PPL = (x̄ − LSL) / (3 · s). Empty without a lower limit.
Result.Ppk: The actual overall performance Ppk, tile “Ppk (Overall Actual)”: the smaller of PPU and PPL, with only one limit its value. Like Cpk, but with the overall standard deviation s.
Result.CpCI: The confidence interval of Cp as a pair of lower and upper bound, via the χ² distribution with the estimator's ν degrees of freedom: Cp · √(χ²(α/2; ν)/ν) to Cp · √(χ²(1 − α/2; ν)/ν). The tile shows it after “CI” with the level in percent. Empty when Cp is missing or the estimator has no degrees of freedom.
Result.CpkCI: The confidence interval of Cpk as a pair of lower and upper bound, after Bissell as a normal approximation: Cpk ± z · SE with SE = √(1/(9n) + Cpk²/(2ν)), ν the degrees of freedom of the estimator for σ within. Empty when the estimator has no degrees of freedom.
Result.PpCI: The confidence interval of Pp as a pair of lower and upper bound, via the χ² distribution with n − 1 degrees of freedom. Empty when Pp is missing.
Result.PpkCI: The confidence interval of Ppk as a pair of lower and upper bound, after Bissell as a normal approximation with n − 1 degrees of freedom: Ppk ± z · √(1/(9n) + Ppk²/(2(n − 1))).
Result.confidence: The confidence level of the four intervals as a fraction, for example 0.95; the input is in percent and is clamped to 50 to 99.99 %. The tiles show it rounded in percent.
Result.ppmAboveUsl: The expected fraction above USL under the overall model, a normal distribution with x̄ and s, in PPM (parts per million), column “> USL” of the row “Expected overall”. Empty without an upper limit.
Result.ppmBelowLsl: The expected fraction below LSL under the overall model, a normal distribution with x̄ and s, in PPM (parts per million), column “< LSL” of the row “Expected overall”. Empty without a lower limit.
Result.ppmTotal: The expected fraction outside both limits under the overall model, a normal distribution with x̄ and s, in PPM: the sum of below LSL and above USL. Tile “PPM (Defective)” and column “Total” of the row “Expected overall”; below it the tile names the observed and the expected within figures.
Result.ppmWithinBelowLsl: The expected fraction below LSL under the within model, a normal distribution with x̄ and σ within, in PPM; row “Expected within”. Empty without a lower limit.
Result.ppmWithinAboveUsl: The expected fraction above USL under the within model, a normal distribution with x̄ and σ within, in PPM; row “Expected within”. Empty without an upper limit.
Result.ppmWithinTotal: The expected fraction outside both limits under the within model, a normal distribution with x̄ and σ within, in PPM; row “Expected within” and, as “expected within”, tile “PPM (Defective)”.
Result.ppmObservedBelowLsl: The observed fraction of measurements strictly below LSL, in PPM; row “Observed”. Empty without a lower limit.
Result.ppmObservedAboveUsl: The observed fraction of measurements strictly above USL, in PPM; row “Observed”. Empty without an upper limit.
Result.ppmObservedTotal: The observed fraction of measurements outside both limits, in PPM; row “Observed” and, as “observed”, tile “PPM (Defective)”. A value exactly on a limit counts as inside.
Result.zBenchWithin: Z.bench within: the normal quantile of the expected fraction outside both limits under the within model, Z = −Φ⁻¹(p). Infinite when the fraction is 0; undefined for σ = 0 with the mean on a limit.
Result.zBenchOverall: Z.bench overall: the normal quantile of the expected fraction outside both limits under the overall model, Z = −Φ⁻¹(p). The sigma tile names it as “Z.bench overall”.
Result.sigmaLevel: The sigma level, tile “Sigma level (Z.bench within)”: equal to Z.bench within, the normal quantile of the expected fraction outside both limits with σ within. It counts both limits and is therefore at most 3 · Cpk; with only one limit the two are equal.
Result.sigmaLevelShifted: The sigma level by the Six Sigma convention: Z.bench overall + 1.5. The 1.5σ shift is a convention of Six Sigma training, not a measured result; the sigma tile names it as “Six Sigma convention (+1.5σ)”.
Result.cpkStatus: The verdict on Cpk: “Capable” from 1.33, “Conditional” from 1.0, otherwise “Not capable”. It colours the Cpk tile and is the overall verdict.
Result.cpStatus: The verdict on Cp: “Capable” from 1.33, “Conditional” from 1.0, otherwise “Not capable”. It colours the Cp tile; empty when Cp is missing.
Result.overall: The overall verdict of the status bar, equal to the verdict on Cpk: “PROCESS CAPABLE” from Cpk 1.33, “CONDITIONALLY CAPABLE” from 1.0, otherwise “PROCESS NOT CAPABLE”.

process-capability.specHint: For one-sided specification, leave the unused field empty.
process-capability.noWorksheet: No worksheet available. Create a worksheet with measurement data first.
process-capability.errNoLimits: At least one specification limit (LSL or USL) must be specified.
process-capability.errUslLeqLsl: USL must be greater than LSL.
process-capability.zBenchNote: Z.bench is the standard normal quantile of the total fraction outside both limits. It equals 3 · Cpk only when the fraction beyond the far limit is negligible. The 1.5σ shift is a Six Sigma training convention, not a measurement.
process-capability.subgroupHint: 1 = individuals. From 2 on, consecutive values form subgroups of that size. Pp/Ppk always use overall s.
process-capability.subgroupColumnHint: A new subgroup starts whenever the ID changes. Rows without a measurement or without an ID are skipped.
process-capability.subgroupEmbeddedHint: Example data use the fixed size.
process-capability.subgroupColumnMissing: Choose a column with subgroup IDs from the same sheet as the measurements.
process-capability.kindSubgroups: subgroups with at least two values
process-capability.errWithinSubgroupTooLarge: R̄/d2 is tabulated for subgroups of up to 100 values.
process-capability.errWithinSpanTooLarge: The moving range span w must not exceed 100 or the number of values.
process-capability.errWithinMethodInvalid: This estimator does not fit the data.
process-capability.interpPass: Process capable — spread and centering within tolerance.

ishikawa.whenToUse: When possible causes of a problem are to be collected, ordered by 6M and rated by the team, so that the most likely ones get tested with experiments; states can be kept as snapshots and compared. For a single chain of causes by asking why, use 5-Why.

read.help: Read the problem statement, images, expert team, cause tree with ratings, snapshots, experiments and facts. Image data and snapshot contents appear only as their size.

setTab.help: Open a tab: problem, facts, hypotheses or experiments.

setProblem.help: Set the problem statement: what deviates, where, by how much.

params.text: The statement; empty clears it.

addExpert.help: Add a member to the expert team. Every member rates every cause from 0 to 9.

params.name: The name; must differ from the others, regardless of case.

renameExpert.help: Rename a member of the expert team; their ratings stay.

params.name: The new name; must differ from the others.

removeExpert.help: Remove a member from the expert team, with their ratings.

addRow.help: Append a main cause to the end of the cause tree.

addSubRow.help: Add a sub-cause under a cause; it inherits that cause’s category.

setRowField.help: Set one field of a cause: name, category, description or status. Only main causes carry a category.

params.key: Which field.
params.value: The new value, as described per field.

deleteRow.help: Delete a cause with its sub-causes, without asking. Links from experiments go.

duplicateRow.help: Copy a cause with its sub-causes and ratings; the copy follows right after it.

moveRowBefore.help: Move a cause with its sub-causes before another; it takes that cause’s parent. If the target lies inside the moved subtree, nothing moves and the result is false.

setRating.help: Set one member’s rating of a cause, from 0 (unlikely) to 9 (very likely). The mean and the Pareto follow.

params.value: A whole number from 0 to 9; null clears the rating.

setCategoryLabels.help: Give the six categories own names, for example 6P instead of 6M. Categories not named keep theirs.

params.labels: New name per category: man, machine, environment, material, measurement, method. Empty restores the default name; two categories must not share a name.

setFilter.help: Show only the causes of one category, or all.

params.category: all or a category: man, machine, environment, material, measurement, method.

setParetoSource.help: Show the current ratings or those of a snapshot in the Pareto.

params.snapshotId: A snapshot; null shows the current state.

exportCSV.help: Download the problem statement, cause tree with ratings and facts as CSV; the result is the same text.

saveSnapshot.help: Keep the current problem statement, expert team and cause tree as a snapshot.

params.name: The name; empty gives Snapshot with today’s date.

loadSnapshot.help: Restore a snapshot, without asking: problem statement, expert team and cause tree are replaced.

compareSnapshot.help: Compare the current state with a snapshot. The table marks new and changed causes; the result lists new, removed and changed causes with old and new mean.

closeCompare.help: End the comparison with a snapshot.

addExperiment.help: Add an experiment that tests causes.

setExperimentField.help: Set one field of an experiment: title, description, responsible, status, start, end, cost in euros or effort in hours.

params.key: Which field.
params.value: The new value, as described per field.

setExperimentHypotheses.help: Set which causes an experiment tests.

params.hypothesisIds: The identifier of each cause, such as H-001; an empty list unlinks all.

addFact.help: Add a fact: an established observation that supports the search for causes.

setFactField.help: Set one field of a fact: name, description, date or owner.

params.key: Which field.
params.value: The new text; the date as YYYY-MM-DD or empty.

problem.help: The problem statement: what deviates, where, by how much.

images.help: Images that draw the line: what belongs to the problem and what does not, each with a caption. Image data appears only as its size.

experts.help: The expert team: every member rates every cause from 0 to 9.

catLabels.help: Own names of the six categories; where one is missing, the default name applies.

rows.help: The cause tree: main and sub-causes with identifier, category, name, description, status and the ratings by each member of the expert team.

snapshots.help: Kept states with name and time. Their contents appear only as their size; the comparison shows what changed.

experiments.help: The experiments with title, description, responsible, status, period, cost and the causes they test.

facts.help: The facts: observations with name, description, date and who reported them.

RowFields.name: Short name of the cause.
RowFields.category: The 6M category of a main cause; sub-causes inherit it.
RowFields.description: What the cause is and why it is suspected.
RowFields.status: How far the check has got: open, testing, confirmed or rejected.

ExperimentFields.title: Short title of the experiment.
ExperimentFields.description: What is tried and how the result is measured.
ExperimentFields.status: Where the experiment stands: planned, running, done or cancelled.

FactFields.name: What was observed.
FactFields.description: Details and source of the observation.

columns.avgScore: Mean of the ratings by all members of the expert team, from 0 to 9; when compared with a snapshot, the change stands next to it.

charts.gantt: Schedule of the experiments from start to end; the line marks today.
charts.cost: Cost in euros and effort in hours of all experiments, summed up over time.
charts.costRate: Cost in euros and effort in hours per day, spread over the run time of the experiments.

ishikawa.name: Ishikawa 6M
ishikawa.description: Root cause analysis with 6M categories and expert scoring
ishikawa.problemPlaceholder: e.g. Scrap rate for part X increased by 12%…
ishikawa.expertDuplicate: An expert with this name already exists.
ishikawa.trendMinSnaps: At least 1 snapshot + current state needed.
ishikawa.loadSnapConfirm: Overwrite current state with this snapshot?
ishikawa.delRowConfirmWithSubs: Really delete hypothesis "{name}"? This will also delete {count} sub-hypothesis.
ishikawa.delRowConfirmWithSubs_other: Really delete hypothesis "{name}"? This will also delete {count} sub-hypotheses.
ishikawa.renameCatsHint: Optionally provide a case-specific term for each category. Leave empty to use the default name.
ishikawa.problemScopeInHint: Images that show the problem — typical failure images considered in the Ishikawa.
ishikawa.problemScopeOutHint: Images that should NOT be considered — to clearly delimit what is explicitly NOT the problem.
ishikawa.imageTooLarge: "{name}" could not be compressed below 100 KB — please choose a smaller image.
ishikawa.noFacts: No facts recorded yet. Click "+ Fact" to add the first one.
ishikawa.chooseHypothesesHint: Select the hypotheses this experiment helps to verify.
ishikawa.noExperiments: No experiments planned yet. Click "+ Experiment" to add the first one.
ishikawa.ganttNoData: No experiments with start and due date.
ishikawa.costChartNoData: No experiments with cost or effort.
ishikawa.chooseExperimentsHint: Select the experiments that help verify hypothesis "{name}".
ishikawa.noExperimentsToLink: No experiments created yet. Switch to the "Experiments" tab to add the first one.

makigami.name: Makigami Matrix
makigami.description: Swim-lane process analysis with processing/waiting times and waste classification
makigami.title: Process title
makigami.rolesEmpty: No roles yet – add one via the "Role" button.
makigami.stepsEmpty: No steps yet – add one via the "Step" button.
makigami.delRoleConfirm: Delete role "{label}"? Participation in all steps will be removed.
makigami.kpiPCEHint: Process Cycle Efficiency = Σ Processing / Lead Time
makigami.settingsUnitsHint: The seconds factor controls how the free-text parser converts each unit (e.g. 1 d = 28800 s ≙ 8-hour workday).
makigami.settingsResetConfirm: Really reset all categories and units to defaults?
makigami.whenToUse: When a cross-department process is to be recorded step by step with responsibility, processing time, waiting time and waste categories so that idle time becomes visible; not for the flow logic itself with its decisions and branches, which is what a flowchart is for.

setTitle.help: Sets the name of the process under study.

params.text: The name of the process. An empty string clears it; a missing argument is an error.

addRole.help: Adds a role without a name, in the matrix as a new row at the very bottom, and returns its id.

addStep.help: Adds a process step without a title at the end of the chain, in the matrix as a new column on the far right, and returns its id.

setRoleLabel.help: Sets the name of a role.

params.roleId: The id of the role as read() lists it under roles. An unknown id is an error.
params.label: The name of the role. An empty string clears it; a missing argument is an error.

setStepTitle.help: Sets the title of a process step.

params.stepId: The id of the process step as read() lists it under steps. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The title of the step. An empty string clears it; a missing argument is an error.

setStepDescription.help: Sets the description of what happens in a process step, i.e. what takes place in that step.

params.stepId: The id of the process step as read() lists it under steps. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The description of the activity. An empty string clears it; a missing argument is an error.

setStepNotes.help: Sets the note of a process step, e.g. observations, hand-offs or bottlenecks; empty clears it.

params.stepId: The id of the process step as read() lists it under steps. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The note on the step. An empty string clears it; a missing argument is an error.

setStepProcessTime.help: Sets the processing time of a process step — the time actually spent working on the case. The duration is text made of a number and a unit, e.g. 4h 30min, 1d or 45min, and counts towards the processing total and the key figures. An unreadable text is stored and marked invalid, but does not count.

params.stepId: The id of the process step as read() lists it under steps. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The duration as text made of a number and a unit, e.g. 30 min or 1 d 2 h; the units recognised are listed in timeUnits. An empty string clears the entry; an unreadable text is stored but does not count towards the key figures and returns false. A missing argument is an error.

setStepWaitTime.help: Sets the waiting time of a process step — the time the case lies idle. The duration is text made of a number and a unit, e.g. 4h 30min, 1d or 45min, and counts towards the waiting total and the key figures. An unreadable text is stored and marked invalid, but does not count.

params.stepId: The id of the process step as read() lists it under steps. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The duration as text made of a number and a unit, e.g. 30 min or 1 d 2 h; the units recognised are listed in timeUnits. An empty string clears the entry; an unreadable text is stored but does not count towards the key figures and returns false. A missing argument is an error.

setStepExpanded.help: Unfolds or folds the card of a process step. The state is stored; it changes nothing about the content of the step.

params.stepId: The id of the process step as read() lists it under steps. An unknown id is an error.
params.expanded: true unfolds the card, false folds it. Any other value — a missing argument included — is an error.

setParticipation.help: Decides whether a role takes part in a process step. On the step card each role is a button that a click marks or releases; in the matrix a click on the cell of role and step toggles the same thing.

params.stepId: The id of the process step as read() lists it under steps. An unknown id is an error.
params.roleId: The id of the role as read() lists it under roles. An unknown id is an error.
params.participates: true makes the role take part, false takes the participation back. Any other value — a missing argument included — is an error.

setMuda.help: Decides whether a waste category (Muda) marks a process step. On the step card each category is a button that a click sets or releases. The eight classic categories (TIMWOODS+S) are preset; the settings let you adapt them.

params.stepId: The id of the process step as read() lists it under steps. An unknown id is an error.
params.mudaId: The id of the waste category as read() lists it under mudaCategories. An unknown id is an error.
params.marked: true marks the step, false takes the marking back. Any other value — a missing argument included — is an error.

params.stepId: The id of the process step as read() lists it under steps. An unknown id is an error.

removeRole.help: Removes a role together with its participations in every step.

params.roleId: The id of the role as read() lists it under roles. An unknown id is an error.

reorderSteps.help: Places a process step in front of another; the remaining ones move up.

params.draggedId: The id of the step that should move. An unknown id is an error.
params.targetId: The id of the step it should go in front of. The same id as draggedId leaves the order unchanged; an unknown id is an error.

reorderRoles.help: Places a role in front of another; the remaining ones move up.

params.draggedId: The id of the role that should move. An unknown id is an error.
params.targetId: The id of the role it should go in front of. The same id as draggedId leaves the order unchanged; an unknown id is an error.

addMudaCategory.help: Adds a waste category without a code or a name and returns its id.

setMudaCategory.help: Changes the named fields of a waste category; all others stay as they are.

params.mudaId: The id of the waste category as read() lists it under mudaCategories. An unknown id is an error.
params.data: An object holding exactly the fields that should change — code (the short code in the matrix), label (the name) or color (a hex value such as #4a90e2). Whatever is not in it stays unchanged; a missing object, an object without any of these fields and a value that is not a string are errors.

deleteMudaCategory.help: Removes a waste category and its markings on every step.

params.mudaId: The id of the waste category as read() lists it under mudaCategories. An unknown id is an error.

addTimeUnit.help: Adds a time unit without a code and one second long, and returns its id.

setTimeUnit.help: Changes the named fields of a time unit; all others stay as they are.

params.unitId: The id of the time unit as read() lists it under timeUnits. An unknown id is an error.
params.data: An object holding exactly the fields that should change — label (the code recognised inside a duration text) or factorSeconds (the length of the unit in seconds, a number greater than 0). Whatever is not in it stays unchanged; a missing object, an object without any of these fields, a label that is not a string and a factorSeconds of 0 or less are errors.

deleteTimeUnit.help: Removes a time unit. Duration texts that use only this unit are unreadable afterwards and no longer count towards the key figures.

params.unitId: The id of the time unit as read() lists it under timeUnits. An unknown id is an error.

resetSettingsToDefaults.help: Restores the eight shipped waste categories and the four shipped time units; markings on categories that fall away are dropped.

setSettingsOpen.help: Opens or closes the settings area for waste categories and time units. The state is stored; it changes nothing about the data.

params.open: true opens the area, false closes it. Any other value — a missing argument included — is an error.

title.help: The name of the process under study.

roles.help: The roles involved, in display order; in the matrix they are the rows, on each step card selectable buttons. Per role: id (this is how the actions address it) and label (its name).

steps.help: The process steps in flow order. Per step: id (this is how the actions address it), title, description, notes, roleIds (the roles taking part), mudaIds (the waste categories assigned), processTime and waitTime as duration text plus expanded (whether the card is unfolded).

mudaCategories.help: The waste categories a step can point to, preset with the eight TIMWOODS+S categories. Per category: id (this is how the actions address it), code (the short code in the matrix), label (a name of your own; empty means the shipped one applies) and color as a hex value.

timeUnits.help: The time units recognised inside a duration text. Per unit: id (this is how the actions address it), label (the code used in the text, e.g. min) and factorSeconds (its length in seconds; a working day counts 28800).

settingsOpen.help: Whether the settings area for waste categories and time units is open.

pairwise-comparison.name: Pairwise Comparison
pairwise-comparison.description: Prioritize criteria through systematic pairwise comparison. Every criterion is judged against every other.
pairwise-comparison.whenToUse: When a handful of equally ranked criteria needs a justified order and handing out points directly would be too arbitrary — every criterion is put against every other one, three to fifteen criteria; not when the criteria are to be weighted against SEVERAL outputs, which is what the C&E matrix is for.

addCriterion.help: Appends a criterion to the list.

params.text: The name of the criterion; surrounding whitespace is dropped. The call returns ok when the criterion was added, otherwise empty (empty text), duplicate (the name is already in the list) or max (15 criteria are already recorded) — all three are refusals, not errors.

removeCriterion.help: Removes a criterion. A running comparison becomes invalid: matrix, pair order and progress go back to empty.

params.i: The number of the criterion, counted from 0. A number that names no criterion is an error.

startComparison.help: Starts the comparison: forms every pair of the criteria in shuffled order and switches to the Comparison tab. With fewer than three criteria no comparison starts — that is not an error.

chooseLeft.help: Decides the pending pair for the left criterion (left arrow key): it gets 1 point, the other 0. Then the next pair follows; after the last one the view switches to the Result tab. While no comparison is running — before the start or once all pairs are decided — nothing happens; that is not an error.

chooseRight.help: Decides the pending pair for the right criterion (right arrow key): it gets 1 point, the other 0. Then the next pair follows; after the last one the view switches to the Result tab. While no comparison is running — before the start or once all pairs are decided — nothing happens; that is not an error.

tieCurrent.help: Rates the pending pair as equally important (space bar): both criteria get 0.5 points. Then the next pair follows. While no comparison is running — before the start or once all pairs are decided — nothing happens; that is not an error.

setViewPhase.help: Switches the displayed tab: Criteria, Comparison or Result. Comparison is only reachable while a comparison is running, Result only once it is finished.

params.phase: The work phase: input (record criteria), compare (decide pairs) or results (ranking and matrix). Any other value is an error. compare needs a running comparison, results a finished one — if the work phase is not reachable the call returns false — a refusal, not an error.

cycleCell.help: Advances the rating of a matrix cell by one step: 0 to 0.5, 0.5 to 1, 1 back to 0. The opposite cell travels along. On the diagonal — a criterion against itself — and while no comparison is running the call returns false; both are refusals, not errors.

params.i: The number of the row's criterion, counted from 0. A number that names no criterion is an error.
params.j: The number of the column's criterion, counted from 0. A number that names no criterion is an error.

criteria.help: The criteria in input order, addressed by their number from 0. At most 15; a comparison needs at least 3.

matrix.help: The comparison matrix: matrix[i][j] says how criterion i fared against criterion j — 1 won, 0.5 tied, 0 lost. Empty while no comparison is running; the diagonal has no meaning.

pairs.help: The shuffled order of the pairs to decide, each entry the two criterion numbers. Empty while no comparison is running; with n criteria there are n·(n−1)/2 pairs.

currentPair.help: How many pairs are already decided — and therefore the index of the next one in pairs. Equal to the length of pairs means finished.

viewPhase.help: The displayed work phase: input (record criteria), compare (decide pairs) or results (ranking and matrix). A persisted display state — it belongs to the saved project.

result.help: The evaluation: points per criterion and ranking, each figure described individually under keys; null until all pairs are decided.

Result.scores: The points per criterion, in the order of the criteria list — the Σ column of the comparison matrix. Each comparison gives 1 point for a win, 0.5 for equally important and 0 for a loss; the points are the sum of a matrix row without the diagonal. With n criteria at most n − 1 points are possible, and all points together add up to n·(n − 1)/2, the number of pairs.
Result.maxScore: The highest score reached. The longest bar in the ranking belongs to it; every other bar is shorter in proportion of its points to it.
Result.ranking: The ranking: all criteria in descending order of points. With equal points the order of the criteria list is kept; places 1 to 3 are highlighted in colour.

RankEntry.name: The name of the criterion as it appears in the criteria list.
RankEntry.score: The points of the criterion: 1 per comparison won, 0.5 per equally important one, 0 per comparison lost. The ranking shows them with one decimal place (3.5).
RankEntry.idx: The number of the criterion in the criteria list, counted from 0 — the same number as the row and column of the comparison matrix.

pairwise-comparison.emptyHint: Add at least {n} criteria to start the comparison.
pairwise-comparison.noResults: No results yet — please add criteria and run the comparison first.
pairwise-comparison.resetConfirm: Really reset all criteria and ratings?
pairwise-comparison.duplicateWarning: This criterion has already been added.

ce-matrix.name: C&E Matrix
ce-matrix.whenToUse: When several process inputs are to be ranked by how strongly they act on the outputs that matter to the customer — the weighted row sum says which input to investigate first; not for rating failure modes by occurrence and detection, which is what the FMEA is for.

read.help: Returns the matrix, the scale and the permitted ratings.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

addInput.help: Appends another input (row) to the matrix and returns its row number.

addOutput.help: Appends another output (column) with a customer importance of 1 to the matrix and returns its column number.

removeInput.help: Removes an input together with its ratings; the remaining rows move up.

params.r: The row number of the input, counted from 0. A number that names no input is an error. The last remaining row stays — the call then returns false, which is a refusal and not an error.

removeOutput.help: Removes an output together with its ratings and its customer importance; the remaining columns move left.

params.c: The column number of the output, counted from 0. A number that names no output is an error. The last remaining column stays — the call then returns false, which is a refusal and not an error.

setScore.help: Rates the crossing of an input with an output.

params.r: The row number of the input, counted from 0. A number that names no input is an error.
params.c: The column number of the output, counted from 0. A number that names no output is an error.
params.value: The rating from the active scale; null clears the rating. The default scale 0-10 allows every integer from 0 to 10, the scale 0-1-3-9 only 0, 1, 3 and 9, the scale 0-3-7-10 only 0, 3, 7 and 10. A value the active scale does not allow is an error.

setScale.help: Switches the rating scale. Existing ratings stay unchanged, including those the new scale does not allow.

params.id: The scale: 0-10 (every integer from 0 to 10), 0-1-3-9 or 0-3-7-10. Any other value is an error.

params.r: The row number of the input, counted from 0. A number that names no input is an error.
params.text: The new name of the input; an empty text clears it.

params.c: The column number of the output, counted from 0. A number that names no output is an error.
params.text: The new name of the output; an empty text clears it.

setWeight.help: Sets the customer importance of an output — the factor its ratings carry into the row sums.

params.c: The column number of the output, counted from 0. A number that names no output is an error.
params.value: The customer importance, an integer from 1 to 10. Any other value is an error.

allowedScores.help: The ratings setScore accepts on the active scale — exactly the values of the scale named in scale.

inputs.help: The inputs (rows) in display order, addressed by their row number from 0.

outputs.help: The outputs (columns) in display order, addressed by their column number from 0.

scores.help: The ratings that are set, addressed as scores["row-column"] with numbers from 0. A crossing without an entry counts as 0 in the sums.

weights.help: The customer importance of each output, 1 to 10, in column order; with it the ratings go into the row sum.

rowSums.help: The row sum per input, in the order of inputs; each value is the sum of rating times weight over all outputs.

AgentRead.rowSums: The sum per input: each rating multiplied by the weight of its output and added up, in the order of the inputs. The “Σ Row” column shows it; the higher, the more strongly the input acts on the weighted outputs.

ce-matrix.legendInfo: Σ = weighted sum of row / column
ce-matrix.scoreRejected: “{value}” is not on the scale — allowed: {allowed}.
ce-matrix.offScale: {count} rating(s) are not on the new scale and are marked.

activity-flowchart.name: Activity Flowchart
activity-flowchart.description: Chain of activities and decisions with rework loops
activity-flowchart.whenToUse: When a process is a chain of activities and yes/no decisions with rework loops — not for a plain chain without branches (Process Map covers that).

read.help: Returns the chain and the bands that steps can stand in.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

appendStep.help: Appends an activity or decision to the chain and returns its id.

params.stepId: The step's id. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The new title.

params.stepId: The step's id. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The new description.

params.stepId: The decision's id. An unknown id, or a step that is not a decision, is an error.
params.text: The new question text.

setDecisionTarget.help: Sets the target of a decision's no branch. The yes branch has no target — it is the value stream, which flows on to the next step anyway.

params.stepId: The decision's id. An unknown id, or a step that is not a decision, is an error.
params.target: The new target: 'end' for process end, or another step's id from the same band the decision itself sits in — a jump back is shown as a rework loop. An unknown id, the step's own id, or a step from a different band, is an error.

setStepBand.help: Sets an existing step's band; its chain position stays.

params.stepId: The step's id. An unknown id is an error.
params.bandId: The id of an existing band ('main' or 'no:<id>'). An unknown band id, or a band whose decision does not stand before this step in the chain, is an error.

removeStep.help: Removes a step from the chain. For a decision, dissolves its band: the steps in it inherit the removed decision's own band.

params.stepId: The id of the step to remove. An unknown id is an error.

insertInBand.help: Inserts a new activity step at a chain gap and returns its id.

params.idx: The gap to insert at (0 = before the first step, up to the chain length = at the end). A value outside that range or a non-integer is an error.
params.bandId: The id of an existing band ('main' or 'no:<id>'). An unknown band id is an error.

addActivityToBand.help: Appends an activity to the end of a band; the agent gets the identifier of the new activity back.

params.bandId: The id of an existing band ('main' or 'no:<id>'). An unknown band id is an error.

addDecisionToBand.help: Appends a decision to the end of a band and opens a band of its own for it below; the agent gets the identifier of the new decision back.

params.bandId: The id of an existing band ('main' or 'no:<id>'). An unknown band id is an error.

clearExit.help: Clears a band's re-entry point; its detour then ends where its own steps end.

params.bandId: The id of a band other than the main path. An unknown band id, or the main path itself, is an error.

setSubstepsExpanded.help: Shows or hides a step's sub-steps; display only, the content stays.

params.stepId: The id of the step whose sub-steps are shown or hidden. An unknown id is an error.
params.expanded: true shows the sub-steps, false hides them.

addSubstep.help: Appends an empty sub-step to a step.

params.stepId: The id of the step that gets the new sub-step. An unknown id is an error.

removeSubstep.help: Removes a sub-step from its parent step.

params.parentId: The id of the parent step. An unknown id is an error.
params.substepId: The id of the sub-step to remove.

params.stepId: The id of the parent step. An unknown id is an error.
params.substepId: The id of the sub-step. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The new title.

bands.help: The bands from top to bottom, main path first — exactly the bandId values that setStepBand, insertInBand, addActivityToBand and addDecisionToBand accept. Per band: id ('main' or 'no:<id>'), ownerId (the id of the decision that opens it, null for the main path), label and depth.

steps.help: The chain in order. Each step carries id, title, description, kind ('activity' or 'decision'), branchId (the band it sits in), expanded and substeps (each with id and title); a decision additionally carries decision ({label, noTarget}).

activity-flowchart.addStepToBand: Add an activity to this detour
activity-flowchart.addDecisionToBand: Add a decision to this detour
activity-flowchart.insertHere: Insert here — or drop a card here to move it
activity-flowchart.emptyHint: No steps yet — use the toolbar to add an activity or decision.
activity-flowchart.importHint: Pick a source. Its steps are appended to the end of the chain.
activity-flowchart.importEmptyHint: No matching source (SIPOC / Process Map) found in this project.
activity-flowchart.exportImageComingSoon: Image export lands in a later release.
activity-flowchart.pickEntryTitle: Click the re-entry point — without one the stream ends here
activity-flowchart.clearRejoin: Drop the re-entry — the stream then ends here

opportunity-flowchart.name: Opportunity Flowchart
opportunity-flowchart.description: Two-column flow: value-added steps versus rework
opportunity-flowchart.whenToUse: When an existing chain needs sorting into value-added work versus rework — not for capturing a new process without that distinction yet.

appendStep.help: Appends a step to the chain and returns its id.

params.side: Column the new step lands in: 'va' value-added or 'nva' rework.

params.stepId: The step's id. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The new title.

params.stepId: The step's id. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The new description.

setSide.help: Sets a step's column; its position in the chain stays.

params.stepId: The step's id. An unknown id is an error.
params.side: Column of the step: 'va' value-added or 'nva' rework. A value outside that set is an error.

insertAt.help: Inserts a new step at a gap in the chain and returns its id.

params.idx: The gap to insert at (0 = before the first step, up to the chain length = at the end). A value outside that range or a non-integer is an error.
params.side: Column of the new step: 'va' value-added or 'nva' rework.

removeStep.help: Removes a step from the chain.

params.stepId: The id of the step to remove. An unknown id is an error.

setSubstepsExpanded.help: Shows or hides a step's sub-steps; display only, the content stays.
