correlation.name: Correlation Analysis
correlation.description: Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall correlation between variables
correlation.whenToUse: When two or more numeric variables may be related: computes the correlation of two columns (Pearson, Spearman and Kendall side by side, with confidence interval and diagnostics) or of three or more columns as a correlation matrix; each column needs at least 5 numeric values.

read.help: Returns the chosen columns, the parameters, the selectable columns, the mode and the result. result holds the analysis of exactly two columns, matrixResult the matrix of three or more; both are null otherwise. result is also null with two columns when the analysis failed (fewer than 4 paired values, which includes a column without usable values, or a column without variance); errorMsg then names the reason.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets one parameter; the analysis reruns (confidenceLevel) or the matrix is rebuilt (the other keys).

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. For filterMinR and filterMaxP null means no filter.

setColumns.help: The data collection columns that supply this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. The order matters: the first column is X, the second Y; with fewer than two columns the results are discarded, and duplicate entries count once.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeMultiSlots; this module only has 'columns'.
params.refs: List of column references { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of columns from pickableColumns, in the wanted order; [] clears the selection.

runAnalysis.help: Recomputes with the chosen columns: pairwise with two, as a matrix with three or more. With fewer than two columns nothing is computed; the error message is cleared and result and matrixResult stay as they are.

clearResults.help: Discards result, matrixResult and the error message; the chosen columns stay.

colRefs.help: The chosen columns in order, each { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }; the first is X, the second Y.

confidenceLevel.help: Confidence level as a fraction, for example 0.95.

matrixMethod.help: The method the correlation matrix shows: 'pearson', 'spearman' or 'kendall'. Only relevant with three or more columns.

filterMinR.help: The matrix hides pairs with |r| below this value; null means no filter.

filterMaxP.help: The matrix hides pairs with a p-value above this value; null means no filter.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state: confidenceLevel, plus matrixMethod, filterMinR and filterMaxP while mode is 'matrix'.

activeMultiSlots.help: The slots setColumns accepts in the current state.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumns accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'. Only columns of a numeric, currency, percent, date or time type with at least 5 values convertible to a number.

mode.help: 'pairwise' with two columns and a result without error, 'matrix' with three or more columns once the matrix is computed, 'none' otherwise.

result.help: The pairwise evaluation of two columns, each figure described individually under keys; null with fewer or more than two columns, with fewer than 4 pairs or without spread.

matrixResult.help: The correlation matrix from three columns, each figure described individually under keys; null with fewer than three columns; cells that cannot be computed are null.

errorMsg.help: The reason a two-column analysis gave no result, or an empty string: “At least 4 paired values required (currently: 2).” with the actual number of pairs, so “(currently: 0)” for a column without usable values, or “Calculation not possible — variance = 0.” for a column without variance.

Params.confidenceLevel: The confidence level as a fraction between 0.5 and 0.9999, so 0.95 rather than 95; the Confidence Level (%) input shows and takes percent. With α = 1 − level it sets every confidence interval of Pearson, Spearman and Kendall, pairwise as well as in the matrix. A change recomputes.
Params.matrixMethod: Which coefficient the correlation matrix shows: Pearson, Spearman or Kendall, chosen with the buttons above the matrix. Selectable only with three or more columns. The choice changes the display only; the matrix is always computed for all three coefficients.
Params.filterMinR: Filter |r| ≥: the matrix hides cells whose coefficient is below this value in absolute terms; 0 to 1 is allowed, empty means no filter. While a filter is active, cells that cannot be computed are always hidden. Affects only the matrix display, not the result.
Params.filterMaxP: Filter p ≤: the matrix hides cells whose p-value is above this value or missing; 0 to 1 is allowed, empty means no filter. Affects only the matrix display, not the result.

PairResult.n: Number of paired values, row n: the rows in which both columns hold a number. Below 4 pairs there is no analysis.
PairResult.df: Degrees of freedom n − 2, row Degrees of Freedom (df); the t-values of Pearson and Spearman are tested with them.
PairResult.confidenceLevel: The confidence level as a fraction the confidence intervals were computed with, for example 0.95.
PairResult.pearson: The Pearson coefficient r with t-value, p-value, R² and confidence interval, card Pearson r; it measures the linear relationship.
PairResult.spearman: The Spearman coefficient ρ with t-value, p-value, ρ² and confidence interval, card Spearman ρ; it is Pearson's r of the ranks and measures a monotonic relationship.
PairResult.kendall: Kendall's τ with z-value, p-value, concordant and discordant pairs and confidence interval, card Kendall τ; it compares pairs of values moving the same and opposite ways and is usually smaller in absolute terms than r and ρ.
PairResult.descriptive: Means, standard deviations and covariance of the paired values, section Descriptive Statistics.
PairResult.diagnostics: The check of the assumptions, section Data Diagnostics: normality by Jarque-Bera, skewness, kurtosis, monotonicity index and outliers; the recommendation is built from it.
PairResult.recommendation: The recommended coefficient with reasons and points; the interface marks its card Recommended and lists the reasons in the tooltip.
PairResult._x: The paired values of the first chosen column (X) in row order; the scatter plot is drawn from them.
PairResult._y: The paired values of the second chosen column (Y) in row order; the scatter plot is drawn from them.
PairResult._nameX: The name of the first chosen column (X), as the scatter plot shows it on the axis.
PairResult._nameY: The name of the second chosen column (Y), as the scatter plot shows it on the axis.

LinearStat.r: The correlation coefficient between −1 and 1, card title Pearson r or Spearman ρ: for Pearson the covariance divided by the product of the standard deviations, s_XY / (s_X · s_Y); for Spearman the same value for the ranks, tied values get the mean rank. The card interprets the absolute value: from 0.9 very strong, from 0.7 strong, from 0.5 moderate, from 0.3 weak, below that very weak, positive or negative by the sign. From 0.7 the number is green (positive) or red (negative), from 0.4 yellow.
LinearStat.t: t-value r · √(df / (1 − r²)) with df = n − 2, row t-statistic; for Spearman with ρ in place of r. With a coefficient of exactly ±1 it is unbounded.
LinearStat.p: Two-sided p-value of the t-test for no relationship (coefficient 0) with n − 2 degrees of freedom, row p-value; with a coefficient of exactly ±1 it is 0. A small p-value suggests the relationship is not due to chance.
LinearStat.r2: The square of the coefficient, row R² for Pearson or ρ² for Spearman; the row also shows the value in percent. For Pearson it is the share of the spread of Y that a straight line in X explains.
LinearStat.ci: The confidence interval at the chosen level as lower and upper limit, bar Confidence Interval below the card. Computed through the Fisher z-transformation: for Pearson with standard error 1/√(n − 3), for Spearman after Bonett-Wright with √((1 + r²/2)/(n − 3)), as in Minitab, then transformed back. With a coefficient of exactly ±1 both limits equal the coefficient.

KendallStat.tau: Kendall's τ-b between −1 and 1, card title Kendall τ: (concordant − discordant pairs) / √((n₀ − Tₓ)(n₀ − Tᵧ)) with n₀ = n(n − 1)/2 and Tₓ, Tᵧ the pairs with equal X or Y values; 0 when the denominator is 0. The card interprets the absolute value with the same levels as r: from 0.9 very strong, from 0.7 strong, from 0.5 moderate, from 0.3 weak.
KendallStat.z: z-value τ / √v with v = 2(2n + 5)/(9n(n − 1)), row z-statistic; a normal approximation without a correction for ties.
KendallStat.p: Two-sided p-value from z, 2 · (1 − Φ(|z|)), row p-value; the test is for τ = 0.
KendallStat.concordant: Number of pairs of values moving the same way, row Concordant: pairs of rows in which X and Y go in the same direction. Pairs with equal X or Y values count neither here nor as discordant.
KendallStat.discordant: Number of pairs of values moving opposite ways, row Discordant: pairs of rows in which X rises while Y falls or the other way round. Pairs with equal X or Y values count neither here nor as concordant.
KendallStat.ci: The confidence interval τ ± z · √v at the chosen level, with z the 1 − α/2 quantile of the normal distribution, limited to −1 to 1; bar Confidence Interval below the card. With τ = ±1 both limits are τ.

Descriptive.meanX: Arithmetic mean x̄ of the paired X values, row Mean X, shown with three decimals.
Descriptive.meanY: Arithmetic mean ȳ of the paired Y values, row Mean Y, shown with three decimals.
Descriptive.stdX: Sample standard deviation s of the paired X values with divisor n − 1, row Std Dev X.
Descriptive.stdY: Sample standard deviation s of the paired Y values with divisor n − 1, row Std Dev Y.
Descriptive.cov: Sample covariance Σ(x − x̄)(y − ȳ)/(n − 1), row Covariance; its sign is the direction of the relationship.

Diagnostics.normX: The verdict on normality of X by Jarque-Bera, row Normality X (JB): the row shows ≈ normal or ≠ normal with the JB value, green when normal, yellow otherwise.
Diagnostics.normY: The verdict on normality of Y by Jarque-Bera, row Normality Y (JB): the row shows ≈ normal or ≠ normal with the JB value, green when normal, yellow otherwise.
Diagnostics.skewX: Sample skewness of X, n/((n − 1)(n − 2)) · Σ((x − x̄)/s)³, row Skewness X: 0 means symmetric, positive a longer right tail.
Diagnostics.skewY: Sample skewness of Y, n/((n − 1)(n − 2)) · Σ((y − ȳ)/s)³, row Skewness Y: 0 means symmetric, positive a longer right tail.
Diagnostics.kurtX: Excess kurtosis of X by the adjusted sample formula, row Kurtosis X: 0 like the normal distribution, positive more peaked with heavier tails, negative flatter.
Diagnostics.kurtY: Excess kurtosis of Y by the adjusted sample formula, row Kurtosis Y: 0 like the normal distribution, positive more peaked with heavier tails, negative flatter.
Diagnostics.mono: Monotonicity index as a fraction, row Monotonicity Index in percent: the share of concordant among all pairs of values without ties, 1 when there are no such pairs. Green from 85 %, yellow from 70 %, red below; below 0.7 Pearson and Spearman each lose one point in the recommendation.
Diagnostics.outliers: Number of outliers, row Outliers (IQR): counted are the residuals of the regression line of Y on X outside Q1 − 1.5 · IQR to Q3 + 1.5 · IQR. The row shows None in green at 0, otherwise the count in yellow.

Normality.normal: True when the Jarque-Bera value is below 5.99, the χ² limit with 2 degrees of freedom at 5 %; the column then counts as approximately normal.
Normality.jb: Jarque-Bera statistic JB = n/6 · (skewness² + kurtosis²/4) with the excess kurtosis; the row shows it with two decimals.
Normality.label: The display text of the verdict, ≈ normal or ≠ normal; it is the same in both languages.

Recommendation.best: The coefficient with the most points: pearson, spearman or kendall; on a tie Pearson comes before Spearman before Kendall. Its card carries the Recommended badge.
Recommendation.reasons: The reasons for the recommendation in checking order: normality, outliers, gap between Pearson and Spearman, sample size and, when low, monotonicity. Each reason points through its identifier to an interface text that the recommendation tooltip shows.
Recommendation.scores: The points per coefficient the recommendation follows from.

Reason.ok: True when the finding speaks for the recommended coefficient; the tooltip then shows a check mark, otherwise a warning sign. For recNormal, recNoOutliers and recLinear that means Pearson; for recLargeN it only says the sample is large enough (20 pairs or more).
Reason.key: The identifier of the finding, pointing to an interface text: recNormal or recNotNormal, recNoOutliers or recOutliers, recLinear or recNonlinear (Pearson and Spearman differ by more than 0.1), recLargeN or recSmallN (fewer than 20 pairs), plus recLowMono when the monotonicity index is below 0.7.
Reason.params: The numbers inserted into the text: count (outliers), delta (gap between the absolute values of r and ρ, as text with three decimals), n (pairs) or pct (monotonicity in whole percent); missing for findings without a number.

MethodScores.pearson: Points for Pearson, starting at 0: +3 when X and Y are both normal; +1 without outliers, −2 with outliers; +1 when the absolute values of r and ρ differ by at most 0.1; −1 with a monotonicity index below 0.7.
MethodScores.spearman: Points for Spearman, starting at 0: +2 when at least one column is not normal; +2 with outliers; +2 when the absolute values of r and ρ differ by more than 0.1; −1 with a monotonicity index below 0.7.
MethodScores.kendall: Points for Kendall, starting at 0: +2 when at least one column is not normal; +3 with outliers; +1 when the absolute values of r and ρ differ by more than 0.1; +2 with fewer than 20 pairs.

MatrixResult.names: The column names in selection order; they are the row and column headers of the correlation matrix, and each cell refers to two of them by position.
MatrixResult.matrix: The coefficients per method (Pearson r, Spearman ρ, Kendall τ-b) as a square table over all chosen columns; the correlation matrix shows the one chosen with the buttons. It is symmetric with 1 on the diagonal; a column pair with fewer than 4 paired values cannot be computed and stays empty for all three methods. If a column has no variance, Pearson and Spearman stay empty and Kendall τ-b gives 0. The filters do not change it.
MatrixResult.ciMatrix: Per coefficient a square table of confidence intervals, each cell with lower and upper limit, computed as pairwise: Fisher z for Pearson, Bonett-Wright for Spearman, normal approximation for Kendall. The diagonal and cells that cannot be computed are empty.
MatrixResult.pMatrix: Per coefficient a square table of two-sided p-values: Pearson and Spearman from t with n − 2 degrees of freedom, Kendall from z. The diagonal and cells that cannot be computed are empty.
MatrixResult.nMatrix: The number of paired values per cell; on the diagonal the number of values in the column, 0 when two columns share no row.
MatrixResult.pairs: For each column pair above the diagonal with at least 4 paired values one entry with the raw values; the scatter plots are drawn from them.

MatrixByMethod.pearson: The Pearson coefficients r of all column pairs as a square table; 1 on the diagonal, cells that cannot be computed empty.
MatrixByMethod.spearman: The Spearman coefficients ρ of all column pairs as a square table; 1 on the diagonal, cells that cannot be computed empty.
MatrixByMethod.kendall: Kendall's τ-b of all column pairs as a square table; 1 on the diagonal, cells that cannot be computed empty.

MatrixPair.i: The position of the first column in the column names, counted from 0; always smaller than that of the second.
MatrixPair.j: The position of the second column in the column names, counted from 0.
MatrixPair.x: The paired values of the first column in row order.
MatrixPair.y: The paired values of the second column in row order.

correlation.noWorksheet: Add a Worksheet module first to provide data.
correlation.noNumericColumns: No numeric columns found in any worksheet.
correlation.placeholderText: Select numeric columns — the correlation analysis runs automatically. 2 columns: detailed view. 3+: correlation matrix.
correlation.kendallHint: Kendall τ typically yields lower absolute values than Pearson r and Spearman ρ — this is inherent to the method.
correlation.recNormal: Both variables are approximately normally distributed — Pearson r is optimally applicable.
correlation.recNotNormal: At least one variable is not normally distributed — rank-based methods (Spearman/Kendall) are more robust.
correlation.recOutliers: {count} outliers detected in residuals — Pearson r is biased. Rank-based methods are more resistant.
correlation.recNoOutliers: No outliers detected — Pearson r is not biased by extreme values.
correlation.recNonlinear: Pearson r and Spearman ρ differ by Δ = {delta} — indicates non-linear but monotonic relationship.
correlation.recLinear: Pearson and Spearman agree well (Δ = {delta}) — linear relationship likely.
correlation.recSmallN: Small sample (n = {n}) — Kendall τ has better statistical properties for small n.
correlation.recLargeN: Sufficient sample size (n = {n}) — all three methods are statistically reliable.
correlation.recLowMono: Monotonicity index low ({pct}%) — relationship may not be monotonic.

histogram.whenToUse: Show the distribution of one or more numeric columns as frequency bars, with summary statistics and a confidence interval.

read.help: Read the data rows, the binning, the confidence level and the columns each slot accepts, and the figures shown next to the chart.

setDatasets.help: Set the data rows. A row consists of a value column and optionally a group column; the button "Add dataset" adds a row. Incomplete rows are kept but not plotted. The agent replaces the whole list in one call.

params.rows: A list of rows, each { value, group }: 'value' — a numeric column (required for the row to be plotted); 'group' — an optional column that splits the row into series. Each entry is a column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from read().pickableColumns of that slot, or null. [] clears the list.

setParam.help: Set an analysis option. read().activeParams names the options valid right now.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

datasets.help: Per data row its columns, each column of a row described individually under keys.

binMode.help: How bins are formed: auto or manual.

binWidth.help: The fixed bin width with binMode manual, or null.

confLevel.help: The confidence level of the statistics in percent.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slot keys a row may carry: value, group.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setDatasets accepts, each { key, name }; the key is instanceId|sheetId|columnId.

stats.help: Per plotted series its statistics and confidence intervals, each figure described individually under keys; null while nothing can be computed.

Params.binMode: How the bins (the bars) are formed: automatically or with a fixed width. Automatic: width = range of all visible values divided by ⌈log₂ n⌉ + 1 bins (at least 3, Sturges), rounded to a round value; n counts the values of all visible series. Fixed: the set bin width applies; if it is empty, the width is determined automatically.
Params.binWidth: The fixed width of each bin, a number greater than 0 in the units of the values. Empty means automatic width. The option can only be chosen with a fixed width.
Params.confLevel: The confidence level in percent, greater than 0 and less than 100 (for example 95). It determines the confidence intervals in the statistics table.

Dataset.valueRef: The value column of the row (slot V), numeric and required. Without it the row is kept but not plotted. Empty until one is chosen.
Dataset.groupRef: The group column of the row (slot G), optional; it splits the row into series, one per group value. Empty until one is chosen.

SeriesStats.referenceLine: The dashed line of this series, labelled “— Fit” in the legend. It passes through the points at the first and third quartile. Empty while the series has fewer than two values.

ReferenceLine.slope: The slope of the line: how much the normal quantile (the vertical axis, labelled as a probability in percent) rises per unit of the measured value (the horizontal axis). It is positive and larger the more tightly the values are packed; roughly it is the inverse of the spread.
ReferenceLine.intercept: The intercept of the line: the normal quantile at a measured value of 0. Together with the slope, normal quantile = slope · value + intercept; the line crosses the 50 percent level where the value equals minus intercept divided by slope, roughly at the mean.

doe-planner.name: DoE Planner
doe-planner.description: Design of Experiments: Full Factorial, Fractional, Plackett-Burman, CCD, Box-Behnken, Taguchi
doe-planner.analysisIncomplete: Please fill in all response values in the worksheet first ({pct}% filled).
doe-planner.analysisSingular: Model cannot be computed (singular matrix). Check your data.
doe-planner.tip_full: All factor combinations are tested. For 2-level factors: 2^k runs; for mixed levels: product of all level counts. Ideal for few factors (2–4) when all main effects and interactions are needed.
doe-planner.tip_frac: Only a fraction of combinations is tested (2^(k−p) runs). Saves runs with many factors, at the cost of confounding some interactions.
doe-planner.tip_pb:
Screening design with resolution III. Very efficient for identifying the few significant factors out of many.

When to use:
• Many factors (7–47) but limited experimental budget
• Goal: identify the 3–5 most important factors (Pareto principle)
• Early project phase — the question is 'which factors matter?', not 'how exactly do they interact?'
• Runs = next multiple of 4 above the factor count → e.g. 12 runs for 11 factors

When NOT to use:
• Interactions matter — PB confounds main effects with 2-factor interactions (resolution III)
• Precise effect estimation needed — use 2^(k−p) with resolution ≥ V instead
• Few factors (≤ 5) — a full factorial is often more economical and provides clean interaction estimates
• Nonlinear effects expected — PB has only 2 levels, no curvature check

Typical workflow:
1. PB screening → find significant factors
2. Fix non-significant factors at their economical level
3. Follow-up design (2^k or CCD) with remaining factors for detailed modeling
doe-planner.tip_ccd: Central Composite Design for response surface modeling. Enables quadratic models and optimization.
doe-planner.tip_bb: Box-Behnken design: 3-level, no extreme points (corners). Ideal when extreme combinations must be avoided. Requires 3–7 factors.
doe-planner.tip_taguchi: Taguchi orthogonal array: Robust design with few runs. Focus on signal-to-noise ratio and robustness.
doe-planner.tip_dopt: D-optimal design: Maximizes the determinant of X'X (information matrix). Minimizes the volume of the confidence ellipsoid for all parameter estimates.
doe-planner.tip_aopt: A-optimal design: Minimizes the trace of (X'X)⁻¹. Minimizes the average variance of all parameter estimates.
doe-planner.tip_gopt: G-optimal design: Minimizes the maximum prediction variance across the design space. Ensures uniform prediction quality.
doe-planner.tipTwoLevelOnly: This design is only available for factors with exactly 2 levels. Reduce the number of levels or choose a different design (e.g. Full Factorial, Box-Behnken, or Taguchi).
doe-planner.optimalInfo_dopt: D-optimal designs maximize the determinant of the information matrix, providing the most precise overall parameter estimates for a given number of runs.
doe-planner.optimalInfo_aopt: A-optimal designs minimize the average variance of parameter estimates. They provide the best average precision across all model coefficients.
doe-planner.optimalInfo_gopt: G-optimal designs minimize the maximum prediction variance. They ensure the most uniform prediction quality across the entire design space.
doe-planner.optimalMinRunsNew: Minimum: {min} additional runs on top of the {m} existing rows.
doe-planner.tipOptimalQuadratic: Include squared terms (x²) in the model. Requires more runs but enables quadratic response surface modeling.
doe-planner.optimalTooFewRuns: Too few runs — at least {min} are needed for the selected model.
doe-planner.optimalTooFewRunsNew: Too few additional runs — at least {min} are needed on top of the {m} existing rows.
doe-planner.forbiddenHint: Factor-level combinations that are physically impossible or unwanted. The optimiser avoids them. "Any" leaves the factor unconstrained for that rule.
doe-planner.modelTermsHint: Interactions known to be physically decoupled can be excluded from the model. That lowers the minimum run count and improves precision of the remaining effects.
doe-planner.modelTermsHintHier: Pick every term the model should contain. Marginality is enforced: a higher-order term pulls in all of its subterms; turning off a main effect cascades out every interaction that contained it.
doe-planner.previewHint: Temporary — adjust factor values or pre-fill responses. Only "Create datasheet" turns this into a real datasheet.
doe-planner.previewStaleNote: Factor values were edited manually — the reported optimality score refers to the original suggestion and is no longer guaranteed for the edited values.
doe-planner.worksheetCreateHint: A datasheet is only created after confirmation. Measurement results will then be entered there.
doe-planner.worksheetStaleWarning: The design has changed — the linked datasheet no longer matches the current plan. "Recreate" discards the old datasheet.
doe-planner.bbNotAvailable: Box-Behnken is not available for k={k} (supported: {min}–{max} factors).
doe-planner.fracNotAvailable: No fractional factorial designs available for k={k} factors (supported: {min}–{max}).
doe-planner.taguchiNotAvailable: No suitable Taguchi array for k={k} factors with {levels} levels available.
doe-planner.recFull: For {k} factors (2-level), a full factorial design is recommended.
doe-planner.recFrac: For {k} factors, a fractional factorial design is recommended.
doe-planner.recPB: For many factors ({k}), a Plackett-Burman screening is ideal.
doe-planner.recBB: For 3-level factors, a Box-Behnken design is recommended.
doe-planner.recTaguchi: For 3-level factors, a Taguchi array is a good choice.
doe-planner.resLegendFull: Full factorial — all main effects and interactions independently estimable.
doe-planner.resLegendVII: Main effects and 2-factor interactions not aliased with 4-factor or lower interactions.
doe-planner.resLegendVI: Main effects not aliased with 4-factor interactions; 2-factor interactions not aliased with 3-factor interactions.
doe-planner.resLegendV: Main effects and 2-factor interactions independently estimable; 2-factor interactions aliased with 3-factor interactions.
doe-planner.resLegendIV: Main effects not aliased with 2-factor interactions; 2-factor interactions aliased with each other.
doe-planner.resLegendIII: Main effects aliased with 2-factor interactions — screening designs only.
doe-planner.factorUnitCategoricalDisabled: Categorical factors carry no physical unit.
doe-planner.tipRandomize:
Randomization protects against systematic nuisance variables (e.g. fatigue, temperature drift, material batches). RECOMMENDED in most cases.

Do NOT randomize when:
• Changeover between factor levels is very costly or time-consuming (e.g. furnace temperature)
• Split-plot designs are intentionally used
• EVOP is running and sequence must be fixed

Rule of thumb: when in doubt, always randomize.
doe-planner.tipReplicates:
Replication repeats the entire design 1:1. Each factor combination is run multiple times under identical conditions.

Benefits:
• Provides an independent estimate of pure error (repeatability)
• Increases statistical power for detecting effects
• Enables lack-of-fit testing for the regression model

Rule of thumb:
• 1 replicate = no replication (screening phase, limited budget)
• 2 replicates = standard for confirmatory experiments
• 3+ replicates = high-precision studies or noisy processes
doe-planner.tipCenterPoints:
Center points are replicates at the midpoint of all factors (all levels set to their center value).

Benefits:
• Estimate pure experimental error (Replicate Error) — without them, unreplicated 2^k designs have no independent error estimate
• Curvature check — if the center mean deviates significantly from the model prediction, quadratic effects are present
• Efficient: only 3 extra runs for both benefits

When to use:
• RECOMMENDED for 2^k and fractional factorial designs without other replicates
• Not needed for CCD (has its own center points) or Box-Behnken
doe-planner.factorLevelsError: Please set at least the low and high level for all factors.
doe-planner.selectResError: Please select a design from the table.
doe-planner.stepEvaluateDesc: Evaluate design quality before running experiments: efficiency, confounding (aliases), variance inflation factors, and statistical power.
doe-planner.noEvaluation: Please generate an experiment design first.
doe-planner.tipDEff: D-Efficiency: Measures precision of parameter estimation. 100% = optimal design. Based on the determinant of X'X.
doe-planner.tipAEff: A-Efficiency: Measures average estimation accuracy of all parameters. Based on the trace of (X'X)^-1.
doe-planner.tipGEff: G-Efficiency: Ratio of average to maximum prediction variance. 100% = uniform prediction quality.
doe-planner.tipCondNum: Condition number: Measure of numerical stability. Ideally close to 1. Values >1000 indicate collinearity.
doe-planner.tipMaxLev: Maximum leverage: Largest influence of any single design point on the estimate. Ideal: p/n.
doe-planner.tipVIF: VIF measures how much a coefficient's variance is inflated due to correlation with other predictors. VIF=1 = perfectly orthogonal. VIF>5 = concerning → adjust the design (add more runs or choose a higher resolution). VIF>10 = severe multicollinearity → fundamentally change the design, or drop the confounded terms from the model during regression analysis.
doe-planner.tipAlias: Shows which effects are confounded (aliased) in a fractional factorial design. Aliased effects cannot be estimated independently.
doe-planner.noAliases: No confounding — all effects are independently estimable (full factorial design).
doe-planner.tipPower: Statistical power: probability of detecting an effect of a given size. Power ≥ 80% is generally considered adequate.
doe-planner.powerDesc: n={n} runs, df(Error)={dfError}, α={alpha}. Power for various standardized effect sizes (Δ/σ):
doe-planner.powerSaturated: Power cannot be computed: the model is saturated (df(Error) = 0). Add replicates or reduce the model.
doe-planner.decisionDesc: What should happen after this analysis?
doe-planner.decisionConfirm_repeat: Repeat this phase? A new cycle with the same factor settings will be created.
doe-planner.decisionConfirm_recenter: Re-center? The best point becomes the new center. Factor levels will be adjusted automatically.
doe-planner.decisionConfirm_stop: Complete the project? No further phases will be created.
doe-planner.evopRec_repeat: Recommendation: Repeat cycle — no significant effects detected yet.
doe-planner.evopRec_recenter: Recommendation: Re-center — significant effects detected. Use the best point as the new center.
doe-planner.evopRec_stop: Recommendation: Complete — no significant effects after multiple cycles. Process is stable.
doe-planner.configureLeft: Configure factors, responses, and design type in the left panel.
doe-planner.augmentHint: Appends additional optimal runs to the linked datasheet. Already-conducted runs stay unchanged; only the new rows are chosen D/A/G-optimally.
doe-planner.sourceHint: Columns are matched to factors and responses by name. Existing runs are kept as fixed rows; only the additional runs are chosen optimally.
doe-planner.sourceMappingOk: {rows} runs will be reused, {responses} response column(s) detected.
doe-planner.sourceSkipped: ({n} row(s) skipped — missing or invalid values.)
doe-planner.sourceMissingFactors: No columns found for these factors: {names}.
doe-planner.tipDispersion: Models the mean and ln(s²) as two separate responses — identifies factor settings that reduce process variability independently of the mean (dual-response approach after Vining & Myers). Requires at least 2 replicates per design point.
doe-planner.dispersionNoReplicates: Dispersion analysis requires at least 2 replicates per design point. Increase the replicates option in the left panel or add repeat runs in the worksheet.
doe-planner.dispersionZeroVar: {n} design point(s) with variance = 0 (all replicates identical) — these are excluded from the log-s² model.
doe-planner.dispersionModelNotFitted: Model could not be fitted (too few points or singular).
doe-planner.dispersionNoModel: No log-s² model available — all design points had variance = 0 or too few usable points.
doe-planner.dispersionConclusionNone: No factors with significant dispersion effect detected — process variability does not appear to be controllable through the investigated factors. Check other sources (measurement system, raw material, environment).
doe-planner.dispersionPreferInteraction: Interaction effect — read level combination from contour plot

doe-advisor.whenToUse: When an improvement project still has to settle WHICH design of experiments fits — screening, interactions, optimisation, robustness or mixture — or when the Overview tab with all designs and the comparison of the central composite designs are needed; not for planning or evaluating a concrete experiment, that is what the design planner and its evaluation are for.

read.help: Returns the advisor state and the answer options of the open question.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

switchTab.help: Switches the displayed area: Overview of the designs, the guided Advisor or the CCD comparison of central composite designs.

params.tab: overview shows the Overview tab with all designs, wizard the guided advisor, ccd the comparison of the central composite designs. Any other value is an error.

answer.help: Answers the open question and moves on to the next one — or to the recommendation, when the path ends there. If the advisor already stands on its recommendation, no question is open: everything stays as it is and the call returns false.

params.opt: The chosen option of the open question. Which question is open is in currentStep; which options it has is named by the error message. An option that question does not know is an error.

back.help: Goes back one question and discards the answer that led away from it. If the advisor stands on the first question, nothing happens.

restart.help: Starts the advisor over: first question, no answers, no trail.

currentOptions.help: The answer options of the open question — exactly the values answer(opt) accepts. Empty once the advisor stands on its recommendation.

tab.help: The displayed area: overview the Overview tab with all designs, wizard the guided advisor, ccd the comparison of the central composite designs.

currentStep.help: The id of the open question — phase, goal, screening-curvature, factor-count, factor-levels, robustness-type, limits or corners — or result:<key> once a recommendation stands; result:none means no design of experiments is due in this phase yet. The question itself is a translated text and lives in no field; the recommendation is under recommendation.

answers.help: The answers given, one per question. The key is phase, goal, screeningCurvature, factorCount, factorLevels, robustnessType, limits or corners, the value the chosen option.

history.help: The ids of the answered questions in the order they were answered; the last entry is the one back() returns to.

recommendation.help: The recommended design, each entry described individually under keys. Empty while the advisor is still asking a question or no design is due in this phase yet.

Recommendation.designId: The key of the recommended design, for example "ccd-rotatable"; the same one the result card holds for the design.
Recommendation.name: The name of the recommended design as a translated text, as it appears in the heading of the result card.
Recommendation.factors: The range of factors the design suits, as a translated text, for example "2–6", as it appears in the result card under "Factors".
Recommendation.levels: The level specification of the design as a translated text, for example "5" or "3+ or mixed", as it appears in the result card under "Levels".
Recommendation.effort: The effort specification of the design as a translated text, for example "2^k runs (e.g. 4 factors = 16)", as it appears in the result card under "Effort".

doe-advisor.name: DoE Advisor
doe-advisor.description: Overview of DoE designs and a guided wizard for design selection
doe-advisor.overviewTitle: DoE designs in Six Sigma — selection overview
doe-advisor.overviewLead: Comparison of the most common experimental designs. Number of factors, levels and effort show when each design pays off.
doe-advisor.phaseGuideTitle: Rule of thumb for selection in the DMAIC cycle
doe-advisor.ccdLead: Rotatable (CCC, Circumscribed) versus Face-Centered (CCF) — the two most-used response-surface designs.
doe-advisor.resultNoneTitle: No DoE yet — start with data analysis
doe-advisor.resultNoneBody: In the Define and Measure phases the focus is on sharpening the problem, identifying factors and verifying the measurement system. DoE comes earliest in Analyze (screening) or Improve (optimization). Use Project Charter, SIPOC, Process Map, MSA and Process Capability instead.

full.name: Full factorial (2^k)
full.tip: DMAIC phase Improve, when all main and interaction effects must be determined reliably
full.note: Delivers all effects and interactions completely; effort grows exponentially

full-general.name: Full factorial (general)
full-general.tip: When factors have more than two levels or mixed / categorical levels (e.g. material A/B/C, pressure 1/2/3 bar)
full-general.note: Complete information even for multi-level or categorical factors; effort grows quickly with the number of levels

fractional.name: Fractional factorial (2^(k-p))
fractional.tip: Screening with a moderate number of factors when resources are limited
fractional.note: Very efficient; aliasing — keep an eye on resolution (III, IV, V)

plackett-burman.name: Plackett-Burman
plackett-burman.tip: Early screening with many factors when only main effects are sought
plackett-burman.note: Highly economical; interactions are aliased with main effects

dsd.name: Definitive Screening Design (DSD)
dsd.tip: Modern screening when quadratic effects are also suspected
dsd.note: Detects main effects, curvature and some 2-factor interactions; a strong compromise

ccd-rotatable.name: CCD — Rotatable (CCC, Circumscribed)
ccd-rotatable.tip: RSM optimization when factor ranges can be expanded freely and maximum statistical quality is desired
ccd-rotatable.effort: α = (2^k)^(1/4); factorial part + star points outside the cube + center points
ccd-rotatable.note: Statistically optimal: direction-independent prediction variance (rotatable). Star points lie OUTSIDE the original factor range — requires expandable limits

ccd-face.name: CCD — Face-Centered (CCF)
ccd-face.tip: RSM optimization when factor limits are hard (safety, specification, machine limits)
ccd-face.effort: α = 1; star points centered on the cube faces, all runs within the original factor range
ccd-face.note: Practical with hard limits; only 3 levels per factor. Not rotatable — prediction quality at the corners weaker than along the axes

box-behnken.name: Box-Behnken design
box-behnken.tip: Optimization when extreme corner points (e.g. all maxima) are physically not allowed
box-behnken.note: Only 3 levels, no extreme combinations; needs at least 3 factors

taguchi.name: Taguchi (orthogonal arrays)
taguchi.tip: Robust design, separation of noise and control factors, target-on-spec quality
taguchi.note: Focus on signal-to-noise ratio and robustness; interactions hard to separate

dispersion.name: Dispersion DoE
dispersion.tip: Variance itself as the response — find which factors drive variability without explicit noise factors
dispersion.note: Models the mean AND log(s²) as separate responses; identifies variance-reducing settings — requires true replicates, not pseudo-repetitions

mixture.name: Mixture designs (Simplex-Lattice / Simplex-Centroid)
mixture.tip: Recipes / formulations where proportions sum to 100 %
mixture.note: Specifically for mixtures (pharma, chemistry, food); no independent factors

d-optimal.name: D-optimal designs
d-optimal.tip: Restrictions in the design space, unequal factor costs, individual model approaches
d-optimal.note: Tailored algorithmically; requires a clear model

evop.name: EVOP (Evolutionary Operation)
evop.tip: DMAIC phase Control / running production: continuous, small improvement on the live process without production downtime
evop.levels: 2–3 (small steps around the current operating point)
evop.effort: Many cycles with minimal variations around the setpoint
evop.note: Uses regular production as the experiment; minimal scrap risk; slow learning, only small effects detectable

define-measure.designs: (no DoE yet — start with data analysis)

analyze.goal: Reduce many potential factors to the few relevant ones (screening)
analyze.designs: Plackett-Burman, fractional factorial, Definitive Screening Design

improve.goal: Understand interactions and find the optimum
improve.designs: Full factorial (2^k / general), CCD (rotatable / face-centered), Box-Behnken, D-optimal, mixture designs

improve-robustness.goal: Make the process insensitive to noise

control.goal: Continuous, small improvements on the live process

phase.question: Which DMAIC phase is your project in?

define-measure.label: Define / Measure
define-measure.help: Problem is being scoped, factors collected, measurement system verified.

analyze.label: Analyze
analyze.help: Many candidate factors must be filtered down to the few relevant ones (screening).

improve.label: Improve
improve.help: Factors are known — understand interactions and locate the optimum.

control.label: Control
control.help: Live serial process is to be improved gently without production downtime.

goal.question: What is the primary goal of the experiment?

screening.label: Screening
screening.help: Identify the few truly important factors out of many.

interactions.label: Understand interactions
interactions.help: Cleanly separate main and interaction effects — e.g. with 2^k or resolution V.

optimization.label: Find the optimum (RSM)
optimization.help: Build a response-surface model, estimate curvature and the optimum.

robustness.label: Robustness / signal-to-noise
robustness.help: Make the process insensitive to noise, minimize variation.

mixture.label: Mixture / formulation
mixture.help: Components sum to 100 % — no independent factors.

screening-curvature.question: Do you expect quadratic (curved) effects, and how many factors are you screening?

yes.label: Yes — curvature possible, 6–20 factors
yes.help: Definitive Screening Design captures main effects, curvature and some interactions in one step.

no.label: No — only linear effects, 5–10 factors
no.help: Classical fractional factorial with sufficient resolution (at least IV).

many-factors.label: Very many factors (>10), main effects only
many-factors.help: Plackett-Burman is highly economical — interactions are deliberately aliased.

factor-count.question: How many factors do you want to vary systematically?

few.label: Few (2–4 factors)
few.help: Full factorial is feasible and delivers all main and interaction effects in full.

many.label: Medium to many (5+ factors)
many.help: Full plan becomes too large — use a fractional factorial with sufficient resolution.

factor-levels.question: How many levels should the factors have?

two.label: Exactly 2 levels per factor
two.help: Classical 2^k plan — high/low per factor, linear effects and interactions fully estimable.

multi-or-mixed.label: 3+ levels or mixed / categorical factors
multi-or-mixed.help: General full factorial — e.g. material A/B/C or 3 pressure levels. Effort equals the product of the level counts.

noise-factors.label: With explicit noise factors (inner-outer array)
noise-factors.help: Control factors in the inner array, noise factors in the outer array — Taguchi optimizes the signal-to-noise ratio.

dispersion-only.label: Model variability itself (no explicit noise factors)
dispersion-only.help: Dispersion DoE: 2^k with replication; mean and log(s²) are analyzed separately to find variance-reducing settings.

limits.question: Can the factor limits be extended beyond the original range?

expandable.label: Yes, limits are expandable
expandable.help: Star points may lie outside the cube (α > 1) — rotatable CCD is statistically optimal.

hard.label: No, limits are hard (safety, specification, machine limits)
hard.help: All runs must stay inside the original factor range — star points centered on the cube faces.

corners.question: Are extreme corner combinations (all factors at maximum/minimum at the same time) physically allowed?

allowed.label: Yes, corners are allowed
allowed.help: Face-centered CCD uses cube corners for maximum span under hard limits.

forbidden.label: No, corners are forbidden
forbidden.help: Box-Behnken avoids corner points entirely — all runs lie on midpoints and edges.

constrained.label: Complex restrictions / individual model terms
constrained.help: D-optimal design is fitted algorithmically to the constrained space and the chosen model.

reasoning.full: Few factors and the wish for a complete picture of all main and interaction effects argue for a full factorial (2^k). Effort is manageable and the analysis is unambiguous.
reasoning.full-general: Few factors with more than two levels or mixed / categorical levels — the general full factorial covers every factor combination. Effort equals the product of level counts and grows quickly: 3×3×3 = 27 runs, 2×3×4 = 24 runs.
reasoning.fractional: Medium to high number of factors with a limited run budget — fractional factorial samples the design space efficiently. Watch the resolution: III for screening only, IV for clean main effects, V for clean interactions too.
reasoning.plackett-burman: Very many factors and pure main-effect screening — Plackett-Burman is the most economical choice. Follow up with a detailed design (2^k or CCD) on the top factors.
reasoning.dsd: Screening with suspected curvature — Definitive Screening Design captures main effects, quadratic effects and some interactions in approximately 2k+1 runs.
reasoning.ccd-rotatable: RSM optimization with expandable factor limits — rotatable CCD provides direction-independent prediction variance and is statistically optimal. Star points lie outside the cube.
reasoning.ccd-face: RSM optimization with hard factor limits — face-centered CCD stays strictly within the defined range (α = 1) and uses only 3 levels per factor. Not rotatable, but practical.
reasoning.box-behnken: Optimization, but extreme corner combinations are not allowed — Box-Behnken avoids corners entirely and uses only 3 levels per factor. At least 3 factors required.
reasoning.taguchi: Robustness against noise is the goal — Taguchi arrays optimize the signal-to-noise ratio. Interactions are deliberately deprioritized; the focus is on a target-true, low-variation process.
reasoning.dispersion: Variance reduction without explicit noise factors — a 2^k plan with replication models the mean (μ) and the dispersion (log s²) as two separate responses. This identifies factor settings that minimize variance independently of the mean — the core idea of the dual-response approach.
reasoning.mixture: Components sum to 100 % — mixture designs (Simplex-Lattice / Simplex-Centroid) honor that constraint and yield a valid model for recipes, formulations and blends.
reasoning.d-optimal: Complex restrictions or individual model terms — D-optimal designs are fitted algorithmically to the constrained space and the chosen model. Requires a clear model.
reasoning.evop: Live serial production with small, safe variations around the setpoint — EVOP uses regular production as the experiment. No downtime, but slow learning and only small effects detectable.

range.label: Factor range
range.rotatable: must be expandable — star points exceed ±1
range.face: stays strictly within the defined range

application.label: Typical application
application.rotatable: lab processes, free parameters, academic studies

ccd.ruleBody: Choose rotatable when the factor range can be expanded freely and maximum statistical quality is required. Choose face-centered when factor limits cannot be exceeded for physical, safety or regulatory reasons — by far the more common case in industrial Six Sigma.

fmea.name: FMEA
fmea.description: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis with RPN calculation
fmea.sortedByAP: Sorted by AP (H → L, then S, O, D)
fmea.apSourceNote: Scale texts: our own wording based on the AIAG-VDA FMEA Handbook (2019). AP assignment per the handbook's table. All texts can be edited.

10.criterion: Danger to the health or safety of workers or end users.

9.criterion: Legal or regulatory requirements are not met.

8.criterion: Product without its primary function; full scrap or line stop at the customer.

7.criterion: Primary function reduced; sorting and partial scrap.

6.criterion: Comfort or secondary function fails; off-line rework.

5.criterion: Secondary function reduced; rework of part of the lot.

4.criterion: Appearance or noise bothers most customers; in-line rework.

2.criterion: Only attentive customers notice; minor process disruption.

10.criterion: No prevention control; the failure is practically certain.

9.criterion: Prevention barely effective; the failure occurs very often.

8.criterion: Prevention of little effect; the failure occurs often.

7.criterion: Prevention of limited effect; the failure recurs.

6.criterion: Prevention partly effective; the failure occurs occasionally.

5.criterion: Prevention effective; the failure occurs sporadically.

4.criterion: Prevention effective and proven; the failure is rare.

3.criterion: Proven prevention; the failure is very rare.

2.criterion: Prevention per proven standard; isolated cases only.

1.criterion: Failure prevented by design of the process, e.g. poka-yoke.

10.criterion: No inspection in place or inspection unsuitable.

8.criterion: Effectiveness of the inspection method not proven.

7.criterion: Manual visual or audible inspection, of limited reliability.

6.criterion: Manual inspection with aids, e.g. a gauge.

5.criterion: Proven manual or machine inspection after the process step.

4.criterion: Automatic inspection downstream; the defective part is rejected.

3.criterion: Automatic inspection in the process step; the defective part is rejected.

2.criterion: The cause is detected automatically; no defective part is made.

1.criterion: The failure cannot occur or is always detected.

10.criterion: Safe operation impaired; danger to people.

9.criterion: Product does not meet legal or regulatory requirements.

8.criterion: Product unusable for its intended purpose.

4.criterion: Appearance, noise or feel bothers most customers.

3.criterion: Appearance, noise or feel bothers many customers.

2.criterion: Only a few attentive customers notice.

10.criterion: New technology without experience; no prevention.

9.criterion: First use of a new design; prevention not aimed at the requirement.

8.criterion: New design based on similar technology; little experience.

7.criterion: Known design in a new application.

5.criterion: Carry-over with changes; prevention partly proven.

3.criterion: Minor change to a proven design; prevention tested.

10.criterion: No test or inspection method in place.

9.criterion: Test method not designed for this failure.

7.criterion: Proven method; test only after production release.

6.criterion: Proven method before production release; pass/fail test.

5.criterion: Proven method before production release; test to failure.

4.criterion: Proven method before production release; degradation test.

3.criterion: Proven method early in development; pass/fail test.

2.criterion: Proven method early in development; test to failure or degradation.

1.criterion: Failure excluded or always detected by the method.

fmea.effectPlaceholder: What happens if the failure occurs?
fmea.controlPlaceholder: How is the failure or its cause detected?
fmea.justificationPlaceholder: Why is no action taken for AP H?
fmea.tipS: Severity – How severe is the effect of the failure on the customer? (1 = none, 10 = critical)
fmea.tipO: Occurrence – How likely is it that the failure occurs? (1 = unlikely, 10 = very frequent)
fmea.tipD: Detection – How likely is it that the failure is detected before delivery? (1 = certain, 10 = almost impossible)
fmea.sevHighDesc: Customer strongly affected, function severely limited
fmea.burndownNoData: No rated risks with dated actions available.
fmea.whenToUse: When a process or a design should be surveyed systematically for what can go wrong, what effect it has, how often it occurs and how reliably it is detected — rated by action priority (AIAG-VDA) or risk priority number, with actions and their effect on the rating; not for collecting possible causes without rating them, that is what Ishikawa and the cause-and-effect matrix are for.

setMethod.help: Selects the rating method of the FMEA: AP (action priority per AIAG-VDA) or RPN (risk priority number = severity × occurrence × detection).

params.m: The method: ap rates by action priority (AIAG-VDA), rpn by risk priority number (severity × occurrence × detection). Any other value is an error.

setFmeaType.help: Sets the type of the FMEA; it selects the action-priority scale texts.

params.type: The type: process for a process FMEA, design for a design FMEA. Any other value is an error.

addRisk.help: Adds an empty risk and returns its id.

deleteRisk.help: Removes a risk with its actions.

params.id: The id of the risk as read() lists it under risks. An unknown id is an error.

resetScales.help: Discards all custom scale texts; the shipped ones apply again.

sortByPriority.help: Sorts the risks by the active rating method, the most urgent first.

setScaleValue.help: Sets a custom scale text; it replaces the shipped one.

params.key: The key of the scale cell. For the risk priority number these are sevNone, sevNoneDesc, sevLow, sevLowDesc, sevMod, sevModDesc, sevHigh, sevHighDesc, sevVHigh, sevVHighDesc, occUnlikely, occUnlikelyRate, occLow, occLowRate, occMod, occModRate, occHigh, occHighRate, occVHigh, occVHighRate, detCertain, detCertainDesc, detHigh, detHighDesc, detMod, detModDesc, detLow, detLowDesc, detVLow and detVLowDesc; for the action priority ap.<type>.<dimension>.<level>.meaning or .criterion with type process or design, dimension sev, occ or det and level 1 to 10. Any other key is an error.
params.text: The new text. An empty string leaves the cell empty; a missing argument is an error.

setRiskValue.help: Sets one field of a risk.

params.riskId: The id of the risk as read() lists it under risks. An unknown id is an error.
params.field: Which field; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per field are given under keys.

setRiskCollapsed.help: Collapses or expands a risk card.

params.riskId: The id of the risk. An unknown id is an error.
params.collapsed: true collapses the card, false expands it. Any other value is an error.

addRiskAction.help: Appends an empty action to the risk; it then sits as the last row of the actions table. The position of the new action, starting at 0, is the return value.

params.riskId: The id of the risk. An unknown id is an error.

removeRiskAction.help: Removes one action of a risk.

params.riskId: The id of the risk. An unknown id is an error.
params.actionIndex: The position of the action in actions, starting at 0. A position where the risk has no action is an error.

setActionValue.help: Sets one field of an action.

params.riskId: The id of the risk. An unknown id is an error.
params.actionIndex: The position of the action in actions, starting at 0. A position where the risk has no action is an error.
params.field: Which field; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per field are given under keys.

risks.help: The risks in editing order. Per risk: id (that is how the actions address it), step (the process step under review), failureMode, effect, cause, prevention (the prevention control), control (the detection control), specialChar (the special characteristic: CC, SC or empty), justification (why a risk with high action priority has no action), sev (severity), occ (occurrence) and det (detection), collapsed (whether the card is collapsed) and actions. Per action: text (the action), resp (the person responsible), date (the due date), done (whether it is finished), deltaS, deltaO and deltaD (by how many levels it lowers severity, occurrence and detection). Severity, occurrence and detection are strings from 1 to 10 or empty, the deltas strings from 0 to 9. The risk priority number, the action priority and the projected values are computed and are in no field. Bulk data: without options.fields = ['risks'] only the extent is returned.

scales.help: The custom scale texts, one text per scale-cell key; null means the shipped ones apply.

method.help: The rating method: ap by action priority (AIAG-VDA), rpn by risk priority number.

fmeaType.help: The type of the FMEA: process for a process FMEA, design for a design FMEA. It selects the action-priority scale texts.

RiskField.step: The process step or component this risk card examines; free text.
RiskField.failureMode: The potential failure mode: the way in which the step or component can fail at its task. Free text.
RiskField.effect: The potential effect of failure: what the customer or the next process notices of the failure. It drives the severity rating. Free text.
RiskField.cause: The potential cause of failure: why the failure mode occurs. It drives the occurrence rating. Free text.
RiskField.prevention: The prevention control: what stops the cause from occurring in the first place. It feeds into the occurrence rating. Free text.
RiskField.control: The detection control: what detects the failure or its cause before it reaches the customer. It feeds into the detection rating. Free text.
RiskField.specialChar: The special characteristic: CC for a critical, SC for a significant characteristic, empty for none. From a severity of 9 the card points out that it should be checked, while none is set.
RiskField.justification: The justification why a risk with high action priority (H) gets no action. With the AP method the field appears while such a risk has neither an action text nor a justification, and stays visible once filled. Free text.
RiskField.sev: The severity (S) of the failure for the customer, 1 to 10: 1 means no noticeable effect, 10 a safety hazard or regulatory violation; empty means not yet rated. Together with occurrence and detection it gives the priority: with the AP method through the AIAG-VDA handbook table (H, M or L), with RPN as the product severity × occurrence × detection.
RiskField.occ: The occurrence (O), 1 to 10: 1 means the failure is unlikely, 10 that it occurs very frequently; empty means not yet rated. Together with severity and detection it gives the priority (AP table or RPN = severity × occurrence × detection).
RiskField.det: The detection (D), 1 to 10: 1 means the failure is certain to be detected, 10 that it is almost never detected – so a high number is bad; empty means not yet rated. Together with severity and occurrence it gives the priority (AP table or RPN = severity × occurrence × detection).

ActionField.text: The action that is meant to reduce the risk; free text. A risk with high action priority and no action text needs a justification.
ActionField.resp: Who is responsible for the action (Resp.); free text.
ActionField.date: The due date of the action as YYYY-MM-DD; empty means no deadline. Actions with a date form the course in the burndown.
ActionField.done: Whether the action is implemented, yes or no. In the burndown it only then counts toward the actual course.
ActionField.deltaS: By how many levels, 0 to 9, the action is meant to lower the severity. The projection of the risk is severity minus the sum over all its actions, at least 1.
ActionField.deltaO: By how many levels, 0 to 9, the action is meant to lower the occurrence. The projection of the risk is occurrence minus the sum over all its actions, at least 1.
ActionField.deltaD: By how many levels, 0 to 9, the action is meant to lower the detection number, that is improve detection. The projection of the risk is detection minus the sum over all its actions, at least 1.

attribute-test.name: Attribute Tests
attribute-test.description: Tests for proportions, rates and counts: 1 and 2 proportions, Fisher's exact, chi-square association, McNemar, equivalence (TOST), 1 and 2 Poisson rates
attribute-test.ratePooled: Use pooled estimate of the rate for the test
attribute-test.pooled: Use pooled estimate of p for the test
attribute-test.cellLegend: Per cell: observed / expected / contribution to χ²
attribute-test.basisExact: Decision based on the exact binomial test
attribute-test.basisPearson: Decision based on Pearson χ² (two-sided); the direction applies to Fisher's exact test only
attribute-test.h0Assoc: H₀: row and column variable are independent
attribute-test.noteNormalApprox: The normal approximation is not suitable here (n·p₀ or n·(1 − p₀) < 5, or x = 0 or x = n). Use the exact test.
attribute-test.notePooled: The z-test uses the pooled estimate of p; the confidence interval stays unpooled.
attribute-test.warnExpectedBelow1: At least one expected count is below 1 – the χ² test is unreliable.
attribute-test.warnShareBelow5: {share} % of the expected counts are below 5 (more than 20 %) – the χ² test is unreliable.
attribute-test.hintEnterCounts: Enter counts to run the test.
attribute-test.hintPickColumns: Select columns to run the test.
attribute-test.errXGreaterN: The number of events must not exceed n.
attribute-test.errP0Range: p₀ must lie strictly between 0 and 1.
attribute-test.errResponseLevels: The response column needs exactly 2 distinct values.
attribute-test.errGroupLevels: The group column needs exactly 2 levels.
attribute-test.errTableTooSmall: The table needs at least 2 × 2 cells with observations.
attribute-test.statDiscordant: Discordant pairs (event → no event / no event → event)
attribute-test.basisExactPoisson: Decision based on the exact Poisson test
attribute-test.basisZRate: Decision based on the z-test for the rate difference
attribute-test.basisExactMcNemar: Decision based on the exact McNemar test
attribute-test.basisTost: Decision based on two one-sided tests (TOST) against the equivalence bounds
attribute-test.h0McNemar: H₀: the proportion is the same before and after
attribute-test.h0McNemarLabeled: H₀: the proportion is the same for {before} and {after}
attribute-test.noteRatePooledIgnored: With a hypothesized difference ≠ 0 the test runs without the pooled rate.
attribute-test.h0Equiv: H₀: Δ ≤ lower bound or Δ ≥ upper bound (Δ = p₁ − p₂, or p − p₀ for one sample)
attribute-test.h1Equiv: H₁: lower bound < Δ < upper bound
attribute-test.noteRateNormalApprox: The normal approximation is not suitable here (λ₀·t < 5). Use the exact test.
attribute-test.noteNoDiscordant: No discordant pairs – there is nothing to test.
attribute-test.noteSmallDiscordant: Fewer than 10 discordant pairs – use the exact p-value, not the χ² approximation.
attribute-test.noteEquivDegenerate: Both proportions are 0 (or both 1) – the normal approximation cannot be used, so there is no equivalence result.
attribute-test.noteNotEquivalentIsNotEqual: No significant difference does not mean that the proportions are equivalent. Whether the difference is small enough is shown by the equivalence test.
attribute-test.notePairedUseMcNemar: Were the same units inspected before and after? Then McNemar's test is the right one.
attribute-test.noteEquivBoundsPractical: The equivalence bounds are a practical decision, not a statistical one. Fix them before looking at the data.
attribute-test.noteEquivCiOutside: The confidence interval does not lie entirely within the equivalence bounds.
attribute-test.errExposure: Exposure must be a number greater than 0.
attribute-test.errLambda0: The hypothesized rate λ₀ must be greater than 0.
attribute-test.errDiff0: The hypothesized difference must be a number.
attribute-test.errPairsLength: The before and after columns must have the same length.
attribute-test.errPairLevels: Both columns together need exactly 2 distinct values.
attribute-test.hintEnterBounds: Enter the equivalence bounds. They are a practical decision, not a statistical one: which difference would still count as equivalent in practice? Fix them before looking at the data.
attribute-test.errBoundsContainOne: The bounds must enclose 0 (lower < 0 < upper); they apply relative to the target p₀.
attribute-test.deltaOne: Equivalence margin δ (pp, relative to p₀)
attribute-test.noteRateNotTestable: There are no events in either sample, yet the difference is to be tested against a value other than 0 – nothing can be tested.
attribute-test.errBoundsOrder: The lower bound must be smaller than the upper bound.
attribute-test.whenToUse: When counts of events are compared: tests one proportion against a hypothesized value, two proportions against each other (z test and Fisher's exact test), the equivalence of proportions (TOST), paired proportions before and after (McNemar), one or two Poisson rates (events per exposure) or the association of two categorical variables (chi-square on a cross table). The counts are given as summarized numbers or taken from worksheet columns.

setPairCell.help: Sets a count of the McNemar 2 × 2 table with summarized input: how many pairs were in the given state before and after.

params.value: The count as text, '' clears the cell.

checkEquivalence.help: Switches to the equivalence test with two samples, like the “Check with equivalence test” button below a non-significant two-proportion test. It shares counts and columns with the two-proportion test, so they stay; the equivalence bounds stay unchanged.

read.help: Returns the entered configuration, the keys and roles valid in the current state, the selectable columns, the selectable event values and the result. result is null while the inputs are incomplete or invalid; errorMsg then names the reason (an input hint or a refusal such as a too small table) and is empty while a result exists.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets one parameter; the test reruns. Switching testKind or inputMode keeps all other inputs, so switching back loses nothing.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. summary values and p0 as text containing a number.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. If the current event value does not occur in the new response column, its last value counts as the event.

params.slot: One of the roles in activeColumnSlots: response (response column), counts (counts for rates), before and after (McNemar), group, rowVar or colVar.
params.ref: The reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns for that role, or null to clear the role.

setTableCell.help: Sets one count of the cross table used by the association test with summarized input.

params.row: Row index, 0 is the first row.
params.col: Column index, 0 is the first column.
params.value: The count as text, '' clears the cell.

setTableRowName.help: Sets the name of one row of the cross table.

params.row: Row index, 0 is the first row.
params.name: The name as text, '' clears it.

setTableColName.help: Sets the name of one column of the cross table.

params.col: Column index, 0 is the first column.
params.name: The name as text, '' clears it.

addRow.help: Appends a row with empty counts to the cross table; its name is the next letter.

addCol.help: Appends a column with empty counts to the cross table; its name is the next one of X, Y, Z and then C4, C5 and so on.

removeRow.help: Removes one row of the cross table with its counts. Only while the table has more than two rows (at least two remain); otherwise an error.

params.row: Row index, 0 is the first row.

removeCol.help: Removes one column of the cross table with its counts. Only while the table has more than two columns (at least two remain); otherwise an error.

params.col: Column index, 0 is the first column.

runAnalysis.help: Recomputes the test from the current inputs. Missing or invalid inputs are no refusal of the action: result becomes null and errorMsg names the reason.

ratePooled.help: For two rates: true uses the pooled rate for the z statistic, as long as the hypothesized difference is 0.

exposurePerRow.help: The exposure per worksheet row for rates from columns, as entered; the total exposure is the number of rows times this value.

equiv.help: The equivalence test settings: samples (1 or 2), symmetric (true for ±delta), delta, lower and upper as text in percentage points.

testKind.help: The kind of test: 'one' (one proportion), 'two' (two proportions), 'equiv' (equivalence of proportions), 'mcnemar' (paired proportions), 'rate1' (one Poisson rate), 'rate2' (two Poisson rates) or 'assoc' (association in a cross table).

inputMode.help: Where the counts come from: 'summary' (entered numbers) or 'columns' (worksheet columns).

direction.help: The alternative hypothesis: 'two-sided', 'greater' or 'less'. With the association test only active once a result for a 2 x 2 table exists.

alpha.help: The significance level, greater than 0 and less than 1. Starts from the confidence level of the settings.

p0.help: The hypothesized proportion for one proportion, as entered; it must lie between 0 and 1, exclusive.

pooled.help: For two proportions: true uses the pooled standard error for the z statistic.

summary.help: The summarized counts as entered: x and n (one proportion), x1, n1, x2 and n2 (two proportions), t, t1, t2, lambda0 and diff0 (rates), pairs { labels, counts } (McNemar) and table { rows, cols, counts } (association), all as text.

colRefs.help: The chosen column per role: response, counts, before, after, group, rowVar and colVar, each { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } or null.

eventValue.help: The value of the response column that counts as event, or null while there is none.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state.

activeColumnSlots.help: The roles setColumn accepts in the current state: none with summarized input; with column input response (proportions and equivalence, plus group for two samples), counts (rates, plus group for two rates), before and after (McNemar) or rowVar and colVar (association test).

pickableColumns.help: Per role the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'. Any column with at least 2 values.

eventValueOptions.help: The values setParam accepts for eventValue: the distinct values of the chosen response column, for McNemar of both paired columns together; empty while there is none.

result.help: The test report: figures, notes, decision and, for the association test, the cross table, each figure described individually under keys; null while the inputs are incomplete or invalid (errorMsg gives the reason).

errorMsg.help: The reason there is no result: an input hint while counts or columns are missing, or the refusal (for example a table that is too small or a p0 outside the range); an empty string while a result exists.

Action.key: Identifier of the offered next step; currently only “actionCheckEquivalence” (below a non-significant two-sided two-proportion test), run via checkEquivalence.

equiv.samples: “1 sample” tests whether one proportion is equivalent to p₀; “2 samples” tests whether the difference of two proportions lies within the bounds. Default: 2 samples. The test shares its counts with the one- or two-proportion test.
equiv.symmetric: “Symmetric bounds (±δ)” uses one margin δ for both sides, “Separate bounds” a lower and an upper bound. Default: symmetric.
equiv.delta: Equivalence margin δ in percentage points, a number greater than 0: equivalent means the difference (p − p₀ for one sample) lies between −δ and +δ. The margin is a subject-matter decision, not a statistical one.
equiv.lower: Lower equivalence bound in percentage points, below 0; relative to p₀ for one sample. It must be below the upper bound.
equiv.upper: Upper equivalence bound in percentage points, above 0; relative to p₀ for one sample. It must be above the lower bound.

Params.exposurePerRow: “Exposure per row” for rates from columns: which exposure (time, area, units) belongs to one row of the counts column, a number greater than 0, default 1. The total exposure is the number of rows with a value times this exposure, per group for two rates.
Params.ratePooled: Pooled rate for the two-rate z-test. When checked, the test computes the standard error from the common rate (x₁ + x₂)/(t₁ + t₂); this applies only while the hypothesized difference Δ₀ is 0, otherwise a note appears and the test uses separate estimates. The confidence interval of the difference always stays unpooled. Default: unchecked.
Params.testKind: The test type, chosen in the “Test” section: “1 proportion” tests one proportion against the hypothesized proportion p₀, “2 proportions” compares the proportions of two samples, “Equivalence (proportions)” tests whether a proportion or a difference lies within subject-matter bounds, “McNemar (paired)” compares proportions of the same units before and after, “1 Poisson rate” and “2 Poisson rates” test events per exposure, “Chi-square association” tests whether two categorical variables of a cross table are associated. Default is “2 proportions”; switching keeps all other inputs.
Params.inputMode: The input type in the “Input” section: “Summarized” takes counts entered by hand (events and trials, or the cross table), “Columns” counts them from columns of a data collection. Default is “Summarized”.
Params.alpha: Significance level α, a number strictly between 0 and 1, for example 0.05. H₀ is rejected when the deciding p-value is below α; α also sets the confidence level of the interval, 1 − α in percent, rounded to one decimal.
Params.direction: The alternative hypothesis: “≠ two-sided”, “> greater” or “< less”. For one and two proportions it sets the p-values and the confidence interval; one-sided, the interval extends to 0 or 1 (one proportion) or to −1 or 1 (difference). For the association test it appears only for a 2 × 2 table and affects only Fisher's exact test; Pearson χ² stays two-sided.
Params.p0: Hypothesized proportion p₀ for the one-proportion test, as a number with a point or comma, for example 0.5 (default). It must lie strictly between 0 and 1, otherwise there is no result.
Params.pooled: Pooled estimate of p for the z-test of two proportions. When checked, the test computes the standard error from the common proportion p̄ = (x₁ + x₂)/(n₁ + n₂): SE = √(p̄(1 − p̄)(1/n₁ + 1/n₂)); otherwise from both proportions separately. The confidence interval of the difference always stays unpooled. Default: unchecked.

labels.before: Label of the first time point of the McNemar table, such as “Before” or an inspector's name; shown in hypotheses and figures. Empty means “before”, with column input the column name.
labels.after: Label of the second time point of the McNemar table, such as “After”; shown in hypotheses and figures. Empty means “after”, with column input the column name.

summary.diff0: Hypothesized difference Δ₀ of the rates λ₁ − λ₂ when comparing two rates, default 0. Only at 0 are the conditional exact test and the pooled rate available.
summary.lambda0: Hypothesized rate λ₀ for the one-rate test, events per unit of exposure, a number greater than 0.
summary.t2: Exposure (t) of sample 2 when comparing two rates, a number greater than 0.
summary.t1: Exposure (t) per sample for comparing two rates, rows “Sample 1” and “Sample 2”, a number greater than 0. The sample's rate is events / t.
summary.t: Exposure (t) for the one-rate test: the amount of observation the events refer to (time, area, units), a number greater than 0. The rate is λ̂ = events / t.
summary.x: Events for the one-proportion test: how often the event of interest occurred, a whole number from 0, at most the number of trials. If events and trials are both empty, nothing is computed.
summary.n: Trials (n) for the one-proportion test: the number of observations, a whole number greater than 0. The estimated proportion is p̂ = events / n.
summary.x1: Events per sample when comparing two proportions, rows “Sample 1” and “Sample 2”: how often the event occurred in that sample, a whole number from 0, at most its number of trials.
summary.n1: Trials (n) per sample when comparing two proportions, rows “Sample 1” and “Sample 2”: the number of observations in that sample, a whole number greater than 0. The sample's proportion is events / n.
summary.x2: Events in sample 2 when comparing two proportions, a whole number from 0, at most the trials of sample 2.
summary.n2: Trials (n) in sample 2 when comparing two proportions, a whole number greater than 0.

Params.eventValue: With column input, the value of the response column that counts as an event (“Event =”); for McNemar it applies to both paired columns. The response column needs exactly two distinct values; without a choice, as in Minitab, the last value in natural sort order is used.

Result.decisionParams: Placeholders of the equivalence decision: lower and upper bound (formatted), the unit (% for one sample, pp for two) and α. Equivalence test only.
Result.actions: The next steps below the result: for a non-significant two-sided two-proportion test the “Check with equivalence test” button, because no difference does not mean equivalent. Otherwise the field is missing.
Result.kind: The test type the report was computed for, as chosen in the “Test” section: one proportion, two proportions, equivalence, McNemar, one rate, two rates or chi-square association.
Result.stats: The figure rows of the table under “Results”, different for each test type: counts, proportions, confidence interval, test statistic and p-values; each row is explained individually: hold Alt and click the question mark next to its label.
