Result.notes: Notes below the decision: skipped rows with missing values, the unsuitable normal approximation (one proportion), the pooled z-test (two proportions), removed empty rows or columns and the warnings about small expected counts (association test).
Result.decision: The decision against α: “Reject H₀” (reject) when the deciding p-value is below α, otherwise “Do not reject H₀” (keep); for the equivalence test “equivalent” or “not shown” (notEquivalent). The deciding test is the exact binomial test for one proportion, the z-test for two proportions, the exact Poisson test for one rate, the z-test of the difference for two rates, the exact test for McNemar, the TOST for equivalence and Pearson χ² (always two-sided) for the association test. The basis is shown next to the decision.
Result.basisKey: Identifier of the sentence naming the basis of the decision: exact binomial test, z-test, exact Poisson test, z-test of the rate difference, exact McNemar test, TOST or Pearson χ².
Result.table: The cross table of the association test with observed and expected counts and each cell's contribution to χ²; empty for one and two proportions.

Stat.key: Identifier of the figure row, unique within one test type; the same identifier can mean different things in different test types.
Stat.labelKey: Identifier of the row's label text; for Fisher's exact test of a 2 × 2 table in the association test there is one per direction (two-sided, one-sided greater, one-sided less); when comparing two proportions the Fisher row always carries the same label without a direction, even for a one-sided alternative.
Stat.params: Placeholders of the label: the confidence level in percent, the group name or the degrees of freedom; missing for rows without placeholders.
Stat.value: The value as formatted text, as in the table: four decimals, χ², G² and Yates with three, p-values below 0.0001 as “< 0.0001”, counts as “x / n”, confidence intervals as lower and upper bound; decimal point in both languages, “–” for a value that cannot be computed.

Note.key: Identifier of the note text shown below the decision.
Note.params: Placeholders of the note: the number of skipped rows, the names of removed rows or columns, or the rounded percentage of cells with an expected count below 5; missing for notes without placeholders.

CrossTable.cols: The column levels of the cross table; columns without observations are removed.
CrossTable.rows: The rows of the cross table; rows without observations are removed.

CrossRow.name: The row level, on the left of the cross table.
CrossRow.cells: The cells of the row, one per column level.

CrossCell.obs: Observed count of the cell, the top number.
CrossCell.exp: Expected count under independence: row total · column total / grand total, with two decimals.
CrossCell.contrib: Each cell shows three numbers: the observed count o, the count expected under independence e = row total · column total / grand total, and the contribution (o − e)²/e to Pearson χ². Large contributions show where the association lies.

equiv.counts: Events and trials of the sample as “x / n”.
equiv.counts1: Events and trials of the first group as “x / n”.
equiv.counts2: Events and trials of the second group as “x / n”.
equiv.estimate: The estimate: for one sample the proportion p̂ in percent, for two the difference p̂₁ − p̂₂ in percentage points.
equiv.ci: Confidence interval at level 1 − 2α, as it belongs to two one-sided tests at level α. If it lies entirely within the bounds, the proportions are equivalent.
equiv.bounds: The equivalence bounds in the unit of the estimate; for one sample p₀ plus the bounds, clipped to 0 to 100 %.
equiv.pLower: p-value of the one-sided test against the lower bound.
equiv.pUpper: p-value of the one-sided test against the upper bound.
equiv.pValue: p-value of the TOST, the larger of the two one-sided p-values. Equivalent when it is below α.

mcnemar.discordant: The discordant pairs as “b / c”: b changes from event to no event, c from no event to event. Only they contribute to the test.
mcnemar.pBefore: Proportion of pairs with the event at the first time point.
mcnemar.pAfter: Proportion of pairs with the event at the second time point.
mcnemar.diff: Difference of the proportions after − before.
mcnemar.ci: Wald confidence interval of the paired difference, level 1 − α; one-sided for a directional alternative with −1 or 1 as the open bound.
mcnemar.pExact: p-value of the exact McNemar test, the binomial test of c among b + c pairs with p = 0.5, in the chosen direction. Basis of the decision.
mcnemar.chi2: McNemar χ² = (b − c)² / (b + c) without continuity correction; two-sided only.
mcnemar.pChi2: p-value of McNemar χ² with one degree of freedom, for information only.
mcnemar.chi2Cc: McNemar χ² with continuity correction: (|b − c| − 1)² / (b + c); two-sided only.
mcnemar.pChi2Cc: p-value of the corrected χ², for information only.

rate2.rate1: Rate of the first group λ̂₁ = x₁ / t₁; group name from the group column, “1” with summarized input.
rate2.rate2: Rate of the second group λ̂₂ = x₂ / t₂.
rate2.diff: Difference of the rates λ̂₁ − λ̂₂.
rate2.ci: Confidence interval of the difference from the normal approximation with separate standard error, level 1 − α, always unpooled.
rate2.z: Statistic z = (λ̂₁ − λ̂₂ − Δ₀) / SE; SE from the pooled rate when checked and Δ₀ = 0, otherwise separate.
rate2.pValue: p-value of the z-test in the chosen direction. Basis of the decision.
rate2.pExactCond: p-value of the conditional exact test: given the total x₁ + x₂, x₁ is binomial with p = t₁/(t₁ + t₂). Only for Δ₀ = 0 and at least one event, for information.
rate2.ratio: Rate ratio λ̂₁ / λ̂₂; missing when the second group has no event.
rate2.ratioCi: Exact confidence interval of the rate ratio from the Clopper-Pearson interval of the conditional binomial proportion, level 1 − α.

rate1.rate: Estimated rate λ̂ = x / t, events per unit of exposure.
rate1.ci: Exact Garwood confidence interval from chi-square quantiles, level 1 − α; one-sided for a directional alternative.
rate1.pExact: p-value of the exact Poisson test in the chosen direction, two-sided twice the smaller tail, at most 1. Basis of the decision.
rate1.pNormal: p-value of the normal approximation, for information only; suitable from λ₀·t ≥ 5, otherwise a note appears.

one.counts: Events and trials of the sample as “x / n”.
one.ci: Exact Clopper-Pearson confidence interval from beta distribution quantiles, level 1 − α. One-sided for a directional alternative, the open side extending to 0 or 1; for x = 0 the lower bound is 0, for x = n the upper bound is 1.
one.pExact: p-value of the exact binomial test: for “> greater” P(X ≥ x), for “< less” P(X ≤ x), two-sided twice the smaller tail, at most 1. Basis of the decision: H₀ is rejected when it is below α.
one.z: Test statistic of the normal approximation z = (p̂ − p₀) / √(p₀(1 − p₀)/n).
one.pNormal: p-value of the normal approximation from z in the chosen direction, for information only. Suitable only when n·p₀ ≥ 5, n·(1 − p₀) ≥ 5 and 0 < x < n; otherwise a note appears and the exact test applies.

two.counts1: Events and trials of the first group as “x / n”; group name from the group column, “1” with summarized input.
two.counts2: Events and trials of the second group as “x / n”; group name from the group column, “2” with summarized input.
two.p1: Proportion of the first group p₁ = x₁ / n₁.
two.p2: Proportion of the second group p₂ = x₂ / n₂.
two.diff: Difference of the proportions p₁ − p₂.
two.ci: Wald confidence interval of the difference: p₁ − p₂ ± z₁₋α/₂ · SE at level 1 − α, the standard error always unpooled, even when the test is pooled. One-sided for a directional alternative, with −1 or 1 as the open bound.
two.z: Test statistic z = (p₁ − p₂) / SE; SE pooled or separate, depending on the “Use pooled estimate of p for the test” checkbox. If SE is 0, “–” is shown.
two.pValue: p-value of the z-test in the chosen direction. Basis of the decision: H₀ is rejected when it is below α.
two.pFisher: p-value of Fisher's exact test of the 2 × 2 table of events and non-events in both groups, in the chosen direction; two-sided, the sum over all tables at most as likely as the observed one. For information only.

assoc.pearson: Pearson χ² = Σ (o − e)²/e over all cells, with DF = (rows − 1)·(columns − 1). Unreliable when an expected count is below 1 or more than 20 % are below 5; a warning then appears.
assoc.pPearson: p-value of Pearson χ², always two-sided. Basis of the decision: H₀, independence, is rejected when it is below α.
assoc.lr: Likelihood ratio G² = 2 · Σ o · ln(o/e) over the cells with observations, with the same DF as Pearson χ².
assoc.pLR: p-value of the likelihood ratio G², for information only.
assoc.yates: χ² with Yates correction, only for a 2 × 2 table: Σ max(0, |o − e| − 0.5)²/e.
assoc.pYates: p-value of the Yates-corrected χ² with one degree of freedom, only for a 2 × 2 table.
assoc.pFisher: p-value of Fisher's exact test, only for a 2 × 2 table. It is the only figure that follows the chosen alternative hypothesis; with a one-sided alternative the label names the direction.

hypothesis-test.name: Hypothesis Test
hypothesis-test.description: Variance and mean tests with automatic normality assessment and power analysis
hypothesis-test.whenToUse: When you need to decide whether an observed difference in location or spread goes beyond the noise — one mean against a target value, two samples against each other, or k groups together. Requires metric data in a data collection.

read.help: Returns the configuration and the computed result. result is null while the inputs are incomplete.

params.options: Optional; this module carries no bulk data.

runAnalysis.help: Computes with the current configuration. Calling it repeatedly is harmless; incomplete inputs leave result at null.

setCategory.help: Chooses what is being tested: the spread (Variances) or the location (Means). The recomputation only follows on the next tick, because the column pickers are remounted — a query in the same batch still sees the old or an empty result.

params.cat: 'variance' or 'mean'. Any other value is an error.

setTestType.help: Chooses the sample layout: one sample against a target value, two samples against each other, or k groups. The recomputation only follows on the next tick, because the column pickers are remounted — a query in the same batch still sees the old or an empty result.

params.type: 'one', 'two' or 'k'. Any other value is an error.

setDirection.help: Chooses the direction of the alternative hypothesis. One-sided only if the question was one-sided beforehand — not afterwards because it fits better that way.

params.direction: 'two-sided', 'greater' or 'less'. Any other value is an error — it would be computed as 'less'.

params.alpha: For example 0.05. Seeded from the settings.

setPowerGoal.help: Sets the desired power goal for the sample-size assessment.

setTargetValue.help: Sets the target value of the one-sample test (σ²₀, σ₀ or μ₀).

params.value: The target value; for spread it must be positive.

setTargetType.help: Defines whether the target value of the one-sample spread test is entered as a variance or as a standard deviation.

params.targetType: 'variance' or 'stddev'. Any other value is an error.

setEqualVariances.help: Location with two or k samples: assume equal variances. With two samples this runs the pooled t-test, with k Fisher's one-way ANOVA with Tukey. Off is the default — the Welch t-test and Welch ANOVA with Games-Howell do not need that assumption.

params.flag: true for the pooled t-test or Fisher's ANOVA.

setColumn1.help: Points sample 1 at a column of a data collection.

params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } — the values are in the data collection's read().

setColumn2.help: Points sample 2 at a column of a data collection.

params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }, or null to clear it.

setColumnsK.help: Points the k-sample test at several columns.

params.refs: List of column references; every group needs at least three values.

direction.help: Direction of the alternative hypothesis: 'two-sided', 'greater' or 'less'.

targetValue.help: The entered target value: μ₀ or σ²₀ for one sample, the hypothesised mean difference μ_d₀ for the paired test.

targetType.help: Whether the spread target value counts as a variance or as a standard deviation.

colRef1.help: Column reference of the first sample.

colRef2.help: Column reference of the second sample.

colRefsK.help: The column references of the k-sample test.

equalVariances.help: Whether equal variances are assumed: the pooled t-test instead of Welch with two samples, Fisher's ANOVA instead of Welch with k.

result.help: The result as a display model (formatted texts; labels in the interface language, numbers with a decimal point), each figure described individually under keys; null while the inputs are incomplete.

ResidualPlot.residuals: The residuals per observation, value minus group mean, in group order.
ResidualPlot.fitted: The fitted values per observation, the mean of its group.

Result.residualPlot: The data of the four residual plots (residuals versus fits, probability plot, histogram, order) below the result. Only for k samples on the Fisher or Welch route, otherwise null.
Result.isK: True for the test type “k Samples”, otherwise false. When true, the interface shows a normality card per group, the group overview and, where applicable, the pairwise comparisons, but no power analysis.
Result.allNormal: True when every sample counts as normally distributed, that is, the Anderson-Darling test gives p ≥ α for each sample; Shapiro-Wilk is shown as well but does not decide. The interface shows this as the route step “Normality: Yes/No”.
Result.normCards: The normality assessment, one card per sample: one or two for one- and two-sample tests, k for the test type “k Samples”.
Result.route: The chosen main procedure, as the route under “Algorithm Routing” shows it. Normality is decided by the Anderson-Darling test alone, with p ≥ α. For variances: one sample always uses the χ² variance test, two samples the F-test when all are normal, otherwise Levene (Brown-Forsythe), k samples Bartlett or Levene. For means: when all samples are normal, the parametric test; otherwise it stays when every sample has n ≥ 20 (the rank test is added as a cross-check); otherwise the rank route. Parametric means the one-sample t-test, the Welch t-test (pooled t-test only when equal variances are assumed) or one-way ANOVA; the rank route means Wilcoxon signed-rank, Mann-Whitney U or Kruskal-Wallis.
Result.varEquality: The variance equality. For two samples, means and the parametric route it is only the assumption from the checkbox “Assume equal variances”, without figures; for k samples and means it is the Levene test (Brown-Forsythe) with figures in the section “Variance Equality”. Empty for variance tests, for one sample and on the rank route of two samples.
Result.main: The main test in the section “Test Result”: hypotheses and figures of the chosen procedure.
Result.secondary: The rank test next to the parametric result in the section “Rank-based comparison test”: Wilcoxon, Mann-Whitney U or Kruskal-Wallis. Only on the route “not normally distributed, but every sample has n ≥ 20”, otherwise empty.
Result.power: The power analysis, only for one- and two-sample tests; empty for the test type “k Samples”.
Result.pairwise: The pairwise comparisons, only for at least three groups; empty for two groups and outside “k Samples”.

Route.name: Name of the chosen procedure as formatted text, always the English procedure name, such as “One-Way ANOVA” or “Welch t-Test”.
Route.algoId: Identifier of the matching page in the Algorithm Lab; the interface opens it through the button next to the procedure name. Empty text when there is no page.

NormCard.label: Name of the sample as formatted text: “S1” or “S2” for one- and two-sample tests, the column name from the data collection for k samples.
NormCard.badgeClass: Display class of the interface; colours the verdict badge green for normal and red for not normal.
NormCard.badgeText: The verdict as formatted text, “Normal” or “Not normal”; it follows the Anderson-Darling test alone: normal when p ≥ α.
NormCard.rows: Two rows of the test table: Shapiro-Wilk and Anderson-Darling.
NormCard.metrics: The sample figures as formatted texts: n, x̄, s and s². x̄ carries the t confidence interval of μ, x̄ ± t(1 − α/2; n − 1) · s/√n, s² the χ² interval of σ², (n − 1)s²/χ²(1 − α/2) to (n − 1)s²/χ²(α/2), s its square roots; all at level 1 − α.

NormRow.name: Name of the test as displayed text, “Shapiro-Wilk” or “Anderson-Darling”, column “Test”.
NormRow.algoId: Identifier of the Algorithm Lab page for the button next to the test name.
NormRow.stat: The test statistic as formatted text with four decimals: W for Shapiro-Wilk, A² for Anderson-Darling. Column “Statistic”.
NormRow.p: The p-value of the test as formatted text with four decimals, column “p”.
NormRow.pClass: Display class of the interface; colours the p-value red when p < α and green otherwise.
NormRow.decisionIcon: Identifier of the symbol before the decision: a warning symbol when p < α, a check mark otherwise.
NormRow.decisionText: The decision as formatted text, column “Decision”: “Reject” when p < α, meaning the normality assumption is rejected, otherwise “Do not reject”.

Metric.label: Label of the figure as formatted text, as the interface shows it, such as “Test Method”, “Statistic”, “p”, “df”, “n”, “x̄”, “s²” or “95% CI”; which figures appear changes with test and route.
Metric.value: The value as formatted text: numbers mostly with four decimals; exceptions are the degrees of freedom (whole numbers, “df1 / df2” for k-sample tests, one decimal for Welch), the sample sizes n, k and N (whole numbers), the effect size (three decimals), α (as set) and the power (percent with one decimal); the test method as its English name, intervals as lower and upper bound; “–” for a value that cannot be computed.
Metric.valueClass: Display class of the interface; colours the p-value red when p < α and green otherwise, sets test method and intervals in smaller type and colours power by whether the goal is achieved. Missing in the normality cards.
Metric.title: Tooltip of the figure as formatted text, a short explanation; for the p-value possibly with the way it was computed, exact or by normal approximation. May be empty.
Metric.algoId: Identifier of the Algorithm Lab page, only on the test method and on the Hodges-Lehmann estimate; empty text when there is no page.
Metric.ci: Only in the normality cards: the confidence interval at level 1 − α as formatted text, the t interval of μ for x̄, the χ² interval of σ² for s², its square roots for s. Missing for n; empty when the interval cannot be computed, that is, when n < 2 or s or s² is not greater than 0.

VarEquality.varsEqual: True when the variances count as equal: for two samples the assumption from the checkbox “Assume equal variances”, for k samples a non-significant Levene test, p ≥ α.
VarEquality.metrics: The figures of the Levene test (Brown-Forsythe) as formatted texts: test method, statistic, df as “df1 / df2” and p. Only for k samples, empty for two samples.
VarEquality.trailLabelKey: The translation key of the route step, not a displayed text: “varEqualLabel” (shown as “Equal variances assumed”) for two samples, “varDiffLabel” (shown as “Significant variance difference (Levene)”) for k samples.
VarEquality.trailYes: Whether the route step is answered with “Yes”: for two samples when equal variances are assumed; for k samples the other way round, when the Levene test shows a difference.

MainResult.modelSummary: The model summary of the one-way ANOVA as in Minitab: S with four decimals, R², R²(adj) and R²(pred) in percent; R²(adj) and R²(pred) not below 0 %, R²(pred) “–” when a group has only one value. Only on the Fisher and Welch routes, otherwise null.
MainResult.ciHeader: Header of the confidence interval column as formatted text with the level in percent. k samples only.
MainResult.showCi: Whether the column with the per-group confidence intervals is shown; true on the Fisher and Welch routes. k samples only.
MainResult.h0: The null hypothesis as formatted text with symbols, such as “μ₁ = μ₂ = … = μₖ” or “σ² ≤ 4.0000”; for one sample it contains the target value, and the sign follows the direction: two-sided =, greater ≤, less ≥.
MainResult.h1: The alternative hypothesis as formatted text with ≠, > or <; for k samples “at least one μ differs” or “at least one variance differs”.
MainResult.ciNote: A note on the interval as formatted text, missing for k samples. When two sample means show no significant difference it gives the range of the difference μ₁−μ₂ and says that equality is not shown by this; on the Mann-Whitney route it gives the shift η₁−η₂ or says that the samples are too small for level 1 − α. Otherwise empty.
MainResult.h0Class: Display class of the interface; marks the H₀ box as rejected when p < α, otherwise as accepted.
MainResult.h1Class: Display class of the interface; marks the H₁ box the other way round from the H₀ box.
MainResult.h0Tip: Tooltip of the H₀ box as formatted text, such as “H₀ is rejected: p … < α …”; empty for k samples.
MainResult.h1Tip: Tooltip of the H₁ box as formatted text, “Significant” or “Not significant” with the verdict on H₀; empty for k samples.
MainResult.metrics: The figures of the main test as formatted texts: always test method, statistic and p; depending on the test also df, the confidence interval at level 1 − α, on the Mann-Whitney route the Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the shift, x̄ or x̄₁ and x̄₂, s² or s²₁ and s²₂; for k samples k, N and the pooled variance s²ₚ.
MainResult.anovaRows: The ANOVA table, only for k samples with one-way ANOVA, three rows: Between Groups, Within Groups, Total. Empty for other procedures.
MainResult.groupRows: The group overview, only for k samples: one row per selected column.
MainResult.showCld: Whether the column “Group” with the grouping letters is shown; true as soon as the pairwise comparisons supply letters, that is, from three groups on. Only for k samples.

AnovaRow.src: Source of variation as formatted text: “Between Groups”, “Within Groups” or “Total”. Column “Source”.
AnovaRow.ss: Sum of squares as formatted text, column “SS”: between groups Σ nᵢ(x̄ᵢ − x̄)², within groups the sum of squared deviations from the group mean, total the sum of both.
AnovaRow.df: Degrees of freedom as formatted text, column “df”: k − 1 between groups, N − k within, N − 1 total.
AnovaRow.ms: Mean square as formatted text, column “MS”: SS divided by df; “—” in the row Total.
AnovaRow.f: F value as formatted text, column “F”: MS between divided by MS within, only in the row Between Groups, otherwise “—”.
AnovaRow.p: p-value of the F-test as formatted text, column “p”, only in the row Between Groups, otherwise “—”; below α the means differ significantly.
AnovaRow.pClass: Display class of the interface; colours the p-value red when p < α and green otherwise, empty in the other rows.
AnovaRow.bold: Whether the row appears in bold; only the row Total.

GroupRow.ci: Confidence interval of the group mean as formatted text with lower and upper bound, level 1 − α; only on the Fisher and Welch routes, otherwise empty.
GroupRow.name: Name of the group as displayed text, the column name from the data collection. Column “Group”.
GroupRow.n: Number of values in the group as formatted text, column “n”.
GroupRow.mean: Mean x̄ of the group as formatted text with four decimals, column “x̄”.
GroupRow.variance: Sample variance s² of the group as formatted text with four decimals, column “s²”.
GroupRow.letters: The grouping letters (Compact Letter Display) from the pairwise comparisons as formatted text, column “Group”: groups sharing a letter do not differ significantly, groups without a shared letter differ. Empty for two groups.

SecondaryResult.metrics: The figures of the comparison test as formatted texts: test method (on the large-sample path Wilcoxon, Mann-Whitney U or Kruskal-Wallis, for the Bonett test on two variances Levene), statistic and p.
SecondaryResult.title: The section title as displayed text: “Rank-based comparison test”, for the Bonett test on two variances “Levene test (cross-check)”.
SecondaryResult.note: The note below the section title as displayed text: why the comparison test is shown next to the main test and what it checks differently.

PowerInfo.goalPct: The power goal in percent as formatted text, a whole number without the percent sign; the box shows it as “Power Goal: 80%”.
PowerInfo.goalBoxClass: Display class of the interface; colours the box green when the current power reaches the goal, otherwise as a warning.
PowerInfo.requiredLine: The line “Required n” as formatted text, “per group” for two samples: the smallest n between 4 and 5000 at which the power reaches the goal; for two samples with equally sized groups. From 5000 on, that is, if the goal is not reached by then, it reads “> 5000”. After it “Achieved” or “Not achieved” for the current power.
PowerInfo.metrics: The figures as formatted texts: current power in percent with one decimal, n (n₁ / n₂ for two samples), the effect size and α. The effect size is the variance ratio s²/σ²₀ or s²₁/s²₂ for variances, Cohen's d = |x̄ − μ₀|/s or |x̄₁ − x̄₂|/sₚ for means, with three decimals.
PowerInfo.note: Note below the power as displayed text: for the Bonett test “Computed assuming normality — approximation only.”, because the power formula assumes normality; empty for every other method.

PairwiseSection.methodName: Procedure of the pairwise comparisons as its English name, label “Method”, always two-sided: for variances the F-test when all are normal, otherwise Levene (Brown-Forsythe); for means the pooled t-test, the Welch t-test when Levene shows a variance difference, on the rank route Mann-Whitney U.
PairwiseSection.methodAlgoId: Identifier of the Algorithm Lab page for the button next to the procedure name.
PairwiseSection.hint: The note below the matrix as formatted text: “Bonferroni-corrected across m = … pairs” with m = k(k − 1)/2, for means extended by the remark that below the corrected p-value stands the confidence interval of the difference μ(row)−μ(column), on the rank route the Hodges-Lehmann interval of the shift.
PairwiseSection.headers: The column headers of the matrix as displayed texts: the group names, that is, the column names from the data collection.
PairwiseSection.rows: The rows of the matrix, one per group.
PairwiseSection.lettersJoined: The grouping letters of all groups in column order as formatted text, joined by commas; the same letters as in the group overview.

PairwiseRow.head: The row header as displayed text: the group name, that is, the column name from the data collection.
PairwiseRow.cells: The cells of the row, one per group; only the upper triangle is filled, the diagonal and the cells below show “—”.

PairwiseCell.cls: Display class of the interface; colours the filled cells as not significant or significant and marks the cells on the diagonal and below as empty.
PairwiseCell.title: Tooltip of the cell as formatted text with the raw p-value, the corrected p-value and the verdict; empty in empty cells.
PairwiseCell.text: The Bonferroni-corrected p-value as formatted text: p · m, at most 1, with m = k(k − 1)/2 pairs. From α upwards the pair counts as not significantly different, below as significant. “—” in empty cells.
PairwiseCell.ci: The confidence interval at level 1 − α/m as formatted text: for means the t interval of the difference μ(row) − μ(column), by Welch for unequal variances, on the rank route the Hodges-Lehmann interval of the shift. Empty for variance tests and in empty cells.
PairwiseCell.key: Identifier of the cell from row and column number, counted from 0; for display only.

hypothesis-test.pairedDiffHint: Difference d = column 1 − column 2, paired by row
hypothesis-test.dataPlaceholder: Values separated by comma, space or newline
hypothesis-test.pairedDropped: {n} pairs; {k} rows without a partner dropped
hypothesis-test.pairedDropped_one: {n} pairs; {k} row without a partner dropped
hypothesis-test.pairedTooFew: Only {n} complete pairs – the paired test needs at least 3.
hypothesis-test.pairedTooFew_one: Only {n} complete pair – the paired test needs at least 3.
hypothesis-test.pairedNoVariation: All differences are equal – without variation no test is possible. Did you pick two different columns?
hypothesis-test.placeholderText: Enter data and run analysis to see results.
hypothesis-test.errMin3: At least 3 data points required for Sample 1.
hypothesis-test.errMin3Sample2: At least 3 data points required for Sample 2.
hypothesis-test.secondaryNote: The data are not normally distributed, but every group has n ≥ 20. The parametric test is then robust and remains the main result. The rank test checks a different hypothesis (a shift of the distribution rather than the means) and serves as a cross-check.
hypothesis-test.ciRatioUndefinedNote: The confidence interval cannot be reported: the confidence set for σ²₁/σ²₂ splits into separate pieces (very unequal sample sizes or kurtoses). The p-value remains valid.
hypothesis-test.secondaryNoteLevene: For two variances Minitab shows Bonett and Levene. Levene is listed as a cross-check; it is two-sided only and gives no confidence interval.
hypothesis-test.testNotComputable: The test cannot be computed for these data (too few values, no spread, or an unbounded confidence interval).
hypothesis-test.varEqual: No significant difference in variances (p ≥ α)
hypothesis-test.tipTestMethod: Test method used — selected automatically based on sample count, normality, and variance equality
hypothesis-test.tipStatistic: Value of the test statistic (e.g. t, χ², F, W) — compared against the critical threshold of its distribution
hypothesis-test.tipPValue: p-value: probability of seeing the observed (or more extreme) data if H₀ were true. p < α → reject H₀
hypothesis-test.tipDf: Degrees of freedom of the test statistic — determine the shape of the reference distribution
hypothesis-test.tipBigN: Total sample size across all groups
hypothesis-test.tipMean1: Arithmetic mean of the first sample
hypothesis-test.tipMean2: Arithmetic mean of the second sample
hypothesis-test.tipMeanDiff: Mean of the pairwise differences d = column 1 − column 2
hypothesis-test.tipAlpha: Significance level α — risk threshold for Type I error
hypothesis-test.tipCohensD: Cohen's d: effect size of the mean difference, standardized by the spread
hypothesis-test.tipCurrentPower: Current power 1 − β: probability of detecting an effect that truly exists
hypothesis-test.tipRequiredN: Sample size required to reach the target power at the current effect size
hypothesis-test.tipVarianceRatio: Ratio of sample variances — effect size for variance tests
hypothesis-test.tipConfidenceInterval: Confidence interval: range that covers the true parameter with (1 − α) probability
hypothesis-test.pairwiseCiHint: below p_adj the CI of the difference μ(row)−μ(column)
hypothesis-test.ciDiffNote: No significant difference – differences μ₁−μ₂ between {lo} and {hi} are consistent with the data. This does not show equality.
hypothesis-test.ciPairedDiffNote: No significant difference – mean differences between {lo} and {hi} are consistent with the data. This does not show equality.
hypothesis-test.tipHlEstimate: Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the location shift: median of all n₁·n₂ pairwise differences x − y
hypothesis-test.ciShiftNote: No significant difference – shifts η₁−η₂ between {lo} and {hi} are consistent with the data. This does not show equality.
hypothesis-test.ciShiftTip: Hodges-Lehmann confidence interval of the location shift. Target {level}%, achieved {achieved}% ({method}).
hypothesis-test.pairwiseShiftCiHint: below p_adj the CI of the shift η(row)−η(column) (Hodges-Lehmann)
hypothesis-test.tipModelS: S: standard deviation of the residuals (square root of MS within); in the units of the data
hypothesis-test.tipR2: R²: share of the total variation explained by the group membership
hypothesis-test.tipR2adj: R² (adj): R² adjusted for the number of groups; negative values are shown as 0 %
hypothesis-test.tipR2pred: R² (pred): how well the model predicts new observations (from PRESS); negative values are shown as 0 %
hypothesis-test.tipGroupCi: Confidence interval of the group mean: from the pooled standard deviation (Fisher) or the group's own standard deviation (Welch)
hypothesis-test.pMethodNormal: normal approximation with tie and continuity correction
hypothesis-test.groupingHint: Samples sharing a letter are not significantly different (Compact Letter Display)

resampling.name: Resampling
resampling.description: Bootstrap confidence intervals and permutation tests for one, two, paired and k samples
resampling.whenToUse: When a statistic of one, two, paired or k samples needs a confidence interval or a test without assuming a distribution: bootstraps the interval (BCa or percentile) and tests by permutation (two samples, paired, k groups) or against a target value (one sample). Each sample needs at least 2 numeric values (10 for Ppk).

read.help: Returns the design (mode, statistic and its parameters, contrast, direction, target), the chosen columns, the run settings (B, seed, confidence, ciMethod), the selectable sets, the run state and the result. result is null until a run has completed; a cancelled or failed run leaves it as it was.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets one parameter. A value outside its range is accepted; validationMsg then names the reason and compute does not run. Changing mode resets a statistic the new mode does not offer to 'mean'.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. The call does not check ranges; a violation appears in validationMsg right away, and compute then does not run.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. For 1 sample it is the sample, for 2 samples one of the two groups, paired “Before (X)” and “After (Y)”.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeColumnSlots: 'colRef1' in every mode except 'k', plus 'colRef2' in modes 'two' and 'paired'.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns, or null to clear the slot.

setColumns.help: The data collection columns that supply this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. The order is the order of the groups, duplicate columns count once, and at least 3 columns are needed to compute.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeMultiSlots; this module only has 'colRefsK', and only in mode 'k'.
params.refs: List of column references { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of columns from pickableColumns; [] clears the selection.

rollSeed.help: Draws a new random seed between 1 and 2147483647.

compute.help: Runs the resampling and returns after the last pass; result holds the new summary. It does not run while a run is in progress or while validationMsg names a reason (invalid parameters, missing or too short columns, fewer than 3 groups in mode 'k', the ratio contrast with values of zero or below); result then stays as it was and no error is raised. A failed run leaves result as it was and names the reason in errorMsg.

cancel.help: Aborts a run in progress; result stays as it was and errorMsg stays empty. Without a run nothing happens.

mode.help: The sample design: 'one' (one sample against a target), 'two' (two groups), 'paired' (before and after pairs) or 'k' (three or more groups).

statisticId.help: The statistic that is resampled; one of statisticOptions.

statParams.help: { trim, p, lsl, usl }: trimming share (statistic 'trimmedMean'), quantile level (statistic 'quantile'), lower and upper specification limit as text (statistic 'ppk'). Only the entries of the chosen statistic count.

contrast.help: How two groups are compared: 'difference' or 'ratio'. Only relevant in mode 'two'; the ratio needs positive values.

direction.help: The alternative of the test: 'two-sided', 'greater' or 'less'. Only relevant in modes 'two' and 'paired'.

target.help: The hypothesised value as text; '' means none. Only relevant in mode 'one'.

colRef1.help: The first sample column { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } (the sample, the first group or the first side of the pairs), or null.

colRef2.help: The second sample column { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } (modes 'two' and 'paired'), or null.

colRefsK.help: The group columns of mode 'k' in order, each { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }.

B.help: Number of resamples or permutations; valid from 1000 to 100000.

seed.help: Random seed, an integer from 0 to 2147483647; the same seed and inputs give the same result.

confidence.help: Confidence level as a fraction between 0 and 1 exclusive, for example 0.95.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state: mode, statisticId, B, seed, confidence and ciMethod always, plus the keys that statistic and mode need.

statisticOptions.help: The statistics the current mode offers: all except 'ppk' in mode 'k', only 'mean', 'median' and 'trimmedMean' in mode 'paired'.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts in the current state: 'colRef1' in mode 'one', 'colRef1' and 'colRef2' in modes 'two' and 'paired', none in mode 'k'.

activeMultiSlots.help: The slots setColumns accepts in the current state: 'colRefsK' in mode 'k', none otherwise.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns it accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'. Only columns of a numeric type with at least 2 values.

running.help: true while a run is in progress.

stale.help: True when a result exists that was computed from inputs other than the current ones; the interface then shows the note “Result outdated”.

validationMsg.help: The reason compute would not run (invalid parameter, missing or too short column, fewer than 3 groups in mode 'k', the ratio contrast with values of zero or below), or an empty string. A running run does not set it.

errorMsg.help: The reason the last run failed, or an empty string; a new run and a cancelled run leave it empty.

result.help: The most recent successfully computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null until the first successful computation.

Params.mode: The design, buttons “1 sample”, “2 samples”, “Paired” and “k samples”: one sample on its own (bootstrap interval, optionally against a target value), two independent samples (bootstrap of the difference and a permutation test), paired values (bootstrap and sign-flip test on the differences d = x − y) or at least three groups (global permutation test with pairwise comparisons after Holm). Switching resets a statistic the new design does not offer to the mean. Any other value is an error right away.
Params.statisticId: The statistic θ, field “Statistic”, computed from each sample: mean, median, standard deviation and variance (both with n − 1), trimmed mean, quantile (type 7 as in R), coefficient of variation s / x̄ and Ppk = min((USL − x̄) / 3s, (x̄ − LSL) / 3s). Paired offers only mean, median and trimmed mean, k samples all except Ppk. A statistic the design does not offer is an error right away. The default is the mean.

statParams.trim: The trim fraction per side, field “Trim fraction per side”, only for the trimmed mean: ⌊n · fraction⌋ values are dropped from each end of the sorted values, as in R. Allowed is 0 up to below 0.5, default 0.1. A value outside this range is accepted; the hint line names the violation right away, and “Compute” stays disabled until it is fixed.
statParams.p: The quantile p, field “Quantile p”, only for the quantile statistic: the share of values below the estimated quantile, computed with type 7 as in R. Allowed is 0 < p < 1, default 0.95. A value outside this range is accepted; the hint line names the violation right away, and “Compute” stays disabled until it is fixed.
statParams.lsl: The lower specification limit, field “Lower spec limit (LSL)”, only for Ppk: text with a number (comma or point), empty means no lower limit. Ppk needs at least one of the two limits, both must be readable, LSL must lie below USL, and each sample needs at least 10 values. On a violation the hint line names it right away, and “Compute” stays disabled until it is fixed.
statParams.usl: The upper specification limit, field “Upper spec limit (USL)”, only for Ppk: text with a number (comma or point), empty means no upper limit. Ppk needs at least one of the two limits, both must be readable, USL must lie above LSL, and each sample needs at least 10 values. On a violation the hint line names it right away, and “Compute” stays disabled until it is fixed.

Params.contrast: The contrast, field “Contrast”, only for two samples: “Difference θ₁ − θ₂” or “Ratio θ₁ / θ₂” of the statistic of both groups; for the ratio the permutation test checks log θ₁ − log θ₂. The ratio needs strictly positive values and a positive statistic in both groups; on a violation the hint line names it right away, and “Compute” stays disabled until it is fixed. The default is the difference; any other value is an error right away.
Params.direction: The alternative hypothesis, field “Alternative hypothesis”, for two samples and paired: “two-sided (≠)” counts assignments with |T| ≥ |T₀|, “greater (>)” those with T ≥ T₀, “less (<)” those with T ≤ T₀. It only affects the p-value of the permutation test, not the bootstrap interval. The default is two-sided; any other value is an error right away.
Params.target: The target value H₀, field “Target value H₀”, only for one sample: text with a number, empty means no test. With a target the column “Decision” shows “Reject H₀” when it lies outside the displayed confidence interval of the chosen interval method, otherwise “Retain H₀”; the interval limits belong to the interval. Unreadable text is accepted; the hint line names the violation right away, and “Compute” stays disabled until it is fixed. The target is not part of the fingerprint; changing it does not make the result outdated.
Params.B: The number of replications B, field “Replications B”: this many bootstrap resamples are drawn, and the permutation test uses this many random assignments when it does not enumerate exactly. An integer from 1000 to 100000, default 10000; more replications smooth the result and take longer. A non-integer is an error right away, an integer outside the range is accepted; the hint line names the violation right away, and “Compute” stays disabled until it is fixed.
Params.seed: The seed of the random number generator, field “Seed”: the same inputs with the same seed give the same result. An integer from 0 to 2147483647, default 42; “Roll a new seed” draws one between 1 and 2147483647. A non-integer is an error right away, a value outside the range is accepted; the hint line names the violation right away, and “Compute” stays disabled until it is fixed.
Params.confidence: The confidence level, field “Confidence level”, as a fraction, for example 0.95 for 95 %: the coverage of the bootstrap intervals; the statement line tests p-values against α = 1 − level. Allowed is 0 < level < 1, default 0.95; the input field of the interface only allows 0.5 to 0.999. A value outside this range is accepted; the hint line names the violation right away, and “Compute” stays disabled until it is fixed.
Params.ciMethod: The interval method, field “Interval method”: “BCa” (bias-corrected and accelerated) or “Percentile”. Both are always computed; the choice only decides which interval the tables, chart and decision show, and it is not part of the fingerprint. The default is BCa; any other value is an error right away.

Result.inputsHash: The fingerprint of the inputs, eight hexadecimal characters (FNV-1a) over design, statistic and its parameters, contrast (two samples only), alternative hypothesis (two samples and paired), B, seed, confidence level and the cleaned data. Target value and interval method are not included. If the fingerprint of the current inputs differs, the result counts as outdated.
Result.mode: The design the result was computed with (1 sample, 2 samples, paired, k samples), as of the start of the computation. It decides which of the parts bootstrap, permutation test and k-sample analysis are filled.
Result.statisticId: The statistic the result was computed with, as of the start of the computation.
Result.contrast: The contrast of the computation, difference or ratio. It is always stored, even when the design does not use it; it only takes effect for two samples.
Result.direction: The alternative hypothesis of the computation, two-sided, greater or less. It is always stored, even when the design does not use it; it only takes effect for two samples and paired.
Result.confidence: The confidence level of the computation as a fraction, for example 0.95.
Result.B: The number of replications of the computation.
Result.seed: The seed of the computation; with it and the same inputs the result can be reproduced exactly.
Result.labels: The names of the sample columns in their order, “?” when a column can no longer be found. For k samples they fill the column “Group”; the column “Pair” of the pairwise comparisons joins two of them.
Result.n: The number of evaluated values per sample, column “n”; text and empty cells are dropped. Paired counts only rows where both sides hold a number, so the same number appears twice.
Result.boot: The bootstrap analysis for one, two and paired samples; empty for k samples.
Result.perm: The permutation test for two samples and paired; empty for one and for k samples.
Result.k: The analysis for k samples: global permutation test, per-group results and pairwise comparisons; empty for the other designs.

Boot.estimate: The estimate θ̂ from the original data, column “Estimate θ̂”: for one sample θ(x), for two samples θ(x) − θ(y) or θ(x) / θ(y) depending on the contrast, paired θ(d) of the differences d = x − y. The chart “Bootstrap distribution” marks it as a line. For k samples the same column shows the pooled statistic.
Boot.se: The bootstrap standard error, column “Standard error”: the standard deviation (with n − 1) of the finite bootstrap replicates. Empty when fewer than 2 finite replicates exist.
Boot.bias: The bias, column “Bias”: mean of the finite replicates minus θ̂. A value near 0 means the statistic hits on average. Empty without a finite replicate or without a finite θ̂.
Boot.ci: Both confidence intervals of the estimate, percentile and BCa. The column “Confidence interval” shows the one of the chosen interval method as lower and upper limit separated by a semicolon, and a dash when it is missing, with the method in parentheses in the header.
Boot.decision: The verdict on the target value, column “Decision”: “reject” when the target lies outside the confidence interval of the chosen interval method (table: “Reject H₀”), “retain” when it lies inside (“Retain H₀”). Only in the one-sample setup with a target value, otherwise the field is empty; the read surface computes it with the interval method and target currently set.
Boot.bins: The chart “Bootstrap distribution”: a histogram of the B bootstrap replicates θ̂* in 30 classes of equal width. Each replicate is the statistic of a sample drawn with replacement from the data. The title inside the chart names what was computed: with two samples the difference (or ratio) between them, paired the statistic of the differences, not the samples themselves. The line θ̂ marks the estimate from the original data, the shaded area the confidence interval of the chosen interval method. The narrower the distribution, the more precisely θ̂ is determined. If the area includes 0 for a difference (1 for a ratio), no difference is established. Single replicates are not stored.

Intervals.percentile: The percentile interval as in R boot.ci “perc”: lower and upper limits are the quantiles (1 − level)/2 and (1 + level)/2 of the replicates, interpolated on the normal scale between neighbouring ordered replicates (at the edge the smallest or largest value applies). Empty with fewer than 2 finite replicates or when all replicates are equal.
Intervals.bca: The BCa interval (bias-corrected and accelerated) as in R boot.ci “bca”: the percentiles are shifted using z₀ from the share of replicates below θ̂ and the acceleration a from jackknife influence values. If BCa cannot be determined, this holds the percentile interval.
Intervals.bcaFallback: True when BCa could not be determined and the percentile interval was used instead: fewer than 2 finite replicates, θ̂ not finite, all replicates on one side of θ̂ (z₀ infinite), a non-finite influence value or a non-finite acceleration, for example when all influence values are 0. With method BCa the note “BCa not available (e.g. replicates without spread) – percentile interval shown.” appears; for groups and pairwise comparisons the fallback applies without a note.

Bin.x0: The lower limit of the class. The 30 classes have equal width and span from the smallest to the largest finite value; if all values are equal there is one class from value − 0.5 to value + 0.5, without finite values none.
Bin.x1: The upper limit of the class; the last class ends exactly at the largest value.
Bin.count: The number of finite values in the class.

Perm.observed: The observed test statistic T₀, column “Observed T”: for two samples the difference θ(x) − θ(y), for the ratio contrast log θ(x) − log θ(y); paired θ(d) of the differences. The chart “Permutation distribution” marks T₀, two-sided also −T₀.
Perm.pValue: The p-value, column “p-value”: the share of assignments whose T is at least as extreme as T₀ in the direction of the alternative hypothesis (two-sided |T| ≥ |T₀|, greater T ≥ T₀, less T ≤ T₀). Exact means p = hits / number of assignments, Monte Carlo p = (1 + hits) / (B + 1). The statement line calls the difference significant when p < α = 1 − confidence level; the table shows values below 0.0001 as “< 0.0001”.
Perm.exact: True when all assignments were enumerated: with at most 20000 possible assignments (two samples N! / (n₁! · n₂!), paired 2ⁿ signs) the module computes exactly and without randomness, otherwise Monte Carlo with B random assignments and p = (1 + hits) / (B + 1). The column “Permutations” shows “exact” or “Monte Carlo” before the number.
Perm.permutations: The number of evaluated assignments, column “Permutations”: exactly the number of all assignments (at most 20000), otherwise B; for Monte Carlo p = (1 + hits) / (B + 1), so p never becomes 0. For two samples the pooled values are redistributed across the groups, paired the signs of the differences are flipped.
Perm.bins: The chart “Permutation distribution”: a histogram of the test statistic T* in 30 classes of equal width. For each T* the values are reassigned to the groups at random (paired: the signs of the differences are flipped at random) and the statistic is compared again; for a ratio T = ln θ(x) − ln θ(y). The histogram thus shows which values of T arise by chance alone when the null hypothesis holds. The red line marks the observed T, for a two-sided test also −T. The share of replicates at least as extreme is the p-value: if T lies far out in the distribution, the difference is significant.

KResult.estimate: The statistic θ of all values together (pooled); in the design k samples the column “Estimate θ̂” of the result table.
KResult.observed: The observed test statistic T₀ = Σ nᵢ · (θᵢ − θ)², column “Observed T”: how far the group statistics θᵢ, weighted by their size nᵢ, spread around the pooled statistic θ.
KResult.pValue: The p-value of the global test, column “p-value”: one-sided, the share of assignments with T ≥ T₀; exact p = hits / number of assignments, Monte Carlo p = (1 + hits) / (B + 1). Below α = 1 − confidence level at least one group differs.
KResult.exact: True when all assignments of the pooled values to the groups were enumerated (N! / Π nᵢ! at most 20000); otherwise Monte Carlo with B assignments.
KResult.permutations: The number of evaluated assignments of the global test, column “Permutations”: all of them when exact (at most 20000), otherwise B.
KResult.bins: The chart “Permutation distribution”: a histogram of the global test statistic T* = Σ nᵢ (θ̂ᵢ − θ̂)² in 30 classes of equal width. For each T* all values are reassigned to the k groups at random. The histogram thus shows which values of T arise by chance alone when all groups are equal. The red line marks the observed T; the share of replicates to its right is the p-value. If T lies far out to the right, at least two groups differ.
KResult.groups: The result per group in the order of the columns, table “Groups”.
KResult.posthoc: The pairwise comparisons of all k · (k − 1) / 2 group pairs, table “Pairwise comparisons (Holm)”.

KGroup.estimate: The statistic θ of the group, column “Estimate θ̂” of the group table.
KGroup.ci: Both bootstrap confidence intervals of the group from B resamples, percentile and BCa; the column “Confidence interval” shows the one of the chosen interval method.

PostHoc.i: The position of the first group of the pair in the column list, counted from 0. The column “Pair” shows both group names separated by a dash.
PostHoc.j: The position of the second group of the pair, counted from 0, always greater than that of the first.
PostHoc.contrast: The difference θᵢ − θⱼ of the two group statistics; the column “Estimate θ̂” of the pairwise comparisons shows it. Pairwise comparisons always use the difference.
PostHoc.ci: Both bootstrap confidence intervals of the difference, percentile and BCa; the column “Confidence interval” shows the one of the chosen interval method. If it contains 0, no difference is shown.
PostHoc.pRaw: The unadjusted p-value of the pair, column “p raw”: two-sided permutation test of just these two groups, exact with at most 20000 assignments, otherwise Monte Carlo.
PostHoc.pHolm: The Holm-adjusted p-value, column “p Holm”, as R p.adjust “holm”: the m raw p-values sorted ascending, the r-th multiplied by (m − r + 1), made monotone and capped at 1. This keeps the risk of a false alarm across all pairs together at α.
PostHoc.exact: True when the test of the pair enumerated all assignments (at most 20000), otherwise Monte Carlo; the column “p-value method” shows “exact” or “Monte Carlo”.

sample-size.name: Sample Size
sample-size.description: Calculate the required sample size for variance and mean tests
sample-size.whenToUse: When you need to know how many observations a test requires: computes the required sample size for variance tests (chi-square, F) and mean tests (one- and two-sample t) from the effect to detect, the significance level and the target power.

read.help: Returns the ten inputs, the keys valid in the current state and the result. result is null while the inputs are incomplete or not positive numbers.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets one input; the calculation reruns.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. sigma0, sigmaAlt, ratio, delta, sigma as text containing a number; '' clears the value.

runAnalysis.help: Calculates the required sample size from the current inputs. While the inputs are incomplete or not positive numbers result stays null.

category.help: Which kind of test the sample size is for: 'variance' or 'mean'.

alpha.help: The significance level as a number; null until it is taken from the settings.

power.help: The target power (1 − β) as a number; null until it is taken from the settings.

sigma0.help: Hypothesized standard deviation σ₀ as entered; applies to variance with one sample.

sigmaAlt.help: Expected standard deviation σ₁ as entered; applies to variance with one sample.

ratio.help: Variance ratio σ²₁/σ²₂ as entered; applies to variance with two samples.

delta.help: Mean difference Δ to detect, as entered; applies to mean tests.

sigma.help: Standard deviation σ, as entered; applies to mean tests.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state.

result.help: The required sample size, each figure described individually under keys; null while an effect input is missing or not positive.

Params.category: The test category, buttons “σ² Variances” and “μ Means”: variances (variance) plan a test on the spread, means (mean) a t-test on the location. The choice decides which effect inputs apply.
Params.testType: The test type, buttons “1-Sample” and “2-Sample”: one compares one sample with a target value, two compares two equally sized groups with each other. With two samples the computed size is per group.
Params.direction: The direction, field “Direction”: “Two-sided” detects a deviation in either direction, “Greater” and “Less” only one in that direction. A one-sided test needs fewer observations only when it points in the direction of the effect. For means Δ always counts as a positive, upward deviation; “Less” therefore never reaches the target power and ends at the upper limit of 5000. For variances the direction must match the effect: “Greater” when σ₁ is above σ₀ or the ratio above 1, “Less” when below; otherwise the search also ends at 5000.
Params.alpha: The significance level α, the accepted probability of reporting an effect that does not exist; a number from 0.0001 to 0.5. Prefilled from the confidence in the settings (95% gives 0.05). A smaller α requires more observations.
Params.power: The target power 1 − β, label “Target Power (1 − β)”: the probability of actually detecting an existing effect of the given size; a number from 0.5 to 0.9999, prefilled from the settings (typically 0.8). Higher power requires more observations.
Params.sigma0: The hypothesized standard deviation σ₀, label “Hypothesized Std. (σ₀)”: the spread assumed by the hypothesis H₀ under test, as text containing a positive number. Only for variances with one sample; the effect is the ratio σ₁² / σ₀².
Params.sigmaAlt: The expected standard deviation σ₁, label “Expected Std. (σ₁)”: the spread whose deviation from σ₀ the test should detect, as text containing a positive number. Only for variances with one sample; the closer σ₁ is to σ₀, the more observations are needed.
Params.ratio: The variance ratio σ²₁ / σ²₂, label “Variance Ratio (σ²₁ / σ²₂)”: the factor by which the variances of the two groups should differ, as text containing a positive number. Only for variances with two samples; a ratio close to 1 requires very many observations.
Params.delta: The mean difference Δ to detect, label “Difference (Δ)”, as text containing a positive number in the unit of the measurements: with one sample the distance to the target, with two the distance between the group means. Only for means; together with σ it gives the effect size Cohen's d = Δ / σ.
Params.sigma: The standard deviation σ of the measurements, label “Std. Dev. (σ)”, as text containing a positive number; with two samples it applies to both groups. Only for means; a larger σ makes the same difference harder to detect.

Result.nRequired: The required sample size n, tile “Required n” (with two samples “per group”): the smallest n from 4 on at which the power reaches the target power. The search runs up to 5000. If the target power is reached only at 5000 or not at all, this is 5000 and the tile shows “> 5,000” (German “> 5.000”) instead of the number; the summary above the tiles names the same value. The effect is then hardly detectable.
Result.totalN: The total size, tile “Total n”: with two samples n per group times two, with one sample equal to n. The tile appears only with two samples; from an n of 5000 on it shows “> 10,000” (German “> 10.000”).
Result.alpha: The significance level α used in the calculation, tile “α”; equal to the input.
Result.power: The target power 1 − β used in the calculation, as a fraction; the tile “Target Power” shows it as a percentage rounded to whole numbers. The size n reaches at least this power unless it sits at the upper limit of 5000, where the search ends.
Result.effectLabel: The name of the effect size as the tile shows it: “Variance Ratio” for variance tests, “Cohen's d” for mean tests.
Result.effectValue: The effect size the test should detect; the tile shows it with three decimals. Variances, one sample: σ₁² / σ₀². Variances, two samples: the entered ratio σ²₁ / σ²₂. Means: Cohen's d = Δ / σ.
Result.algoId: The procedure whose power was calculated; the interface uses it to link the Algorithm Lab. chi-square-variance: χ² test of one variance with n − 1 degrees of freedom. f-test: F-test of two variances with n − 1 degrees of freedom each. one-sample-t-test: t-test with noncentrality Δ · √n / σ and n − 1 degrees of freedom. two-sample-t-test: t-test with noncentrality Δ / (σ · √(2/n)) and 2n − 2 degrees of freedom.

sample-size.placeholderText: Enter parameters on the left and run the calculation.
sample-size.resultSummary: With n = {n}, a power of {power}% is achieved at α = {alpha}.
sample-size.nOverflow: The required sample size reaches or exceeds 5,000 — the effect is very difficult to detect with these parameters.
sample-size.errRatio: Please enter a valid variance ratio > 0.
sample-size.errSigma0: Please enter a valid hypothesized standard deviation > 0.
sample-size.errSigmaAlt: Please enter a valid expected standard deviation > 0.
sample-size.errSigma: Please enter a valid standard deviation > 0.

data-import.whenToUse: When data from a third-party source is to be brought into a data collection; for an agent from CSV or JSON text, with profiles for common measuring-machine exports.

read.help: Returns the source imported last, the parser options, the keys valid in the current format, the sheets with their columns and the state of the parse. Parsed data is not stored: after a reload sheets is empty until imported again. Read the values themselves from the worksheet after sendToWorksheet.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

importText.help: Reads CSV or JSON text like a file and fills sheets. Returns the number of sheets, or null when the parse failed; the reason is then in errorMsg. An empty text is a parse failure, not a rejection.

params.text: The content as text; CSV is always read as UTF-8.
params.format: One of the formats in textFormats, csv or json; any other value is an error.

setParam.help: Sets a parser option and reads the data again with it. Values outside the range are rejected, not clamped.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

selectSheet.help: Chooses the sheet of the file whose columns are sent to the worksheet; the chosen one is highlighted.

params.index: The number of the sheet in sheets, from 0; any other number is an error.

sendToWorksheet.help: Sends the columns of the chosen sheet to a new worksheet. If there is no data or no columns, nothing is sent. The agent receives the new worksheet; without data or columns it receives none.

file.help: The source imported last, each item described individually under keys; null before anything is imported.

csvOptions.help: The CSV options; each is described under setParam as the key csvOptions.<name>.

xlsxOptions.help: The XLSX options; each is described under setParam as the key xlsxOptions.<name>.

aqdefOptions.help: The AQDEF options; each is described under setParam as the key aqdefOptions.<name>.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current format; empty without a source.

sheets.help: The parsed sheets with name, row count and columns (name, type); empty without data.

activeSheetIdx.help: The number of the sheet sendToWorksheet sends.

errorMsg.help: The message of the last parse failure, null without failure.

csvOptions.preset: The export profile, a set of defaults for the CSV export of a measuring software. Generic leaves everything at the defaults (automatic delimiter, UTF-8, column header row, no skipped rows). Zeiss CALYPSO uses semicolon, Windows-1252 and skips 4 rows, Hexagon PC-DMIS comma, UTF-8 and 4 rows, Mitutoyo MeasurLink comma, UTF-8 and no rows; all three read the first remaining row as header. A profile sets delimiter, encoding, skipped rows and column header row at once; the individual options can still be changed afterwards.
csvOptions.delimiter: The character that separates the columns: automatic (detected from the content), comma, semicolon, tab or pipe.
csvOptions.encoding: The encoding of the file: UTF-8, Windows-1252 (Excel) or Latin-1 (ISO-8859-1); it decides whether umlauts appear correctly. It does not apply to pasted text, which is already characters; the field is hidden then.
csvOptions.hasHeader: Whether the first row (after the skipped ones) holds the column headers. Without column headers it counts as data, and the columns are named C1, C2 and so on.
csvOptions.skipRows: Skip header rows: how many rows at the start of the file are discarded before reading; a whole number of at least 0. Meant for metadata that some measuring machines write above the table.

xlsxOptions.hasHeader: Whether the first row of each sheet holds the column headers. Without column headers it counts as data, and the columns are named C1, C2 and so on.

aqdefOptions.encoding: The encoding of the Q-DAS file. The default is Windows-1252 because Q-DAS files in the DACH region are mostly saved that way; Latin-1 (ISO-8859-1) and UTF-8 are also available.

ImportFile.name: The file name; for pasted text, the name of the text input.
ImportFile.size: The size as the file card shows it: bytes as a whole number with B, kilobytes with one decimal and KB, megabytes with two decimals and MB.
ImportFile.formatId: The detected format as the file card names it, for example Text file (CSV / TSV / TXT); missing if the format was not recognised.
ImportFile.source: Where the source comes from: a chosen or dropped file, or pasted text.

data-import.name: Data Import
data-import.description: Read data from third-party formats (Minitab .mpx, CSV/TSV/TXT, Excel/ODS, JSON/NDJSON, Q-DAS AQDEF) into a worksheet
data-import.dropHint: or click to choose a file
data-import.supportedFormats: Supported formats: Minitab Project (.mpx), CSV / TSV / TXT, Excel (.xlsx/.xlsm/.xls) / ODS, JSON / NDJSON, Q-DAS AQDEF (.dfq/.dfd)
