random-generator.whenToUse: When random data from a known distribution or from weighted categories is needed — for practice, simulations or test data — reproducible through the seed.

read.help: Returns the distribution, its parameters, sample size and seed, the categories, the selectable sets and a summary of the generated values. generated is null while there are no values; read the values themselves from the worksheet after toWorksheet.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

selectDistribution.help: Chooses the distribution and generates values at once with the sample size and seed that apply to it.

params.key: One of the distributions in distributions, attributive included; any other value is an error.

setDistParam.help: Sets one parameter of the chosen distribution; the formula above the fields shows where it enters, the allowed range is given below the field. Values outside the range are rejected, not clamped. The values are generated again at once.

params.id: One of the parameters in activeDistParams, for example mu or sigma. Which apply depends on the distribution.
params.value: A number within min to max from activeDistParams; numbers given as text are accepted.

setParam.help: Sets the sample size or the seed and generates again at once. Values outside the range are rejected, not clamped.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

addAttribute.help: Adds an attribute (a category) to the attributive distribution, with an empty name and weight 1, and generates again. Categories without a name are skipped when generating. The agent receives the id of the category.

removeAttribute.help: Removes a category of the attributive distribution and generates again.

params.attrId: The id of a category from attributes; any other id is an error.

setAttribute.help: Sets the name or the weight of a category of the attributive distribution and generates again. Categories with an empty name or a weight of 0 or less are skipped when generating.

params.attrId: The id of a category from attributes, or the one addAttribute returned.
params.key: Which field; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

generate.help: Generates the values with the current inputs. Without a chosen distribution nothing happens; a failure of the distribution is reported in errorMsg, not as a rejection.

toWorksheet.help: Sends the generated values to a new worksheet, into an existing empty column or as a new column to an existing sheet. If there are no values, nothing is sent. The agent receives the receiving worksheet; without values it receives none.

params.target: null for a new worksheet, otherwise a column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from targetColumns; columnId '__new__' appends a new column to the sheet.

currentDist.help: The chosen distribution, one of the keys in distributions, or null.

distributions.help: All distributions selectDistribution accepts, attributive included.

params.help: The parameters of the chosen continuous or discrete distribution as numbers, by id.

activeDistParams.help: The parameters setDistParam accepts in the chosen distribution, each with id, bounds (null without a bound) and default.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state; empty without a chosen distribution.

count.help: Sample size of a continuous or discrete distribution.

seed.help: Random seed of a continuous or discrete distribution.

attributes.help: The categories of the attributive distribution, each with id, name and weight.

attrCount.help: Sample size of the attributive distribution.

attrSeed.help: Random seed of the attributive distribution.

generated.help: Summary of the generated values, each item described individually under keys; null while no values are generated. The cards show the statistics with four decimals, magnitudes from 10⁶ or below 0.001 in exponential notation.

targetColumns.help: The targets toWorksheet accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'. Per sheet with an empty column it lists its empty columns followed by an entry with columnId '__new__' (name is the sheet name) that appends a new column. A null target creates a new worksheet.

errorMsg.help: The message when the distribution could not produce values, otherwise empty.

Params.count: Count (n): the sample size for a continuous or discrete distribution, a whole number from 1 to 100,000. A change generates the values again at once.
Params.seed: Seed: the starting value of the random generator for a continuous or discrete distribution. The same seed gives the same values, so the sample is reproducible. Any whole number except 0 is allowed, because 0 would silently count as 42. A change generates the values again at once.
Params.attrCount: Count (n): the sample size for the attributive distribution, a whole number from 1 to 100,000. A change generates the values again at once.
Params.attrSeed: Seed: the starting value of the random generator for the attributive distribution. The same seed gives the same values, so the sample is reproducible. Any whole number except 0 is allowed, because 0 would silently count as 42. A change generates the values again at once.

AttributeFields.name: Attribute: the name of the category. It may be empty; categories without a name are skipped when generating.
AttributeFields.weight: Weight of the category, a number from 0. The share of a category is its weight divided by the sum of all weights; the column "Share" shows it in percent. A category with weight 0 is skipped when generating.

Generated.n: n: the number of generated values, equal to the set count (n).
Generated.mean: Mean x̄ = Σx / n, the sum of the generated values divided by their count. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.sd: Std.Dev. s = √(Σ(x − x̄)² / (n − 1)), the sample spread of the generated values with denominator n − 1. Not defined for a single drawn value: the result is then empty. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.median: Median: the middle of the generated values sorted ascending, for an even count the mean of the two middle ones. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.min: Min: the smallest of the generated values. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.max: Max: the largest of the generated values. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.skewness: Skewness g₁ = m₃ / m₂^1.5 with the central moments m₂ = Σ(x − x̄)² / n and m₃ = Σ(x − x̄)³ / n (denominator n, not corrected). Positive: the long tail is on the right, negative: on the left; 0 for symmetric values. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.kurtosis: Kurtosis as excess: m₄ / m₂² − 3 with m₂ = Σ(x − x̄)² / n and m₄ = Σ(x − x̄)⁴ / n (denominator n, not corrected). 0 matches the normal distribution, positive means more peaked with heavy tails, negative flatter. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.frequency: The frequency per category, sorted descending by count; each entry gives name and count. The card "Categories" counts the entries, the card "Most frequent" names the first one. Only for the attributive distribution.

normal.mu: Mean (μ): the location of the distribution, around which the values scatter. Allowed: any number; default 0.
normal.sigma: Std. Dev. (σ): the scale, the spread of the values around the location. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.
normal.epsilon: Skewness (ε): the asymmetry: 0 gives symmetric values, positive values make the distribution right-skewed (long right tail), negative values left-skewed. Allowed: any number; default 0.
normal.delta: Tailweight (δ): how heavy the tails are: 1 gives the normal distribution, values below 1 make the tails heavier, values above 1 lighter. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 1.

chisquare.k: Degrees of freedom (k): they set the shape of the chi-square distribution; the larger, the more symmetric. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 5.

f_dist.d1: Degrees of freedom d₁: the number of degrees of freedom in the numerator of the F distribution. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 5.
f_dist.d2: Degrees of freedom d₂: the number of degrees of freedom in the denominator of the F distribution. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.

t_dist.nu: Degrees of freedom (ν): they set the shape of the t distribution; the larger, the closer it is to the normal distribution. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.

uniform.a: Lower bound (a): the lower bound, below which no values occur. Allowed: any number; default 0.
uniform.b: Upper bound (b): the upper bound, above which no values occur; it should exceed the lower bound, otherwise the values lie reversed between b and a. Allowed: any number; default 1.

beta.alpha: Shape α: the first shape of the beta distribution; together with β it decides whether the values between 0 and 1 lie more to the left or to the right. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 2.
beta.beta: Shape β: the second shape of the beta distribution; together with α it decides whether the values between 0 and 1 lie more to the left or to the right. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 5.

cauchy.x0: Location (x₀): the location, the center of the Cauchy distribution (its median). Allowed: any number; default 0.
cauchy.gamma: Scale (γ): the scale, the width of the Cauchy distribution. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

exponential.lambda: Rate (λ): the rate: how many events occur per unit; the mean of the values is 1/λ. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

gamma_dist.alpha: Shape (α): the shape of the gamma distribution; 1 gives the exponential distribution, larger values make it more symmetric. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 2.
gamma_dist.beta: Scale (β): the scale of the gamma distribution, by which all values are stretched. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

laplace.mu: Location (μ): the location, the center of the Laplace distribution. Allowed: any number; default 0.
laplace.b: Scale (b): the scale, the width of the Laplace distribution. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

gumbel_max.mu: Location (μ): the location of the Gumbel distribution for maxima (its mode). Allowed: any number; default 0.
gumbel_max.beta: Scale (β): the scale, the width of the Gumbel distribution for maxima. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

logistic.mu: Location (μ): the location, the center of the logistic distribution. Allowed: any number; default 0.
logistic.s: Scale (s): the scale, the width of the logistic distribution. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

loglogistic.alpha: Scale (α): the scale of the log-logistic distribution, which is also its median. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.
loglogistic.beta: Shape (β): the shape of the log-logistic distribution; the larger, the more tightly the values lie around the scale. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

lognormal.mu: Log-Mean (μ): the mean of the logarithms of the values (not of the values themselves). Allowed: any number; default 0.
lognormal.sigma: Log-Std.Dev. (σ): the standard deviation of the logarithms of the values (not of the values themselves). Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

gumbel_min.mu: Location (μ): the location of the Gumbel distribution for minima (its mode). Allowed: any number; default 0.
gumbel_min.beta: Scale (β): the scale, the width of the Gumbel distribution for minima. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

triangular.a: Minimum (a): the minimum, the smallest possible value. Allowed: any number; default 0.
triangular.c: Mode (c): the mode, the most frequent value; it should lie between the minimum and the maximum. Allowed: any number; default 0.5.
triangular.b: Maximum (b): the maximum, the largest possible value; it should exceed the minimum. Allowed: any number; default 1.

weibull.alpha: Shape (α): the shape of the Weibull distribution; 1 gives the exponential distribution, above 1 the failure rate rises over time. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.5.
weibull.beta: Scale (β): the scale of the Weibull distribution (characteristic life: 63.2 % of the values lie below it). Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

bernoulli.p: Success prob. (p): the probability that a trial succeeds and yields 1; otherwise 0 results. Allowed: number from 0 to 1; default 0.5.

binomial.n: Trials (n): how often the trial is repeated for each generated value; the value counts the successes. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.
binomial.p: Success prob. (p): the probability that a single trial succeeds. Allowed: number from 0 to 1; default 0.5.

geometric.p: Success prob. (p): the probability that a single trial succeeds; the value counts the failures before the first success. Allowed: number from 0.0001 to 1; default 0.3.

negbinomial.r: Successes (r): how many successes are waited for; the value counts the failures up to then. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 5.
negbinomial.p: Success prob. (p): the probability that a single trial succeeds. Allowed: number from 0.0001 to 1; default 0.5.

hypergeometric.N: Population size (N): the number of all elements drawn from without replacement. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 100.
hypergeometric.K: Success states (K): how many of the N elements are successes; it should be at most as large as N. Allowed: number from 0, whole numbers are usual; default 30.
hypergeometric.n: Sample size (n): how many elements are drawn for each generated value; it should be at most as large as N, and the value counts the successes among them. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.

integer.a: Minimum (a): the smallest whole number that can occur; it should not be larger than the maximum. Allowed: any number, decimals are rounded down; default 1.
integer.b: Maximum (b): the largest whole number that can occur; it should not be smaller than the minimum. Allowed: any number, decimals are rounded down; default 6.

poisson.lambda: Rate (λ): the mean number of events per unit; it is both the mean and the variance of the values. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 5.

mvnormal.mu1: Mean μ₁: the location of the first component of the two-dimensional normal distribution; it determines the generated values. Allowed: any number; default 0.
mvnormal.mu2: Mean μ₂: the location of the second component; the generated column holds only the first component, so μ₂ does not currently change it. Allowed: any number; default 0.
mvnormal.sigma1: Std.Dev. σ₁: the spread of the first component around its mean μ₁. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.
mvnormal.sigma2: Std.Dev. σ₂: the spread of the second component around its mean μ₂; the generated column holds only the first component, so σ₂ does not currently change it. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.
mvnormal.rho: Correlation ρ: how strongly the two components are related (-1 opposite, 0 independent, 1 in step); the generated column holds only the first component, so ρ does not currently change it. Allowed: number from -0.999 to 0.999; default 0.5.

FrequencyRow.name: The name of the category.
FrequencyRow.count: How often the category occurs among the generated values.
FrequencyRow.share: The share of the category among all generated values, as a number from 0 to 1 (count divided by the number of values); the display shows it as a percentage.

random-generator.errGenerate: The values could not be generated: {message}
random-generator.name: Random Generator
random-generator.description: Generate reproducible samples from statistical distributions
random-generator.selectDistribution: Select a distribution on the left to get started.

model-data-generator.whenToUse: When synthetic data from a known regression model is needed — to practise DOE analysis and regression, or to test methods against a known “true” model — with factors, coefficients, noise and a seed for reproducible results.

read.help: Returns the factors and terms with their indices, the intercept, the response name, the sampling method, sample size, noise, seed and a summary of the generated values. generated is null until data exists; read the rows themselves from the worksheet after toWorksheet.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

addFactor.help: Appends a factor with a default name and the range 0 to 100. The terms are rebuilt and all coefficients reset to 0, and a generated result is discarded. The agent receives the index of the new factor.

removeFactor.help: Removes a factor. The terms are rebuilt and all coefficients reset to 0, and a generated result is discarded. The last factor stays: the action then returns false and changes nothing.

params.index: The index of a factor from factors; any other value is an error.

setFactor.help: Sets the name or a range limit of a factor; a generated result is discarded. The coefficients are kept. Invalid values are rejected.

params.index: The index of a factor from factors; any other value is an error.
params.key: Which field; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and permitted range are given per key under keys.

setBeta.help: Sets the coefficient of a term. An already generated result stays until the next generate and keeps the old values until then.

params.index: The index of a term from terms; any other value is an error.
params.value: A finite number; numbers given as text are accepted.

setIntercept.help: Sets the intercept β₀ of the model equation. An already generated result stays until the next generate.

params.value: A finite number; numbers given as text are accepted.

setYName.help: Sets the name of the response Y; it appears in the equation, the table and the export. It must not be empty and must not name a factor, since the Y column would otherwise overwrite a factor column. An already generated result stays until the next generate.

params.value: The name as text, not empty and not a factor name.

setSamplingMethod.help: Chooses the sampling method: random (Monte Carlo), Latin Hypercube (LHS) or full factorial. Takes effect on the next generate.

params.value: One of the methods in samplingMethods; any other value is an error.

setSampleSize.help: Sets the number of rows. With the full factorial method the number of levels is fixed (3 levels up to 4 factors, otherwise 2); the number only sets how often each level combination is repeated (n divided by the number of combinations, rounded, at least 1), so the row count usually differs from it. Takes effect on the next generate. Values outside the range are rejected, not clamped.

params.value: An integer from 10 to 100000; numbers given as text are accepted.

setNoiseStd.help: Sets the standard deviation σε of the normally distributed noise added to the modelled Y value. 0 produces values without noise. Takes effect on the next generate.

params.value: A number from 0; numbers given as text are accepted.

setSeed.help: Sets the seed, the starting value of the random generator. The same seed with the same settings gives the same data. Takes effect on the next generate.

params.value: An integer; numbers given as text are accepted.

generate.help: Generates the data with the current settings and shows it in the preview. The agent receives the summary of the Y values, the same as generated; it reads the rows from the worksheet after toWorksheet.

toWorksheet.help: Opens the generated data in a new worksheet and switches to it. If no data exists yet, it generates first. The agent receives the id of the new worksheet.

factors.help: The factors, each with index, name, min and max. The index addresses the factor in setFactor and removeFactor.

terms.help: All terms of the model — main effects and interactions — each with index, label, order and beta, zeros included. The index addresses the term in setBeta. The list changes with the number of factors.

intercept.help: The intercept β₀ of the model equation.

yName.help: Name of the response Y, also the column name of the generated data.

samplingMethod.help: The chosen sampling method, one of the methods in samplingMethods.

sampleSize.help: The requested number of rows; with the full factorial method only a guide for the repetitions per level combination.

noiseStd.help: Standard deviation σε of the noise added to the modelled Y value.

seed.help: Seed, the starting value of the random generator; the same seed gives the same data.

maxOrder.help: The upper limit of the interaction order among the terms; with fewer factors the terms stop at the factor count. It is fixed and cannot be changed.

generated.help: Summary of the generated Y values, each item described individually under keys; null until data exists. It is computed on generate. addFactor, removeFactor and setFactor discard it. The other setters — setBeta, setIntercept, setYName, setSamplingMethod, setSampleSize, setNoiseStd, setSeed — leave it in place until the next generate. The cards show the figures with four decimals, magnitudes from 10⁶ or below 0.001 in exponential notation.

FactorFields.name: Name of the factor, also the column name of the data. It must not be empty and must not equal another factor or the response Y.
FactorFields.min: Lower limit of the factor range, a number. It must not exceed the upper limit.
FactorFields.max: Upper limit of the factor range, a number. It must not be below the lower limit.

Generated.n: N: the number of generated rows.
Generated.mean: Mean of the generated Y values.
Generated.sd: Standard deviation of the generated Y values.
Generated.min: Min: the smallest generated Y value.
Generated.max: Max: the largest generated Y value.

model-data-generator.name: Model Data Generator
model-data-generator.description: Generate synthetic datasets from configurable regression models
model-data-generator.factorsDesc: Define the input variables of your process. Each factor is normalized to [0, 1] for the model equation.
model-data-generator.outputDesc: Give your response variable Y a descriptive name — it will be used in the equation, table, and export.
model-data-generator.interactionDesc: Up to which order should interactions be included?
model-data-generator.modelDesc: Y = β₀ + Σ βᵢ·xᵢ + Σ βᵢⱼ·xᵢ·xⱼ + … + ε  (factors normalized to [0, 1])
model-data-generator.generateDesc: Configure sampling method, size, noise, and seed.

distribution-fit.name: Distribution Fit
distribution-fit.description: Fit data to multiple distributions and rank by Goodness-of-Fit test
distribution-fit.whenToUse: When it is unclear which distribution describes a measured characteristic: fits normal, lognormal, Weibull, exponential and further distributions to one numeric column and ranks them by goodness of fit; requires at least 5 values.

read.help: Returns the chosen column, the data type, the selectable sets and the result. result is null while no analysis exists; errorMsg is empty without a column and otherwise names the reason.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets the data type; the analysis reruns on the chosen column.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeColumnSlots; this module only has 'value'.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns, or null to clear.

runAnalysis.help: Computes with the chosen column. Without a column result stays null and errorMsg stays empty; with fewer than 5 values result stays null and errorMsg names the reason.

columnRef.help: The chosen data column as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }, or null.

dataType.help: How the data is treated: 'auto', 'continuous' or 'discrete'.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts in the current state.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'.

result.help: The ranking of fitted distributions with statistics and normality tests, each figure described individually under keys; null without a column, with fewer than 5 values or without spread.

errorMsg.help: The reason no result exists (too few values, zero variance), or an empty string.

Params.dataType: How the column is treated, label Data Type: Auto, Continuous or Discrete, default Auto. Continuous fits only the continuous distributions (Normal, Log-Normal, Weibull, Exponential, Gamma), Discrete only Poisson and Binomial. Auto takes both families when all values are integers, otherwise only the continuous ones. A change recomputes.

Result.stats: The statistics of the data from the Descriptive Statistics section: count, location, spread and shape, computed on all numeric values of the column.
Result.results: The fitted distributions, sorted descending by the p-value of their goodness-of-fit test; the # column shows the rank, rank 1 carries the BEST FIT tag next to its name. The data type decides which distributions are fitted; a distribution with too few suitable values is missing from the list.
Result.normalityTests: The four normality tests Shapiro-Wilk, Anderson-Darling, Jarque-Bera and D'Agostino-Pearson on the same values, shown in the Normality Deep-Dive; a test that cannot be computed is missing. The overall verdict counts only computed tests and treats p ≥ 0.1 as passed and p < 0.05 as rejected.
Result._dataType: The data type this computation ran with, Auto, Continuous or Discrete; a copy of the setting at the time of the computation.

DescStats.n: Number of values, tile n: all numeric cells of the column; empty and non-numeric cells do not count.
DescStats.mean: Arithmetic mean x̄ = Σx/n, tile Mean. The tiles show four decimals, in exponential format with four decimals from 1,000,000 up or below 0.0001 (except 0); a non-finite value appears as a dash.
DescStats.stdDev: Sample standard deviation s = √(Σ(x − x̄)²/(n − 1)), tile Std Dev.
DescStats.median: The middle value of the sorted data, for an even count the mean of the two middle ones; tile Median.
DescStats.skewness: Adjusted sample skewness n/((n − 1)(n − 2)) · Σ((x − x̄)/s)³, tile Skewness: 0 for symmetric data, positive with a long right tail, negative with a long left tail.
DescStats.kurtosis: Excess kurtosis by the sample formula n(n + 1)/((n − 1)(n − 2)(n − 3)) · Σ((x − x̄)/s)⁴ − 3(n − 1)²/((n − 2)(n − 3)), tile Excess Kurtosis. The normal distribution has 0; positive means heavier tails, negative lighter ones.
DescStats.min: The smallest value of the column, tile Min.
DescStats.max: The largest value of the column, tile Max.

Fit.name: The name of the distribution, column Distribution: Normal, Log-Normal, Weibull, Exponential, Gamma, Poisson or Binomial; next to it the tag continuous or discrete.
Fit.type: The family of the distribution: cont for continuous, disc for discrete; the interface shows it as the tag continuous or discrete next to the name. Continuous ones are assessed with the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, discrete ones with the χ² goodness-of-fit test.
Fit.params: The estimated parameters, each as symbol and value; the Parameters column shows them as symbol=value. Normal: μ = x̄ and σ = s of all values. Log-Normal: μ_log and σ_log, mean and standard deviation of the ln values. Exponential: λ = 1/x̄. Gamma: α = x̄²/s² and β = x̄/s² (method of moments). Weibull: shape k from the maximum-likelihood equation (Newton's method, start 1.2) and scale λ = (Σxᵏ/n)^(1/k). Log-Normal, Exponential, Gamma and Weibull use only the positive values and need at least 3 of them, Weibull at least 5. Poisson: λ = x̄; Binomial: n = largest value, p = x̄/n; both use only the non-negative integer values and need at least 3, Binomial additionally a largest value above 0. If the values do not suffice, the distribution is missing. The goodness-of-fit test, by contrast, runs on all values of the column.
Fit.ks: The Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, for continuous distributions only; for discrete ones it is missing and the χ² goodness-of-fit test takes its place. The Test column shows K-S or χ² respectively.
Fit.chi2: The χ² goodness-of-fit test, for discrete distributions only (Poisson, Binomial); for continuous ones it is missing and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test takes its place. The Test column shows χ² for it.
Fit.score: The p-value of the goodness-of-fit test, for continuous distributions that of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, for discrete ones that of the χ² test; the ranking is sorted by it. The p-Value column shows it with four decimals (below 0.0001 as 0.0000), the Fit Quality column as a bar that is full from p = 0.2, with the verdict Good at p ≥ 0.1, Borderline at 0.05 ≤ p < 0.1 and Poor below. A large p-value only means that no deviation can be detected, not that the distribution is proven to fit.

KsTest.D: The Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic D: the largest vertical distance between the empirical distribution function of the values and the fitted distribution function, from 0 to 1; smaller is better. The Statistic column shows D for continuous distributions and the χ² value of the goodness-of-fit test for discrete ones.
KsTest.p: The p-value from the Kolmogorov distribution, approximated with z = (√n + 0.12 + 0.11/√n) · D (Stephens) and clamped to 0 to 1. The parameters come from the same data and the computation does not correct for that (no Lilliefors correction); the p-value therefore tends to be too large.

ChiSquareTest.chi2: The χ² statistic Σ(O − E)²/E over the classes k = 0 to largest value + 5 (one class per whole number), with observed frequency O and expected frequency E = n · P(k); classes with E < 1 are dropped. The Statistic column shows it for discrete distributions.
ChiSquareTest.df: The degrees of freedom: number of classes with E ≥ 1 minus 2, at least 1. A class is each whole-number value k from 0 up to the largest value + 5.
ChiSquareTest.p: The p-value 1 − F(χ²) of the χ² distribution with df degrees of freedom, clamped to 0 to 1.

NormalityTest.name: The name of the test as the Normality Deep-Dive card shows it: Shapiro-Wilk, Anderson-Darling, Jarque-Bera or D'Agostino-Pearson.
NormalityTest.p: The p-value of the test against the null hypothesis of normality; empty when the test has too few values. The card's verdict is Passed at p ≥ 0.1, Borderline at 0.05 ≤ p < 0.1 and Rejected below.
NormalityTest.W: The Shapiro-Wilk statistic W (algorithm AS R94), only in the Shapiro-Wilk entry; values close to 1 indicate normality.
NormalityTest.A2: The Anderson-Darling statistic A², unadjusted, only in the Anderson-Darling entry. The p-value uses the adjusted A² · (1 + 0.75/n + 2.25/n²) after D'Agostino and Stephens.
NormalityTest.JB: The Jarque-Bera statistic n/6 · (S² + K²/4) from moment skewness S and excess K, p-value from χ² with 2 degrees of freedom; only in the Jarque-Bera entry and only from 8 values on, empty below.
NormalityTest.K2: The D'Agostino-Pearson statistic K², the sum of the squared z-values of skewness and kurtosis, p-value e^(−K²/2) from χ² with 2 degrees of freedom; only in the D'Agostino-Pearson entry and only from 20 values on, empty below.
NormalityTest.skewness: The skewness as the test computes it; only for Jarque-Bera and D'Agostino-Pearson and only when the test was computed.
NormalityTest.exKurtosis: The excess kurtosis as the test computes it (normal distribution 0); only for Jarque-Bera and D'Agostino-Pearson and only when the test was computed.
NormalityTest.skewZ: The z-value of skewness after D'Agostino (1970), only for D'Agostino-Pearson from 20 values on. With fewer than 20 values the field is present but empty.
NormalityTest.kurtZ: The z-value of kurtosis after Anscombe and Glynn (1983), only for D'Agostino-Pearson from 20 values on. With fewer than 20 values the field is present but empty.
NormalityTest.tooSmall: True when the test had too few values and was not computed: Jarque-Bera below 8, D'Agostino-Pearson below 20 values; the card then shows a notice instead of a verdict. Otherwise the entry is missing.

distribution-fit.noWorksheet: Add a Worksheet module first to provide data.
distribution-fit.noNumericColumns: No numeric columns found in any worksheet.
distribution-fit.placeholderText: Select a data column and run the analysis to see results.
distribution-fit.exampleHint: Showing results for built-in example data (n = {n}). Select a worksheet column for your own data.
distribution-fit.errMin5: At least 5 data points are required.
distribution-fit.errGeneric: An error occurred during the analysis.
distribution-fit.interpGood: Data is consistent with this distribution (p ≥ 0.10). Do not reject.
distribution-fit.interpModerate: Borderline case (0.05 ≤ p < 0.10). Use with caution.
distribution-fit.interpPoor: Distribution does not fit the data well (p < 0.05). Reject.
distribution-fit.nddConfirmedText: All four tests pass at α = 0.05. The data is consistent with a normal distribution. Six Sigma tools like Cpk, control charts, and t-tests may be used without restriction.
distribution-fit.nddBorderlineText: No test clearly rejects H₀, but at least one p-value is borderline. Normality is plausible but not conclusive. Larger sample or supplementary tests recommended.
distribution-fit.nddMixedText: The tests disagree. Some reject normality, others do not. Check for outliers, sample size issues, or consider Box-Cox transformation.
distribution-fit.nddRejectedText: The majority of tests reject H₀. The data is not normally distributed. Consider alternatives: Log-Normal, Weibull, or non-parametric methods.
distribution-fit.nddSWDesc: Gold standard with highest statistical power. Compares order statistics with theoretical normal values.
distribution-fit.nddADDesc: Especially sensitive in the distribution tails. Weights deviations at the extremes more heavily.
distribution-fit.nddJBDesc: Asymptotic test based on skewness and kurtosis (χ² with 2 df). Reliable for large samples (n > 30).
distribution-fit.nddDPDesc: Omnibus test: combines skewness and kurtosis Z-scores. Shows why normality fails.
distribution-fit.nddTooSmall: Sample size too small for this test.
distribution-fit.nddTooSmallJB: n < 8 — Jarque-Bera requires at least 8 data points.
distribution-fit.nddTooSmallDP: n < 20 — D'Agostino-Pearson requires at least 20 data points.

outlier-test.name: Outlier Test
outlier-test.description: Run classical outlier tests (Grubbs, Dixon Q, Generalized ESD, Tukey IQR, Hampel, Z-Score) in parallel on a column
outlier-test.whenToUse: When a measured characteristic may contain outliers: tests one numeric column with up to seven methods (Grubbs, Dixon Q, generalized ESD, Tukey IQR, Hampel, Z-score, modified Z-score) and reports which values each method flags; requires at least 3 numeric values.

read.help: Returns the chosen column, the parameters, the selectable sets and the result. result is null while no column is chosen or it has fewer than 3 numeric values; errorMsg only names why drawing the chart failed.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets one parameter; the analysis reruns on the chosen column.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. For esdMaxOutliers null means automatic; enabled is a list of method ids.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. Empty and non-numeric cells are skipped; with fewer than 3 numbers the evaluation stays empty.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeColumnSlots; this module only has 'value'.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns, or null to clear.

runAnalysis.help: Runs all enabled methods on the chosen column. Without a column or with fewer than 3 numeric values result stays null and nothing else happens.

setChartMethod.help: Chooses which method the chart highlights; “Union of all methods” highlights every value any method flagged. Only methods that flagged something in the current result can be chosen.

params.method: One of the values in chartMethodOptions. A method that flagged nothing in the current result is an error.

colRef.help: The chosen data column as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }, or null.

alpha.help: Significance level of Grubbs, Dixon Q and generalized ESD.

side.help: Which tail Grubbs and Dixon Q test: 'two-sided', 'upper' or 'lower'.

tukeyFactor.help: Fence multiplier of the Tukey IQR rule.

hampelK.help: Threshold of the Hampel identifier in scaled MAD units.

esdMaxOutliers.help: Upper limit of outliers for generalized ESD; null chooses it automatically.

enabled.help: The methods that are run, in the fixed order of the module.

chartMethod.help: The method the chart highlights: 'all' or one of chartMethodOptions. It falls back to 'all' when the method no longer flags a value after a rerun.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts in the current state.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'.

chartMethodOptions.help: The values setChartMethod accepts: 'all' plus every method that flagged at least one value in the current result.

result.help: The flagged points per method, each figure described individually under keys; null without a column or with fewer than 3 numbers.

errorMsg.help: Why drawing the chart failed, or an empty string. Too few values give no message; result is null then.

Params.alpha: The significance level α of Grubbs, Dixon Q and generalized ESD; the other four methods do not use it. A smaller α requires a clearer outlier before it is flagged. Allowed are 0.0001 to 0.5; Dixon Q reads its critical values from a table for 0.10, 0.05 and 0.01 and interpolates in between, outside that range the nearest table value applies.
Params.side: The test side of Grubbs and Dixon Q: “Two-sided” tests the most extreme value in either direction, “Upper outlier only” only the largest, “Lower outlier only” only the smallest value. Grubbs uses the t quantile at α/(2n) two-sided and at α/n one-sided. Generalized ESD always tests two-sided, the other methods have no direction.
Params.tukeyFactor: The factor k of the Tukey IQR rule: every value outside the fences Q1 − k·IQR and Q3 + k·IQR is flagged, with IQR = Q3 − Q1. 1.5 marks potential, 3.0 extreme outliers. Allowed are 0.1 to 10.
Params.hampelK: The threshold k of the Hampel identifier: a value is flagged when |x − median| / (1.4826·MAD) > k; 1.4826·MAD estimates σ under normality. Default is 3, allowed are 0.1 to 20.
Params.zThreshold: The threshold of the Z-score rule: a value is flagged when |x − x̄| / s > threshold, i.e. when it lies more than that many standard deviations from the mean. Typical is 3; on small samples outliers mask each other because they shift x̄ and s themselves. Allowed are 0.1 to 10.
Params.modZThreshold: The threshold of the modified Z-score after Iglewicz and Hoaglin: a value is flagged when |0.6745·(x − median) / MAD| > threshold. Median and MAD are robust against the outliers themselves. Typical is 3.5, allowed are 0.1 to 10.
Params.esdMaxOutliers: The maximum number k of outliers generalized ESD checks, a whole number from 1 to 50. Empty means automatic: ⌊n/4⌋, at least 1 and at most 10. The method removes, step by step, the value with the largest Rᵢ = |x − x̄| / s of the remaining data and compares it with the critical value λᵢ; outliers are the values up to the last step with Rᵢ > λᵢ. The steps stop early when fewer than 3 values are left or the remaining data have no spread (s = 0); then there are fewer than k steps.
Params.enabled: The methods that run, in fixed order: Grubbs' Test (G = max|x − x̄| / s above the critical value, at most one outlier), Dixon Q Test (gap ratio Q above the table value, at most one outlier, only for 3 to 30 values), Generalized ESD (up to k outliers), Tukey IQR Rule (outside the fences), Hampel Identifier (robust distance to the median above k), Z-Score (distance to x̄ in units of s above the threshold) and Modified Z-Score (robust z value above the threshold). Duplicate entries count once.

Result.n: The number of values used from the column; empty and non-numeric cells are skipped. The evaluation is missing while no column is chosen or it has fewer than 3 numbers.
Result.flaggedIdxs: The positions flagged by at least one method, ascending and counted from 0 over the values used. The tile “Flagged (any test)” shows how many there are. The table “Flagged Points” counts from 1 in column “#”, i.e. position plus 1; column “Σ” shows how many methods flagged the point.
Result.methods: One entry per enabled method, in the order of the method list, including methods that are not applicable to the data. The tile “Active methods”, by contrast, counts only the methods that ran without error.

MethodResult.id: The method identifier: grubbs, dixon-q, generalized-esd, tukey-iqr, hampel, z-score or modified-z.
MethodResult.flagged: The positions this method flagged, counted from 0 over the values used; Grubbs and Dixon Q flag at most one value. Empty when nothing stands out or the method is not applicable; without spread (MAD = 0 for Hampel and modified Z-score, s = 0 for Z-score) the method runs without error and flags nothing. The table “Flagged Points” appears only when at least one method flagged something; it has one column with a check mark for each method that ran without error.
MethodResult.error: Empty when the method ran; otherwise the reason it is not applicable: min4 fewer than 4 values (generalized ESD, Tukey IQR rule), zeroVariance no spread (Grubbs: s = 0, Dixon Q: range 0), dixonRange Dixon Q only for 3 to 30 values. Fewer than 3 values do not occur here, because then the analysis does not run at all. The interface shows “Method not applicable” with the text belonging to this code.
MethodResult.metrics: The method's key figures, the same numbers as on its card under “Methods”; which keys are present depends on the method. The field is empty when the method is not applicable.
MethodResult.steps: The steps of generalized ESD in the order of the table on its card. For all other methods the field is empty.

MethodMetrics.statistic: The test statistic, shown as “G” for Grubbs and “Q” for Dixon Q on the card: for Grubbs the largest distance of a value from the mean in standard deviations, for Dixon Q the gap ratio (distance to the neighbor divided by the range). A value above the critical value flags the extreme value.
MethodMetrics.critical: The critical value for the test statistic, shown as “Gₜ” for Grubbs and “Qₜ” for Dixon Q; it depends on the number of values, α and the test side. If the statistic is above it, the extreme value counts as an outlier.
MethodMetrics.pValue: The p-value of the Grubbs test. It exists for Grubbs only and belongs to the statistic G; if it is below α the extreme value is flagged and the tile turns red, otherwise green.
MethodMetrics.mean: The mean x̄ of all values used; the basis of the distance for Grubbs and the Z-score. Outliers shift it themselves.
MethodMetrics.sd: The standard deviation s of all values used; it measures the distance for Grubbs and the Z-score. For the Z-score, 0 means all values are equal and nothing is flagged.
MethodMetrics.detected: The number of outliers generalized ESD found: the steps up to the last one in which Rᵢ is above λᵢ. Above 0 the tile turns red, at 0 green.
MethodMetrics.maxOutliers: The maximum number of outliers generalized ESD tested, that is, its number of steps. Without a setting it is ⌊n/4⌋, at least 1 and at most 10.
MethodMetrics.q1: The first quartile Q1 of the Tukey IQR rule: a quarter of the values lie below it.
MethodMetrics.median: The median: the middle value of the sorted data. Tukey, Hampel and modified Z-score use it as a robust center that outliers hardly shift.
MethodMetrics.q3: The third quartile Q3 of the Tukey IQR rule: a quarter of the values lie above it.
MethodMetrics.iqr: The interquartile range IQR = Q3 − Q1 of the Tukey IQR rule; it sets how far the fences lie from the quartiles.
MethodMetrics.fenceLower: The lower fence of the Tukey IQR rule, Q1 − k·IQR with the factor k as set. Values below it are flagged.
MethodMetrics.fenceUpper: The upper fence of the Tukey IQR rule, Q3 + k·IQR with the factor k as set. Values above it are flagged.
MethodMetrics.mad: The MAD, the median of the absolute deviations from the median, a robust measure of spread for Hampel and modified Z-score. If it is 0 the method runs without error and flags nothing.
MethodMetrics.madScaled: The MAD multiplied by 1.4826 (card “1.4826·MAD”); for normal data this estimates the standard deviation. The Hampel identifier measures the distance to the median in this unit.
MethodMetrics.k: The threshold k of the Hampel identifier, as set: a value is flagged if its distance from the median is more than k scaled MADs.
MethodMetrics.threshold: The threshold of the method, as set. For the Hampel identifier it is the distance from the median above which a value is flagged (k times scaled MAD); for the Z-score and the modified Z-score it is the threshold on the z value.

EsdStep.i: The step number from 1. Each step tests the most conspicuous value of the remaining data and then removes it.
EsdStep.value: The value tested in this step: the one farthest from the mean of the remaining data.
EsdStep.R: The statistic Rᵢ of this step: the distance of the value from the mean of the remaining data in standard deviations.
EsdStep.lambda: The critical value λᵢ of this step. If Rᵢ is above it, the value counts as an outlier; the row is then marked with a cross.

outlier-test.tipTukeyFactor: Factor for Q1 − k·IQR / Q3 + k·IQR. 1.5 marks 'potential', 3.0 'extreme' outliers.
outlier-test.tipHampelK: Threshold in MAD units (1.4826·MAD ≈ σ under normality). Default k = 3.
outlier-test.tipZThreshold: Threshold in standard deviations — typically 3. Distorted by masking on small samples.
outlier-test.tipEsdMax: Maximum number of outliers ESD will check. Leave blank for auto: ⌊n/4⌋, capped at 10.
outlier-test.err_dixonRange: The Dixon test only applies to 3 to 30 values.
outlier-test.hintDegenerateMad: MAD = 0 (more than half the values are identical). Method yields no result.
outlier-test.hintDegenerateSd: Standard deviation = 0 (all values identical). Method yields no result.
outlier-test.placeholderText: Pick a numeric column — outlier tests are computed automatically.

contour-plot.name: Contour Plot
contour-plot.description: Visualize response surfaces z = f(x, y) as contour diagrams
contour-plot.title: Contour Plot
contour-plot.emptyText: Configure model and axes — diagram is drawn automatically
contour-plot.coeffLabel: Coefficients: β₀ + β₁x + β₂y + β₃x² + β₄y² + β₅xy
contour-plot.formulaHint: Variables: x, y · operators: + − * / ^ ** · functions e.g. sin, cos, exp, sqrt, log, ln, min, max, pow · Math. prefix optional, angles in radians.
contour-plot.formulaErrVar: Unknown variable '{name}' — only x and y are allowed.
contour-plot.whenToUse: Draw the response surface of a two-factor model as contour lines — from polynomial coefficients or an own formula in x and y — optionally with measured points.

read.help: Read the model, coefficients or formula, axis ranges, labels, data columns and the formula error, and the min, max and optimum of the surface.

setColumn.help: Assign a data column to a slot. The other slots keep their columns. With all three set, measured points are shown.

params.slot: 'x' — the first factor; 'y' — the second factor; 'z' — the measured response.
params.ref: A column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from read().pickableColumns of that slot, or null to clear the slot.

setParam.help: Set an option of the response surface. read().activeParams names the options valid right now.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

setCoefficient.help: Set one of the six polynomial coefficients b0…b5. Not available while modelType is 'custom'.

params.index: Which coefficient, a whole number from 0 to 5.
params.value: The coefficient, a finite number.

modelType.help: The model form: quadratic, interaction or custom.

b.help: The six coefficients β₀…β₅ of the model, without effect with a custom formula; the fields run from β₀ to β₅.

customFormula.help: The own formula in x and y, used with modelType custom.

xLabel.help: The label of the x factor.

yLabel.help: The label of the y factor.

xMin.help: Lower end of the x range.

xMax.help: Upper end of the x range.

yMin.help: Lower end of the y range.

yMax.help: Upper end of the y range.

colRefX.help: The column of the X values (slot x), optional: measured points over the surface once all three slots are chosen. Empty while none is chosen.

colRefY.help: The column of the Y values (slot y), optional: measured points over the surface once all three slots are chosen. Empty while none is chosen.

colRefZ.help: The column of the measured response (slot z), optional: measured points over the surface once all three slots are chosen. Empty while none is chosen.

formulaError.help: The rejection of the custom formula, each entry described individually under keys; null while the formula is valid or no custom formula is in use.

activeParams.help: The options setParam accepts in the current state.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts: x, y, z.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; the key is instanceId|sheetId|columnId.

surface.help: The evaluated surface over the axis range, each figure described individually under keys; null if the model cannot be evaluated.

Params.modelType: The form of the response surface. Quadratic and "Linear + interaction" both compute z = β₀ + β₁·x + β₂·y + β₃·x² + β₄·y² + β₅·x·y with all six coefficients; the only difference is the name of the choice. With "Custom formula" the formula in x and y applies instead of the coefficients.
Params.customFormula: The own formula for z in the variables x and y. Allowed are numbers, the operators + − * / ^ and **, parentheses, constants such as PI and E, and functions such as sin, cos, tan, exp, sqrt, abs, log (base 10), ln (natural), min, max and pow; a Math. prefix is optional, angles are in radians. An invalid formula is accepted and reported below the formula. The field exists only with a custom formula.
Params.xLabel: The name of the X factor; it appears on the axis and in the hint at the pointer. In the interface it is set in the chart editor.
Params.yLabel: The name of the Y factor; it appears on the axis and in the hint at the pointer. In the interface it is set in the chart editor.
Params.zLabel: The name of the response (Z); it appears in the chart title and in the hint at the pointer.
Params.xMin: The lower end of the X axis. The surface is drawn and sampled over the range from X min to X max. It is not checked that X min is smaller than X max.
Params.xMax: The upper end of the X axis. The surface is drawn and sampled over the range from X min to X max. It is not checked that X max is greater than X min.
Params.yMin: The lower end of the Y axis. The surface is drawn and sampled over the range from Y min to Y max. It is not checked that Y min is smaller than Y max.
Params.yMax: The upper end of the Y axis. The surface is drawn and sampled over the range from Y min to Y max. It is not checked that Y max is greater than Y min.

Surface.zMin: The smallest value of the surface. The surface is evaluated on a grid of 100 × 100 points (default; adjustable in the chart editor under "Grid resolution") over the axis range; the "Z Min" card shows the value.
Surface.zMax: The largest value of the surface on the same grid; the "Z Max" card shows the value.
Surface.range: The range of the surface, largest minus smallest value (Z max − Z min); the card shows it as Z range and below it the number of contour levels.
Surface.optimum: The highest point of the grid. The "Optimum (Max)" card shows its value and below it its x and y; with equally high points the first in grid order counts.

SurfacePoint.x: The X value of the point on the grid.
SurfacePoint.y: The Y value of the point on the grid.
SurfacePoint.z: The value of the surface at this point.

FormulaError.code: The kind of error: illegal character, invalid number, empty formula, syntax error, surplus characters at the end, unknown variable (only x and y are allowed) or unknown function. The interface shows the translated text for it below the formula.
FormulaError.token: The offending character, the invalid number, or the unknown variable or function; it appears in the text below the formula. With an empty formula, a syntax error and surplus characters it is missing.

control-chart.name: Control Chart
control-chart.description: SPC control charts for process stability
control-chart.baselineHint: Empty = use all values as baseline
control-chart.stagesHint: Number of the last point of each stage — each stage gets its own limits and is judged by them. Empty = single baseline.
control-chart.stagesSplitSubgroup: Boundary {stages} lies inside a subgroup of {n} — that subgroup is counted in the earlier stage. Use multiples of {n}.
control-chart.phase2Hint: Phase II locks the current limits and checks new data against them. Only available without stages.
control-chart.phase2_needsData: Load data first, then freeze the limits.
control-chart.phase2_noStages: Not available in stage mode — clear stages or thaw first.
control-chart.phase2_columnChanged: Different column selected — frozen limits discarded, Phase I recomputes.
control-chart.annotationExcludeHint: Excluded points stay on the chart but no longer influence UCL/LCL. Does not apply with multiple stages or frozen limits.
control-chart.specHint: For Cp/Cpk calculation. Shown as lines on the chart.
control-chart.secondaryRulesHint: On the MR, R and S chart only tests 1–4 apply; tests 5–8 check the individuals or X̄ chart only.
control-chart.noViolations: No rule violations — process is stable.
control-chart.whenToUse: Monitor a process over time with Shewhart limits: I-MR for single values, X̄-R or X̄-S for subgroups, with Nelson rules, stages, annotations and frozen Phase II limits.

read.help: Read all inputs, the limits per subchart, capability, rule violations and per point the values and limits.

setColumn.help: The data collection column with the measurements; after a change the analysis is recomputed. Frozen limits of a different column are discarded; the answer says whether that happened.

params.slot: 'value' — the measured values in time order (required, at least 2).
params.ref: A column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from read().pickableColumns.value, or null to clear it.

setParam.help: Set an analysis option and recompute.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. For baselineCount, usl and lsl, null or '' clears the field.

setAnnotation.help: Annotates a point with a comment or excludes it from the limit computation; the analysis is then recomputed. Without a comment and without exclusion the annotation is removed.

params.index: The 0-based point of the first subchart (the subgroup for X̄ charts); it must exist in the current result.
params.excluded: true leaves the point out of the limit calculation.

setPhase2.help: Freezes the current limits for Phase II monitoring or releases them again. Without a result or with stages nothing is frozen; the answer says whether frozen limits apply afterwards.

runAnalysis.help: Recompute with the current column values, for example after the data changed.

subgroupSize.help: Values per subgroup: 1 for I-MR, 2 to 10 for X̄-R, 2 to 25 for X̄-S.

baselineCount.help: Points used to compute the limits, or null for all.

stagesText.help: The stage boundaries as entered (last point of each stage), '' for none.

annotations.help: One annotation per point index, each entry described individually under keys; an excluded point is left out of the limits.

frozenLimits.help: The limits frozen for Phase II, or null; each entry described individually under keys.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts: value.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts for the current chart type.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; the key is instanceId|sheetId|columnId.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null without a column or with fewer than 2 numbers.

points.help: One row per plotted point (subgroup for X̄ charts): per subchart id its value and limits (i, iCl, iUcl, iLcl, mr, …) and signal. read({ fields: ['points'] }) returns them in full.

Params.chartTypeId: Control chart type: I-MR for individual values (individuals chart and moving range chart), X̄-R for subgroups (mean and range chart) or X̄-S for subgroups (mean and standard deviation chart). Switching keeps the subgroup size within the range of the new type; I-MR always computes with n = 1.
Params.subgroupSize: Subgroup size (n): the number of consecutive values that form one subgroup, a whole number from 2 to 10 for X̄-R and from 2 to 25 for X̄-S. Not available for I-MR. Leftover values at the end that do not fill a subgroup are ignored.
Params.baselineCount: Baseline count: how many individual values from the start of the series the limits are computed from, a whole number of at least 1; empty means all values. For X̄ charts it is rounded up to whole subgroups. Excluded points within it do not enter the limits; the baseline does not get longer because of them. When frozen limits apply, the value takes effect only after unfreezing. With stages it is not used; each stage then computes from all of its values. The input field starts at 2, the check accepts any whole number from 1.
Params.stagesText: Stage boundaries: the number of the last individual value of each stage, separated by comma, semicolon or space, e.g. 12, 25. Only whole numbers greater than 0 and less than the number of values count. Each stage gets its own limits and is judged by them. If a boundary falls inside a subgroup, that subgroup is counted in the earlier stage and a hint appears. Empty means a single baseline; with stages no limits can be frozen for Phase II.
Params.usl: USL: upper specification limit of the individual values, empty for none. It is shown as a line on the chart and enters Cp, Cpu and Cpk.
Params.lsl: LSL: lower specification limit of the individual values, empty for none. It is shown as a line on the chart and enters Cp, Cpl and Cpk.
Params.enabledRules: The checked Nelson Rules, numbers 1 to 8: 1 one point beyond 3σ; 2 nine points on the same side of the center line; 3 six points increasing or decreasing; 4 fourteen points alternating up and down; 5 two of three points beyond 2σ on the same side; 6 four of five points beyond 1σ on the same side; 7 fifteen points within 1σ; 8 eight points beyond 1σ on both sides. Only rule 1 is preset, because every further rule raises the false alarm rate. The individuals or X̄ chart is checked; on the MR, R or S chart only rules 1 to 4 apply.

Result.chartType: The control chart type used: I-MR, X̄-R or X̄-S. It determines the subcharts: i and mr, xbar and r, or xbar and s.
Result.subgroupSize: The subgroup size (n) used; 1 for I-MR.
Result.n: Number of points of the first subchart: for I-MR the usable numbers of the column (empty and non-numeric cells are dropped), for X̄ charts the number of subgroups.
Result.baselineEnd: How many individual values, not subgroups, the baseline covers: the baseline count, or all values when it is empty or stages are set.
Result.stages: The stage boundaries used, as numbers of the last individual value of each stage, ascending and without duplicates; boundaries outside the series are dropped. Empty without stages.
Result.frozen: True when frozen Phase II limits apply: chart type, subgroup size and column must match the time of freezing, and no stages may be set. The points are then judged against these limits instead of recomputed ones.
Result.subcharts: The limits per subchart of the chart type: i and mr for I-MR, xbar and r for X̄-R, xbar and s for X̄-S. With stages they hold the limits of the last stage, i.e. the process as it runs now.
Result.capability: Process capability against USL and LSL, computed from the center line CL and σ̂ of the first subchart, converted to individual values for X̄ charts; with stages from the last stage, with frozen limits from the frozen values. Empty when no specification limit is set or σ = 0. Which figures exist depends on which limits are set.
Result.violations: The rule violations of the first subchart (individuals or X̄ chart) under the checked Nelson Rules, once per point and rule, sorted by point. The check of the second subchart only shows in the chart's badge.
Result.signals: The points of the first subchart with at least one rule violation, each only once, counted from 0 over the plotted points (subgroups for X̄ charts). The violations tile counts these points.

SubchartLimits.cl: CL (Center Line) of the subchart: the mean of the baseline points without excluded points, i.e. x̄ on the individuals chart, x̄̄ on the X̄ chart and MR̄, R̄ or S̄ on the dispersion chart. When frozen limits apply (Phase II), CL, UCL, LCL and σ̂ are the values computed at freezing, not those of the current baseline. The CL tile shows the center line of the first subchart, its sub-line σ̂; with several stages the values of the last stage.
SubchartLimits.ucl: UCL, upper control limit of the subchart. I-MR: x̄ + 3 · MR̄/1.128, MR chart 3.267 · MR̄. X̄-R: x̄̄ + A₂ · R̄, R chart D₄ · R̄. X̄-S: x̄̄ + A₃ · S̄, S chart B₄ · S̄. The constants depend on n. With frozen limits the value computed at freezing applies. The UCL / LCL tile shows the UCL of the first subchart with the LCL below.
SubchartLimits.lcl: LCL, lower control limit of the subchart. I-MR: x̄ − 3 · MR̄/1.128, MR chart 0. X̄-R: x̄̄ − A₂ · R̄, R chart D₃ · R̄. X̄-S: x̄̄ − A₃ · S̄, S chart B₃ · S̄. The constants depend on n; D₃ and B₃ are 0 for small n. With frozen limits the value computed at freezing applies.
SubchartLimits.sigma: σ̂, the estimated spread of the points of this subchart, one third of the distance from the center line to the UCL. Individuals chart MR̄/1.128; X̄ chart R̄/(d₂ · √n) or S̄/(c₄ · √n); dispersion chart (UCL − CL)/3. The zones of the Nelson Rules (1σ, 2σ, 3σ) refer to it. With frozen limits the value computed at freezing applies.

Capability.cp: Cp = (USL − LSL)/(6σ): how often the spread fits into the tolerance, regardless of location. Only with both specification limits; the Cpk tile shows Cp in its sub-line.
Capability.cpu: Cpu = (USL − x̄)/(3σ): distance of the mean to the upper specification limit in units of three σ. Only with a USL.
Capability.cpl: Cpl = (x̄ − LSL)/(3σ): distance of the mean to the lower specification limit in units of three σ. Only with an LSL.
Capability.cpk: Cpk, the smaller of Cpu and Cpl, with only one limit its value. σ is MR̄/1.128 for I-MR and σ of the means · √n for X̄ charts; x̄ is the center line of the first subchart, with stages of the last stage; with frozen limits x̄ and σ come from the frozen values. The tile is green (capable) from 1.33, yellow (conditionally capable) from 1.0, red below.

Violation.index: The violating point of the first subchart, counted from 0 over the plotted points: for I-MR the usable numbers without empty cells, for X̄ charts the subgroups.
Violation.ruleId: The number of the violated Nelson rule, 1 to 8, in the same numbering as the Nelson Rules selection.

Annotation.comment: Comment / cause for the point, e.g. a tool break on shift 3; empty for none. The point is marked on the chart.
Annotation.excluded: Exclude point from limit computation: the point stays visible on the chart but no longer influences UCL and LCL. The analysis is then recomputed. Does not apply with multiple stages or when frozen limits are in effect.

FrozenLimits.chartTypeId: The control chart type at the time of freezing. The frozen limits only apply while the same type is selected.
FrozenLimits.subgroupSize: The subgroup size (n) at the time of freezing. The frozen limits only apply with the same subgroup size.
FrozenLimits.columnRef: The measurement column at the time of freezing. If a different column is chosen, the frozen limits are discarded.
FrozenLimits.baselineEnd: How many individual values the baseline covered at the time of freezing.
FrozenLimits.primary: The frozen limits of the first subchart (individuals or X̄ chart): center line, UCL, LCL and σ̂, unchanged from the computation at the time of freezing.
FrozenLimits.secondary: The frozen limits of the second subchart (MR, R or S chart): center line, UCL, LCL and σ̂, unchanged from the computation at the time of freezing.
FrozenLimits.excludedIndices: The points that were excluded from the limit computation at the time of freezing, counted from 0.

time-weighted-chart.name: Control Chart (Time-Weighted)
time-weighted-chart.description: EWMA and CUSUM for small persistent shifts
time-weighted-chart.typeHint_ewma: Smooths the series and detects small persistent drifts.
time-weighted-chart.typeHint_cusum: Accumulates deviations from target — very sensitive to 1σ shifts.
time-weighted-chart.baselineHint: Number of points used to estimate target and σ (empty = all).
time-weighted-chart.sigmaMethodHint: MR̄/d₂ is more robust against outliers in the baseline.
time-weighted-chart.paramNote_ewma: Rule of thumb: λ = 0.10 with L = 2.7 for 1σ shifts; λ = 0.20 with L = 3 as a balanced default.
time-weighted-chart.paramNote_cusum: Rule of thumb: to detect a Δ·σ shift, choose k = Δ/2; h = 4 or 5.
time-weighted-chart.whenToUse: Detect small, persistent shifts earlier than a Shewhart chart: EWMA weights recent values, CUSUM accumulates deviations from the target.
