setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: 'value' — the measured values in time order (required, at least 3).
params.ref: A column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from read().pickableColumns.value, or null to clear it.

setParam.help: Set an analysis option and recompute.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. For baselineCount, targetOverride and sigmaOverride, null or '' clears the field.

runAnalysis.help: Recompute with the current column values, for example after the data changed.

sigmaMethod.help: σ estimator from Phase I: 'mr' (average moving range) or 'sd' (standard deviation).

baselineCount.help: Phase I length (the first n values), or null for all values.

targetOverride.help: Target used instead of the Phase I mean, or null.

sigmaOverride.help: σ used instead of the estimate when greater than 0, or null.

hSigma.help: CUSUM decision interval h in σ.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts: value.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts for the current chart type.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; the key is instanceId|sheetId|columnId.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null without a column, with fewer than 3 numbers or without spread.

points.help: One row per value — EWMA { ewma, ucl, lcl, signal }, CUSUM { cPlus, cMinus, signalHigh, signalLow }. read({ fields: ['points'] }) returns them in full.

Params.chartTypeId: The chart procedure: ewma (exponentially weighted moving average) smooths the series and detects small persistent shifts; cusum (cumulative sums, tabular) accumulates deviations from the target and is very sensitive to shifts of about 1σ. The procedure decides which parameters exist: λ and L only for EWMA, k and h only for CUSUM. After a change the analysis is recomputed.
Params.sigmaMethod: How σ is estimated from the baseline as long as no spread σ > 0 is given: mr is MR̄ / d₂ (average moving range divided by 1.128, robust against outliers), sd the sample SD with n − 1 in the denominator. The module starts with mr. If a spread σ > 0 is given, the choice has no effect.
Params.baselineCount: How many of the first used values form the baseline (Phase I) from which target (mean) and σ are estimated, unless they are given. Empty (shown as “all”) means all values; a number larger than the number of values acts like all. Whole numbers from 1 are allowed, the input field only allows 2 and up. With a single value σ cannot be estimated: there is then no result unless σ is given.
Params.targetOverride: The target μ₀ the chart refers to, instead of the baseline mean. Any number is allowed; empty (shown as “auto”) means the baseline mean. For EWMA it is the start value z₀ and the center line, for CUSUM the value from which deviations are accumulated. After a change the analysis is recomputed.
Params.sigmaOverride: The given spread σ of the individual values instead of the estimate from the baseline; a number from 0. Only a value greater than 0 is used: 0 acts like empty (shown as “auto”), and σ is then estimated from the baseline. A given spread makes the choice of the σ estimation method irrelevant.
Params.lambda: EWMA only: the weight λ (smoothing) of the newest value, zᵢ = λ·xᵢ + (1 − λ)·zᵢ₋₁ with z₀ = target μ₀. Greater than 0 and at most 1; the input field allows 0.05 to 1. A smaller λ smooths more and detects small shifts earlier; λ = 1 gives an individuals chart without smoothing. Preset 0.2. CUSUM has no such field.
Params.L: EWMA only: the limit width L in multiples of σ. At point i the limits are target ± L·σ·√(λ/(2 − λ)·(1 − (1 − λ)^(2i))), i = 1, 2, …; they widen at first and approach target ± L·σ_z. Greater than 0; the input field allows 1 to 5. Preset 3. CUSUM has no such field.
Params.kSigma: CUSUM only: the reference value k (allowance) in multiples of σ; in units of the measured values this gives k · σ (see the result). Deviations from the target up to k are not accumulated: C⁺ = max(0, x − target − k + previous C⁺). Rule of thumb for a shift of Δ·σ: k = Δ/2. Greater than 0; the input field allows 0.1 to 2. Preset 0.5. EWMA has no such field.
Params.hSigma: CUSUM only: the decision interval h in multiples of σ; in units of the measured values this gives h · σ (see the result). A signal arises as soon as C⁺ or C⁻ is greater than h. 4 or 5 are common. Greater than 0; the input field allows 2 to 10. Preset 4. EWMA has no such field.

Result.chartType: The procedure that was used: ewma or cusum. It decides which further figures exist.
Result.n: Number of used numbers in the series; empty and non-numeric cells are already removed. A result exists from 3 numbers on. The numbers of the signal points count these numbers from 0, not the worksheet rows. The sub-line of the Signals tile shows n as “of n data points”.
Result.target: The target μ₀ that was used: the given target, otherwise the baseline mean (of the first baseline count values). Tile “μ₀ (target)”; its sub-line shows σ̂, the spread of the individual values that was used (result σ), both with four decimals. Missing when the value is not finite.
Result.sigma: The spread σ of the individual values that was used: the given one if it is greater than 0, otherwise estimated from the baseline (MR̄ / 1.128 or sample SD with n − 1, depending on the σ estimation method). It appears as σ̂ in the sub-line of the tile “μ₀ (target)”. A result exists only if σ is greater than 0.
Result.lambda: EWMA only: the weight λ that was used. It appears in the sub-line of the tile “σ_z (steady state)”.
Result.L: EWMA only: the limit width L in multiples of σ that was used.
Result.cl: EWMA only: the center line of the chart; it equals the target μ₀, where the EWMA value z also starts. Missing when the value is not finite.
Result.sigmaSteady: EWMA only: the steady-state spread σ_z = σ·√(λ/(2 − λ)), the limit of the spread of the EWMA value z for long series; the limits approach target ± L·σ_z. Tile “σ_z (steady state)”; its sub-line shows the λ that was used.
Result.signals: EWMA only: the numbers of the points whose EWMA value z lies strictly outside the limits (z above the upper or below the lower limit). The numbers count the used numbers from 0, not the worksheet rows. The tile “Signals” shows their count; the sub-line gives the number of data points.
Result.k: CUSUM only: the reference value in units of the measured values, k = (field k in σ) · σ, with the spread σ that was used. It appears in the sub-line of the tile “h (limit)”. Missing when the value is not finite.
Result.h: CUSUM only: the decision interval in units of the measured values, h = (field h in σ) · σ, with the spread σ that was used. A signal arises as soon as C⁺ or C⁻ is greater than h. Tile “h (limit)”; its sub-line shows k in units of the measured values. Missing when the value is not finite.
Result.signalsHigh: CUSUM only: the numbers of the points at which the upper sum C⁺ = max(0, x − target − k + previous C⁺) is greater than h, that is signals upward. The numbers count the used numbers from 0, not the worksheet rows. The signals tile counts these together with the downward signals.
Result.signalsLow: CUSUM only: the numbers of the points at which the lower sum C⁻ = max(0, target − x − k + previous C⁻) is greater than h, that is signals downward. The numbers count the used numbers from 0, not the worksheet rows. The signals tile counts these together with the upward signals.

run-chart.name: Run Chart
run-chart.description: Median run chart with four runs tests
run-chart.alphaHint: Threshold below which a test is flagged (default 0.05).
run-chart.testDesc_clustering: Too few runs about the median — level shift or mixed population
run-chart.testDesc_mixtures: Too many runs about the median — superimposed sources
run-chart.testDesc_trends: Too few runs ↑/↓ — drift, wear, warm-up effect
run-chart.testDesc_oscillation: Too many runs ↑/↓ — over-correction, systematic zigzag
run-chart.whenToUse: Look at a series over time for non-random patterns — clustering, mixtures, trends, oscillation — before building control limits.

read.help: Read the chosen column, alpha, the median, the run counts, the four test p-values and the plotted values.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: 'value' — the measured values in time order (required, at least 3 numbers for a result).
params.ref: A column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from read().pickableColumns.value, or null to clear it.

setParam.help: Set an analysis option and recompute.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

runAnalysis.help: Recompute with the current column values, for example after the data changed.

alpha.help: The significance level of the runs tests, 0 < alpha < 1.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts: value.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts: alpha.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; the key is instanceId|sheetId|columnId.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null without a column or with fewer than 3 numbers.

points.help: One row per plotted value in data order: { value }. read({ fields: ['points'] }) returns them in full.

Params.alpha: Significance level α of the four runs tests, greater than 0 and less than 1 (default 0.05). A test is flagged when its p-value is below α; the smaller α, the more rarely a test is flagged. The input field only allows 0.001 to 0.5, the check accepts any value between 0 and 1.

Result.n: Number of usable numbers in the series; empty and non-numeric cells are already filtered out. A result exists from 3 numbers.
Result.median: Median of the series: the middle value of the numbers sorted ascending, for an even count the mean of the two middle ones. It is the center line of the run chart and splits the points into above and below. The tile sub-line shows n.
Result.runsAboutMedian: Runs about the median: number of uninterrupted sequences of points on the same side of the median; values exactly on the median count as “below”. For a random series 2·m₁·m₂/N + 1 runs are expected (m₁ points above, m₂ below, N all). Too few runs point to clustering, too many to mixtures. The tile sub-line also shows the runs up and down.
Result.runsUpDown: Runs up and down: number of uninterrupted sequences of rising or falling steps between consecutive points; ties are skipped. With n as the number of steps without a tie plus 1, a random series is expected to have (2n − 1)/3 runs with variance (16n − 29)/90. Too few runs point to trends, too many to oscillation.
Result.flagged: Number of tests, 0 to 4, whose p-value is below α. 0 means: no sign of a non-random cause. From 1 there is a sign of clustering, mixtures, trends or oscillation. The tile sub-line shows α.
Result.tests: The four runs tests in fixed order: clustering, mixtures, trends, oscillation. Each entry has the test, its p-value, the number of counted runs and the verdict.

RunTest.id: Which test: clustering (too few runs about the median), mixtures (too many runs about the median), trends (too few runs up and down), oscillation (too many runs up and down).
RunTest.p: p-value of the test from the normal approximation of the runs: z = (runs − expected)/√variance. Clustering and trends: Φ(z); mixtures and oscillation: 1 − Φ(z). With spread 0, p = 1.
RunTest.observed: Number of counted runs the test is based on: for clustering and mixtures the runs about the median, for trends and oscillation the runs up and down.
RunTest.flagged: True when the p-value is below α; the test is then flagged.

attribute-control-chart.whenToUse: Control-chart counted data: p and np for defectives, c and u for defects, with Nelson-type rules on the plotted points.

read.help: Read the chart type, chosen columns, settings, limits, rule violations and per point the value, n and limits.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: 'defects' — defectives (p, np) or defects (c, u) per sample (required); 'size' — the sample size per sample, only for p and u.
params.ref: A column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from read().pickableColumns of that slot, or null to clear the slot (allowed in any chart type).

setParam.help: Set an analysis option and recompute.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. For baselineCount, null or '' clears the field.

runAnalysis.help: Recompute with the current column values, for example after the data changed.

defectsRef.help: The defectives or defects column (slot 'defects'), or null.

sizeRef.help: The sample size column (slot 'size', used by p and u), or null.

constantN.help: The constant sample size of the np chart.

baselineCount.help: Phase I length, or null for all points.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts for the current chart type.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts for the current chart type.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; the key is instanceId|sheetId|columnId.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null without the required columns or with fewer than 2 usable points.

points.help: One row per plotted point: { value, n, ucl, lcl, signal }; n is null for the c chart. read({ fields: ['points'] }) returns them in full.

Params.chartTypeId: The control chart type: p (fraction of defective units per sample, sample size may vary), np (number of defective units at a constant sample size n), c (number of defects per unit at a constant inspection opportunity) or u (defects per unit at a varying inspection opportunity). It determines which columns and settings exist: the sample size column only for p and u, the constant sample size only for np.
Params.constantN: The constant sample size n of the np chart, a whole number of at least 1; it enters the center line n · p̄ and σ = √(n · p̄ · (1 − p̄)). It exists only for the np chart; the screen allows 1 and up, and so does the check.
Params.baselineCount: How many of the first usable points form the baseline (Phase I), a whole number of at least 1; center line and limits are computed from it, the rules then check all points. Empty means all points; if the number exceeds the point count, all points count as well. The screen field requires at least 2, the agent check accepts 1 and up.
Params.enabledRules: The checked rules, a list from 1 (one point beyond UCL or LCL), 2 (9 points in a row on the same side of the center line), 3 (6 points in a row rising or falling), 5 (2 of 3 points beyond 2σ, same side) and 6 (4 of 5 points beyond 1σ, same side). Only rule 1 is preselected. Rules 4, 7 and 8 do not exist for attribute charts: counted data often has equal neighbours, so rule 4 (alternating up and down) would be unreliable; 7 and 8 are not provided. Rules 5 and 6 are checked only when σ stays the same, so not for p and u with varying sample sizes (the limits differ per point there), and not when σ = 0; they are then silently skipped even if checked.

Result.chartType: The control chart type used: p, np, c or u.
Result.statistic: The plotted quantity: proportion (p chart), count (np and c chart) or rate (defects per unit, u chart).
Result.valid: The number of usable points. For np and c these are the numbers in the defects column (empty and non-numeric cells are dropped); for p and u the rows where the defect count and the sample size are numbers and the size is greater than 0. The Violations tile shows it as the total.
Result.cl: The center line, computed from the baseline: for p the fraction p̄ = sum of defects / sum of sizes, for np n · p̄, for c the mean c̄ of the counts, for u ū = sum of defects / sum of sizes. The CL (Center Line) tile shows it with four decimals.
Result.ucl: The upper control limit UCL = center line + 3σ, with σ = √(p̄ · (1 − p̄) / n) for p, √(n · p̄ · (1 − p̄)) for np, √c̄ for c and √(ū / n) for u. It applies to all points alike and is a number only then. If the limits vary per point (p and u with unequal sample sizes) it is empty, as are LCL and σ; the limits per point are given with the individual points. The UCL / LCL tile then shows, under the label UCL̄ / LCL̄, the mean of the per-point limits, not this empty value.
Result.lcl: The lower control limit LCL = center line − 3σ, floored at 0 because counted values are not negative; σ as for the upper limit. Empty when the limits vary per point.
Result.sigma: The spread σ used for the limits and for rules 5 and 6 (formula per chart type under the upper limit). Empty when the limits vary per point.
Result.variableLimits: True when the limits differ per point: this happens for p and u as soon as the sample sizes are not all equal. UCL, LCL and σ are then empty, and rules 5 and 6 are not checked.
Result.violations: The rule violations under the checked rules, once per point and rule, sorted by point. The point counts from 0 over the usable points, so without dropped rows and not over the worksheet rows. For rules 2, 3, 5 and 6 every point of the pattern is its own violation.
Result.signals: The points with at least one rule violation, each only once, sorted by point and counted like the violations (from 0, over the usable points). The Violations tile counts exactly these points, not the individual rule violations.

Violation.index: The violating point, counted from 0 over the usable points (after empty rows are dropped), not over the worksheet rows.
Violation.ruleId: The violated rule: 1, 2, 3, 5 or 6 (meaning under the checked rules).

attribute-control-chart.name: Control Chart (Attribute)
attribute-control-chart.description: SPC charts for count data: p, np, c, u
attribute-control-chart.typeHint_p: Fraction of defective units per sample. Sample size may vary.
attribute-control-chart.typeHint_np: Number of defective units with constant sample size n.
attribute-control-chart.typeHint_c: Number of defects per unit; inspection opportunity constant.
attribute-control-chart.typeHint_u: Defects per unit; inspection opportunity variable.
attribute-control-chart.sizeHint: Number of inspected units per data point.
attribute-control-chart.constantNHint: Same sample size for every data point.
attribute-control-chart.baselineHint: Empty = use all values as baseline.
attribute-control-chart.noViolations: No rule violations — process is stable.

rare-event-chart.description: g and t charts for rare events
rare-event-chart.typeHint_g: Geometrically distributed count of units between two events.
rare-event-chart.typeHint_t: Time span between events with the Nelson power transform.
rare-event-chart.dataHint_t: Column of time spans between events (positive values).
rare-event-chart.originalScaleNote: KPIs on the original scale (back-transformed); chart on the transformed scale.
rare-event-chart.whenToUse: Monitor rare events: the g chart counts opportunities between events, the t chart the time between events.

read.help: Read the chart type, the chosen column, the limits, the signal points and the plotted values.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: 'value' — counts (g chart) or times (t chart) between events (required, at least 2 usable values).
params.ref: A column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from read().pickableColumns.value, or null to clear it.

setParam.help: Set an analysis option and recompute.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

runAnalysis.help: Recompute with the current column values, for example after the data changed.

columnRef.help: The column of counts or times between events (slot 'value'), or null.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts: value.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts: chartTypeId.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; the key is instanceId|sheetId|columnId.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null without a column or with fewer than 2 usable values (the t chart counts only positive ones).

points.help: One row per plotted point: { value, signal }; value on the plotted scale, null where the t chart drops a non-positive value. read({ fields: ['points'] }) returns them in full.

Params.chartTypeId: Chart type: g for the number of opportunities (for example days or cases) between rare events, t for the time between events (positive values only). The choice determines center line, limits and scale of the chart.

Result.chartType: The computed chart type, g or t, as set in the selection.
Result.n: Number of usable values in the series; the t chart counts only values greater than 0. A result exists from 2 values. The sub-line of the signals tile names this number.
Result.cl: Center line (CL) on the original scale. g chart: mean ḡ of the series. t chart: mean ȳ of the transformed values y = t^(1/3.6), transformed back (ȳ^3.6). The tile sub-line shows σ̂, for the t chart on the transformed scale.
Result.ucl: Upper control limit (UCL) on the original scale. g chart: ḡ + 3σ with σ = √(ḡ(ḡ + 1)). t chart: ȳ + 3σ with σ = MR̄/1.128 on the transformed scale, transformed back (y^3.6). The tile sub-line shows the lower control limit (LCL).
Result.lcl: Lower control limit (LCL) on the original scale. g chart: max(0, ḡ − 3σ). t chart: ȳ − 3σ, capped at 0 and transformed back (y^3.6). The tile shows it as the sub-line next to UCL.
Result.sigma: Spread σ of the chart. g chart: √(ḡ(ḡ + 1)). t chart: MR̄/1.128, the mean moving range of the transformed values divided by 1.128, so on the transformed scale and not on the scale of center line and limits. The tile shows it as σ̂ next to the center line of the original scale.
Result.transformed: True for the t chart: it is drawn on the transformed scale y = t^(1/3.6). False for the g chart.
Result.plotted: Center line, limits and σ on the plotted scale. For the g chart these are the same values as above, for the t chart the transformed ones.
Result.signals: Positions (from 0) of the points strictly above the upper or below the lower limit of the plotted scale, counted among the numbers of the column (empty and non-numeric cells left out, not the worksheet rows); with the t chart, non-positive values count as a gap. The tile counts these points.

PlottedLimits.cl: Center line on the plotted scale.
PlottedLimits.ucl: Upper control limit on the plotted scale.
PlottedLimits.lcl: Lower control limit on the plotted scale.
PlottedLimits.sigma: Spread on the plotted scale; for the t chart the same transformed spread as above.

multivariate-control-chart.name: Multivariate Control Chart (Hotelling T²)
multivariate-control-chart.variablesHint: Two or more numeric columns — observations per row.
multivariate-control-chart.baselineHint: Number of baseline observations for mean vector and covariance (m > p required).
multivariate-control-chart.errTooFewRows: Too few complete rows — need at least p+1 = {p}+1 observations.
multivariate-control-chart.err_singular: The covariance matrix is singular: at least one variable is constant or can be computed from the others.
multivariate-control-chart.err_rowLengthMismatch: All rows must have the same number of values.
multivariate-control-chart.err_baselineTooSmall: The baseline phase needs more rows than variables.
multivariate-control-chart.whenToUse: Monitor several correlated characteristics together: Hotelling T² flags rows whose combination is unusual even when each value alone is in control.

baselineCount.help: Rows used for Phase I, or null for all rows.

points.help: One row per complete data row: { t2, signal }. read({ fields: ['points'] }) returns them in full.

Params.alpha: The false-alarm rate α of the T² limit: the probability that a new point after the baseline lies above the upper limit UCL while the process is stable and the data are normally distributed. For the baseline rows themselves, which are checked as well, this rate does not hold exactly. UCL = p(m + 1)(m − 1)/(m² − m·p) · F(1 − α; p, m − p) with the F quantile, p variables and m baseline rows. Greater than 0 and less than 1; the input field allows 0.0001 to 0.5. Preset 0.0027 (3σ equivalent). A smaller α moves UCL further up. After a change the analysis is recomputed.
Params.baselineCount: How many of the first complete rows form the baseline (Phase I) from which mean and covariance are estimated. Empty (shown as “all”) means all rows. The value takes effect only if it is greater than the number of variables p; if it is smaller than or equal to p, all rows are silently used. A number larger than the number of rows acts like all. Whole numbers from 1 are allowed, the input field only allows 2 and up.

Result.n: Number of complete rows, that is rows in which every chosen column holds a number; rows with an empty or non-numeric cell are removed, and for columns of different length the shortest counts. A result exists only if n is greater than p. The numbers of the signal rows count these rows from 0, not the worksheet rows. The sub-line of the Signals tile shows n as “of n data points”.
Result.p: Number of variables (columns) monitored together; a result exists from 2 on. Tile “Variables (p)”; its sub-line shows the baseline rows as “m = … baseline”.
Result.m: Number of baseline (Phase I) rows that mean and covariance come from: all complete rows, or the first baseline count rows if that is greater than p (at most n). m must be greater than p. It appears in the sub-line of the tile “Variables (p)”.
Result.cl: The center line of the T² chart, p(m − 1)/(m − p), as a reference level for the T² values; it is a guide value of the chart, not an exact expectation of T². Missing when the value is not finite.
Result.ucl: The upper control limit of the T² chart, UCL = p(m + 1)(m − 1)/(m² − m·p) · F(1 − α; p, m − p) with the F quantile. Tile “UCL (T²)” with three decimals; its sub-line shows the α that is set. A point signals when its T² is greater than UCL. Missing when the value is not finite.
Result.mean: The mean x̄ of each variable over the baseline rows, in the order of the chosen columns. An entry is missing (empty) when its value is not finite.
Result.covariance: The covariance matrix S of the variables from the baseline with m − 1 in the denominator, p rows by p columns (diagonal: variances). T² uses its inverse; if S is singular, for example with columns that determine each other exactly, there is no result. An entry is missing (empty) when its value is not finite.
Result.signals: The numbers of the complete rows whose T² is greater than UCL, where T²ᵢ = (xᵢ − x̄)ᵀ S⁻¹ (xᵢ − x̄) measures the distance of row i from the baseline mean vector; all complete rows are checked, including those of the baseline. The numbers count these rows from 0, not the worksheet rows. The tile “Signals” shows their count.

short-run-chart.whenToUse: Control-chart short production runs that mix parts with different targets: each value is standardised within its part and plotted on one Z-MR chart.

read.help: Read the chosen columns, the per-part statistics, the Z and MR limits, the signal points and z and MR per value.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: 'values' — the measured values in time order (required); 'groups' — the part or group of each value, numbers or text (required). A result needs at least 4 usable pairs.
params.ref: A column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from read().pickableColumns of that slot, or null to clear the slot.

runAnalysis.help: Recompute with the current column values, for example after the data changed.

groupsRef.help: The part or group column (slot 'groups'), or null.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts: values, groups.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; the key is instanceId|sheetId|columnId.

warningMsg.help: The notice about parts that were skipped (too few values to estimate their spread), or ''.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null without both columns or with fewer than 4 usable pairs of number and group.

points.help: One row per usable value: { z, mr, signalZ, signalMR }. read({ fields: ['points'] }) returns them in full.

Result.n: Number of usable pairs of measurement and part; rows with an empty or non-numeric measurement or an empty part are already removed. A result exists from 4 pairs on. The numbers of the signal points count these pairs from 0, not the worksheet rows.
Result.skipped: Number of measurements that could not be standardised because their part has no spread (σ̂ = 0, also when the part has a single value). They are drawn at z = 0; the interface warns about it.
Result.groups: The figures per part, in the order in which the parts first occur; this is the table below the charts. The “Parts” tile shows their count, its sub-line the number of measurements.
Result.z: The limits of the Z chart: center line 0, upper limit +3, lower −3. Each value is standardised within its part to z = (x − x̄)/σ̂, with the mean x̄ and spread σ̂ of the part; for a stable process z is approximately standard normal.
Result.mr: The limits of the MR chart of the z values: center line MR̄ (mean of the absolute differences |zᵢ − zᵢ₋₁| of consecutive values), upper limit 3.267 · MR̄, lower 0. The “MR̄ (z)” tile shows the center line, its sub-line the upper limit (UCL_MR).
Result.signalsZ: Numbers (counted from 0 among the usable pairs) of the points whose z value lies above +3 or below −3. The “Signals” tile counts these together with the signals of the MR chart.
Result.signalsMR: Numbers (counted from 0 among the usable pairs, from the second point on) of the points whose moving range of the z values lies above the upper limit of the MR chart (UCL_MR).

GroupStats.group: The part or group as it appears in the part/group column, as text.
GroupStats.count: Number of measurements of this part (n).
GroupStats.mean: Mean x̄ of this part's measurements; it is the reference of the standardisation z = (x − x̄)/σ̂.
GroupStats.sigma: Estimated spread σ̂ within the part: MR̄ of the part / 1.128 (d₂ for pairs). If the part has only one value or all its values are equal it is 0 and its values are drawn at z = 0.
GroupStats.mrBar: Mean MR̄ of the absolute differences |xᵢ − xᵢ₋₁| of consecutive measurements within this part, in measurement order; σ̂ is derived from it.

Limits.ucl: Upper control limit (UCL) of the chart.
Limits.lcl: Lower control limit (LCL) of the chart.

short-run-chart.name: Control Chart (Short-Run Z-MR)
short-run-chart.description: Standardised I-MR across parts with different targets
short-run-chart.groupsHint: Identifies the part for each measurement. Mean and σ̂ are computed separately per part.
short-run-chart.warningSkipped: {count} value(s) could not be standardised (part has too few points for σ̂ — shown as z=0).

transformed-imr-chart.name: Control Chart (Box-Cox transformed)
transformed-imr-chart.description: I-MR with Box-Cox transform for non-normal data
transformed-imr-chart.lambdaHint: In auto mode λ is fitted from the data; for Phase-II monitoring freeze it to the Phase-I value.
transformed-imr-chart.errPositiveOnly: Box-Cox requires strictly positive values. Filter the column or use Yeo-Johnson.
transformed-imr-chart.whenToUse: Control-chart skewed, strictly positive data: a Box-Cox transformation makes them near-normal before I-MR limits are computed.

read.help: Read the chosen column, the λ settings, the limits on both scales, the signal points and the transformed values.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed.

params.slot: 'value' — the measured values in time order (required; at least 5, all greater than 0).
params.ref: A column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from read().pickableColumns.value, or null to clear it.

setParam.help: Set an analysis option and recompute.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

runAnalysis.help: Recompute with the current column values, for example after the data changed.

lambdaManual.help: The λ used in manual mode; in auto mode it mirrors the estimated λ after each computation.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts: value.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts now: lambdaMode, and lambdaManual in manual mode.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; the key is instanceId|sheetId|columnId.

errorMsg.help: Why nothing was computed, for example values that are not positive; '' otherwise.

result.help: The computed result, each figure described individually under keys; null without a column, with fewer than 5 numbers, with a value less than or equal to 0, or when the computation fails (errorMsg then gives the reason).

points.help: One row per value: { transformed, signal }. read({ fields: ['points'] }) returns them in full.

Params.lambdaMode: How the λ of the Box-Cox transformation is obtained: “auto (Anderson-Darling)” estimates it from the data, “manual” takes the value entered under λ. The estimate picks, from a grid from −3 to 3 in steps of 0.05, the λ at which the transformed values have the smallest Anderson-Darling statistic (closest to a normal distribution), rounded to 0.01. After a change the chart is recomputed.
Params.lambdaManual: The λ of the Box-Cox transformation y = (x^λ − 1)/λ as used in “manual” mode; for |λ| < 10⁻⁸ the log transformation y = ln x applies. The check accepts any finite number, the input field allows −3 to 3. In “auto (Anderson-Darling)” mode the field is disabled and shows the estimated λ after each computation; when switching to “manual” that is the starting value.

Result.n: Number of usable numbers in the series; empty and non-numeric cells are already removed. A result exists from 5 numbers on, all of which must be greater than 0. The numbers of the signal points count these numbers from 0, not the worksheet rows.
Result.lambda: The λ used for the Box-Cox transformation y = (x^λ − 1)/λ; for |λ| < 10⁻⁸ it is the log transformation y = ln x. In “auto” mode it is the estimated λ (smallest Anderson-Darling statistic on the grid from −3 to 3, step 0.05, rounded to 0.01), in “manual” mode the entered one. The tile shows it with three decimals and the suffix (auto) or (manual).
Result.lambdaAuto: Whether λ was estimated from the data (true) or set by hand (false). The tile shows it as the suffix (auto) or (manual) after λ.
Result.i: The individuals chart on the transformed scale y: center line, upper and lower control limit and spread σ̂. These are the values of the “transformed (y)” column in the table.
Result.iOriginal: The same limits of the individuals chart, converted back to the original scale: x = (λ·y + 1)^(1/λ), for the log transformation x = e^y. They are not symmetric around the center line. A value is missing (empty, “–” in the table) when λ·y + 1 ≤ 0, so the back-transformation is undefined there; typically that hits the lower limit for λ > 0.
Result.mr: The moving range chart of the transformed values: center line MR̄ (mean of the absolute differences |yᵢ − yᵢ₋₁| of consecutive values), upper control limit 3.267 · MR̄, lower 0. It exists on the transformed scale only.
Result.signals: Numbers (counted from 0 among the usable numbers) of the points whose transformed value lies above the UCL or below the LCL of the individuals chart. The “Signals” tile shows their count.

IndividualLimits.cl: Center line of the individuals chart on the transformed scale: the mean ȳ of all transformed values (tile CL (y)). The tile's sub-line shows the spread σ̂.
IndividualLimits.ucl: Upper control limit (UCL) of the individuals chart on the transformed scale: center line + 3 · σ̂.
IndividualLimits.lcl: Lower control limit (LCL) of the individuals chart on the transformed scale: center line − 3 · σ̂.
IndividualLimits.sigma: Estimated spread σ̂ of the transformed values: MR̄/1.128, with the mean MR̄ of the moving ranges and the factor d₂ = 1.128 for pairs. The sub-line of the CL (y) tile shows it.

Limits.ucl: Upper control limit (UCL) of the chart.
Limits.lcl: Lower control limit (LCL) of the chart.

rest-api.name: REST API
rest-api.description: Centrally manage and test REST API endpoints
rest-api.whenToUse: When data should be fetched regularly from a web service — manage endpoints with headers and a schedule, and check the response.

read.help: Returns the endpoints, the active endpoint, the selectable sets and the last response.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

addEndpoint.help: Creates a new endpoint and makes it the active one; its URL, headers and schedule can then be edited. The agent receives the id of the new endpoint.

selectEndpoint.help: Makes an endpoint the active one; the header, mapping, schedule and parameter actions edit it. Clears lastResponse.

params.endpointId: The id of an endpoint in endpoints.

renameEndpoint.help: Renames an endpoint; it does not have to be the active one.

params.endpointId: The id of an endpoint in endpoints.
params.name: The new name; the empty string clears it.

removeEndpoint.help: Removes an endpoint without asking back and stops its schedule. If it was the active one, the first remaining endpoint becomes active.

params.endpointId: The id of an endpoint in endpoints.

setParam.help: Sets one parameter of the active endpoint. A changed schedule interval restarts a running schedule.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

addHeader.help: Add header appends an empty header line to the active endpoint, to be filled with a name and a value afterwards. The agent receives its position in the list of header lines.

setHeader.help: Headers are extra header lines sent along with the request, for example an access key; each consists of a name and a value. Sets name and value of a header line of the active endpoint.

params.index: The index of a header in endpoints[].headers.
params.key: The header name; the empty string clears it.
params.value: The header value; the empty string clears it.

deleteHeader.help: Deletes a request header of the active endpoint.

params.index: The index of a header in endpoints[].headers.

addMapping.help: Add mapping appends an empty mapping between a path in the response and a column to the active endpoint. Mappings are stored but not applied yet. The agent receives its position in the list of mappings.

setMapping.help: Sets path and target column of a mapping of the active endpoint. A column can belong to only one mapping per endpoint.

params.index: The index of a mapping in endpoints[].mappings.
params.jsonPath: The path in the JSON response; the empty string clears it.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns, or null to clear.

deleteMapping.help: Deletes a mapping of the active endpoint.

params.index: The index of a mapping in endpoints[].mappings.

setSchedule.help: Automatic polling switches the schedule of the active endpoint on or off: when on, the module fetches the URL itself at the set interval. The schedule runs only while a URL is set.

params.enabled: true starts the regular requests, false stops them.

sendRequest.help: Send performs a GET request to the URL of the active endpoint and waits for the response, which then appears under Response. This sends a real request over the network and leaves the device. A network error shows as status 0. Without an active endpoint or without a URL nothing happens (without a URL the message "Please enter a URL." appears).

endpoints.help: All endpoints with id, name, url, headers, mappings, writeMode and schedule. Mappings are stored but not applied yet.

activeId.help: The id of the endpoint that the header, mapping, schedule and parameter actions edit, or null.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state; empty without an active endpoint.

scheduleRunning.help: Whether a timer runs for the active endpoint.

pickableColumns.help: The columns setMapping accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'.

lastResponse.help: The last response of the active endpoint: status, status text and content; empty until a request has been sent. The agent receives the status, the status text, whether the request succeeded, and the content.

Params.url: The address to which Send and the automatic polling send a GET request. Any text, not validated; if it is empty, Send shows the message "Please enter a URL.".
Params.writeMode: How the mapped data is to be written into the columns: replace ("Clear columns before writing"), append ("Append data at the end") or prepend ("Insert data at the top"). This applies to the column mappings, which are stored today but not yet applied — so the write mode has no effect yet.

schedule.intervalValue: The interval of the automatic polling (the gap between two fetches) as a whole number from 1 to 999, together with the unit next to it. Changing it while the schedule runs restarts the schedule; the field is disabled while automatic polling is off.
schedule.intervalUnit: The unit of the interval: minutes or hours.

rest-api.columnAlreadyUsed: This column is already assigned to another mapping.

regression.whenToUse: When the relationship between a continuous response and one or more predictors is to be described as an equation — linear, polynomial with interactions, exponential, logarithmic or power — to assess effects, predict, or save a model for optimisation.

read.help: Returns the inputs (X, Y, type, degree, confidence, α, excluded terms), the sets the actions accept now, and the fitted model as numbers in result (null without a fit or after a failed fit; errorMsg then names the reason).

setColumns.help: The data collection columns that supply this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. The order is kept and columns chosen twice count once; if the response is among the new predictors, it is cleared.

params.slot: One of activeMultiSlots; this module only has 'x'.
params.refs: List of column references { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from pickableColumns.x, in order; [] clears X.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. Without a response there is no result.

params.slot: One of activeColumnSlots; this module only has 'y'.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from pickableColumns.y (the columns not chosen as X), or null to clear.

setParam.help: Sets the regression type, the polynomial degree, the confidence level or α and fits again.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. confLevel and alpha as a fraction (0.95, not 95).

setTerm.help: Includes or excludes one polynomial term and fits again; the list of excluded terms in the state and in the result follows.

params.term: A term id from terms (the fitted terms without Intercept, plus the aliased terms of a failed fit).
params.included: true includes the term, false excludes it.

importExperiment.help: Takes the factors and a response of an experimental design as predictors and response and fits; the selector then shows the imported design. With “— Choose experiment —” the link is released and the columns stay.

params.key: A key from experimentImports, or null.

setActiveX.help: For single-X models (exponential, logarithmic, power with several X) chooses the model whose result is shown; the button of the chosen model is highlighted.

params.key: A key from perXKeys.

autoRun.help: Fits when X and Y are set; otherwise discards the result (result becomes null).

runAnalysis.help: Fits the model with the current inputs. On failure result is null and errorMsg names the reason; with aliasing, terms lists the terms setTerm can exclude.

saveAsModel.help: Saves the polynomial model (one or several X) in the project models, new or as an update of the model saved last; the button then reads “Update model”, and “Model saved” appears next to it. Without a model that can be saved nothing is stored.

predict.help: Predicts the response for the given values of the predictors and shows it under “Prediction”; the prediction stays empty when a predictor is left without a value or there is no result.

params.values: An object with one value per predictor id from predictors: a number, or one of the levels for categorical predictors. Missing predictors make the result null.

colRefs.help: The predictor columns X as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }, in order.

yKey.help: The response column Y as key instanceId|sheetId|columnId, or null.

regType.help: The regression type, one of regTypes.

polyDegree.help: The polynomial degree (only used with the polynomial type).

activeDegrees.help: The degrees setParam('polyDegree') accepts now; a degree with too few paired rows for its term count is missing.

confLevel.help: The confidence level as a fraction (0.95).

alpha.help: The significance level α as a fraction (0.05).

excludedTerms.help: The term ids left out of the polynomial.

terms.help: The term ids setTerm accepts now; empty without a polynomial fit or aliasing.

experimentImports.help: The DoE responses importExperiment accepts, each { key, label }.

activeImportSource.help: The DoE response the inputs came from, { experimentId, sourceColumn, transform }, or null.

designNotice.help: Notes on the term set of an experimental design, each figure described individually under keys; null without a term set from an experimental design.

perXKeys.help: The single-X models setActiveX accepts; empty for the polynomial type and without result.

activeXKey.help: The single-X model result shows, or null.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts now.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts: 'y'.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot (x, y) the columns setColumns and setColumn accept, each { key, name }; y leaves out the columns chosen as X.

result.help: The fitted regression model with coefficients and analysis of variance, each figure described individually under keys; null without X or Y or when the fit fails (errorMsg then gives the reason). coefficients[].term is the coefficient name: for a categorical term it carries the level (Material[B]), while terms, excludedTerms and setTerm use the term id without the level (Material).

errorMsg.help: The message of the last failed fit, '' without error.

predictors.help: The inputs of the fitted model, each { id, label, kind, levels? }; empty without result.

canSaveModel.help: true when saveAsModel would store a model now (polynomial type with one or several X, and a result).

savedModelId.help: The id of the model saved last in the project models, or null.

prediction.help: { yHat, piLow, piHigh } of the last prediction, null without one and without result; piLow and piHigh are null where the model gives no prediction interval.

Params.regType: The model form: polynomial (main effects, from degree 2 also squares and interactions, with one or several X), exponential (y = a · eᵇˣ), logarithmic (y = a + b·ln(x)) or power (y = a · xᵇ). The last three fit a separate single model per X and use only suitable rows: exponential y > 0, logarithmic x > 0, power x > 0 and y > 0. A change fits again.
Params.polyDegree: The polynomial degree, 1, 2 or 3, default 1: degree 1 takes only the main effects, degree 2 adds squares and interactions, degree 3 adds cubic terms and higher interactions. A degree can only be chosen when there are more paired rows than terms; otherwise it is locked and the hint below the selection gives the number needed. Only used with the polynomial regression type.
Params.confLevel: The confidence level as a fraction between 0 and 1, so 0.95 instead of 95; the input field shows it in percent. It sets the confidence limits of the coefficients, the confidence and prediction bands in the chart and the prediction interval. The default is the project confidence level; it is independent of the significance level, the two are set separately.
Params.alpha: The significance level α as a fraction between 0 and 1, so 0.05 instead of 5; the input field shows it in percent. It changes no number, only the colouring: rows of the ANOVA and coefficient tables with p < α count as significant, the p-value (F) tile is green below α and yellow below 2α. The default is 1 − the project confidence level; after that it is independent of the confidence level, the two are set separately.

Result.type: The model form actually fitted: polynomial for the polynomial type (with one or several X), otherwise exponential, logarithmic or power for the single-X model shown.
Result.equation: The model equation as text, as shown below the figures, with coefficients rounded to four decimals.
Result.n: Number of rows used: rows with finite values in all X and in Y; for exponential, logarithmic and power only the rows that meet the condition of the model form (y > 0 or x > 0).
Result.R2: Coefficient of determination R² = 1 − SSE/SST: the share of the variation in Y the model explains, from 0 to 1. The tile is green from 0.8 and yellow from 0.5, red below.
Result.adjR2: Adjusted coefficient of determination, tile Adj. R²: 1 − (1 − R²) · (n − 1)/(n − p) with p coefficients including the intercept. It drops when a term costs more degrees of freedom than it explains, so it suits comparing models. The tile takes the colour of R².
Result.R2pred: Predicted coefficient of determination, tile R²(pred): 1 − PRESS/SST, where PRESS is the sum of the squared leave-one-out residuals eᵢ/(1 − hᵢᵢ). It measures how well the model predicts new data; well below R² it points to overfitting. Empty for exponential, logarithmic and power; the tile is then missing as well.
Result.Se: Standard error of the regression, tile Std. Error: S = √MSE, the typical deviation of the observations from the model, in the units of Y.
Result.Fstat: F statistic of the overall model, F = MSR/MSE from the Regression row of the ANOVA table; 0 when MSE is 0. The tile shows two decimals.
Result.fPVal: p-value of the F test, tile p-value (F): the probability of an F at least this large if all coefficients except the intercept were 0, from the F distribution with the degrees of freedom of regression and residuals. Below α the model counts as significant and the tile is green, below 2α yellow. 1 when the model has no degree of freedom or MSE is 0.
Result.dw: Durbin-Watson statistic Σ(eᵢ − eᵢ₋₁)²/SSE over the residuals in data order, between 0 and 4: around 2 no autocorrelation, below 1.5 positive, above 2.5 negative. 0 when SSE is 0; the tile shows three decimals.
Result.coefficients: The coefficient table, one row per estimated coefficient: for the polynomial first Intercept, then the terms; for exponential and power a and b, for logarithmic Intercept and ln(x).
Result.excludedTerms: The terms left out of the polynomial, by hand or because of aliasing, each as term name without level.
Result.anova: The analysis of variance of the model with the rows Regression, one per term, Residuals and Total; the same numbers as in the ANOVA table. For exponential, logarithmic and power there are no term rows.

Coefficient.term: The coefficient name: Intercept, a column name or a square or interaction term. A categorical predictor gets one row per level, whose name carries the level; including and excluding uses the term name without level.
Coefficient.coeff: The estimated coefficient b. The Coefficient column also shows the confidence interval next to it, from the lower to the upper confidence limit.
Coefficient.se: Standard error of the coefficient, column Std. Error: √(MSE · ((XᵀX)⁻¹)ⱼⱼ). Empty for exponential, logarithmic and power.
Coefficient.t: t-value b / Std. Error, tested against 0 with the degrees of freedom of the residuals. Empty for exponential, logarithmic and power.
Coefficient.pval: Two-sided p-value of the t test of b = 0; below α the term counts as significant and the row is highlighted. Empty for exponential, logarithmic and power.
Coefficient.ciLow: Lower confidence limit b − t · Std. Error, with t the (1 + confidence level)/2 quantile of the t distribution with the degrees of freedom of the residuals. Empty for exponential, logarithmic and power.
Coefficient.ciHigh: Upper confidence limit b + t · Std. Error, with the same t as the lower limit. Empty for exponential, logarithmic and power.
Coefficient.vif: Variance inflation factor 1/(1 − R²ⱼ), with R²ⱼ from regressing the predictor on the other continuous predictors that still have a term in the model. Only main effects of continuous predictors have a value, and only with at least two continuous predictors; otherwise empty. If only one of them still has a term in the model, the value is exactly 1. Above 5 the cell turns yellow, above 10 red; if the value over all chosen predictors differs, it is shown next to it in parentheses.

Anova.regression: The Regression row: the variation SSR explained by the model, with the F test of the overall model; degrees of freedom equal to the number of coefficients, not counting the constant term (the intercept for polynomial and logarithmic, the prefactor a for exponential and power).
Anova.terms: One indented row per term. When the polynomial is fitted with term blocks, this is the Type III decomposition per term block: the sum of squares the block explains in addition to all others, with the F test of the block. Otherwise one row per coefficient with SS = t² · MSE and one degree of freedom. Empty for exponential, logarithmic and power.
Anova.error: The Residuals row: the unexplained variation SSE with n − p degrees of freedom and MSE = SSE/(n − p).
Anova.total: The Total row: the total variation SST = Σ(yᵢ − ȳ)² with n − 1 degrees of freedom, the sum of Regression and Residuals.

AnovaRow.term: The term name; only the term rows carry it.
AnovaRow.ss: Sum of squares of the row, column SS: the variation this source explains, that is left over (Residuals) or that is present in total (Total).
AnovaRow.df: Degrees of freedom of the row, column DF.
AnovaRow.ms: Mean square of the row, column MS = SS/DF. Missing in the Total row.
AnovaRow.f: F value of the row, column F: MS of the row divided by MS of the residuals. Only in the Regression row and the term rows.
AnovaRow.p: p-value of the F test of the row, from the F distribution with the DF of the row and the DF of the residuals; below α the row is highlighted as significant. Only in the Regression row and the term rows; empty where no p-value can be computed.

DesignNotice.aliased: The terms the experimental design cannot separate from others and that were therefore excluded, each with the terms it is aliased with.
DesignNotice.saturated: The terms excluded because the model would otherwise be saturated, leaving no degree of freedom for the residuals.

AliasedTerm.with: The terms it is aliased with.

regression.name: Regression Analysis
regression.description: Polynomial regression (degree 1–3, interactions), Exponential, Logarithmic, Power
regression.degreeDisabledHint: Degree {deg} requires more than {terms} data points (currently: {n}).
regression.tipR2: Proportion of variance in Y explained by the model. 0 = no explanatory power, 1 = perfect fit. Values ≥ 0.8 indicate a good model.
regression.tipAdjR2: Like R², but adjusted for the number of predictors. Decreases when unnecessary variables are added — better suited for model comparison.
regression.tipPredR2: Predicted R²: How well the model predicts new data (leave-one-out). A large gap to R² suggests overfitting.
regression.tipStdError: Standard error of the regression (S): Average distance of observations from the regression line. Smaller = better fit. In Y units.
regression.tipFStat: F-statistic: Tests whether the overall model is significant (all coefficients jointly ≠ 0). Larger values indicate a significant model.
regression.tipPValueF: p-value of the F-test: Probability of observing the F-statistic under H₀ (no relationship). p < α → model is significant.
regression.tipDurbinWatson: Durbin-Watson statistic (0–4): Tests for autocorrelation in residuals. ≈ 2 = no autocorrelation, < 1.5 = positive, > 2.5 = negative autocorrelation.
regression.errSelectBoth: Please select both X and Y columns.
regression.errMinData: At least 3 valid data pairs required (currently: {n}).
regression.errInsufficientDf: Too few data points for the chosen model complexity.
regression.designNoticeAliased: {term} is aliased with {with} and was excluded.
regression.designNoticeSaturated: The model would be saturated (no degrees of freedom for error). Excluded: {terms}. Add replicates or center points.
regression.errAliasedTerms: The model cannot be estimated: {term} is aliased with {with}.

response-optimization.name: Response Optimization
response-optimization.description: Combines several saved regression models and searches for the factor point with the highest joint desirability (Derringer-Suich, multi-start Nelder-Mead).
response-optimization.whenToUse: When several saved regression models (responses of one design) must be traded off: assigns each selected model a goal (maximise, minimise, hit a target) with limits and weight, then searches the factor box for the point with the highest composite desirability D (Derringer-Suich, multi-start Nelder-Mead). Needs at least one saved regression model in the project; the models themselves are created in the regression module.

read.help: Returns the target specifications per model, the optimisation id, the saved models as references (id and name), whether an optimisation can run and why not, the stored optimum and the last error. result is null while no optimisation has run in this module (optId is then null) and when the stored optimisation record is gone; it shows the last successful run, not necessarily the current specifications. errorMsg stays empty until a runOptimize run computes nothing.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setSpec.help: Sets one target specification of a saved model: selected, kind (max, min, target), lower, upper, target or weight. Nothing is computed; canOptimize and diagnosticReasons update, the stored result stays until runOptimize runs. Refuses a modelId that is not in selectableModels, an unknown key and a value that does not fit the key.

params.modelId: The id of a model from selectableModels. Any other value is an error.
params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

runOptimize.help: Optimises the selected models together and stores the optimum in the project; it appears under “Result”. If optimisation is blocked (no model selected, R²adj too low, significant lack of fit or different factors across the selected models) nothing is computed, the previous result stays and a message above the button names the reasons. If the computation fails, the result also stays as it was and the message names the error. After a successful run the message disappears.

specs.help: The settings per response, each described under keys.

optId.help: The id of the stored optimisation; null before the first successful runOptimize.

selectableModels.help: The saved models of the project as references { id, name } - no coefficients; read a model in the regression module that created it. Empty while the project has no saved model. These ids are what setSpec accepts as modelId.

canOptimize.help: True only if at least one model is selected and diagnosticReasons is empty; otherwise runOptimize computes nothing.

diagnosticReasons.help: The reasons that block the optimisation, as texts: R²adj below 0.5, significant lack of fit (p below 0.05) or a different factor structure among the selected models. Empty when nothing blocks, and also empty while no model is selected (optimisation is still blocked then).

result.help: The stored optimum, each figure described individually under keys; null until an optimization has run or when the stored data set is missing.

errorMsg.help: Why the last runOptimize computed nothing: the blocking reasons joined by '; ', 'No model selected.' or the engine error. Empty before the first runOptimize and after a successful run; cleared again as soon as the model list, the selection or a target specification changes.

Spec.selected: Whether this model (this response) takes part in the optimisation; the checkbox in the model header. Only included models show their desirability function and contribute to the composite desirability D; initially none is included. Optimising is possible only when at least one model is included and no diagnosis blocks (R²adj below 0.5, significant lack of fit with p below 0.05, or different factors among the selected models).
Spec.kind: The desirability function of the response: Maximise, Minimise or Target value, default Maximise. Maximise: d = 0 for y ≤ Lower, d = (y − Lower) / (Upper − Lower) in between, d = 1 for y ≥ Upper. Minimise mirrors it: d = 1 up to Lower, d = (Upper − y) / (Upper − Lower) in between, d = 0 from Upper on. Target value: d = 1 exactly at the target, falling linearly to 0 towards Lower and Upper, 0 at and beyond the limits. The shape is always linear (exponent 1). If Upper is not above Lower, d jumps straight between 0 and 1 for Maximise and Minimise; for Target value d is then always 0.
Spec.lower: The lower limit of the desirability function in the unit of the response: for Maximise d = 0 here, for Minimise d = 1, for Target value d = 0. The default is the smallest measured value in the model data (0 without data). A finite number; whether it lies below Upper is not checked.
Spec.upper: The upper limit of the desirability function in the unit of the response: for Maximise d = 1 here, for Minimise d = 0, for Target value d = 0. The default is the largest measured value in the model data (1 without data). A finite number; whether it lies above Lower is not checked.
Spec.target: The target at which the desirability function reaches d = 1. Effective only for the Target value function and shown only then; for Maximise and Minimise it stays stored but has no effect. The default is the midpoint between the smallest and largest measured value, 0.5 without measured values. A finite number; whether it lies between Lower and Upper is not checked.
Spec.weight: The weight w of this response in the composite desirability D = (Π dᵢ^wᵢ)^(1/Σwᵢ): a response with weight 2 counts twice as much as one with weight 1. A number greater than 0, default 1.

Result.xOpt: The factor settings of the optimum, one per factor in the order of the factor names: continuous factors as a number (column Value, four decimals), categorical ones as the level name. The search runs inside the box of factor limits of the first selected model (−1 to 1 if none are given) with Nelder-Mead from 8 random starting points (seed 42, at most 400 iterations per start); the start with the highest D wins. With categorical factors every level combination is searched this way on its own and the best one is taken.
Result.yPredictions: The predicted response values at the optimum, each computed from its model’s regression equation, in the order of the model names (column Prediction, four decimals).
Result.dPerResponse: The individual desirability d per response at the optimum, between 0 and 1: the model’s desirability function applied to its prediction (column d, three decimals). 1 means the specification is fully met, 0 means unacceptable.
Result.D: The composite desirability at the optimum, the weighted geometric mean of the individual desirabilities: D = (Π dᵢ^wᵢ)^(1/Σwᵢ) with the weights wᵢ. If any d is 0, D = 0. The tile shows D with three decimals, green from 0.8, yellow from 0.5, red below. D belongs to the last optimisation run: if a specification is changed afterwards, the result is current again only after optimising anew.
Result.ciAtOpt: Confidence interval of the predictions at the optimum; not computed yet and always empty.
Result.paretoFront: Pareto front of the responses; not computed yet and always empty.
Result.factorNames: The factor names from the first selected model, in the same order as the factor settings (column Factor).
Result.modelNames: The names of the included models (responses), in the same order as the predictions and individual desirabilities (column Model).
Result.iter: The number of Nelder-Mead iterations: without categorical factors those of the best of the 8 starts, with categorical factors the sum over all level combinations.

response-optimization.emptyState: No saved models yet. Save a regression model from the Regression module first.
response-optimization.placeholderResult: No optimum computed yet. Select a model, set the desirability spec, then optimise.
response-optimization.lowR2: Model "{name}" has R²adj = {value}, which is below the minimum required for a meaningful optimisation.
response-optimization.factorMismatch: Model "{name}" has a different factor structure than the other selected models.
response-optimization.lackOfFit: Model "{name}" has a significant lack of fit (p = {value}). The polynomial form does not match the data — refit before optimising.
response-optimization.tipD: Composite desirability D — geometric mean of all individual desirabilities

glm-regression.whenToUse: When a response is attributive — good/bad, yes/no, proportions — or a count (defects, complaints), and its relationship with predictors is to be modelled: binary logistic, Poisson or negative binomial, detected automatically on request.

read.help: Returns the inputs (X, Y, trials column, method, confidence, α, cutoff), the sets the actions accept now, and the fit as numbers in result (null without a shown fit or after a failed fit; errorMsg then names the reason). If Y or X is cleared, the last result stays in result.

setColumns.help: The data collection columns that supply this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. The order is kept, columns chosen twice count once and text columns become categorical predictors; if the response is among the new predictors, it is cleared.

params.slot: One of activeMultiSlots; this module only has 'x'.
params.refs: List of column references { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from pickableColumns.x, in order; [] clears X.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. For grouped data a second column supplies the number of trials; the response is then read as a proportion.

params.slot: One of activeColumnSlots: 'y' or 'trials'.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from pickableColumns.y (columns not chosen as X) or pickableColumns.trials (additionally without Y), or null to clear.

setParam.help: Sets the method, the confidence level, α or the classification cutoff. method, confLevel and alpha fit again; cutoff only recomputes classification.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. confLevel and alpha as a fraction; the other becomes 1 minus this value.

swapSuccess.help: For a binary response swaps which level counts as success and fits again; the coefficients change sign and the odds ratios become their reciprocals. Without a binary result nothing happens.

autoRun.help: Fits when X and Y are set; otherwise nothing happens and an earlier result stays.

runAnalysis.help: Fits now. Without X, without Y or with fewer than three rows the result is discarded and errorMsg names the reason.

saveAsModel.help: Saves the displayed fit to the project models, new or as an update of the model saved last, so that other tools can use it. Without a converged fit or without values of the response nothing is saved.

predict.help: Computes the predicted response with confidence limits for the entered term values, as a probability for binomial and as an expected count for Poisson and negative binomial. The limits are missing when the fit does not carry them; if a term is left without a value or there is no result, there is no prediction.

params.values: An object with one number per term from predictionTerms; categorical predictors as 0/1 per dummy term. Missing terms leave the result null.

colRefs.help: The predictor columns X as column references, in order.

yKey.help: The response column as key instanceId|sheetId|columnId, or null.

trialsKey.help: The column with the number of trials per row (grouped binomial data), or null.

method.help: The chosen method: one of methods; 'auto' detects the family from the response.

methods.help: All methods setParam accepts for method.

confLevel.help: Confidence level as a fraction; alpha is 1 minus this value.

alpha.help: Significance level as a fraction; confLevel is 1 minus this value.

cutoff.help: Classification threshold for a binomial fit, from 0 to 1.

successClass.help: For a binary response the level counted as success (1) and the other one as failure; the button next to it swaps them. Empty without a binary response.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts now.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot (x, y, trials) the columns setColumns/setColumn accept, each { key, name }.

result.help: The fitted generalized linear model, each figure described individually under keys; null without a displayed fit.

classification.help: The confusion table at the cutoff, each figure described individually under keys; null without a binomial result.

errorMsg.help: The message of the last failed fit, '' without error.

predictionTerms.help: The terms a prediction takes, in model order (dummies and interactions included); [] without a shown fit.

savedModelId.help: Id of the model saved last in the project models, or null.

prediction.help: The last prediction as numbers (linear, response, ciLower, ciUpper), or null without a prediction, after a new fit or without a shown result.

Params.method: The distribution family, section Method: auto-detection, binomial (logistic regression with logit link), Poisson or negative binomial (both with log link). Auto-detection picks binomial when the response has exactly two levels; for non-negative integers negative binomial when variance/mean exceeds 2, otherwise Poisson; proportions between 0 and 1 are fitted binomially but need a column with the number of trials. A change recomputes.
Params.confLevel: The confidence level as a fraction between 0 and 1, so 0.95 rather than 95; the input shows it in percent. It sets the confidence limits of the coefficients, the ratios and the prediction. The significance level becomes 1 minus this value. A change recomputes.
Params.alpha: The significance level α as a fraction between 0 and 1, so 0.05 rather than 5; the input shows it in percent. The confidence level becomes 1 minus this value, and the confidence limits change accordingly. A change recomputes.
Params.cutoff: The classification cutoff between 0 and 1, default 0.5, set with the slider on the ROC / Classification tab: an observation counts as predicted 1 when its estimated probability reaches at least the cutoff. A new value only recounts the confusion table and its rates; the model is not refitted. Only available with a binomial result.

Result.family: The family actually fitted, with link function and, for negative binomial, the estimated θ; with auto-detection the family it chose.
Result.quasi: Whether quasi-Poisson is active: if the Poisson fit shows χ²/df above 1.5, it is refitted with the dispersion φ = Pearson χ²/df; the coefficients stay, standard errors and confidence intervals are widened by √φ, and a warning gives φ.
Result.autoReason: The reason for the automatic choice. It appears as a hint below the method while “Auto-Detect (recommended)” is chosen; the result holds the key of that hint text. Possible reasons: exactly two levels, count data, overdispersed count data, proportions without trials, or non-negative values as the fallback. Empty when a method is chosen explicitly.
Result.n: Number of rows used, row n: rows with finite values in Y, all X and, where given, the trials.
Result.iterations: Number of IRLS iterations until convergence, row IRLS Iterations; a high count points to a difficult fit such as separation.
Result.aic: Akaike information criterion, tile AIC: −2ℓ + 2k with the log-likelihood ℓ and k parameters (coefficients, plus θ for negative binomial). Smaller is better; only for comparing models of the same response.
Result.bic: Bayesian information criterion, tile BIC: −2ℓ + ln(n) · k; penalises extra parameters more than AIC. Smaller is better.
Result.deviance: Residual deviance: twice the log-likelihood gap to the saturated model. Compared with the null deviance it shows how much the predictors explain.
Result.nullDeviance: Null deviance: the deviance of the intercept-only model, the reference for residual deviance and pseudo-R².
Result.logLikelihood: The maximised log-likelihood ℓ of the model; the basis of AIC, BIC and the pseudo-R².
Result.pseudoR2: The three pseudo coefficients of determination McFadden, Nagelkerke and Cox-Snell, which compare the model's log-likelihood with that of the intercept-only model.
Result.coefficients: The coefficient table, one row per term, Intercept first, then the predictors; a categorical predictor gets one dummy row per level.
Result.auc: Area under the ROC curve, tile AUC, between 0 and 1: 0.5 is guessing, 1 a perfect separation. The tile is green from 0.8, yellow from 0.6, red below. Only with a binomial result, otherwise empty.
Result.hosmerLemeshow: Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test: the observations are split into 10 groups by estimated probability (fewer with little data, at least 4) and observed and expected events are compared by χ² with groups − 2 degrees of freedom; a small p-value speaks against the fit. With fewer than 20 observations (trials for grouped data) the test is skipped and then shows statistic 0 and p = 1. Only with a binomial result, otherwise empty.
Result.overdispersionRatio: χ²/df (Overdispersion): Pearson χ² divided by n − p; the same value as the ratio of the overdispersion check. Above 1.5 the Poisson fit counts as overdispersed. Only for Poisson, otherwise empty.
Result.overdispersion: The overdispersion check on the Diagnostics tab with Pearson χ², degrees of freedom and their ratio. Only for Poisson, otherwise empty.
Result.vif: Variance inflation factors of the predictors, table VIF, same order as vifTerms; the first value belongs to the first predictor after the intercept, i.e. the second row of the coefficient table. Above 5 the cell is marked, above 10 a warning is shown. Only with two or more predictor columns, otherwise empty; a single value is empty when it cannot be computed.
Result.vifTerms: The terms belonging to the values in vif, same order, column “Term” of the VIF table: the predictors after the intercept, i.e. the coefficient terms from the second row on. Empty when no VIF table appears.
Result.warnings: The warnings above the output, for example on separation, few events, slow convergence, overdispersion or quasi-Poisson. The texts are in the language of the interface.
Result.equation: The model equation as text, as shown under Model Equation: logit(p) for binomial, log(μ) for Poisson and negative binomial, equal to the intercept plus coefficient times term, rounded to four decimals.

Family.name: The distribution family: binomial, poisson or negbin; the row Family shows the translated name.
Family.link: The link function that connects the expected value to the linear predictor: logit for binomial, log for Poisson and negative binomial.
Family.theta: The estimated shape parameter θ, row θ (dispersion), of the negative binomial distribution, variance = μ + μ²/θ; a small θ means strong overdispersion. Only for negative binomial, otherwise empty.

PseudoR2.mcfadden: McFadden R², tile McFadden R²: 1 − ℓ/ℓ₀ with the log-likelihood ℓ of the model and ℓ₀ of the intercept-only model. The tile is green from 0.4, yellow from 0.2, red below; values from 0.2 to 0.4 already count as a good fit.
PseudoR2.nagelkerke: Nagelkerke R², tile Nagelkerke R²: the Cox-Snell R² divided by its largest possible value 1 − exp(2ℓ₀/n), so that it reaches 1. The tile is green from 0.8, yellow from 0.5, red below.
PseudoR2.coxSnell: Cox-Snell R²: 1 − exp(−2/n · (ℓ − ℓ₀)); does not always reach 1 even for a perfect fit.

GlmCoefficient.term: The term name: Intercept, a column name, or for categorical predictors one dummy term per level.
GlmCoefficient.estimate: The estimated coefficient b on the link scale (logit or log). The Coefficient column also shows the confidence interval next to it, from the lower to the upper limit.
GlmCoefficient.se: Standard error of the coefficient, column SE, from the inverse Fisher information; widened by √φ under quasi-Poisson.
GlmCoefficient.z: Wald z, column z: the coefficient divided by its standard error.
GlmCoefficient.p: Two-sided p-value of the Wald test of b = 0, 2 · (1 − Φ(|z|)); below α the term counts as significant and is highlighted.
GlmCoefficient.ciLower: Lower confidence limit b − z · SE, with z the (1 + confidence level)/2 quantile of the normal distribution.
GlmCoefficient.ciUpper: Upper confidence limit b + z · SE, with the same z as the lower limit.
GlmCoefficient.ratio: The ratio exp(b) with confidence limits, column OR for binomial (odds ratio) or RR for Poisson and negative binomial (rate ratio): the factor by which the odds or the rate change per unit of the predictor. Empty for the intercept.

Ratio.value: The ratio exp(b): odds ratio for binomial, rate ratio for Poisson and negative binomial; 1 means no effect.
Ratio.lower: Lower limit of the ratio, exp of the coefficient's lower confidence limit.
Ratio.upper: Upper limit of the ratio, exp of the coefficient's upper confidence limit.

HosmerLemeshow.statistic: The χ² statistic of the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, the sum over the groups of (observed − expected)² divided by the expected variance; 0 when the test was skipped.
