HosmerLemeshow.pValue: p-value of the Hosmer-Lemeshow test from the χ² distribution with groups − 2 degrees of freedom; below α it speaks against the fit. 1 when the test was skipped.

Overdispersion.pearsonChi2: Pearson χ²: the sum of the squared Pearson residuals of the Poisson fit, row Pearson χ².
Overdispersion.df: Degrees of freedom, row df: n − p, the number of observations minus the number of coefficients.
Overdispersion.ratio: The ratio χ²/df; under Poisson it should be close to 1.
Overdispersion.overdispersed: Whether overdispersion is detected: true when χ²/df is above 1.5; the hint towards negative binomial regression then appears and quasi-Poisson becomes active. Above 3 the computation counts it as severe, but that is not shown separately.

Classification.cutoff: The cutoff of the confusion table: predicted 1 when the estimated probability reaches at least the cutoff, otherwise predicted 0.
Classification.tp: True positives: actual 1 and predicted 1; for grouped data the trials are counted.
Classification.fn: False negatives: actual 1 but predicted 0; for grouped data the trials are counted.
Classification.fp: False positives: actual 0 but predicted 1; for grouped data the trials are counted.
Classification.tn: True negatives: actual 0 and predicted 0; for grouped data the trials are counted.
Classification.sensitivity: Sensitivity: true positives / (true positives + false negatives), the share of actual ones that are detected; 0 when there are none.
Classification.specificity: Specificity: true negatives / (true negatives + false positives), the share of actual zeros that are detected; 0 when there are none.
Classification.accuracy: Accuracy: (true positives + true negatives) / all, the share of correctly classified observations.
Classification.precision: Precision: true positives / (true positives + false positives), the share of real ones among those predicted as 1; 0 when nothing is predicted as 1.

glm-regression.name: Regression (Attributive)
glm-regression.description: Binary logistic, Poisson, and negative binomial regression for attributive/count data
glm-regression.autoDetectBinary: Response has exactly 2 values → binary logistic regression recommended.
glm-regression.autoDetectPoisson: Response is non-negative integer (count data) → Poisson regression recommended.
glm-regression.autoDetectNegbin: Response is count data with overdispersion (variance > mean) → negative binomial regression recommended.
glm-regression.autoDetectProportion: Response contains proportions (0–1) → binary logistic regression recommended.
glm-regression.autoDetectProportionAmbiguous: Response contains proportions in [0, 1]. Grouped binomial regression requires a trials column per observation; without it the likelihood is ill-defined.
glm-regression.autoDetectDefault: Response is non-negative → Poisson regression used as default.
glm-regression.qqTitle: Normal Q-Q Plot of Deviance Residuals
glm-regression.overdispersionHint: Overdispersion detected (χ²/df > 1.5). Consider using negative binomial regression instead of Poisson.
glm-regression.errorNoX: Please select at least one X variable.
glm-regression.errorTooFew: At least 3 valid data rows required.
glm-regression.errorTooFewForP: More data rows than model parameters required.
glm-regression.errorNotBinary: Binomial regression requires a binary response (exactly 2 distinct values).
glm-regression.errorNoConverge: IRLS did not converge. Try a different method or check data quality.
glm-regression.errorInvalidInput: Please enter valid numbers for all predictors.
glm-regression.warnSeparation: Possible separation detected — coefficients may be unreliable. Check data for predictors that perfectly separate Y.
glm-regression.warnSmallN: Small sample relative to number of parameters (n/p < 10). Results may be unreliable.
glm-regression.warnFewEvents: Few events per predictor (EPV = {epv} < 10). Coefficients and p-values may be biased.
glm-regression.warnSlowConverge: Model required many iterations to converge — may indicate poor conditioning.
glm-regression.warnOverdispersion: Overdispersion detected in Poisson model. Consider switching to negative binomial.
glm-regression.warnQuasiActivated: Quasi-Poisson active (φ = {phi}). Standard errors and confidence intervals were scaled by √φ.
glm-regression.warnSeparationStrong: Complete or quasi-complete separation detected. Coefficients and standard errors are unreliable — drop the separating predictor or merge classes.
glm-regression.warnThetaUnstable: θ estimate did not converge (θ = {theta}). Data are likely near-Poisson — switch the method to Poisson, or fix θ manually.
glm-regression.columnTrialsHint: Number of trials per observation (grouped binomial regression). Y is then read as success proportion.
glm-regression.errorProportionRange: Y must be a proportion in [0, 1] when a trials column is provided.
glm-regression.errorTrialsInvalid: Trial counts must be positive finite numbers (≥ 1).
glm-regression.predictCiUnavailable: Confidence interval unavailable — design matrix is singular.
glm-regression.swapSuccessTitle: Swap classes — flip success/failure and refit
glm-regression.saveAsModelHint: Persists the model project-wide. Selectable in the Response Optimizer.

lessons-learned.name: Lessons Learned
lessons-learned.deleteConfirm: Delete this lesson? This cannot be undone.
lessons-learned.noResults: No lessons match the current filter.
lessons-learned.fieldDescriptionPlaceholder: What exactly happened? What was the context?
lessons-learned.fieldRecommendationPlaceholder: What should be done differently next time?
lessons-learned.whenToUse: When the experiences of a project are to be recorded — what went well, what did not, the root cause and the recommendation with its actions; not for day-to-day task tracking and not for a root-cause analysis itself, which is what the task list and the 5-Why analysis are for.

addLesson.help: Adds a lesson and returns its id.

params.data: An object with title (required) and optionally category (success, problem or improve; default success), impact (high, medium or low; default medium), phase (a phase of the active cycle; default is its last one), owner, description, rootCause, recommendation and actions (a list of texts or of { text, done }). A value outside the named sets is an error, as is a missing object and an object that names no title; an empty title adds nothing and returns null — that is a refusal, not an error.

updateLesson.help: Changes the named fields of a lesson; all others stay as they are.

params.lessonId: The id of the lesson as read() lists it under lessons. An unknown id is an error.
params.data: An object holding exactly the fields that should change — title, category, impact, phase, owner, description, rootCause, recommendation or actions. Whatever is not in it stays unchanged. A value outside the named sets is an error, as is an object that names none of these fields; an empty title passed in changes nothing and returns false.

removeLesson.help: Removes a lesson together with its actions.

params.lessonId: The id of the lesson as read() lists it under lessons. An unknown id is an error.

addAction.help: Appends an action to a lesson.

params.lessonId: The id of the lesson as read() lists it under lessons. An unknown id is an error.
params.text: The text of the action; surrounding whitespace is dropped. An empty text adds nothing and returns -1 — that is a refusal, not an error; a missing argument is an error.

removeAction.help: Removes an action of a lesson; the remaining ones move up.

params.lessonId: The id of the lesson as read() lists it under lessons. An unknown id is an error.
params.actionIndex: The position of the action within the lesson, counted from 0. A position where the lesson holds no action is an error.

setActionDone.help: Ticks an action of a lesson off, or takes the tick back.

params.lessonId: The id of the lesson as read() lists it under lessons. An unknown id is an error.
params.actionIndex: The position of the action within the lesson, counted from 0. A position where the lesson holds no action is an error.
params.done: true ticks the action off, false takes the tick back. Any other value — a missing argument included — is an error.

lessons.help: The recorded lessons in the order they were added, each entry described individually under keys.

LessonEntry.id: The identifier of the lesson; the app assigns it when the lesson is created. Use it to address the lesson when changing or deleting.
LessonEntry.title: The title of the lesson, shown as the heading on the card. It is the only required entry; without a title nothing is saved. Spaces at the edges are removed.
LessonEntry.category: The kind of lesson: Success (success), Problem (problem) or Improvement (improve); Success when not given. The coloured dot on the card and the filters above the list follow it. An unknown value from an import becomes Success.
LessonEntry.phase: The phase of the cycle the lesson belongs to; the phases of the active cycle count, the last one when not given. It is shown as a tag on the card.
LessonEntry.impact: The effect of the lesson on the project in three levels: High (high), Medium (medium) or Low (low); Medium when not given. It is shown as a badge on the card. An unknown value from an import becomes Medium.
LessonEntry.owner: Who is responsible for the lesson, as free text. May stay empty.
LessonEntry.description: What happened, in your own words and as free text. May stay empty.
LessonEntry.rootCause: Why it happened: the cause behind the success or the problem, as free text. May stay empty.
LessonEntry.recommendation: What future projects should do or avoid, as free text. May stay empty.
LessonEntry.actions: The actions that follow from the lesson, as a list; each has a text and a tick for done. The open actions of all lessons are counted by the figure “Open Actions”.
LessonEntry.createdAt: When the lesson was created, as a timestamp in milliseconds; the app sets it. The cards are sorted by it, newest first.
LessonEntry.updatedAt: When the lesson was last changed, as a timestamp in milliseconds; the app sets it on every change, including ticking off an action.

LessonAction.done: Whether the action is done; you tick it off on the card.

calculator.name: Calculator
calculator.description: Scientific calculator with statistics and 6σ mode
calculator.processDataLabel: Process data (add values with Enter or +)
calculator.whenToUse: When a number, a statistic or a process capability has to be computed quickly without setting up a data collection — scientifically, as a location and spread measure over a short list of values, or as Cp/Cpk, sigma level and DPMO from values and specification limits; not for a lasting analysis over a data table, that is what the data collection, the histogram and the process capability analysis are for.

inputText.help: Appends a character or a number to the input line.

params.ch: A character of the input line — a digit, a dot, + - × ÷ ^ ( ) π or e — or a number in decimal notation. Any other value is an error.

inputFn.help: Appends a function together with its opening bracket to the input line.

params.fn: The function with its opening bracket, exactly as the keypad writes it: sin(, cos(, tan(, asin(, acos(, atan(, log(, ln(, sqrt(, cbrt(, exp( or fact(. Any other value is an error.

backspace.help: Deletes the last character of the input line.

clear.help: Clears the input line and the last result.

setAngleMode.help: The DEG/RAD key toggles the angle unit of the trigonometric functions between degrees and radians. The agent sets the unit directly: DEG calculates in degrees, RAD in radians.

params.mode: DEG computes in degrees, RAD in radians. Any other value is an error.

memStore.help: Stores the displayed value in memory — the last result, otherwise the evaluated input line.

params.value: The new memory value; 0 means empty. A value that is not a finite number is an error.

memRecall.help: Appends the memory value to the input line.

switchMode.help: Switches between the tabs Scientific, Statistics and 6 Sigma and clears the input line.

params.m: sci computes scientifically, stats evaluates the statistics data set, sixsigma the process data set. Any other value is an error.

calculate.help: Evaluates the input line and remembers the result. If it holds no computable expression, the last result stays.

calcStat.help: Computes a statistic over the statistics data set and remembers it as the last result. If the data set is empty, too small or has no mode, the call returns null.

params.type: Which statistic; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.

calcSS.help: Computes a metric over the process data set and remembers it as the last result. Without enough values or without both spec limits the call returns null.

params.type: Which statistic; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.

addData.help: Takes the input line as a value into the statistics data set. If it does not start with a number, the data set stays unchanged.

addDataValue.help: Appends a number to the statistics data set and clears the input line.

params.value: The value, as a number or as a number in decimal notation. Any other value is an error.

removeLast.help: Removes the last value of the statistics data set.

addSSData.help: Takes the input line as a value into the process data set. If it does not start with a number, the data set stays unchanged.

addSSDataValue.help: Appends a number to the process data set and clears the input line.

params.value: The value, as a number or as a number in decimal notation. Any other value is an error.

removeLastSS.help: Removes the last value of the process data set.

params.value: The limit as a number or as text; empty text clears it. A value that is neither empty nor a finite number is an error.
The limit as a number or as text; empty text clears it. A value that is neither empty nor a finite number is an error.

mode.help: The active calculator area: sci scientific, stats statistics, sixsigma process capability.

expression.help: The input line as shown in the display. Empty means nothing entered.

lastResult.help: The result of the last computation as a number; null while there is none.

memory.help: The memory value. 0 means empty — the display then shows no M.

angleMode.help: The angle unit of the trigonometric functions: DEG degrees, RAD radians.

dataset.help: The values of the statistics area in the order they were entered. They are filled via "+ Value"; the statistic keys (mean, standard deviation, etc.) calculate on them.

ssDataset.help: The values of the process area in the order they were entered. They are filled via "+ Value"; the process keys (sigma level, DPMO, etc.) calculate on them.

lsl.help: The lower specification limit as text, exactly as entered; empty means not set.

usl.help: The upper specification limit as text, exactly as entered; empty means not set.

StatKey.mean: Mean x̄ key: the sum of all values in the statistics dataset divided by their count, x̄ = Σx/n.
StatKey.median: Median x̃ key: the middle value of the values sorted ascending; with an even count, the average of the two middle values.
StatKey.mode: Mode key: the value that occurs most often. On a tie all most frequent values appear, separated by commas. If every value occurs only once (also with a single value) there is no mode, and the display says so in a message.
StatKey.range: Range key: the largest value minus the smallest value of the dataset.
StatKey.stdS: s (sample) key: the sample standard deviation s = √(Σ(x − x̄)²/(n − 1)), divided by n − 1. Needs at least 2 values, otherwise the message “n ≥ 2 required” appears.
StatKey.stdP: σ (population) key: the population standard deviation σ = √(Σ(x − x̄)²/n), divided by n instead of n − 1. With a single value it is 0.
StatKey.varS: s² variance key: the sample variance s² = Σ(x − x̄)²/(n − 1), the square of the sample standard deviation. Needs at least 2 values, otherwise the message “n ≥ 2 required” appears.
StatKey.varP: σ² variance key: the population variance σ² = Σ(x − x̄)²/n, the square of the population standard deviation, divided by n instead of n − 1.
StatKey.sum: Σ sum key: the sum of all values in the dataset.
StatKey.min: Min key: the smallest value of the dataset.
StatKey.max: Max key: the largest value of the dataset.
StatKey.count: n count key: the number of values in the dataset, as the n line under the value list shows it.
StatKey.q1: Q1 key: the lower quartile, the 25 % quantile. The values are sorted and, at position (n − 1) · 0.25, linearly interpolated between the two neighbouring values; this is the same method as Excel (QUARTILE.INC).
StatKey.q3: Q3 key: the upper quartile, the 75 % quantile. The values are sorted and, at position (n − 1) · 0.75, linearly interpolated between the two neighbouring values; this is the same method as Excel (QUARTILE.INC).
StatKey.iqr: IQR key: the interquartile range, Q3 − Q1, using the linearly interpolated quartiles of the Q1 and Q3 keys.
StatKey.skew: Skewness key: the sample skewness n/((n − 1)(n − 2)) · Σ((x − x̄)/s)³ with the sample standard deviation s; 0 for symmetric data, positive for right-skewed. Needs at least 3 values, otherwise the message “n ≥ 3 required” appears.

CapabilityKey.cp: Cp key: the process capability index Cp = (USL − LSL)/(6 · σ within), the tolerance width over six standard deviations. σ within is the average moving range of neighbouring values divided by 1.128, taken in entry order. Needs at least 2 values and both limits LSL and USL, otherwise “Data + LSL/USL required” appears. The target is not used.
CapabilityKey.cpk: Cpk key: the centred capability index Cpk = min((USL − x̄)/(3σ), (x̄ − LSL)/(3σ)) with σ within (average moving range divided by 1.128, in entry order). It measures the distance from the mean to the nearer limit. Needs at least 2 values and both limits LSL and USL.
CapabilityKey.pp: Pp key: the overall performance index Pp = (USL − LSL)/(6 · s), with the sample standard deviation s of all values (divided by n − 1), that is the overall spread rather than the within spread. Needs at least 2 values and both limits LSL and USL.
CapabilityKey.ppk: Ppk key: the centred overall performance index Ppk = min((USL − x̄)/(3s), (x̄ − LSL)/(3s)) with the sample standard deviation s of all values (divided by n − 1). Needs at least 2 values and both limits LSL and USL.
CapabilityKey.sigma: Sigma-Level key: the benchmark Z (Z.bench) = −Φ⁻¹(p), where p is the fraction outside the limits, both tails together, under a normal distribution with mean x̄ and σ within (average moving range divided by 1.128). No 1.5 σ shift is added. Needs at least 2 values and both limits LSL and USL.
CapabilityKey.dpmo: DPMO key: defects per million opportunities, (P(X < LSL) + P(X > USL)) · 1,000,000, rounded to a whole number. The probabilities come from a normal distribution with mean x̄ and the sample standard deviation s of all values (overall spread). Needs at least 2 values and both limits LSL and USL.
CapabilityKey.yield: Yield % key: the expected fraction within specification, P(LSL ≤ X ≤ USL) · 100 as a percentage with four decimals. The probability comes from a normal distribution with mean x̄ and the sample standard deviation s of all values (overall spread); it is 1 minus the defect fraction of the DPMO key. Needs at least 2 values and both limits LSL and USL.
CapabilityKey.zscore: Z-Score key: −Φ⁻¹(defect fraction), the normal-distribution distance that matches the total fraction outside the limits (both tails together, as for DPMO, with mean x̄ and the sample standard deviation s of all values). No 1.5 σ shift is added. Needs at least 2 values and both limits LSL and USL.
CapabilityKey.mean: x̄ Mean key: the mean of the process dataset, Σx/n. Needs at least 1 value, otherwise “Data required” appears.
CapabilityKey.std: σ Std.Dev. key: the sample standard deviation s = √(Σ(x − x̄)²/(n − 1)) of the process dataset (overall spread, not the within spread). Needs at least 2 values, otherwise “n ≥ 2 required” appears.
CapabilityKey.ucl: UCL key: the upper control limit x̄ + 3 · s with the sample standard deviation s of all values of the process dataset. Needs at least 2 values; the specification limits are not used.
CapabilityKey.lcl: LCL key: the lower control limit x̄ − 3 · s with the sample standard deviation s of all values of the process dataset. Needs at least 2 values; the specification limits are not used.

data-transformation.whenToUse: When non-normal measurements should be transformed for a method that assumes normality — Box-Cox, Yeo-Johnson, Johnson, logarithm, square root, reciprocal, square — and the result is reused as a new column. Requires the measurements as a numeric column of a data collection (at least three values).

read.help: Returns the transformation, the source, the parameters, the selectable sets and the result. result is null while there is no calculation.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

selectTF.help: Chooses the transformation and calculates at once. For Box-Cox and Yeo-Johnson, λ is optimized again for the source.

params.id: One of the transformations in transforms; any other value is an error.

setColumn.help: Points the transformation at a numeric column of a data collection and calculates at once; for Box-Cox and Yeo-Johnson, λ is optimized again.

params.slot: One of the slots in activeColumnSlots; this module only has 'source'.
params.ref: Column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns, or null to clear.

setParam.help: Sets one parameter of the current transformation; the calculation follows after a short pause. Values outside the range are rejected, not clamped.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: A number within the range from activeParams; text containing a number is accepted.

runAnalysis.help: Calculates the transformation with the current source and parameters. Fewer than three finite values leave result at null.

toWorksheet.help: Sends the transformed series to a new worksheet, into an existing column (replacing its values) or as a new column to an existing sheet and returns the receiving worksheet. Without a result nothing is sent and nothing is returned.

params.target: null for a new worksheet, otherwise a column reference from targetColumns; columnId '__new__' appends a new column to the sheet.

currentTF.help: The chosen transformation, one of the ids in transforms.

columnRef.help: The chosen source column as { instanceId, sheetId, columnId }, or null.

params.help: The parameters of the chosen transformation, each described under keys; empty for transformations without parameters.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state, each with its range.

activeColumnSlots.help: The slots setColumn accepts in the current state.

pickableColumns.help: Per slot the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'.

targetColumns.help: The targets toWorksheet accepts, each { key, name }: per sheet its columns followed by an entry with columnId '__new__' (name is the sheet name) that appends a new column; a null target creates a new worksheet.

result.help: Statistics before and after the transformation, each figure described individually under keys; null without a column, with fewer than 3 values or when the transformation fails on the data (errorMsg gives the reason).

errorMsg.help: The message the module gives when the calculation fails, otherwise empty.

Params.lambda: The exponent λ, label Lambda (λ), range −5 to 5. Box-Cox computes (x^λ − 1)/λ, and ln x at λ = 0, for values > 0 only; Yeo-Johnson computes ((x + 1)^λ − 1)/λ for x ≥ 0 (ln(x + 1) at λ = 0) and −((1 − x)^(2 − λ) − 1)/(2 − λ) for x < 0 (−ln(1 − x) at λ = 2). λ is estimated when Box-Cox or Yeo-Johnson is chosen and at least 3 values are present, and for every new column: the grid from −3 to 3 in steps of 0.05 is searched and the λ with the smallest corrected Anderson-Darling A² is chosen, rounded to 0.01. Before the first estimate Box-Cox uses λ = 0 and Yeo-Johnson λ = 1. If the column contains values ≤ 0, Box-Cox switches to Yeo-Johnson with a notice.
Params.gamma: The shift γ of the Johnson transformation, label γ, range −5 to 5, default 0. Johnson SU (unbounded) computes γ + δ·asinh((x − ξ)/λ), Johnson SB (bounded) γ + δ·ln(z/(1 − z)) with z = (x − ξ)/λ. γ is not estimated but set by hand.
Params.delta: The shape factor δ of the Johnson transformation, label δ, range 0.1 to 10, default 1; it multiplies the asinh term (SU, unbounded) or the ln term (SB, bounded) in γ + δ·asinh((x − ξ)/λ) or γ + δ·ln(z/(1 − z)). δ is not estimated but set by hand.
Params.xi: The location ξ of the Johnson transformation, label ξ, range −100 to 100, default 0; it is subtracted from every value before scaling, z = (x − ξ)/λ. Johnson SU (unbounded) accepts any values. For Johnson SB (bounded) all values must lie strictly between ξ and ξ + λ, a value exactly on a limit does not suffice; otherwise the calculation fails with “Johnson SB: data must lie within (ξ, ξ+λ)”. ξ is not estimated but set by hand.
Params.lambdaJ: The scale λ of the Johnson transformation, label λ, range 0.1 to 100, default 1; values are divided by it, z = (x − ξ)/λ. For Johnson SB (bounded), ξ + λ is the upper limit that no value may reach; Johnson SU (unbounded) has no limit. λ is not estimated but set by hand; not to be confused with the λ of Box-Cox and Yeo-Johnson.

Result.n: Number of values, row n of the Descriptive Statistics: the finite numbers of the source column; empty and non-numeric cells do not count. With fewer than 3 values there is no result. The transformation keeps the number of values.
Result.transform: The transformation the result was computed with, one of the ids in transforms. It equals currentTF unless the choice or the parameters changed since the last run and the run is still pending.
Result.params: A copy of the parameters the result was computed with, keyed as described under params: lambda for Box-Cox and Yeo-Johnson; gamma, delta, xi and lambdaJ for Johnson SU and Johnson SB; an empty object for Log, Square root, Inverse and Square. Later changes to the inputs do not alter it.
Result.original: The statistics of the source column before the transformation, column Original of the Descriptive Statistics and row Original of the normality test.
Result.transformed: The statistics of the series after the transformation with the current parameters, column Transformed of the Descriptive Statistics and row Transformed of the normality test.

Descriptives.mean: The arithmetic mean x̄ = Σx/n, row Mean; the table shows 4 decimal places.
Descriptives.std: The sample standard deviation s = √(Σ(x − x̄)²/(n − 1)), row Std. Dev.; empty when it cannot be computed, the table then shows a dash.
Descriptives.median: The median, the middle value of the sorted series or the mean of the two middle values for an even count, row Median.
Descriptives.skewness: The sample skewness n/((n − 1)(n − 2)) · Σ((x − x̄)/s)³, row Skewness; 0 for symmetric data, positive for right-skewed data. Empty when all values are equal (s = 0).
Descriptives.kurtosis: The sample excess kurtosis, row Kurtosis (Excess): n(n + 1)/((n − 1)(n − 2)(n − 3)) · Σ((x − x̄)/s)⁴ − 3(n − 1)²/((n − 2)(n − 3)); 0 corresponds to the normal distribution. Empty with exactly 3 values or when all values are equal; the table then shows a dash.
Descriptives.min: The smallest value of the series, row Min.
Descriptives.max: The largest value of the series, row Max.
Descriptives.adStatAdj: The corrected Anderson-Darling A²* = A²·(1 + 0.75/n + 2.25/n²), shown in the normality test row as A² = … with 4 decimals. The larger the value, the further the series departs from the normal distribution. Empty when all values are equal; the verdict is then missing as well.
Descriptives.adPValue: The p-value of the Anderson-Darling test for normality, section Normality Test (Anderson-Darling), shown as p ≈ next to A². The A² shown is already the corrected A²* = A²·(1 + 0.75/n + 2.25/n²); p follows from it after D'Agostino and Stephens. The display judges with α = 0.05: p ≥ 0.05 means Normal, p < 0.05 Not normal. Empty when all values are equal; the verdict is then missing as well.
Descriptives.normal: The verdict of the normality test: yes (Normal) when the p-value is at least α = 0.05, no (Not normal) when it is below. It is the badge after p ≈ in the normality test row. Empty when all values are equal.

data-transformation.name: Data Transformation
data-transformation.description: Transform data (Box-Cox, Johnson, Log, …) for normality
data-transformation.warnBoxCoxFallback: Data contains values ≤ 0 — automatically switched to Yeo-Johnson
data-transformation.errJohnsonSBRange: Johnson SB: data must lie within (ξ, ξ+λ)

unit-converter.name: Unit Converter
unit-converter.whenToUse: When a measured value has to be expressed in another unit — length, area, volume, mass, pressure, temperature, force, torque, energy, power, flow rate, speed, time, angle, rotational speed, pH, concentration, sound or lab values — or when a time has to be converted between two time zones; not for converting a whole data column, that is what the data transformation is for.

read.help: Returns the settings and the selectable units.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

selectCategory.help: Switches the quantity category and resets both units to its defaults.

params.catKey: The key of the category: laenge (length), flaeche (area), volumen, masse (mass), druck (pressure), temperatur, kraft (force), drehmoment (torque), energie, leistung (power), durchfluss (flow rate), geschwindigkeit (speed), zeit (time), winkel (angle), drehzahl (rotational speed), ph, konzentration, schall (sound) or laborwerte (lab values). Any other value is an error.

setFromUnit.help: Sets the unit converted from, and pulls the target unit along when it no longer fits.

params.unitKey: The key of a unit of the active category, as read() reports it under fromUnit. A unit of another category is an error; the error message names the allowed keys.
The key of a unit that fits the source unit. For lab values those are only the units of the same group; any other is an error, and the error message names the allowed keys.

setInputValue.help: Sets the value that is converted.

params.text: The value as text; a comma counts as the decimal separator, empty text clears the entry. Text that is not a number is not an error — nothing is converted then. A missing argument is an error.

swapUnits.help: Swaps the source and the target unit.

params.index: The position of the time zone in the time-zone list, from 0; 0 is UTC, 1 Berlin. Any other value is an error, and the error message names the allowed positions.
The position of the time zone in the time-zone list, from 0; 0 is UTC, 1 Berlin. Any other value is an error, and the error message names the allowed positions.

setTzTime.help: Sets the time that is converted.

params.hhmm: The time as HH:MM from 00:00 to 23:59; empty text clears it. Any other value is an error.

setTzDate.help: Sets the date the conversion refers to.

params.isoDate: The date as YYYY-MM-DD; empty text clears it. Any other value is an error.

swapTimezones.help: Swaps the source and the target time zone.

tzSetNow.help: Sets time and date to the current moment in the source time zone. If the source time zone is unknown, both stay unchanged.

unitKeys.help: The unit keys of the active category — exactly the values setFromUnit accepts.

toUnitKeys.help: The unit keys setToUnit accepts for the current source unit; they depend on fromUnit.

activeCat.help: The key of the active quantity category, e.g. laenge (length) or masse (mass).

fromUnit.help: From: the unit converted from; the value to convert is entered below it. The agent reads the unit key of the active category here.

toUnit.help: To: the unit converted to; the result is shown below it and the agent reads it under result. The agent reads the unit key of the active category here.

inputVal.help: The entered value as text; a comma counts as the decimal separator. Empty means nothing entered. The converted result is read under result.

tzFrom.help: From Timezone: the source time zone, whose time and date are entered below it. The agent reads the position in the time-zone list here; 0 is UTC, 1 Berlin.

tzTo.help: To Timezone: the target time zone, in which the converted result appears below it. The agent reads the position in the time-zone list here; 0 is UTC, 1 Berlin.

tzTime.help: The time of the conversion as HH:MM; empty means not set.

tzDate.help: The date of the conversion as YYYY-MM-DD; empty means not set.

result.help: The result of the unit conversion, each entry described individually under keys. It is shown below the To unit and changes with the input and the units.

timezone.help: The result of the time-zone conversion, each entry described individually under keys. While the time or the date is missing, it is empty.

ConversionResult.value: The converted result as a number, unrounded, as the calculation returns it. Empty when no number is entered or the conversion is not defined for this value.
ConversionResult.text: The result as shown below the To unit: rounded and with a decimal point. A dash while nothing is entered; "undefined" when the conversion is not defined for the value.
ConversionResult.formula: The conversion formula as shown under "Formula", for example "1 bar = 100000 Pa", that is the value of one From unit in the To unit. For logarithmic quantities it reads "logarithmic conversion" with both units; a dash while nothing is entered.

TimezoneResult.text: The converted time in the target time zone as shown under "To Timezone", for example "08:45". A dash while the time or the date is missing.
TimezoneResult.dateText: The date of the converted time with the weekday, as shown below the time; it can differ from the entered date when the conversion crosses midnight. Empty while the time or the date is missing.
TimezoneResult.diffHours: The time difference of the target zone from the source zone in hours, as shown under "Difference": positive when the target zone is later, with fractions for half hours (5.5 for five and a half hours). It accounts for daylight saving at the entered date. Empty while the time or the date is missing.

triz-contradiction-matrix.name: Contradiction Matrix (TRIZ)
triz-contradiction-matrix.whenToUse: When two different engineering characteristics are in conflict — improving one degrades the other — and the matrix should name the proven solution principles for that pair; not when a single characteristic itself would have to hold two opposite values, which is what the physical contradiction is for.

setImproving.help: Sets the characteristic that is to be improved.

params.param: The number of the characteristic from the list of 39 engineering characteristics, 1 to 39 (1 weight of moving object through 39 productivity). A number no characteristic carries is an error; null clears the choice.

setWorsening.help: Sets the characteristic that degrades while improving the other.

params.param: The number of the characteristic from the list of 39 engineering characteristics, 1 to 39 (1 weight of moving object through 39 productivity). A number no characteristic carries is an error; null clears the choice.

setProblemNote.help: Sets the problem note for the contradiction.

params.text: The problem note; an empty text clears it.

setShowMatrix.help: Shows the full 39×39 contradiction matrix or hides it. The value sets the state; it does not toggle.

params.visible: true shows the matrix, false hides it.

swapParams.help: Swaps the improving and the degrading characteristic against each other.

improving.help: The number of the characteristic to be improved (1 to 39), or null while none is chosen.

worsening.help: The number of the characteristic that degrades while improving the other (1 to 39), or null while none is chosen.

problemNote.help: The problem note for the contradiction.

showMatrix.help: Whether the full 39×39 matrix is shown. A persisted display state — it belongs to the saved project, not to the analysis.

triz-contradiction-matrix.subtitle: Pick a parameter to improve and a parameter that worsens — the matrix recommends inventive principles.
triz-contradiction-matrix.problemPlaceholder: e.g. The support structure must become stronger — but then becomes too heavy.
triz-contradiction-matrix.hintSelectBoth: Pick both parameters to see recommendations.
triz-contradiction-matrix.warnSameParameter: Improving and worsening parameters are identical — no contradiction.
triz-contradiction-matrix.noContradiction: No recommendation registered for this combination in the standard matrix.
triz-contradiction-matrix.matrixLegend: Row = improving (↑), column = worsening (↓). Cell number = count of recommended principles. Click a cell to apply the selection.

triz-9-windows.name: 9 Windows (TRIZ System Operator)
triz-9-windows.description: Examine the system on time × hierarchy axes
triz-9-windows.whenToUse: When a problem is to be looked at in its context — three system levels by three time windows — to find causes and solution spaces outside the system itself; not to follow a single chain of causes, which is what 5-why or Ishikawa are for.

setSystemTitle.help: Sets the title of the system under study.

params.text: The system title; an empty text clears the field.

setCellText.help: Writes the text of one of the nine cells of the matrix.

params.row: The row, 0 to 2: 0 subsystem, 1 system, 2 supersystem. Any other value, or a non-integer, is an error.
params.col: The column, 0 to 2: 0 past, 1 present, 2 future. Any other value, or a non-integer, is an error.
params.text: The cell text; an empty text clears it.

setColLabel.help: Labels a column of the time axis.

params.col: The column, 0 to 2: 0 past, 1 present, 2 future. Any other value, or a non-integer, is an error.
params.text: The column label; an empty text brings back the default label.

setRowLabel.help: Labels a row of the system levels.

params.row: The row, 0 to 2: 0 subsystem, 1 system, 2 supersystem. Any other value, or a non-integer, is an error.
params.text: The row label; an empty text brings back the default label.

clearImage.help: Clears the image of a cell; the cell text stays.

params.row: The row, 0 to 2: 0 subsystem, 1 system, 2 supersystem. Any other value, or a non-integer, is an error.
params.col: The column, 0 to 2: 0 past, 1 present, 2 future. Any other value, or a non-integer, is an error.

systemTitle.help: The title of the system under study.

colLabels.help: The three column labels of the time axis, in the order past, present, future. An empty entry means the column shows its default label.

rowLabels.help: The three row labels of the system levels, in the order subsystem, system, supersystem. An empty entry means the row shows its default label.

cells.help: The nine cells, addressed as cells[row][col] with three rows and three columns each. triz-physical-contradiction.name: Physical Contradiction (TRIZ)
triz-physical-contradiction.description: One parameter must be A and ¬A — resolution via four separation principles
triz-physical-contradiction.whenToUse: When a single parameter would have to hold two opposite values at the same time and the contradiction is to be resolved by separation in time, space, condition or system level — not for a contradiction between two different characteristics, which is what the contradiction matrix is for.

setParameter.help: Sets the technical parameter that has to carry both opposing requirements.

params.text: Name of the parameter, for example wing length or hardness; an empty text clears the field.

setRequirementA.help: Sets requirement A — one side of the contradiction.

params.text: Requirement A together with its rationale; an empty text clears the field.

setRequirementNotA.help: Sets requirement not-A — the opposite side of the contradiction.

params.text: The opposing requirement together with its rationale; an empty text clears the field.

setProblemNote.help: Sets the problem note: why both requirements are impossible at the same time.

params.text: The problem note; an empty text clears it.

setSolutionNote.help: Sets the solution note for the chosen separation principle.

params.text: The solution note; an empty text clears it.

setPrincipleNote.help: Sets the note for one of the four separation principles.

params.key: Which separation principle; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.text: The note for that principle; an empty text clears it.

selectPrinciple.help: Chooses the separation principle that resolves the contradiction; only then does a solution note make sense.

params.key: The separation principle: time, space, condition or system (system level). null clears the choice; any other value is an error.

swap.help: Swaps the two opposing requirements against each other.

parameter.help: The technical parameter that has to carry both opposing requirements.

requirementA.help: Requirement A — one side of the contradiction.

requirementNotA.help: Requirement not-A — the opposite side of the contradiction.

problemNote.help: The problem note: why both requirements are impossible at the same time.

principleNotes.help: One note per separation principle, addressed as principleNotes[principle]. The four keys are time, space, condition and system (system level).

selectedPrinciple.help: The chosen separation principle (time, space, condition or system) or null while none is chosen.

solutionNote.help: The solution note for the chosen separation principle.

PrincipleNotes.time: Note on separation in time: the parameter takes different values at different times, for example a wing that is extended for take-off and retracted in cruise. It records how this fits the problem.
PrincipleNotes.space: Note on separation in space: the parameter takes different values at different places, for example a screw with a hard head and an elastic shaft. It records how this fits the problem.
PrincipleNotes.condition: Note on separation by condition: the parameter takes different values depending on load, temperature or speed, for example photochromic glasses that are dark in sunlight and clear in shade. It records how this fits the problem.
PrincipleNotes.system: Note on separation at the system level: the whole behaves differently from its parts, for example a bicycle chain that is flexible as a whole while its individual links are rigid. It records how this fits the problem.

time.name: Separation in time
time.question: Can the parameter take different values at different moments?
time.example: Folding wing — long for take-off, short at cruise. Also: landing gear, airbag, saw blade (cut vs. return stroke).

space.name: Separation in space
space.question: Can the parameter take different values in different regions of the system?
space.example: Screw — hard head, elastic shaft. Also: drill bit sharp at the tip, progressive eyeglass lenses.

condition.name: Separation on condition
condition.question: Can the parameter take different values depending on load, temperature, speed, user …?
condition.example: Non-Newtonian fluid — liquid at rest, solid under impact. Also: photochromic glasses, memory foam, ABS.

system.name: Separation between system levels
system.question: Does the contradiction dissolve when you switch between sub-, system and supersystem?
system.example: Bicycle chain — flexible as a whole, rigid in each link. Also: stranded wire (thin threads, thick strand), sandwich composites.

example.requirementA: long — for high lift at take-off and slow flight
example.requirementNotA: short — for low drag at cruise
example.problemNote: Classical textbook example. The contradiction matrix gives no clear advice here because the same parameter contradicts itself.

principleNotes.time: Variable geometry: wing extended for take-off, retracted at cruise (swing wing — F-14, B-1).
principleNotes.space: Inner wing long (lift), wingtips short and swept (drag) — swept wings, winglets.
principleNotes.condition: Flaps / slats deployed only at low speed (speed-dependent).
principleNotes.system: Smaller main wing plus a separate high-lift subsystem (flaps, slats) as its own subsystem.

example.solutionNote: Swing-wing mechanism: an actuator sets the effective span per flight phase. Plus flaps for transitions (condition separation).

triz-evolution-trends.name: Trends of Technical Evolution (TRIZ)
triz-evolution-trends.description: Eight classical evolution trajectories — locate the system and identify the next stage jump
triz-evolution-trends.whenToUse: When the question is where a system sits on the classical evolution trajectories and which stage jump comes next — not to resolve a specific contradiction or pick a variant.

params.stage: The stage reached, zero-based. -1 clears the classification; any other value outside this trend's scale is an error. dynamism has five stages (0 to 4); aggregation, scale, automation, completeness, controllability and matching have four each (0 to 3); uneven has none.

setTrendNotes.help: Sets a trend's note — what the placement means for this system in concrete terms and which step comes next.

aggregation.name: Aggregation
aggregation.description: A system evolves from a single element to several, then many, finally an integrated whole.
stages: Mono — a single element performs the function.
Bi — two similar elements cooperate.
Poly — many similar or diverse elements.
Integrated system — the elements functionally merge into one unit.

dynamism.name: Dynamism
dynamism.description: Rigid systems become increasingly mobile — up to dissolution into a field.
stages: Rigid — fixed shape, no motion.
Jointed — discrete joints enable single degrees of freedom.
Elastic — continuous deformation (springs, membranes).
Fluid / powdery — formless, freely flowing.
Field — the mechanical substance disappears, a field acts (magnetic, electric, acoustic …).

scale.name: Scale
scale.description: The working level of the system shifts to ever smaller structures.
stages: Macro — parts in cm to m range.
Meso — structures in mm range.
Micro — μm structures (MEMS, microfluidics).
Nano / molecular — direct manipulation of individual molecules / atoms.

automation.name: Automation
automation.description: Human intervention is progressively replaced by machine, control loop, and finally autonomy.
stages: Manual — human operates directly.
Mechanised — tool amplifies human force / precision.
Automatic — fixed sequence without intervention in normal operation.
Autonomous — system decides on its own, learns, adapts.

completeness.name: Completeness
completeness.description: A technical system gradually internalises all four sub-functions: engine / transmission / tool / control.
stages: Tool — passive component, external energy source.
+ Transmission — power transmission integrated.
+ Engine — energy conversion on board.
+ Control — complete system with feedback loop.

controllability.name: Controllability
controllability.description: From open, uncalibrated operation to learning feedback loops.
stages: Open loop — no feedback, fixed set-point.
Measured — sensor delivers actual value, operator corrects.
Adaptive control — closed loop adjusts actuation automatically.
Smart — learning loop, model-predictive, context-aware.

matching.name: Niche matching
matching.description: From universal mass product to self-adapting system.
stages: Universal — one size fits all.
Adjustable — discrete settings chosen by the user.
Individually fitted — custom-made per user / application.
Self-adapting — system adjusts to user / environment automatically.

uneven.name: Uneven development
uneven.description: Which subsystem lags and limits the whole? The classical bottleneck phenomenon.
uneven.notesPlaceholder: Which component is at an older stage than the rest and thereby blocks the jump on another trend?

aggregation.notes: Today: LED matrix (poly). Next stage: integrated lighting system with front + side-light coupling through a shared sensor suite.

dynamism.notes: Today: swivel modules (jointed). Next stage: elastically deformable light source / OLED foil, then a field solution (laser phosphor).

scale.notes: Today: meso (mm-scale LEDs). Next stage: micro-LED arrays for pixel-precise light distribution.

automation.notes: Today: automatic (sensor switch, high-beam assist). Next stage: autonomous lighting that masks individual road users.

completeness.notes: Complete (energy + transmission + light source + control). Trend saturated — progress shifts to other lines.

controllability.notes: Adaptive control (curve light, speed, oncoming traffic). Next stage: learning / context-aware (weather data, map topography).

matching.notes: Adjustable (level correction, drive mode). Next stage: individual lighting signature per driver, then self-adapting to vision profile.

uneven.notes: The on-board electrical system (12 V architecture) is at 1980s level — limits power and switching speed of modern LED matrix systems.

params.mode: auto shows only the classes matching the diagnosis, all shows all five. Any other value is an error.

setClassExpanded.help: Expands or collapses a class of standard solutions.

params.cls: The number of the standard class, 1 to 5. Any other number is an error.

s1.help: Substance S1 — the substance that exerts the action.

s2.help: Substance S2 — the substance being acted upon.

field.help: The field type between the substances: M, A, T, C, E or Mg; empty while none is chosen.

link.help: The link between the substances: useful, insufficient, excessive, harmful or missing; empty while none is chosen.

problemNote.help: The problem note for the substance-field model.

notes.help: One note per annotated standard solution, addressed as notes[id] with the id in the form class.group.number (for example 2.2.5). Only standard solutions carrying a note appear.

selected.help: The standard solutions marked as under consideration, addressed as selected[id] with the value true. Only marked ones appear.

filterMode.help: The list filter: auto shows only the classes matching the diagnosis, all shows all five.

expandedClasses.help: The numbers of the expanded standard classes, 1 to 5. A persisted display state — it belongs to the saved project, not to the analysis.

diagnosis.help: The diagnosis derived from S1, S2, field type and link, with situation and suggestedClasses. It is not stored.

Diagnosis.situation: The state of the model, derived from the substances, field type and link and not stored: partial (S1 or S2 missing), incomplete (no field or link missing), complete-useful (complete, useful action), complete-insufficient (complete, insufficient action), complete-excessive (complete, excessive action), complete-harmful (complete, harmful action). The “Diagnosis” line shows it as a sentence.
Diagnosis.suggestedClasses: The numbers of the suggested standard classes, 1 to 5: 1 for partial, incomplete and complete-harmful, 2 for complete-insufficient, complete-excessive and complete-useful, plus 3 for a useful action and 5 for an excessive or harmful one. The “Diagnosis” line shows them under “Suggested classes”.

triz-sufield.subtitle: Model the interaction as a substance-substance-field triangle and use the diagnosis to find the matching standard solutions.

situation.partial: S1 or S2 missing — please name both substances.
situation.incomplete: Incomplete model (no field) — a new interaction must be built.
situation.complete-useful: Complete, useful — improvement & next-generation jump possible.
situation.complete-insufficient: Complete but insufficient — strengthen or dynamise the field.
situation.complete-excessive: Complete but excessive — damp the action / self-limit.
situation.complete-harmful: Complete but harmful — destroy or neutralise the Su-Field.

errors.notAnAction: Entry {index} is not an action object.
errors.duplicateId: The id "{id}" appears more than once.
errors.unknownParam: Action "{op}" does not know the field "{param}".
errors.wrongType: Field "{param}" of "{op}" must be {expected}, but is {actual}.
errors.forwardRef: Reference to "{id}" does not point backwards.
errors.unresolvedRef: Reference to "{id}" cannot be resolved; "available" lists the action ids a reference may point to.
errors.unresolvedRefId: Reference to "{id}" cannot be resolved: that action id has no result. "available" lists the action ids that already have one.
errors.unresolvedRefPath: Path "{path}" cannot be resolved in the result of "{id}"; segment "{segment}". "available" lists the keys of that level.
errors.badShape: Path "{path}" does not exist in the result shape of "{id}"; segment "{segment}".
errors.nullableRef: Path "{path}" in action "{id}" descends into a field that can be null at runtime. Reference the field itself and branch in a second batch.
errors.unknownPhaseInCycle: Unknown phase "{phase}" in the active cycle.
errors.viewmodelNotAlive: Instance "{instance}" is not active (view not open).
errors.methodNotAgentAction: Module "{module}" does not release "{method}" as an action — whether the method exists internally makes no difference. Only what "available" lists is callable; a different spelling of the same name changes nothing.
errors.moduleNotAgentReady: Module "{module}" is not released for agents.
errors.moduleSingleton: Module "{module}" may exist only once per project; the instance "{instance}" already exists.
errors.addNotPersisted: Module "{module}" was not added: the project state did not accept the write.
errors.flushFailed: The batch wrote successfully, but the state could not be saved: {detail}

usage.intro: Qprovement is a browser-based Six Sigma toolkit. This surface reads the project state, adds tools and calls their actions — through the same calls the user interface uses.
usage.call: window.qprovement.interact() returns this description. window.qprovement.interact(action) or interact([action, …]) executes and returns a Promise.
usage.actionForm: An action is { op, … } with the fields from the action catalog. Unknown fields are an error. Giving an action its own id makes it referenceable.
usage.refForm: A reference to an earlier result is the object { $from: '<id>', path: '<dot-path>' }. The path knows keys and numeric indices only — no arithmetic, no filters. If you need to compute, read and send a second batch.
usage.nullableForm: In a result shape, { $nullable: … } means “this shape or null at runtime”. $nullable is a word of the grammar, not a key — reference the field itself and branch in a second batch instead of descending into the shape.
usage.batchForm: The whole batch is validated before anything runs. On the first runtime error execution stops; partial results already obtained are returned.
usage.errorForm: Each entry returns { ok: true, result } or { ok: false, error, message, available? }. available names the valid alternatives.
usage.availability: Modules without a release appear in the catalog with available: false. They are described but not operable — tell the user which tool would be right now and let them drive it.
usage.limits: You get numbers, not pictures: you cannot see a chart. There is no undo — the user was prompted to export when granting access.
usage.viewSwitch: instance.call shows the target instance before calling its method — the viewmodel only lives in the active view. A batch that calls several instances switches the view accordingly; that is intended, and it is how the user sees what is being worked on.
usage.keysForm: module.describe describes actions and read fields including keys: for a generic setter such as setParam every allowed key, for a result field such as result every figure, each with type and help, nested in the keys of the next level. An empty keys list means no declared structure. optional: true means the key is absent in some states, for example per chart type or with a one-sided tolerance. A type such as Object<string, …> is a map whose keys come from the data, for example one per appraiser; keys then describes one entry. The same help text appears in the interface at the label when the user holds Alt.
